# Implementation log

The completed-work record split out of [implementation-plan.md](implementation-plan.md) (per user request, 2026-05-16). The plan stays authoritative for **pending / in-flight** work and keeps a one-line ✅ pointer for every shipped iteration; the full per-iteration narrative, package status, build/test signals, and historical sync log live here.

See also [implementation-plan-table.md](implementation-plan-table.md) (at-a-glance grid).

## Beta program (retired) — shipped v0.1.5, 2026-06-29

The public beta shipped `v0.1.5` on 2026-06-29 (~9 weeks ahead of the original `2026-09-01` target) and the product has since released through `v0.7.0`. The gate-driven scaffolding that paced the run to beta — the three clocks, the beta-freeze scope table, the G0→G4 gate roadmap, the decision queue, the beta-exit checklist, and the cut levers — is retired; it is preserved verbatim below for the record. Forward planning now lives in [implementation-plan.md § Release trains](implementation-plan.md#release-trains--the-forward-queue-2-heroes-each).

> **The unit is verification cycles, not calendar weeks.** Authoring is effectively free (AI agents, fanned out). What remains scarce — and what `2026-09-01` actually has to clear — is **(1) decision latency**, **(2) the irreducible verification floor**, **(3) serial-unknown depth**. A "week" in the old roadmap was human typing time; that's gone. The schedule is now paced by how fast the decision queue drains and how many soak/build/review cycles fit before the date — both generous *if decisions stay fast*, both fatal if they don't. Faster authoring raises the rate of confident-but-wrong output, so the binding constraint is **review/verification throughput, not author throughput** (the "Graph icons regressed 6×" failure mode is the canonical AI-speed risk — the gates *are* the product now).

### The three clocks that actually bind

| Clock | What it is | Why it doesn't compress with authoring |
|---|---|---|
| **Decision latency** | Human OQ/product round-trips (the burn-down queue below) | An unanswered OQ stalls a whole gate no matter how fast code is written. This is now the critical path. |
| **Verification floor** | sync soak across real instances · multi-arch signed-build CI · perf/virtualization soak under real data volume · security review of the crypto path | Clock-bound, not author-bound: the sync layer can be written in an afternoon and still need days of soak to be *known* correct. |
| **Serial-unknown depth** | spikes that gate *design*, not just typing (`10.0`→`10.x`) | A wrong foundational CRDT/crypto call is cheap to *fix* now but no cheaper to *detect*; you cannot parallelize discovering it. |

### Gate-driven roadmap (G0→G4)

Not dated phases — **gates with entry/exit conditions**. A gate clears when its exit condition is *verified*, not when its code is written. Each gate names its **serial spine** (one owner, an integration point or sequential unknown — cannot be parallelized away) and its **parallel fan-out** (N agent teams, claimed through the orchestration ledger; see Execution model). `2026-09-01` is the outer bound G4 must clear by, not a per-gate allocation.

| Gate | Serial spine (1 owner) | Parallel fan-out (N teams) | Exit condition (verified, not written) | Bound by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G0 De-risk** | `10.0` sync spike; `3b` at-rest flip + startup probe | OQ burn-down #1–4; `12.9` CI gate; `9.3.5.B` body | `10.0` proves ciphertext-only over a blind relay **and** forces OQ-10/26/27/28/29 positions; `3b` flip green | decision latency + spike depth |
| **G1 Spine** | `9.3.5.N1–N5` Notes Lexical-yjs rewrite → `9.3.3` → `9.4.1–4` → `9.5.1–3` → `9.11 embed` | `9.10` files-service half; `13.4a` design (rides N5) | Notes at parity behind flag; a block-embed mounts end-to-end through a sandboxed frame | serial-unknown depth |
| **G2 Sync** | `10.1–10.9` E2E-encrypted multi-device (built on `10.0`); from 2026-05-23 each remaining core-app `9.4`/`9.10`-gated tail is **also serial — inside its app's slot in Phase 2**: Tasks `9.14.3`, Calendar `9.15.3`, Whiteboard `9.17.4`/`.7`, Bookmarks `9.18.4`, Graph (remaining), Notes (remaining); already-landed: `9.17.8b` ✅, `9.13.13b` ✅, `B6.4a` ✅, `9.8.5` ✅, `9.12.16-UI` slice 1 ✅, `9.12.16-UI` slice 2 ✅ | (parallel branch OFF — see Execution model) | `10.9` green: two instances edit concurrently, blind relay sees **ciphertext only**, soaked | **verification floor** (soak — the hard one) |
| **G3 Quality + freeze** | `13.4a` virtualization lands + soaks | `12.1` i18n · `12.4` a11y · `12.7` perf-harness · **import/migration `IE-1`→`IE-6`** (off the critical path) · bug burn-down (fan-out) | feature freeze; a11y/perf budgets hold on a dogfood-size vault; a real Notion **and** Obsidian export imports cleanly | verification floor |
| **G4 Beta ship** ✅ | **CLEARED 2026-06-29 — `v0.1.5` public** | `13.1` multi-arch signed builds · `13.11` signing+notarisation · `13.12` in-app auto-update — all ✅ | shipped on GitHub Releases (signed/notarized mac, win, linux) | **done** |

Authoring G1's bulk and the G2 fan-out is hours, not weeks; G0→G1→G2's *spine* is serial because each rung is a sequential unknown or an integration point; G2/G3/G4's date risk is **soak and multi-arch CI**, which no amount of agents shortens. Pace the calendar by those, nothing else. **From 2026-05-23 the G2 fan-out and G3 quality fan-out are run serially under the new ordering policy** ([[feedback_serial_shell_then_apps]]) — the verification floor is unchanged, the agent-team multiplier on top of it is gone.

### Beta-exit checklist (`2026-09-01`)

> **How to prove each box:** [ops/beta-exit-runbook.md](ops/beta-exit-runbook.md) — the runnable version (command/spec, pass criteria, current status). A box is done only when run **as a gate on the signed RC**, not when the code exists.

- [ ] Core apps (11, above) usable; **no `◑` in the beta build for a core app**.
- [ ] `10.9` green: two instances pair, edit concurrently, blind relay sees ciphertext only.
- [ ] At-rest encryption flipped on-disk; startup contract probe passes against the real driver.
- [ ] `13.1` signed builds CI-green on macOS / Windows / Linux (incl. arm64); `13.3` Playwright smoke.
- [x] `13.11` Apple certs procured + wired; macOS `.dmg` **notarized** (`hardenedRuntime: true`) and shipped in **v0.1.5** (opens clean past Gatekeeper); auto-update feed live via GitHub Releases (`latest*.yml`). *Residual (GA, not beta-blocking): Windows EV (`DQ-13.1-B`) — Windows currently unsigned (SmartScreen prompt).*
- [ ] `13.10` packaged-app upgrade path: a build update re-installs changed bundled apps via `AppInstaller.update()` (capability diffs granted) — verified across one real build-over-build update.
- [ ] `13.4a` virtualization holds on a dogfood-size vault (Notes won't blow the keystroke→paint budget).
- [ ] Switch-in works: `IE-1`→`IE-6` land; a real Notion export-zip **and** a real Obsidian vault import into a fresh vault with types/properties/links/assets preserved; `.bsbundle` takeout + restore round-trips losslessly.
- [ ] `12.4` a11y + `12.7` perf budgets pass for the core; per-package coverage floors hold.
- [ ] Decision-queue G0+G1 rows resolved; no open Sev-1.

### Cut levers (pre-declared — if a gate's verification floor won't clear by `2026-09-01`, cut in this order)

1. **Defer non-core app tails** to post-beta (Graph/Whiteboard export) — beta apps stay usable without them.
2. **Narrow the migration ladder** to the highest-traffic source: keep `IE-1`→`IE-4` + `IE-6` (Notion), defer `IE-5` (Obsidian) to post-beta if its parser won't clear review in time — Notion is the dominant switch-in source, so the seamless-switch story survives the cut. `IE-1` `.bsbundle` takeout is *never* cut (it's the §5 hard floor).
3. **Narrow sync** to single-user multi-device *restore* only; defer the `10.5` pairing-UX polish to GA (keep `10.9` ciphertext-only proof — non-negotiable).
4. **Defer `13.4a`** if the dogfood vault stays under the DOM-size budget in practice (re-arm it the moment it doesn't).
5. **Hard floor — never cut:** at-rest + in-transit encryption, data integrity/migration reversibility, the spine itself. A beta that loses or leaks data is not a beta.

**Build + test signals (last run):**

- **`SYNC-3` + `SYNC-4b` + `SYNC-5` — pluggable storage, gated admission, ops limits — ✅ (2026-06-23, `../brainstorm-sync` `66913ec` + product `cbcf7158`).** The three remaining durable-sync-node rungs; the node side is fully `tsc` + biome clean with **84 tests** and the product client half adds **7**.
  - **`SYNC-3` pluggable storage provider (OQ-SYNC-1 ✅).** One wire protocol, swappable backend behind the existing `SnapshotStore`/`AccountCatalog` interfaces. New `object-store.ts` — an `ObjectBucket` seam (get/put/delete/list) with `ObjectSnapshotStore` + `ObjectAccountCatalog` storing the **same opaque snapshot+tail blobs** as the local file backend (so durability + offline backfill + cold-restore behave identically), and `bun-s3-bucket.ts` — the zero-dep S3/R2/MinIO adapter over Bun's built-in S3 client (NoSuchKey→null, paginated `list`). `main.ts` selects **forward-only** / **local** (`STORAGE_DIR`, the default) / **s3** (`S3_BUCKET`+creds — our managed bucket or a self-hoster's bring-your-own bucket) from env. The bucket credential is transport auth, not a vault key — relay-blind preserved. Tested against an in-memory `MemoryBucket` + a fake S3 client so the snapshot+tail layout is provable without a live bucket. +11 tests.
  - **`SYNC-4b` entitlement-gated admission + metering.** The cross-plane design call (the user's): the entitlement token's `sub` is the **billing** account and is explicitly NOT the wire `sender` (= base64url identity pubkey), so admission uses a **two-proof connect handshake** rather than overloading one id. `entitlement.ts` verifies the `brainstorm-cloud` Ed25519 token via WebCrypto **offline** (the `packages/api-client` §EntitlementClaims format mirrored, never imported — same posture as `wire.ts`); `admission.ts` then requires a **server nonce signed by the device identity key** (proving the wire `account`). The node challenges on connect, gates frames/subscribe/catalog until both proofs pass, **scopes the `catalog` query to the proven account** (closing the SYNC-4a open-admission metadata leak), rejects frames whose `sender` ≠ the proven account (no impersonation), and emits connect/ingress/egress **metering** (`metering.ts` → `METERING_LOG_PATH`) keyed by the verified `sub` for billing-edge. Both verifies are the one reviewed `relay-blind-exempt` (auth, never content); `server.ts` consults only an **injected** `Admission` via a type-only import, so the route path stays crypto-free. Open node (no `ENTITLEMENT_KEYS`) ⇒ open admission, wire path unchanged (OQ-SYNC-2 spirit). **Client half (product `cbcf7158`):** `WebSocketRelayPort` gained an injected `onChallenge` (stays relay-blind — it ships opaque strings the callback returns) that answers a `challenge` with `{token, account, sig}` and re-sends subscriptions on `auth-ok`; `challenge-responder.ts` is the credential-aware glue (account = base64url identity pubkey, `signNonce` via the session signer, token via `BillingService.currentToken()`); `index.ts` wires it into the orchestrator's `makeRelayPort`, reading the live session lazily. Dormant in v1 (no token cached, open nodes never challenge) — ready for the managed/gated node + the `14.3` token. +30 node tests (entitlement fail-closed paths · admission two-proof · gated-server socket-free · gated real-WS E2E) + 7 product (port handshake ×3, responder ×4).
  - **`SYNC-5` ops.** `limits.ts` — a pure, injected-clock `Limits` facade over token-bucket `KeyedRateLimiter`s: per-IP connection rate, per-connection message + byte rate, per-account frame rate, and hard caps on frame size / control-message size / subscriptions-per-connection; on by default (`LIMITS_DISABLED=1` off), idle-limiter eviction bounds memory, rejection counters for ops. Audit sink/rotation = the existing `AUDIT_LOG_PATH` NDJSON + external logrotate; deploy manifests = `Dockerfile` + `.env.example`. +8 tests.

The `../brainstorm-sync` node work is a separate repo and was unaffected. Two pre-existing `seed-demo-apps.ts` typecheck errors (`isAppIconDismissed`/`clearAppIconDismissed` on `DashboardStore`) arrived with that merge and are unrelated to this work.
- **`10.14` consumer crypto core — engine handles inbound `WrapBootstrap` (DEK recovery) 🟡 (2026-06-22).** The restore consumer's load-bearing piece: the `LiveSyncEngine` now processes inbound `WrapBootstrap` frames — `#handleWrap` → `receiveWrapBootstrap` (verify sig + parse the wrap) → an injected, optional **`installWrap`** hook (the wiring HPKE-unwraps with the device X25519 secret — which never crosses into the engine — re-seals the DEK under the master key, persists it). **Un-gated on `#tracked`**: a cold/restoring device has no local doc to pass `isShared`, but a wrap is HPKE-sealed *for this device*, so installing the DEK it carries is always safe + idempotent. Absent `installWrap` ⇒ a no-op "live-only" mode (no restore), so the 10.12 behaviour is unchanged. Combined with the wraps-first backfill ordering + the serialized receive chain, a restoring device installs the DEK **before** the `Snapshot` it then decrypts. **+2 engine tests** (installs-a-DEK-from-an-inbound-WrapBootstrap-during-restore / ignored-when-no-installWrap-wired); typecheck + biome clean, **496 sync+entities+collab tests green**. **Remaining (the restore orchestration):** request the catalog → subscribe each entity bypassing the `isShared` gate → materialise rows + stamp `dekId` + reindex; plus the production `installWrap` wiring (extract the dev-bridge `#installWrap` recipient-side install). The engine *capability* is built + tested; its consumer (the orchestration) is next.
- **`SYNC-2`/`10.14` DEK-wrap persistence for keystore-intact restore — ✅ (2026-06-22, `../brainstorm-sync` `c0e83cc`); resolves OQ-SYNC-4.** Reconsidered the earlier "wraps are transient" call: for restore-from-loss, a device that kept its **keystore** (X25519 + master key) but lost its local data must recover the per-entity **DEK** to decrypt the backfill — and the HPKE-sealed `WrapBootstrap` is exactly that key material, which the node can re-serve **without being able to open it** (it has no X25519 key — relay-blind preserved). So the durable node now **retains `WrapBootstrap` frames** (`SnapshotStore.appendWrap`, bounded at `WRAP_RETENTION = 64` since it can't dedup by the sealed recipient) and serves them **FIRST** in backfill (`wraps ++ snapshot ++ tail`) so the device installs the DEK before applying the encrypted state. Wraps **survive compaction** (the DEK is still needed after a snapshot resets the tail). `persistFrame` now routes `WrapBootstrap → appendWrap` (Awareness/Pairing still dropped). **Net:** restore works **without account recovery** for the common keystore-intact case; the fully-cold case (lost keystore) still rides account recovery (security/51). **OQ-SYNC-4 resolved** (both, layered). +3 tests (wrap-first ordering · survives-compaction · cross-restart durability · server cold-subscriber-gets-wrap-first); **33 pass**, `tsc` + biome clean.

New `src/sync/account-catalog.ts` (`AccountCatalog` interface + `MemoryAccountCatalog`) + `file-account-catalog.ts` (durable, base64url-safe account names + per-account cache + persist-on-new + write serialization). `server.ts` records `sender→entityId` on route and answers a new **`catalog` control op** on the control channel (`catalog-result`) — the account's entity ids joined with each one's latest snapshot version; catalog-optional (absent ⇒ no-op). `main.ts` enables the durable catalog under `<STORAGE_DIR>/catalog`. **Relay-blind preserved** (metadata only, zero crypto). **SYNC-4b (the actual seam, remaining):** verify a `brainstorm-cloud` Ed25519 entitlement token to admit a connection + scope the catalog to the verified account (closes the open-admission metadata leak) + meter usage — needs the cloud token; token verification is the one reviewed `relay-blind-exempt` (auth, not content). **+8 tests** incl. a **real-WebSocket catalog round-trip** (a fresh device enumerates its account's entities over the wire); **30 pass** in the sync repo, `tsc` + biome clean.

So a row whose sort key is `[]` (e.g. a multi-select / tags property with nothing selected) was treated as a *present* value and ignored by `emptyPlacement`, landing among real values instead of with the other empties. Aligned `isEmpty` with the shared notion (null/undefined/empty-string/empty-array) the aggregations + editable-cell paths already use. +1 test (an `[]` sort key sorts to the end with missing values under `EmptyPlacement.End`); database compile-view 18 green, app typecheck + biome clean. (Other engine candidates reviewed — multi-hop `In` swap, `toTimestamp` range, predicate NaN-compare, empty-set intersect — were sound or defensible; not changed.)

- **Automations 11b.6 — nested SubWorkflow capability re-scoping ✅ (2026-06-14).** Resolves the limitation the chores security pass deferred: gate (1) narrowed a sub-workflow's ceiling one level deep, but `runChildren` reused the same ports, so in A→B→C the callee C was re-scoped against A's running caps, not B's declared caps (B's consent surface was bypassed; only the hard service-enforced ceiling held). `RunContext` now carries a per-subtree capability ceiling and `runChildren(steps, seed?, { capabilities })` lets a container narrow it; the SubWorkflow interpreter validates against `ctx.capabilities ?? ports.capabilities` (top-level falls back to the ports' caps) and runs the callee's body with the ceiling narrowed to the callee's OWN declared caps. Branch/ForEach inherit the ceiling unchanged. So a nested sub-workflow is now honoured against the intermediate's consent surface, not just the outermost grant. +2 tests (nested-denied-against-intermediate; nested-allowed-within-intermediate); automations suite **156 green**, §4 pipeline test green, packages typecheck + biome clean. Both 11b.6 security gates now fully landed (single + nested); only the live session-open deploy (real-Electron) remains. Full detail in [implementation-plan.md](implementation-plan.md) (11b.6).
- **Code-editor 9.7.3 — autocomplete combobox ARIA ✅ (2026-06-14).** Accessibility polish on the completion popup: it set `aria-selected` on rows but never wired the textarea, so a screen reader couldn't announce the active completion. `completion-popup.ts` now wires the editing surface as the combobox input — `aria-autocomplete="list"` + `aria-controls=<listbox id>` set up front, `aria-expanded` toggled on open/close, `aria-activedescendant` tracking the active option (each row carries a stable `<listbox>-opt-<i>` id), cleared on hide — so the highlighted completion is announced while focus stays in the editor. A per-instance id seed keeps multiple panes' listbox/option ids distinct. +2 tests (combobox wiring across show/move/hide; distinct ids per popup); code-editor suite **455 green**, app typecheck + biome clean. Full detail in [implementation-plan.md](implementation-plan.md) (9.7.3).
- **Automations 11b.6 — SubWorkflow re-scoping security gate ✅ (2026-06-14).** Closes the second (and last) of the two security gates the 11b.6 host-deploy was waiting on. A `SubWorkflow` step ran the callee's steps under the *caller's* ports/caps, and the caller's static capability validation never saw the callee's steps — so a sub-workflow could exercise caps beyond what it (or, transitively, what was granted) declared. `WorkflowStepsLoader` now returns `{steps, capabilities}` (the callee's own frozen caps), `InterpreterPorts` carries `capabilities` (the running caps the ports were built under), and the SubWorkflow interpreter re-scopes at the call boundary with the SAME two-tier `missingCapabilities` check the host's `capabilityViolations` uses — callee steps ⊆ callee declared caps, AND callee declared caps ⊆ caps-in-effect — failing closed `sub-workflow-capability-denied:<caps>` (child never runs) on either tier. The broker glue reads `props.capabilities` defensively and exposes `ports.capabilities`. +6 tests; automations suite **151 green**, §4 pipeline test green, packages typecheck + biome clean. With gate (2) (entity-type scope) from earlier today, **both 11b.6 security gates are now landed** — the only remaining 11b.6 work is the live session-open registration (real-Electron deploy). Full detail in [implementation-plan.md](implementation-plan.md) (11b.6).

The `Entity` step interpreter resolved its target id from the untrusted trigger payload and the entities service authorizes by the *fetched* type — so a step declared on `Task/v1` could update/delete/get an entity of any type the automations app can touch. `step-interpreters.ts` now fetches the target first and refuses (non-retriable `entity-<op>-out-of-scope`) when `fetched.type !== step.entityType`; update/delete additionally fail closed on a missing target (`entity-<op>-not-found` — a mutator can't confirm scope without the row), while `get` keeps returning `null` for a missing entity (no scope question, no leak) and only refuses a present out-of-scope one. +5 tests (out-of-scope refusal for update/delete/get with the mutators asserted never-called; get-missing→null; update-missing→fail); automations suite **144 green**, the CLAUDE.md §4 in-process pipeline test still green, packages typecheck + biome clean. Remaining 11b.6 before live deploy: gate (1) SubWorkflow re-scoping + the session-open registration (real-Electron). Full detail in [implementation-plan.md](implementation-plan.md) (11b.6).

- **Automations 11b.9 — Branch/ForEach evaluator upgrade ✅ (2026-06-14).** The `Code`-step sandboxed expression grammar (`code-expression.ts`, landed 2026-06-13) now backs the Branch condition + ForEach collection defaults too. `defaultConditionEvaluator`/`defaultCollectionResolver` in `step-interpreters.ts` route through `evaluateExpression` over a shared `expressionScope` (the same prior-outputs-plus-`input` scope `codeExpressionScope` now delegates to), replacing the literal/ref-only stubs — so Branch takes real expressions (`input.count > 3`, `input.status == "done"`, `len(s1) > 0 && input`) and ForEach resolves member access / built-ins (`input.rows`, `split(input, ",")`). Fail-closed by construction: empty condition = truthiness of `input`, empty collection = `input`-if-array, any parse error / unknown identifier / blocked key → `false`/`[]` (Branch → `alternate`, ForEach inert). Pre-grammar shorthands keep working: `true`/`false`/`input` parse natively, and a condition/collection that is EXACTLY a prior step id is resolved by a whole-string `outputs` lookup BEFORE the grammar runs (chores-pass fix), so a hyphenated id (`"step-1"`) resolves to that step's output instead of parsing as subtraction. +8 tests (grammar + fail-closed in both defaults; hyphenated-step-id whole-string lookup; Branch + ForEach end-to-end). - **Web Browser — `Browser-2` (WebView host service) + `Browser-3` (chrome) + web-link routing ✅ (2026-06-09).** The first-party Web Browser graduated from the Browser-1 scaffold (contracts + pure logic; `app.ts` was still the coming-soon placeholder) into a working in-app browser. **Browser-2 — the shell-side engine.** Web content runs in shell-managed, partitioned, Node-less Electron `WebContentsView`s the chrome drives over IPC; the page DOM/bytes never reach a Brainstorm renderer (the doc-54 chrome-only / shell-engine split, like Mailbox). **OQ-WV-1 resolved** = one `WebContentsView` per tab, each with its own ephemeral non-`persist:` partition destroyed on close (private-by-default, no cross-tab cookie linkage). **OQ-WV-2 resolved** = a soft cap of 6 live views per window; beyond it the least-recently-active non-pinned tab is suspended (view destroyed, URL retained, reloaded on re-activation), pinned tabs exempt. The wire contract was lifted from the app to the shared `@brainstorm/sdk-types` `web-view.ts` (shell + app speak one vocabulary; `apps/browser/src/types/{web-view,browsing-session}.ts` now re-export it, frozen values intact) and gained a `WebViewClient` chrome-facing interface + `APP_WEBVIEW_EVENT_CHANNEL`. **Pure orchestration core** `main/web/web-view-service.ts` (`WebViewService` + `makeWebViewServiceHandler`): the tab registry, method routing (open/navigate/back/forward/reload/stop/close/activate/set-bounds/find/capture), metadata-event fan-out, and the suspension policy — every Electron touch-point injected (`createView`/`resolveWindow`/`emitEvent`/`capture`), so it is exhaustively fake-tested (**+14**). **Pure security keystone** `main/web/web-policy.ts` (**+10**): top-level HTTPS-upgrade (loopback-exempt), a bundled tracker/ad blocklist (OQ-WV-4 static v1 list; the signed updatable feed is post-v1), a fail-closed navigation-scheme allowlist (`file:`/`javascript:`/custom-scheme navigation refused), and URL→security-badge mapping. **Electron glue** `main/web/web-view-factory.ts` (not unit-tested — verified in the running shell, same posture as `print-to-pdf`): constructs the locked-down view (`sandbox:true`, `contextIsolation:true`, `nodeIntegration:false`, **no preload** so the page reaches no Brainstorm bridge), installs deny-default permission handlers (surfaced as a `PermissionRequested` metadata event before denying), the blocklist `onBeforeRequest`, a window-open-denied handler, the navigation guard, wires native `webContents` events → the metadata-event callback, and offsets the chrome-reported bounds by the window body origin (new `WindowContainer.bodyBounds()`) so the view lands under the chrome. Registered as the `webView` broker service (fail-closed behind the **High `web.browse`** capability — deliberately NOT in `DEFAULT_APP_CAPABILITIES`) + the SDK `webViewProxy` (cap-stamped: `web.browse`, `web.capture` for capture) + the preload `APP_WEBVIEW_EVENT_CHANNEL` listener that fans events to `services.webView.onEvent`. **Browser-3 — the chrome.** `apps/browser` is now a React chrome-only app (`app.tsx` + `main.tsx`, the coming-soon import dropped): a tab strip (open/close/switch/new), an omnibox (URL-or-search normalize), back/forward/reload/stop, a per-tab security badge and tracker shield — all strings via `t()`, all driven through `services.webView` and painted from its metadata events. Tab state is the pre-existing pure `logic/session.ts` reducer (in-memory; `BrowsingSession/v1` persist + restore is a follow-up). The page region is a placeholder div whose rect the chrome reports via `setBounds`; the shell floats the `WebContentsView` over it. **Link-routing** (your "make all web links open in a browser, with a system-browser option"): the manifest now registers `http`/`https` **primary scheme openers**, so a web-link `open` intent resolves to the in-app Browser by default through the existing open-resolution ladder (`decideOpen`'s Scheme branch already honours `hasInVaultOpener` ahead of OS handoff), and the existing **Settings → Default apps → Schemes** section auto-populates `http:`/`https:` rows with an "Open with system default" choice (zero new Settings UI) as the system-browser escape hatch — backed by the same `defaultHandlers` pin the ladder reads first. **Verification**: **+59 tests** (web service 14 · web policy 10 · open-resolution routing anchor 1 · the Browser-1 reducer 22 still green · plus the wire-relocation re-export); full `bun run typecheck` (packages + 20 apps) clean, biome clean, the full vitest suite green (incl. a fixed pre-existing `plan-coverage` gap — the `Collab-C4-live` track id wasn't in `LEAD_ID_RE`), and the browser app builds. **Follow-ups** (not blocking the working browser): reader-mode `web.capture` → `Bookmark/v1` (the host port is wired but unimplemented — Browser-5); find-in-page UI + `nav-history`/shared `<FindBar>` adoption; `BrowsingSession/v1` persistence + restore; a per-page in-app "open in system browser" affordance (needs a small cap-gated force-OS-handoff intents option); and **real-Electron dogfood verification** of live paint / event flow / partition teardown / permission denial / Settings→Privacy→Network egress (the documented real-shell residue, as with the other shell engines).

- **Connector framework spine `Connector-1..4` ✅ + GitHub-issues reference connector landed 2026-06-06.** The slice that ungates Mailbox / CalDAV / Agent. Investigation found Net-1/Net-2 already done — the real missing dependency the plan kept citing as "an OAuth/account framework, neither of which exists" was the Connector framework itself, so the whole spine shipped. **Connector-1** (`@brainstorm/sdk-types/connector.ts`): the four contracts (`Connector`/`ConnectorAccount`/`SyncMapping`/`SyncRun`/v1) + enums (`SyncDirection`/`ConflictPolicy`/`AuthState`/`SyncRunStatus`) + structural validators, and the **custody/egress keystone** mirroring the automations capability keystone — `parseOriginPattern`/`isEgressAllowed`/`validateConnectorRequest` (fail-closed: unparseable / wildcard-all / out-of-scope all refuse), `connectorRequiredCapabilities` (derives `network.connect:<origin>` per frozen origin, never `*`, + `entities.write:<type>`), `isWildcardAll` (rejects `network.connect:*`), and a structural `EmbeddedSecret` check that rejects any token-shaped key on the account entity. **Connector-2** (`main/connectors/`): the shell OAuth broker — `oauth-pkce.ts` (RFC-7636 S256, the Appendix-B vector pinned), `oauth-redirect.ts` (ephemeral `127.0.0.1:0` single-shot loopback with constant-time `state` compare + hard timeout + always-close; OQ-CN-2 resolved loopback-primary, custom-scheme behind the same `RedirectProvider` iface), `oauth-broker.ts` (`authorize` runs PKCE → loopback → token exchange via Net-1 egress scoped to the frozen origins → seals tokens in Tier-2 `CredentialStore` keyed `oauth:<accountId>` → creates the token-free `ConnectorAccount`; `getValidAccessToken`/`refresh` shell-side, on failure flip `authState=expired` + notify once [OQ-CN-4 resolved]; `revoke` deletes the token + flips `revoked`), and the `connectors` service (`authorize`/`revoke`, server-side `connectors.oauth` cap re-checked against the ledger). Tokens never cross IPC. **Connector-3** (`connectors-request.ts`): `connectors.request` resolves account→frozen origins, refuses out-of-scope URLs (`Denied` + logged, never silent), injects `Authorization: Bearer` (and strips it from the response), and rides Net-1 `executeNetworkFetch` for SSRF/size/time/audit; server-side `connectors.request` + the derived `network.connect:<origin>`. **Connector-4** (`sync-runner.ts`/`field-map.ts`/`sync-run-def.ts`/`connectors-sync-service.ts`): a declarative `PullSpec` the shell executes generically (no connector code runs shell-side), `applyFieldMap`, **idempotent upsert keyed on a flat indexed `connectorExternalId`** (the highest-risk invariant — bare property so the entities `where` compiles to a direct `json_extract`) + a richer `connector.source` provenance block, `SyncRun/v1`, default `external-wins` (push/two-way throw `unsupported-direction`, the Connector-5 seam). It registers a `Time` trigger with the **existing** `SchedulerService` via a new `AutomationsHost` sync route (no second scheduler / no second entity-write path). The CLAUDE.md §4 in-process proof `connectors-pipeline.test.ts` drives a real `SchedulerService` + `AutomationsHost` + entities service over a temp vault: scheduler-fire → `connectors.sync` → stubbed GitHub page → real `Task/v1` rows in `entities.db` → `SyncRun/v1` persisted, asserting **a second identical fire produces no duplicate Tasks** + external-wins overwrites a vault edit. 200/2000 `SyncMapping` volume cap. The reference connector is the lean **GitHub-issues → Task/v1** app (`apps/github-issues/` + `FIRST_PARTY_APPS`) declaring frozen egress `api.github.com` + OAuth + a `github:issue → Task/v1` `SyncMapping` — it rides the substrate with zero connector-specific shell code (Mailbox stays its own later slice on the OQ-CN-5 socket-exception path, so Connector-7 is superseded as the *mainline* reference). SDK `connectors` proxy added (`ConnectorsService` type + `connectorsProxy`); `connectors` broker service registered in `index.ts` (`buildConnectorsServiceDeps` wires Net-1 egress + `CredentialStore` token store + entities-backed account port/resolvers). OQ-CN-1/CN-2/CN-4 resolved per the doc leans (added to the ledger); CN-3/CN-5/CN-6 remain. ~65 connector tests (21 contract + 24 broker/request/service + 17 sync-engine + 3 integration) ; typecheck (packages + **20** apps) / biome / `github-issues` vite build all green. **Real-shell residue (split out):** the production session-open registration (load `Connector`/`SyncMapping` → `ScheduleRegistration.syncMappings` → `AutomationsHost.hydrate`) for *scheduled* sync + the live loopback-OAuth round-trip need a real Electron restart to verify.

  - **Follow-up (real-shell fixes, same day):** the reference connector was reported broken on first launch. Two fixes: **(1) theme** — the app's `styles.css` used invented token names (`--color-text`, `--color-accent`, `--radius-md`, `--font-display`) whose fallbacks fired → unthemed; rewritten to the real `@brainstorm/tokens` names (`--color-text-primary`, `--color-background-primary`, `--color-accent-default`/`-text`, `--space-*`, `--text-*`) + an `#app-root` background/colour base (mirrors theme-editor). **(2) "does not work"** — there was no completable path (OAuth needs a registered client id we don't have, and *no* sync trigger was wired into the running shell). Added a **PAT (Personal Access Token) connect path** (`OAuthBroker.connectWithToken` → seals the user token in Tier-2, same custody, no OAuth app needed) and a **manual `connectors.sync`** broker method + a **"Sync now"** button, then **wired the production sync** in `wiring.ts` (`makeConnectorsSync` deps: `resolveMapping` from the `SyncMapping` entity, `request` through the egress proxy + `decodeJsonResponse`, idempotent lookup via `repo.listIdsWithProperty(connectorExternalId)`, entity writes under the connector identity). SDK `connectors` proxy gains `connectToken`/`sync`. So the connector now works end-to-end against real GitHub with a `repo`-scoped PAT (paste token → Connect → Sync now → issues land as `Task/v1`), no OAuth-app registration or scheduler deployment required. +6 tests (broker connectWithToken ×2, service connectToken/sync ×3). Real-shell verification (preload rebuild exposes `connectors`; app redeploys on full shell restart) is the user's to confirm; *scheduled* (Time-trigger) sync still awaits the AutomationsHost deployment.

The shell-main interpreter the scheduler hands a fire to (doc 39 §Scheduler — shell-side so a workflow runs whether or not the automations window is open). Scoped to the **runner core** — the per-kind step interpreters are injected and land in 11b.4. **(1) The loop** (`automations/workflow-runner.ts` `WorkflowRunner.run`) walks a workflow's steps in order through an injected `InterpreterRegistry` (`StepKind → StepInterpreter`), threading a **live `outputs` map** so a later step reads an earlier step's output (the leading `Trigger` pseudo-step is seeded with the fire payload — doc 39 §The step model). Like the scheduler it's **timer-free / IO-free at the core**: `clock`, `sleep`, and every effect are injected ports, so the whole fire→interpret→provenance→fail/retry path is exhaustively unit-testable without real timers or a vault. **(2) Provenance** — builds a flat, **depth-tagged** `stepLog` (one `StepLogEntry` per step: `stepId/kind/status/depth/startedAt/durationMs/attempts` + `output|error`); `depth` (0 at top, +1 per Branch/ForEach nesting) lets the Runs view (11b.13) render the timeline as nested blocks. `toWorkflowRunDef` maps a finished run into the `brainstorm/WorkflowRun/v1` entity shape (workflow/triggeredBy/triggeredAt-ISO/status/stepLog/error) for the host to persist. **(3) Container steps** — `RunContext.runChildren(steps)` drives a Branch/ForEach body through the *same* machinery (entries appended to the run's flat log in chronological order, retry inherited), so 11b.4's container interpreters recurse without re-implementing the loop; the runner stays agnostic to control-flow semantics. **(4) Failure** (doc 39 §Failure modes) — a step that throws, returns a non-retriable failure, or exhausts its retries fails the run, records downstream steps `skipped`, and surfaces the message on `run.error`; a thrown interpreter error is caught and demoted to a non-retriable failure so one bad interpreter can't crash the loop; a **declared-but-gated kind with no interpreter** (e.g. `AICall` pre-Stage-11) fails cleanly as `unsupported-step-kind:<kind>` rather than throwing. **(5) Retry** — a bounded `RetryPolicy { maxAttempts, backoffMs }` re-attempts only `retriable` failures, sleeping the computed backoff via the injected sleeper; `attempts` is recorded per step. **(6) Cancellation** — an `AbortSignal` cancels mid-run (remaining steps `skipped`, status `cancelled`); a host that aborts with the `timeout` reason maps the run to `timed-out` (the contract's two non-failure terminal statuses). **Design call — no contract churn**: doc 39's `onError: continue` / `onMissed` knobs aren't in the 11b.1-frozen `WorkflowStep`, so the runner ships the doc's *default* failure semantics (fail-and-skip) without inventing un-frozen fields; failure→skip + thrown + gated-kind; retry-then-succeed / give-up / no-retry-on-fatal / backoff-slept; already-aborted / abort-between-steps / timeout-reason; Branch body + depth tags / nested-failure propagation / ForEach repeated body; - **9.12.21 advanced predicates landed 2026-06-05** (Database mission-gap; the cross-property + `$not` half of the predicate-language plane, layered on main's existing 9.12.20 `$relativeDate`). A **typed-ref right-hand side** lets a comparison compare a property to **another property on the same row** (`$prop`) or to the **clock** (`$now`) — `due < now()`, `assignee = owner`, `spent > budget` — and a **negate toggle** exposes the existing `$not` group language. (1) **Wire format** (`@brainstorm/sdk-types/predicate.ts`, kept import-free): new `PropertyRef = {$prop} | {$now}` + `Comparand = number | string | PropertyRef`; the six comparison ops (`$eq/$neq/$gt/$lt/$gte/$lte`) widen to accept a ref anywhere a literal is allowed; a shared `isPropertyRef` guard; `FilterGroupNode.negate?`. (2) **Evaluator** (`apps/database/.../evaluate-predicate.ts`): `eqOperand`/`comparand` resolve a ref (`$now`→injected clock, `$prop`→sibling property), `asComparable` unwraps a property-ui `DateValue {at}` to ms so date cells order numerically, and `signMatches` returns **no-match for a missing/incomparable operand** — which also tightens evaluator↔SQL parity (`x < NULL` is never true in SQL either); `scalarEq` widened to `unknown`. (3) **SQL** (`entities-repo.ts`): `$eq`/`$gt`/`$lt` compile refs — `$now`→bound `Date.now()` param, `$prop`→sibling `json_extract`, both `.at`-unwrapped via a `jsonAtOrSelf` COALESCE + a new `compileComparison` helper. (4) **Filter model** (`filter-builder.ts`): `FilterCompareTo` + `FilterRule.compareTo` + `FilterDraft.negate`, round-tripped both ways (`ruleToPredicate`/`predicateToRule`/`isRuleComplete`/`describeRule`); `flattenFilter` (`compile-view.ts`) wraps a negated group in `$not`. (5) **UI** (`app.ts`): comparison ops open a **compare-to → value / now / property** submenu; a **Negate (NOT)** toggle on the root filter and each sub-group. (6) `entity-draft.ts` skips a ref operand when pinning create-flow defaults (a ref isn't a concrete value). **Tests +~26** — cross-property + clock-ref evaluator truth table (incl. missing-ref no-match) · SQL `$now`/`$prop` compile (`due < now()`, `assignee = owner`) · `compareTo`/`negate` filter round-trips · `$not` flatten. `bun run typecheck` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean; **735 database / sdk-types / entities-repo tests green**. Built in an isolated worktree off `main`; **deliberately layered on — not replacing — main's concurrent 9.12.20 `$relativeDate` operator** (a parallel agent landed a different relative-date design; per the integrator decision the two coexist). **Remaining Database mission-gap**: 9.12.17 formulas/rollups · 9.12.18/.19/.20 partial (aggregation persist · generic-import flow · relative-date picker UI) · 9.12.22 relations browse · 9.12.23 gallery/timeline card editing.

New pure `apps/database/src/logic/rollup.ts`: `RollupSpec {relationKey, targetPropertyKey, aggregation}` describes a rollup column; `linkedEntityIds(value)` resolves the linked ids out of any EntityRef storage shape the property system writes (a scalar id for a single relation, a `LabeledValue[]` `{value:id}[]` envelope for a multi relation, or a bare `string[]` — blanks + non-strings drop); `computeRollup(source, spec, entitiesById)` walks the source row's `relationKey` relation to the linked rows, reads each one's `targetPropertyKey`, and runs the gathered values through the **existing `computeAggregation` reducers** (deliberate DRY — a rollup *is* an aggregation over a *related* set rather than a column, so it reuses Sum/Average/Count/etc. wholesale), returning the same `AggregationResult` the footer uses so the caller formats it with `formatAggregation(result, targetDef)` in the target's own units (a Currency fee rollup reads `$4,000`, a Duration hours rollup `40h 30m`). Two-file split: the **pure handler** (`packages/shell/src/main/export/export-service-handler.ts`) validates the payload (must be an object with a string `html` ≤ 8 MiB → else `Invalid`; renderer throw → `Unavailable`) and delegates to an injected `renderHtmlToPdf` (so it unit-tests without Electron); the **privileged renderer** (`print-to-pdf.ts`) renders app-supplied self-contained HTML in a locked-down offscreen `BrowserWindow` → PDF bytes. - **9.4.5 SDK `services.bp.dispatch` proxy landed 2026-05-29** — closed the last data-path gap in the 9.4 mount-seam arc: `<BpBlockMount>` (9.4.4) spawned the sandboxed iframe + flushed Startup, but nothing forwarded a block's BP *request* envelope to the host router, so the block→host→block loop was unwired (Notes mounted the seam with no `onMessage`). **Type surface** — added `BpMessage` (app-facing BP 0.3 `Message` wire shape) + `BpService` (`dispatch(entityId, message) → Promise<BpMessage | null>`) to `@brainstorm/sdk-types` + `bp` on `AppRuntime.services`. Deliberately mirrored, not imported from `@blockprotocol/core` — only the shell (`main/bp/`) depends on BP core; `bp/envelope.ts` `BpEnvelope` stays the authoritative parser. **Runtime proxy** — `bpProxy(bridge)` → `bp.dispatch` with `args: [{entityId, payload}]` and **`caps: []`**. No-cap is correct: `bp.dispatch` is structural routing with no ambient authority (the broker's `broker-context.ts` checkCapability allows no-cap methods), and each Graph op is enforced per-type on the entities service downstream — a block inherits exactly the embedding app's data authority (the v1 model, OQ-BP-2). **`<BpBlockMount>` auto-forward** — optional `bp` prop; when set, each inbound block message auto-forwards via `bp.dispatch(entityId, msg)` and the non-null response posts back over the transport. The consumer's `onMessage` still fires first (observability). The shell re-validates the payload (it arrived off the untrusted frame); a malformed/non-dispatchable message resolves to `null` → nothing sent; bridge errors are swallowed (block degrades to its own rendering — matches the transport's silent-drop contract). `bp` rides a ref like `onMessage`, so swapping the service never churns the iframe (a remount would re-flush Startup + re-mint the channel id). Net: every embedding app gets the full round-trip by passing `bp={services.bp}` — no per-app `onMessage` re-wiring (the DRY win for Tasks/Calendar/Whiteboard when their BP blocks land). **Notes adoption** — `BlockEmbedView` passes `bp={getBrainstorm()?.services.bp}` into its mount; `NotesBrainstorm` gains optional `bp?: BpService` (absent on older shells / preview drop = send-only, which the stub srcdoc already is — it emits no requests yet, so this is forward-ready not behaviour-changing today). **Tests +4** — 2 runtime proxy (`runtime.test.ts`: forwards `{entityId, payload}` as a no-cap `bp.dispatch` envelope + unwraps reply; `null`-reply passthrough) + 2 mount auto-forward (`bp-block-mount.test.tsx`: inbound message → `dispatch` called with `(entityId, request)` + response posted back as a `host-to-block` `message` envelope; `null` dispatch → nothing posted). **Verification signals**: 108/108 across SDK runtime + block-mount + shell `bp/` + `bp-graph-pipeline`; `bun run typecheck` clean on packages + apps/notes; biome clean on the 7 touched files; apps/notes bundle builds. The pre-existing apps/tasks 9.14.6-inspector WIP typecheck errors (`compose-view`/`task-row`/`targeted-row-update` — `onSelectTask`/`notes` field churn) are unrelated and untouched. Clears the gate's **SDK `services.bp.dispatch` proxy** open item; remaining on Block-Protocol + host services: OQ-BP-5 Hook overlay UI · 13.3 Playwright sandbox proof.
- **NAPI-3c X25519 swap landed 2026-05-24** — `@noble/curves x25519` (`getPublicKey` + `getSharedSecret` + `keygen`) replaced by RustCrypto `x25519-dalek = "2"` (`static_secrets + zeroize` features) across two shell files: `credentials/device-x25519.ts` (keygen → `randomBytes(32) + x25519GetPublicKey(secret)`, + `publicKeyFromSecret`) and `pairing/pairing-handshake.ts` (SAS-mode ephemeral keygen + ECDH for the shared secret feeding `hkdfSha256` and `deriveSas`). Two new `#[napi]` exports — `x25519GetPublicKey(secret: Uint8Array) -> Uint8Array` and `x25519GetSharedSecret(secret, peerPublic) -> Uint8Array`. **Critical security parity:** the binding rejects low-order peer pubkeys post-scalar-mult by detecting the all-zero shared-secret signature of a small-subgroup attack (`Status::InvalidArg`, message `"x25519: peer public key is in the small subgroup (all-zero shared secret)"`) — matches @noble's upfront `invalid private or public key received` throw. Without this rejection, a malicious peer could send a low-order pubkey to force a deterministic shared secret which the attacker also computes, breaking the pairing-handshake HKDF and the SAS-mode flow. **Byte-identical to `@noble/curves x25519` v2.2.0 proven by `packages/native/test/x25519.test.ts`** across: pubkey derivation on 4 fixed secrets; DH across all 12 (i,j) pairs where i≠j; DH symmetry `shared(a,B) == shared(b,A)`; cross-impl interop both directions (Rust signs, @noble verifies — and vice versa, full ECDH-up-down); low-order rejection parity (both implementations throw on the all-zero peer); malformed-length InvalidArg for secret + pubkey. `credentials/hpke.ts` deliberately stays on @noble — its X25519 calls are fused with the labeled-HKDF + chacha20poly1305 construction into the RFC 9180 keystream, so the whole file rewrites against `hpke-rs` in NAPI-3d. Native test count **+6** (29 total). **Recovery note**: midway through this session another agent's `git stash` (the prior cleanup task's stash, merge commit `4ed2016`) was dropped, taking the entire NAPI-1/2/3a/3b/3c working tree with it (tracked-file changes + the whole untracked `packages/native/` source tree). Recovery: the dropped stash's commits stay reachable via reflog/`fsck`, so `git checkout 4ed2016 -- <tracked>` restored my shell-side edits and `git checkout 6000c33 -- packages/native/...` (the stash's "untracked files on" parent commit) restored the Rust source tree byte-identically. Working tree reconciled, no edits regenerated by hand. **Verification signals**: native + shell credentials + pairing + storage **350/350 green** (the +1 vs earlier 349 is the new x25519 low-order rejection test); workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean on touched files. `bun run verify` blocked by the user's parallel-agent uncommitted edits in `entities/entity-dek-store` + `ipc/soak-handlers` + `renderer/settings/membership-section.*` etc., which aren't mine — they exist as `M` in `git status` from the same prior stash and remain unowned in the working tree. The native + crypto subsystem is provably green; the integration/entities tests pass on the targeted subset.

## 2026-06-09 — 13.9 — architecture & performance health audit + fixes

✅ DONE (2026-06-09). A pre-app-work health check before resuming the Phase-2 app serial order: a whole-codebase sweep (three parallel audit passes + the mechanical CI gates) against this project's known low-level trap classes — main-thread blocking, render-loop rebuilds, unbounded caches / lifetime leaks, and IPC + reactivity-layer drift. **Verdict: no CRITICAL problems and no regression of any previously-fixed bug class.** Every documented mitigation was verified still in place: the wrong-key SQLCipher per-kind negative-cache, `resilient-worker` fail-fast + respawn (no 30s hang on worker crash), broker per-app fixed-depth backpressure, the graph `geometryDirty` camera-only gate + dual-source visibility-pause + Pixi `{texture:false}` destroy, the bounded ydoc-worker LRU + resolver retention, and vault-session key zeroing on dispose.

**Closed the four actionable items.** (1) **Whiteboard camera-only repaint** (`apps/whiteboard/src/app.ts`) — pan / drag-pan / wheel-pan / zoom routed through a new `paintCamera()` that updates only the canvas transform + zoom readout + GPU edge re-cull, instead of the full `paint()` that `replaceChildren()`-rebuilt every node DOM subtree and recomputed board bounds on each pointermove. CSS already applies the camera to the node layer, so the node DOM is genuinely unchanged on a viewport move — the same dirty-gating split the graph (`geometryDirty`) and the database timeline already use. (2) **Tasks + Whiteboard onChange coalescer** — both `vaultEntities.onChange` subscriptions gained the 250ms trailing debounce that graph / journal / database / notes already had, so a keystroke-storm of CRDT writes collapses into one reload+render instead of one full re-render per write (they were the two outliers the reactivity-rule warns about). (3) **entities-repo statement-cache cap** (`main/storage/entities-repo/entities-repo.ts`) — the per-handle prepared-statement cache is now LRU-bounded (256, promote-on-hit); only `query()`'s dynamic SQL (variable IN-arity, compiled predicates, inlined `json_extract` order-by paths) can grow it, so a long Database / Graph filtering session no longer retains unbounded native statement handles. Fixed-SQL repos never approach the cap. (4) **Debounced search reindex** (`main/index.ts`) — the write-path reindex trigger is trailing-debounced (250ms) so a burst of sequential entity writes collapses to a single full FTS rebuild; vault-open and the explicit `reindex` hook still fire immediately. Search lags a write by <300ms (imperceptible, already true of the cross-window stale fan-out).

**Deferred by design** (recorded, not done): moving the entity read / derive + FTS-reindex pipeline off the Electron main process into a worker. Today `vault-entities-service.list()` does an unbounded full-vault `SELECT` + O(N) link-derivation on the main thread, and the search reindex is a full (non-incremental) rebuild — both fanned out to every app window per change. It is latent (fine at current dev-vault scale), not an active bug, and the code itself anticipates the fix ("Stage 9.3 → per-entity update"). The debounce above takes the sharpest edge off the write path; the worker migration is a genuine staged change that wants its own OQ + real-shell verification rather than a big-bang in a health-check follow-up.

**Verification:** `bun run verify` (typecheck packages + 20 app builds + 293 in-process pipeline/entities tests) + `bun run lint` (biome + all guards) + the full vitest suite (**10381 passed**, 1 expected-fail, 1020 files) — all green, identical test count before and after the fixes (behaviour-preserving). The whiteboard camera path sits in the documented real-Electron-verify bucket (no DOM-driver harness for `app.ts`). No OQ flips.

## 2026-06-09 — Browser-1 — Web Browser scaffold + `BrowsingSession/v1` + the chrome/engine split keystone

✅ DONE (2026-06-09). First iteration of the **Web Browser** app (group I). A pure contract iteration — no engine yet, the renderer stays the `coming-soon` placeholder until Browser-3 lands the chrome — that freezes the three things every later Browser iteration builds on: the session entity type, the chrome↔shell-engine wire contract, and the tab/history model.

**`brainstorm/BrowsingSession/v1`** (`apps/browser/src/types/browsing-session.ts`) — the ephemeral, vault-local, never-synced-in-v1 tab/history model of one browser window, so a crashed window restores tabs and "reopen closed tab" works (per doc 54, *not* a surveillance log). Modelled as two shapes: the **live** `BrowsingSession`/`BrowserTab` carry runtime metadata painted from host events (`TabLoadState`, `TabSecurityState`, `blockedTrackerCount`); the **persisted** `BrowsingSessionRecord`/`TabSnapshot` drop all of it (a restore re-navigates `history[historyIndex]`). The captured-page artifact is the shared `brainstorm/Bookmark/v1` (OQ-RX-5: `WebPage/v1` retired) — owned by the Bookmarks types, not introduced here. `TabLoadState`/`TabSecurityState` are string enums (no raw discriminators).

**The chrome-only / shell-engine split keystone** (`types/web-view.ts`) — the `WebView` host-service wire contract that resolves doc 54's core tension: web content runs in shell-managed, partitioned, Node-less `WebContentsView`s; the **app renderer is only chrome** with no page DOM or bytes. Defines `WebViewMethod` (open/navigate/back/forward/reload/stop/close/activate/set-bounds/find-in-page/stop-find/capture) with per-method request shapes, `WebViewEventKind` + the **metadata-only** `WebViewEvent` union (title/favicon/url/load-state/security-state/tracker-blocked/find-result/permission-requested/captured/closed — the page DOM, bytes, and live history never cross this boundary), and the `WEB_BROWSE_CAP` (High) / `WEB_CAPTURE_CAP` (Medium) capability constants. Browser-2 implements the host service against these types and lifts the module to a shared wire-types home; defining it now keeps the app independently buildable and pins the split before any engine code lands.

**Pure session reducer** (`logic/session.ts`) — the testable core the chrome renders and persists: clock-free, id-injected (no `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`, so chrome and tests drive it identically and restore is deterministic). `createSession`/`openTab`/`closeTab`/`reopenClosedTab`/`activateTab`/`navigateTab`/`goBack`/`goForward`/`canGoBack`/`canGoForward`/`setPinned`/`applyTabMeta` + the `toRecord`/`fromRecord` live↔persisted round-trip. Back/forward history with forward-branch truncation on a new navigation (standard redo-stack discard), neighbour-picking active marker on close (right-then-left), a bounded reopen-closed ring (`MAX_RECENTLY_CLOSED`), and identity-stable no-op transitions (an unchanged reducer call returns the same reference).

**Manifest** declares `web.browse` + `web.capture`, the `entities.read/write` grants for `BrowsingSession/v1` and the shared `Bookmark/v1` clip target, and registers the `BrowsingSession/v1` entity type with its inline JSON schema. Deliberately **no** `network.connect:*` on the app renderer (least-privilege + the chrome-only split: the shell-side host does all egress under the shared proxy/audit; `web.browse` is the egress consent) and no redundant `intents.dispatch:open` (a default-minimum grant).

**+22 reducer tests** (`session.test.ts`) green; first-party manifest validation + installer + seed suites green (188/188 across `apps/` + `dev/`); `typecheck:apps` (all 20 apps) + biome clean; the browser app builds. No OQ flips — OQ-WV-1..5 + OQ-168 are Browser-2 engine decisions, deliberately untouched by the scaffold.

## 2026-06-01 — 8.8 — `@react-fancy-menus/core` menus swap-in

Brought 8.8 forward (out of post-v1 order) the day `@react-fancy-menus/core@0.1.0` published. **Foundation** — new `@brainstorm/sdk/menus` subpath wraps the dep (OQ-32: SDK pins the exact version, apps inherit): `BrainstormMenuProvider` owns one `MenuStore`, registers the shortcut-suppression seam (`store.isOpen()` → `isAnyShortcutSuppressed`, the contract `shortcut/suppression.ts` was built for), and reconciles open menus onto the renderer-wide `getEscapeStack()` so Escape closes the topmost menu LIFO-nested with `<Popover>` (the dep's own window-Escape handler was being swallowed by the shell's capture-phase escape stack). `menus.css` bridges the dep's `--fm-*` tokens onto Brainstorm's `--color-*`/`--radius-*`/`--shadow-*`/`--z-*` (reactive on theme switch, glass backdrop) **plus a scoped utility shim** — the dep styles its core `.fm-*` chrome but its panel primitives (search/empty/loader/forms/tabs) render with Tailwind/shadcn utility classes it ships no CSS for, so we implement the exact bounded set under `.fm-menu`. Imperative `openContextMenu` + `mountMenuHost()` bridge (via an `active-store` module singleton) serves non-React call sites.

**Migrated surfaces** — cheatsheet + launcher (each a ComposedBody: SearchInput panel over a sectioned list, filtered rows fed in via `updateData` so grouping survives filtering; the component bridges the menu's close lifecycle back to the dashboard boolean); the dashboard icon context menu (`openContextMenu`, deletes the bespoke `DashboardIconContextMenu`); and the shared `openAnchoredMenu` — reimplemented to delegate to `openContextMenu` (Trash/CheckCircle glyphs mapped to Phosphor), which routes **every app's object menu, the graph export menu, and the database/tasks column-adder** through the bridge, with a no-host DOM fallback. All 11 first-party apps call `mountMenuHost()` at boot; menu CSS arrives centrally via `app-theme.css` `@import`. **Not migrated** (dialogs/modals, not menus — kept on `<Popover>`/native): the open-with intent prompt, the icon picker; the OS-native tray stays post-v1 (would need a new renderer tray window, OQ-TRAY-1).

**Verification** — production-shell Playwright specs (`tests/perf/specs/fancy-menus-*.spec.ts`) cover the cheatsheet, launcher, icon context menu, and the graph export menu **in a sandboxed app window** (open / filter / Escape, with screenshots). SDK unit tests cover locale merge, the suppression seam open/close/unmount, the imperative open + fail-soft, and the anchored-menu delegation-vs-fallback. Packages typecheck + biome clean; all 11 apps build; apps typecheck adds zero new errors (one pre-existing graph error is inherited from `main`). Resolves **OQ-33** (the v1 subset = what the migrated surfaces use; grid/participant kinds available but unused). Renames the ~22 doc + 4 code references from the pre-publish placeholder `@fancy-menus/core` to the real `@react-fancy-menus/core`.
