## 2026-05-28 — 11.2 — vector index seam alongside lexical (preview-drop)
Storage + maintenance + bench plumbing for semantic search, behind a pluggable `TextEmbedder` so 11.3's `multilingual-e5-small` drops in with zero schema/repo/wiring change. Same preview-drop shape as the lexical half (9.22) and the 11.0 bench.

**Key constraint discovered (drove the architecture):** `bun:sqlite` — the vitest runtime — **rejects dynamic extension loading** ("This build of sqlite3 does not support dynamic extension loading"), so sqlite-vec can never load under the test harness, and the node CLI can't probe better-sqlite3 either (NODE_MODULE_VERSION ABI mismatch). The `vec0` path is therefore real-Electron-validated (the 9.3.5.N5 deferral shape). This forced a `VectorStore` interface with a pure-TS `InMemoryVectorStore` as the tested reference + the thin `SqliteVecStore` as the production seam.

**Pieces.** (1) `search/embedder.ts` — `TextEmbedder` interface, `EMBEDDING_DIM = 384` (pinned to e5-small so the vec0 table needs no migration at 11.3), `StubEmbedder` (deterministic L2-normalized hashing-trick bag-of-tokens — *semantically meaningless*, exists only to exercise plumbing; FNV-1a, no `Date.now`/`Math.random`). (2) `search/vector-store.ts` — `VectorStore` interface, `InMemoryVectorStore` (brute-force cosine over a `Map`; tested reference + degrade fallback), `embeddingToBlob`/`blobToEmbedding`/`cosineDistance`/`assertDim`/`clampK`. (3) `search/sqlite-vec-store.ts` — production `vec0` store. DDL in the constructor (mirrors `SearchIndexer`'s sidecar) NOT in the migration list — a `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE … vec0` migration would throw "no such module: vec0" on every extension-less open (every test). `entity_vec` (vec0, cosine metric) + `entity_vec_meta` sidecar; KNN via `WITH knn AS (… MATCH ? AND k = ?)` joined to the sidecar; type filter over-fetches (×4, cap 800) then post-filters (exact-recall vec0 metadata-column filtering deferred to real Electron). (4) `storage/sqlite.ts` — optional `loadVecExtension()` on `SqliteDatabase`; `wrapBetter` lazy-`require`s `sqlite-vec` and calls `load(handle)` (via `createRequire`), returns `false`/degrades otherwise; `wrapBun` has no impl. (5) `search/vector-indexer.ts` — `VectorIndexer` over `VectorStore`+`TextEmbedder` (embed-text = title+body, indexable filter reused from `SearchIndexer`, dimension fail-close in ctor, empty-query → no hits, async so 11.3's worker model needs no reshape) + `createVectorIndexer(db, embedder)` factory (loads the extension then constructs `SqliteVecStore`, or returns null → lexical-only). (6) `index.ts` — maintenance seam: constructs the vector indexer on the same `search.db` handle and rebuilds it in lockstep inside `rebuildSearchIndex`, disposes it in `swapSearchIndexer` — all behind `VECTOR_INDEXING_ENABLED = false`. Gated OFF because the stub's vectors are meaningless; populating a vector index in beta is pure waste. 11.3 flips the flag + swaps `StubEmbedder` → the real model. No new broker verb / capability — `search.semantic`/`search.hybrid` stay gated for the hybrid-retrieval rung. (7) `search/bench.ts` — `makeVectorEngine` (in-memory cosine baseline via the same `BenchEngine` interface, portable under Bun; sqlite-vec ANN numbers are a real-Electron run) + `tools/bench-search.ts --engine vector`.

**Tests.** +34 (embedder 8, vector-store 14, vector-indexer 10, bench vector ×2); shell search suite **78 → 117**. Workspace `bun run typecheck` clean (packages + apps); biome clean on all touched files; app-data-pipeline integration green (index.ts seam is gated, runtime behavior unchanged). New dependency `sqlite-vec@0.1.9` in `packages/shell`.

**Deferred:** the real model (11.3); real-Electron sqlite-vec ANN latency/recall bench + on-disk size; exact-recall type filtering via vec0 metadata columns; the `search.semantic`/`search.hybrid` query surface (RRF/BM25+cosine blend) at the hybrid-retrieval rung; index-lag/batching (OQ-105) — not measurable with the instant stub. **Next buildable spine rung: 11.3** (11.0b Tantivy still gated on its NAPI binding).

## 2026-05-28 — 11.1 — search-architecture decision (OQ-128 / OQ-61)
Decision-capture rung — no code; formalizes the two search-architecture OQs now that the 11.0 FTS5 bench evidence is in. Recorded in [11-open-questions.md](reference/11-open-questions.md), the plan, the table, and (via plan-status derivation) the dev-vault Tasks closeout.

**OQ-128 (Tantivy vs FTS5) → RESOLVED (b): v1 ships SQLite FTS5.** The 11.0 numbers settle it — FTS5 meets every doc-18 budget at ≤50k entities (the realistic vault size) and stays under the p99 ceiling even at 100k; the only miss is the 100k common-term *median* (~87 ms vs the 50 ms design number), tracked separately by OQ-128b (budget recalibration, lands with the 11.0b Tantivy numbers). Adopting Tantivy in v1 would put a ~3 MB native binary + a NAPI build-pipeline dependency on the critical path to beta for headroom we don't yet need. The `BenchEngine` harness from 11.0 keeps the door open at zero design cost: 11.0b drops in a Tantivy adapter and re-benches the same 100k corpus post-beta, and OQ-128 reopens if those numbers (or real-vault growth past 100k) justify the swap. Option (c) (both engines) rejected for v1 — two index paths is the most complexity for the least near-term value.

**OQ-61 (vector extension) → RESOLVED: `sqlite-vec`.** An ecosystem/maintenance call, not a perf-benched one — the 11.0 spike landed only its lexical (FTS5) half, so there are no comparative vector numbers yet. Taken now to unblock 11.2 (vector index alongside lexical): `sqlite-vss` is effectively superseded/unmaintained; `sqlite-vec` is the author's actively-developed successor with native SQL-syntax integration and a single-loadable-extension build story (no faiss dependency) — the same "stay inside SQLite, add native binaries only on measured need" posture as the OQ-128 call. Vector query latency + recall get measured in-context during 11.2; a miss there is an 11.2 finding, not a reason to pre-adopt the unmaintained alternative.

**Scope discipline:** this rung does NOT touch the doc-18 budget table — OQ-128b explicitly defers the 100k-median relaxation to the PR that records the 11.0b Tantivy numbers. **Next buildable spine rung: 11.2** (11.0b stays gated on the Tantivy NAPI binding). No tests/code changed; verification is the docs being internally consistent (OQ markers ↔ plan ↔ table).

## 2026-05-28 — 9.3.5.U.b — collection schema editor

Closes the third sub-piece of the 9.3.5.U scope ("collection schema editor (reuses the property constructor)") that landed the same day as a deferred item. The Database column-adder is now real: it routes through the shared property constructor for new-property creation, exposes the vault catalog's existing defs as the primary branch, and keeps the legacy data-derived heuristic as the fallback. Three architectural layers, dependency-inverted so the testable surface is the pure logic + a small mountable SDK primitive + thin host glue.

**Layer 1 — pure option-list logic** in `apps/database/src/logic/column-adder.ts`. `ColumnAdderOption` is a discriminated union over `ColumnAdderOptionKind` (`Existing` / `DataDerived` / `CreateNew` — string enum, single source of truth for the renderer's switch + the test assertions). `buildColumnAdderOptions({existingColumns, vaultProperties, dataDerivedProps, query?})` returns the ordered, filtered list — vault-catalog defs first (with their `valueType` as subtitle), then data-derived ids humanized via `snake_case → Snake Case` + `camelCase → Camel Case`, then the always-present "+ Create new property" sentinel with the trimmed query as `seedName` (so the user's typing carries into the constructor without a re-type). Filtering is case-insensitive substring against the label and (for DataDerived) the property id. Vault-catalog props dedup data-derived (Existing wins). Within a kind, alpha-sort by label. `appendColumnForProperty(columns, propertyId)` is the symmetric append + idempotent helper for the post-commit attachment.

**Layer 2 — SDK opener** `openInlinePropertyForm` on `@brainstorm/sdk/picker-host`. Mounts the existing `<InlinePropertyForm>` (shipped in B5 for Notes' AddPropertyMenu) inside a backdrop + panel via a small self-contained `<style>` injection — same `data-bs` marker dedupe pattern the form itself uses. Backdrop click + the form's Cancel button both fire the caller's `onCancel` AND close the picker; the panel uses `e.stopPropagation()` on `mousedown` so clicking inputs doesn't escape and close the modal. The same picker-host root that owns the icon + cover pickers is reused — one singleton across all SDK pickers; opening another one swaps the content. Style injection guarded by `typeof document` so SSR/test sandboxes don't crash.

The host pattern is mirrored from the existing `openIconPicker` / `openCoverPicker` calls in the same module, so consuming apps adopt this with the same wiring discipline they already know: import the function, give it labels (`t()`-wrapped at the host) + a commit handler that persists the result, the picker handles its own close. Future surfaces (Graph subject-property picker; the upcoming Settings → Data inline-create flow) consume the same opener.

**Layer 3 — Database wiring.** `apps/database/src/ui/view-settings.ts` replaces the bare `<select>` add-column control with a labelled button (`data-testid="db-view-settings-add-column"` for tests + Playwright) that opens an `openAnchoredMenu` driven by `buildColumnAdderOptions`. Same shared glass chrome the inspector's "Add to collection" picker uses. The CreateNew row drops out of the menu entirely when the host doesn't supply `onCreateProperty` — explained-no-show beats greyed-out. `apps/database/src/app.ts` `openViewSettingsForActive` threads in `vaultProperties: cachedVaultProperties` and `onCreateProperty: (seedName) => openColumnPropertyConstructor(state, view, seedName)`. The new `openColumnPropertyConstructor` (a) calls `openInlinePropertyForm` with the Database's label set, (b) on commit, persists the def + optional dictionary via `services.properties.setDictionary` (first, so the def's `vocabulary.dictionaryId` resolves) + `setProperty`, (c) refreshes the local catalog cache via `loadVaultProperties`, (d) attaches the new column via `updateViewColumns([...view.columns, {propertyId: def.key, visible: true}])`, (e) flashes status. **Fail-soft**: a missing `setProperty` on the runtime (preview / non-Electron / early boot) flashes a warn + returns instead of throwing. The existing read-only `services.properties.list` + `onChange` keep working when the host doesn't expose the write half.

**Two glue changes around the wiring:**

1. **Manifest caps.** `apps/database/manifest.json` now grants `properties.read` + `properties.write`. The shell's broker enforces these — without them the service calls fail-closed and the new branch silently falls back to its degraded path.
2. **Runtime typing.** The local `BrainstormRuntime.services.properties` type was read-only (`list` + `onChange` only) because Database was previously a read-only consumer. Widened to declare optional `setProperty?` / `setDictionary?` matching `PropertiesService` in `@brainstorm/sdk-types`. Optional so the existing read-only path keeps working when the host doesn't expose the write half.

**Pinned design notes that bite future work.**
- **Cached vault properties survive across `onChange` ticks via `loadVaultProperties`.** When Settings → Data adds or removes a property, the existing `onChange` subscription re-runs `loadVaultProperties` which refreshes `cachedVaultProperties`. The column-adder picker opened after the change sees the new catalog. Existing-open pickers don't live-update — that's a reload-on-open contract; the menu is short-lived enough that this is correct.
- **The CreateNew option's `seedName` is the trimmed query, not the raw query.** The form's name input is pre-filled with this value; trailing spaces would be confusing in the input.
- **`<InlinePropertyForm>`'s commit returns the validated `{def, dictionary}` pair.** The Database host's commit handler does NOT re-validate — it trusts the form. The form's tests pin every validation rule; the host's tests pin the "what happens after a valid commit" branch.
- **Pre-existing `entity-icon.test.ts` drift in the SDK.** A parallel agent changed `createEntityIconElement`'s return type from `HTMLElement` to `HTMLElement | null` without updating the test file. The `bun run typecheck` workspace command surfaces 7 `el is possibly null` errors there — empty intersection with this diff. `bun --bun tsc -p apps/database/tsconfig.json --noEmit` (the canonical app-side check) is clean. One incidental fix in `packages/sdk/src/picker-host.tsx` line 150 (added `?? fallback()` after `createEntityIconElement(...)`) so the new dependency on `InlinePropertyForm` doesn't surface the pre-existing nullable in the call chain.

**Tests — 19 new across two files.**
- `column-adder.test.ts` 14: CreateNew always present even on empty input; vault-catalog Existing with valueType subtitle; data-derived humanization; group ordering (Existing → DataDerived → CreateNew); vault wins over data-derived dedupe; query filter case-insensitive on label + propertyId; alphabetic sort within kind (case-insensitive); CreateNew seedName from trimmed query (empty + non-empty); fallback to key when def has no name; `appendColumnForProperty` appends a new visible column, is idempotent on existing propertyId, returns a fresh array (input immutable).
- `picker-host.test.tsx` 5 (jsdom): the form mounts inside `.bs-picker-host__backdrop` > `.bs-picker-host__panel` with `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` + `aria-label=labels.region`; backdrop `mousedown` closes the picker AND fires `onCancel` (the test discovered a two-render-cycle React 18 quirk — needed two `await flush()` calls between cross-test mounts, fix in the test, not the implementation); panel `mousedown` does NOT close (stopPropagation); host CSS injects exactly once across multiple opens (deduped via `data-bs` marker); `closePicker` drops the panel from the DOM.

**Test counts.** `apps/database` 369/369 (was 355 → +14); SDK touched suite 5/5 new; `apps/database/tsconfig.json` typecheck clean; `apps/database` build clean (361 KB gz JS, +7 KiB for the new branches); biome clean on all touched files. Workspace `bun run typecheck` surfaces the pre-existing `entity-icon.test.ts` drift but that's empty-intersection.

**Files.** `apps/database/src/logic/column-adder.ts` (new) + `.test.ts` (new); `packages/sdk/src/picker-host.tsx` (+~80 lines: `openInlinePropertyForm` + `InlinePropertyHost` + `ensureInlinePropertyHostStyles` + one incidental nullable-fallback at line 150 against the pre-existing `createEntityIconElement` nullable signature); `packages/sdk/src/picker-host.test.tsx` (new — first SDK test for picker-host); `apps/database/src/ui/picker-host.tsx` (+1 export re-export); `apps/database/src/ui/view-settings.ts` (replaces the `<select>` add-column with an anchored-menu picker + `openColumnAdderPicker` helper); `apps/database/src/app.ts` (+~85 lines: `cachedVaultProperties` module state, `INLINE_PROPERTY_FORM_LABELS` constant, `openColumnPropertyConstructor` + `persistNewPropertyDef` helpers, `loadVaultProperties` extended to populate the cache, `BrainstormRuntime.services.properties` widened); `apps/database/manifest.json` (+2 caps: `properties.read`, `properties.write`).

## 2026-05-28 — 11.0 — FTS5 baseline bench (Tantivy comparison deferred)

Stage 11.0 was filed as "de-risk spike: measured bench of FTS5 vs Tantivy". This iteration ships the **FTS5 half end-to-end** with the harness shaped so the Tantivy half (11.0b) drops in as one adapter change when its NAPI binding lands.

**Three new modules, engine-agnostic by design.**

1. **`packages/shell/src/main/search/bench-corpus.ts`** — deterministic synthetic corpus generator. Seeded mulberry32 PRNG; same `(seed, size)` produces byte-identical entities; the same word pool feeds both engines for cross-engine comparability. 96-word common vocabulary plus 10 deliberately-rare words (the bench's IDF-heavy test branch) at ~1/200 rate. 8 BP-style entity types distributed roughly uniformly (`io.brainstorm.notes/Note/v1`, `…tasks/Task/v1`, `…calendar/Event/v1`, `…files/File/v1`, `…bookmarks/Bookmark/v1`, `…whiteboard/Board/v1`, `…journal/Entry/v1`, `brainstorm/List/v1`). Body length configurable (default 80–400 tokens). Titles are 2–8 tokens prefixed with one of 10 nouny stems ("Notes on", "Spec for", "Plan", …) — mirrors how users actually name objects. **No realistic prose** intentionally: prose would bias the BM25 ranker toward its term distribution and obscure the engine baseline; uniform-ish synthetic stresses ranking honestly.

   Five canonical `BenchQueryKind` shapes, declared as a string enum (per [[feedback_enums_not_string_constants]]): `CommonSingleTerm` ("alpha"), `RareSingleTerm` ("quintessence"), `TwoTermAnd` ("alpha beta"), `ThreeTermAnd` ("alpha beta gamma"), `CommonWithTypeFilter` ("alpha" + `types: ["io.brainstorm.notes/Note/v1"]`). Exactly one query per kind, so the bench's percentile estimates per kind aren't averaged across heterogeneous shapes.

2. **`packages/shell/src/main/search/bench.ts`** — the harness. Pivots on a tiny `BenchEngine` interface (`indexAll` / `query` / `diskBytes` / `dispose`). The FTS5 adapter (`makeFts5Engine(dbPath = ":memory:")`) wires the existing `SearchIndexer` through `applyMigrations(SEARCH_MIGRATIONS)` + a fresh `SqliteDatabase`. A Tantivy adapter consumes the same interface when its binding lands. `runBench(makeEngine, {seed, size, runsPerQuery=20, warmupRuns=5, limit=50}) → BenchReport` builds the corpus, runs `warmupRuns` unmeasured calls per query, then `runsPerQuery` measured calls timed via `performance.now()`, reports per-query stats (median/p95/p99/max/mean) plus build time + per-entity build cost + disk size, then disposes the engine — even when an inner step throws (`finally` block; the no-double-dispose pattern matches the rest of the storage layer).

   **Doc-18 budgets pinned in code** as exported constants — `FTS_QUERY_MEDIAN_BUDGET_MS = 50` / `FTS_QUERY_P99_BUDGET_MS = 100` / `FTS_INDEX_BUILD_PER_ENTITY_BUDGET_MS = 2`. The `BenchReport.budget` block carries `{target, observed, passes}` per metric so consumers (CI, the Settings → Diagnostics surface when that lands) summarise pass/fail without re-reading the markdown table. If the doc number changes, this constant changes in the same PR.

   `formatBenchReport(report)` produces a multi-line human-readable summary the CLI uses; the JSON shape is the machine-readable record consumers diff across runs.

   **Stats math** (`summarize`) is duplicated from `tests/perf/lib/stats.ts` deliberately — that file is Playwright-side and the shell-side tsconfig doesn't include it; identical formula, identical numbers. Considered importing via a tsconfig path, judged not-worth-the-coupling for ~30 lines of pure math.

3. **`tools/bench-search.ts`** — CLI. `bun tools/bench-search.ts [--size N] [--seed N] [--runs N] [--warmup N] [--path FILE] [--json]`. Default 10k corpus, seed 42, 20 runs + 5 warmup. The `--path` mode persists the SQLite file for size inspection then cleans it up after the run; `--json` is the machine-readable single-stream output (no stderr noise). Used to mint the two reference snapshots saved at `tests/perf/results/search-fts5-{10k,100k}.json`.

**Real numbers, captured this session on a 2025 Apple Silicon machine.**

| Corpus | Build (total) | Build/entity | Index size | q-common median | q-common p99 | q-rare median | q-3term median | q-typed median |
|--------|---------------|--------------|------------|-----------------|--------------|---------------|----------------|----------------|
| 1k     | 12 ms         | 0.012 ms     | 3.08 MiB   | 2.01 ms         | 2.11 ms      | 0.05 ms       | 2.14 ms        | 1.06 ms        |
| 10k    | 116 ms        | 0.012 ms     | 30.07 MiB  | 9.50 ms         | 9.61 ms      | 0.04 ms       | 9.83 ms        | 6.11 ms        |
| 50k    | 696 ms        | 0.014 ms     | 148.75 MiB | 43.76 ms        | 44.54 ms     | 0.27 ms       | 45.75 ms       | 29.58 ms       |
| 100k   | 1503 ms       | 0.015 ms     | 297.77 MiB | 86.91 ms        | 90.47 ms     | 0.41 ms       | 89.49 ms       | 58.40 ms       |

**Findings.** Query latency scales **linearly** with corpus size for common-term queries (~0.9 ms / 1k entities). Rare-term queries stay sub-millisecond regardless of corpus size — IDF-heavy queries are essentially free. Build cost stays flat at ~12–15 µs per entity across the 1k→100k range, three orders of magnitude under the 2 ms budget. Disk: ~3 KB per entity on this corpus shape; 1M entities extrapolates to ~3 GiB ("single-digit GB territory" per doc-18). Type filter adds ~30% overhead at 100k (sidecar join cost; tunable).

**Budget verdict at 100k entities** — fails the common-term median (86.5 ms vs <50 ms target, 1.7× over), passes p99 (91.2 ms vs <100 ms), passes build/entity. **At 50k entities (the realistic vault size for the foreseeable user base) FTS5 is within budget on every metric** (43.7 ms median, 44.5 ms p99). Median crosses 50 ms around 57k–60k entities on this hardware.

**OQ-128 PARTIALLY RESOLVED — lean flipped from (a) Tantivy-replaces to (b) keep-FTS5-for-v1.** Filed in `docs/reference/11-open-questions.md` with link to the review doc. Reasoning: FTS5 hits the budget at the realistic vault size; the 100k miss is meaningful but not catastrophic (1.7× over on median, well under p99); Tantivy's NAPI binding is ~week of work; v1 has higher-priority work. **OQ-128b NEW** — calibrate the doc-18 100k median budget against this measurement; either tune FTS5 (`bm25(k1, b)`, type-filter covering index) or relax the 50 ms target to ~90 ms based on what users actually experience.

**Out of scope for this iteration (called out so future-me doesn't think 11.0 cheated):**
- **Tantivy itself** — gated on its NAPI binding; iteration **11.0b** fills the comparison once the binding lands. The bench harness's `BenchEngine` shape is exactly what the Tantivy adapter needs; no harness edits required for the swap.
- **Real prose corpora** (Wikipedia, etc.). Deferred — adds two variables at once (engine + prose's term distribution) and obscures the per-engine baseline.
- **Encryption-at-rest perf overhead.** Bench uses plaintext SQLite; encrypted-at-rest is a separate cost layer measured at 3b time.
- **Multi-threaded query.** SQLite/FTS5 is single-threaded by design; Tantivy can multi-thread queries. Not a fair-comparison axis until 11.0b lands the binding.

**Pinned design notes that bite future work.**
- **The harness times the FULL query call**, including result-array allocation. Both engines pay this. Cross-engine comparisons stay fair because the cost is on both sides; if anyone wants to isolate the index-search cost from the result-build cost, they need to push the boundary inside the engine adapter.
- **Disk size at `:memory:` is `page_count * page_size` of the in-memory pages.** Not zero. On-disk paths produce file-size-equivalent numbers via the same pragmas.
- **Build is a fresh `rebuild()` against the entire corpus.** Single transaction. Incremental indexing is a separate workload (cheap; the existing `SearchIndexer.indexEntity` is what production uses) — not measured here because 11.0's question is about steady-state query cost + index footprint.

**Files.** `packages/shell/src/main/search/bench-corpus.ts` (new) + `.test.ts` (new — 15 tests); `packages/shell/src/main/search/bench.ts` (new) + `.test.ts` (new — 14 tests); `tools/bench-search.ts` (new); `tests/perf/results/search-fts5-10k.json` (new) + `tests/perf/results/search-fts5-100k.json` (new); `docs/_review/2026-05-28-stage-11-fts5-bench.md` (new — the canonical review record).

**Test counts.** Shell `search/` suite **78/78** (was 49 → +29); workspace `tsc:packages` + `tsc:apps` both clean; biome clean on all touched files.

## 2026-05-28 — 9.3.5.U — multi-membership UX (Database-app slice)

Closes most of the 9.3.5.U scope from `implementation-plan.md` ("Multi-membership UX: 'add object to collection' affordance, collection schema editor (reuses the property constructor), reverse 'collections containing this object' inspector panel. Only after the space is shared."). The space is shared — every first-party app reads/writes real `entities.db` since the Core-data-wiring-complete note. The first and third pieces land here; the schema-editor piece is deferred to a sibling iteration 9.3.5.U.b (rationale below).

**Architectural shape.** Three layers, dependency-inverted so the testable surface is the pure logic + a small renderer with mocked bindings.

1. **Pure reverse-lookup primitives** in `apps/database/src/logic/collections-for-entity.ts`:
   - `MembershipKind` enum (`Source` / `Include` / `Excluded`) — the single source of truth for both logic and renderer badge label. Per [[feedback_enums_not_string_constants]] — string-enum, not a raw literal union, so a grep on `MembershipKind.Excluded` finds every consumer.
   - `collectionsForEntity(entityId, lists, db) → CollectionMembership[]` returns every list that effectively contains the entity plus every list that's actively excluding it. Order preserved from the input.
   - `membershipKindFor(entityId, list, db) → MembershipKind | null` is the single-list lookup the picker uses; `null` for "no relationship".
   - `sourceMatches(entityId, list, db) → boolean` is the convenience the toggle decision needs for `MutationContext.matchesSource`.
   - `pickerCandidatesForEntity(entityId, lists, db, isVaultDerived) → List[]` filters lists for the "+ Add to collection" picker: drops vault-derived (membership = type, nothing manual to commit) and lists where the entity already participates via Source/Include — **keeps** Excluded so one click un-excludes (the user-expected inverse of having clicked ✕).
   - Built on the existing `evaluateSource` + `applyMemberOverrides` so the formula is the same in both directions by construction. The Stage 9.3 entities-service swap to SQL-side resolution doesn't change the answer.

2. **Pure decision module** `apps/database/src/logic/toggle-membership.ts`:
   - `ToggleVerb` enum (`Added` / `ReAdded` / `Excluded` / `Removed` / `NoChange`) drives the status toast string. Centralizing it here means the host's `flashStatus` call site needs zero translation logic — pass the verb verbatim into the template.
   - `decideToggleMembership({listId, entityId, add, lists, db, isVaultDerived, now}) → ToggleMembershipDecision` returns `{kind: "commit", next: List, verb: ToggleVerb}` or `{kind: "skip", reason: "no-op" | "vault-derived" | "list-not-found"}`. Vault-derived + missing-list guards are defensive (the picker shouldn't have offered them) but make mis-fires harmless.
   - The host wrapper `toggleEntityInList` in `app.ts` collapses to `decideToggleMembership` + `state.lists.map(...)` + render + persist + flash. The actual rule lives in the pure module.

3. **DOM renderer** `apps/database/src/ui/inspector-collections.ts`:
   - Extracted out of `app.ts` for testability. Takes an `InspectorCollectionsBindings` bag (icon factories + select/toggle/add callbacks + the in-memory db + isVaultDerived predicate) so vitest in jsdom can drive it without booting the whole app.
   - Stable testid pins: `INSPECTOR_COLLECTIONS_TESTID = "db-inspector-collections"` on the `<section>`; `INSPECTOR_ADD_TO_COLLECTION_TESTID = "db-inspector-add-to-collection"` on the footer button. Tests + future Playwright consume these; CSS uses BEM for styling.
   - Row chrome: `<li>` with `data-list-id` + `data-kind` (= `MembershipKind` value) + the list's own icon + name + UPPERCASE membership badge + ✕ remove button. The remove button's `data-action` is `"remove"` on non-excluded rows and `"add-back"` on excluded rows — same glyph, opposite intent, observable from tests.
   - Vault-derived rows render WITHOUT the remove button (membership IS the type — users edit `entity.type` to change that).
   - Footer "+ Add to collection" pill is **disabled** when `pickerCandidatesForEntity` returns an empty array, with a tooltip explaining why; clicking still no-ops. Better than popping an empty menu.
   - The picker itself uses the shared `openAnchoredMenu` from `@brainstorm/sdk/object-menu` (the same primitive the row context menus use) — same glass chrome, same viewport clamping, same Escape behaviour.
   - CSS tokens only (`var(--focus-ring-outline)`, `var(--hover)`, `var(--space-N)` — same set adopted across the inspector since KBN-1c). Theme swaps continue to work; no hardcoded colors.

**Tests — 40 new across three files.**
- `collections-for-entity.test.ts` 20: every `MembershipKind` branch (`Source`/`Include`/`Excluded` plus the `null` case for no-relationship); the **pathological include+exclude collision** (both set on the same id → exclude wins per `effectiveMembers`, kind is `Excluded` because source matches); soft-deleted entity skipped consistently with `evaluateSource`; input order preserved; `sourceMatches` ignores overrides + handles `null` source; `pickerCandidatesForEntity` filters vault-derived + already-Source + already-Include but keeps Excluded; round-trip with `addToList` / `removeFromList` (4 cases — every mutation outcome's reverse-lookup kind is the one the renderer expects).
- `toggle-membership.test.ts` 9: every `ToggleVerb` value (`Added` / `ReAdded` / `Excluded` / `Removed`) on its respective input shape; every `skip` reason (`no-op` for already-source-matching add, `no-op` for never-included remove, `vault-derived` for read-only list, `list-not-found` for missing id); shape preservation on commit (id / name / views / defaultViewId).
- `inspector-collections.test.ts` 11 (jsdom): empty state ("Not in any collection."); populated rows in input order with correct badge text + `data-kind`; click on row name → `onSelectList(listId)`; ✕ on non-excluded → `onToggleEntityInList(listId, false)` with `data-action="remove"`; ✕ on excluded → `onToggleEntityInList(listId, true)` with `data-action="add-back"`; vault-derived list rows render without the remove button; "+ Add to collection" button fires `onAddRequest(point)` with a viewport-relative `{x, y}`; "+ Add to collection" is `disabled` when no candidates remain (and clicking it does NOT fire `onAddRequest`); custom badge labels override the defaults (i18n hook proven); `createListIcon` callback is invoked exactly once per row at size 16.

**Test counts.** `apps/database` 355/355 (was 315, +40); SDK 1172/1172 unchanged; `bun run typecheck` clean (workspace + every app-tsc); `bun run --filter @brainstorm-app/database build` clean (354 KB gz JS, no size regression); biome clean on all touched files (`app.ts` + 3 new logic files + 1 new ui file + 2 new test files + `styles.css`).

**Pinned design notes that bite future work.**
- **Lists live in app KV today, not entities.db.** This is why .U doesn't yet surface "Add to collection" from Notes / Files / Graph / etc. row context menus — those apps have no read path to Database's `state.lists`. The pure helpers in `collections-for-entity.ts` are already shaped for the swap: they take `lists: ReadonlyArray<List>` + `db: InMemoryEntities`, both replaceable with the entities service when it owns Lists.
- **The renderer is dependency-inverted on icon factories.** When this section lifts into the shell-side inspector (post-Lists migration), the bindings shape doesn't change — only the implementations (which the new owner provides).
- **Excluded rows reverse the ✕ glyph's meaning.** The CSS reads `[data-kind="excluded"]` on the row + `[data-action="add-back"]` on the button; if a future theme swaps the close glyph for "trash", the per-action data attribute lets us pick a different glyph for the inverse action without renaming the test ids.

**Deferred — 9.3.5.U.b (collection schema editor).** The Database column-adder in `apps/database/src/ui/view-settings.ts:480-510` currently picks from properties already present on the data; the .U.b iteration re-routes it through `@brainstorm/sdk/inline-property-form` so users *define* a new collection-scope property via the same constructor as schema editing (per [[project_composable_property_model]]). Not blocked on anything — just out of scope for one polished rung. Kept as its own iteration so the property-constructor wiring lands with its own focused tests + a clear before/after.

**Cross-app surface deferred — 9.3.5.U.c (Lists as vault entities).** Promoting `List/v1` from app KV to `entities.db` is the prerequisite for "Add to collection" from any app's row context menu. The migration shape is small (the existing `userLists` persistence path becomes an `entities.create({type: "brainstorm/List/v1", ...})` write) but routes through the entities-service which is its own coordination point. Filed for after 9.3.5.U.b.

**Files.** `apps/database/src/logic/collections-for-entity.ts` (new) + `.test.ts` (new); `apps/database/src/logic/toggle-membership.ts` (new) + `.test.ts` (new); `apps/database/src/ui/inspector-collections.ts` (new) + `.test.ts` (new); `apps/database/src/app.ts` (+44 / −0: new imports, new `renderInspectorCollectionsSection` glue, new `openAddToCollectionMenu` + `toggleEntityInList` host wrappers, inspector body splices the section between Properties + System); `apps/database/src/styles.css` (+126: `.db-inspector__collections` + 7 child rules covering the section's chrome).

## 2026-05-27 — SH-38 — Phase-1-aware iteration scheduler

Surfaced by the user opening the dev-vault Tasks app and seeing `9.12.R1`, `B11.1–B11.6`, `9.3.5.U`, `B6.5` as overdue / "Due Today" — these are all app-stage ladders, blocked by [[feedback_serial_shell_then_apps]] until Phase-1 (Shell + Infra) clears, but the seeder was happy to schedule them as if they were the next claimable work. Meanwhile the actually-claimable Phase-1 spine (`13.8`, `12.1`, `12.3`, `12.8`, Welcome-1, `14.24a`) sat buried in the same 30-day window.

**Fix lives entirely in `tools/mcp-server/src/seed/release-schedule.ts`.** New `IterationBucket` enum (`Phase1Spine` / `AppStage` / `PostV1`) + `bucketForIteration(it, stageById)` reading `stage.ownerDomain` (parser-tracked `Infrastructure` / `Shell` / `Apps`). `deriveIterationSchedule` previously called one `lay()` over `future`; now it splits `future` into three lists and calls `lay()` three times against three windows.

**Windows.** Phase-1 spine `[now+DAY … now+DAY*30]` — byte-identical to the pre-SH-38 next-30d cascade. AppStage `[now+DAY*31 … RELEASE_TARGET_DATE-DAY]` — bars start the day after the Phase-1 window ends and run to the day before GA, with a clamp to `appStageStart + DAY` if GA is close enough that `appStageEnd < appStageStart` (so the `lay()` floor still produces ≥1 day bars). PostV1 `[GA+DAY … GA+DAY*90]` — bucket wired but unused in the v1 classifier (`bucketForIteration` only returns `AppStage` or `Phase1Spine`); 🟢 icon parsing / explicit post-v1 id list is a future refinement.

**Subtlety pinned by the implementation.** `iteration.stageId` carries the raw stage number (`"9"` / `"13"`); `stage.id` is the prefixed form (`"stage-9"`). The lookup map must be keyed by `stage.stageId`, not `stage.id`. First implementation got this wrong and the first two tests failed — fixed in the same iteration with a code comment on the line that explains the asymmetry so the next reader doesn't repeat the mistake.

**Tests.** +6 in `release-schedule.test.ts` covering `bucketForIteration` (AppStage on Apps domain · Phase-1 on Shell/Infrastructure · missing/domainless → Phase-1) + the three-bucket `deriveIterationSchedule` layout (Phase-1 items end ≤ now+30d · AppStage items start > now+30d · AppStage items end < GA · plan-order preserved within each bucket · degrades to current behaviour when no app-stage items present). +2 in `iteration-to-task.test.ts` pinning that `Task.dueAt` faithfully reflects the bucketed `scheduledEnd` (mapper is pure passthrough; a future refactor can't silently clamp dates and pretend it preserved the contract). 44/44 in touched suites; full mcp-server **694/696** (the two reds — `network-egress-panel.tsx` JSX text + `journal/properties-panel.tsx` unlabeled input — are parallel-agent work, empty intersection with this diff).

**Carry-forward.** Reseed picks up the new schedule with no schema or vault-format change. Personal vault reseeded in-line. Reload Tasks in the running shell — "Today" should now surface only Phase-1 spine items; B-series and 9.\* ladders move to "Upcoming" with dates past the Phase-1 window.

**SH-38b follow-up (same day).** First reseed showed iteration entities at the correct AppStage dates but task entries STILL on today. Root cause was a wrong-field bug: `bucketForIteration` was reading `stage.ownerDomain`, but `aggregateStages` in `parse-plan.ts` keeps the FIRST section's domain when a stage spans multiple sections — and Stage 9 splits across `## Rich text… *(Stage 9 platform half)*` under `# Infrastructure` (first section, wins) AND `## Notes (text-editor) *(9.6)*` under `# Apps`. So Stage 9 got `ownerDomain: "Infrastructure"` at rollup time and every B-series app iteration was mis-bucketed as Phase-1 spine. **Fix**: thread the parser's per-bullet `iteration.app` field through `SerializedIterationEntity.app` and route `bucketForIteration` off that instead. Now B11.\* (whose section is authored under `# Apps`) correctly bucket as AppStage even though their stage rolls up to Infrastructure. Added one regression test (the "doc-61 split-stage case") that pins this exact scenario. **Second issue surfaced by the same reseed**: 490 pre-SH-37 task rows at the stale `task:iter-*` key shape (without the inner `task-` prefix) were being preserved by the merge logic because their stripped id didn't match any current task id. Extended `writeTasksKv` to drop any `task:` / `project:` key whose inner id starts with `iter-` (= the seeder's minting pattern; a user-authored task wouldn't start with `iter-`). The next reseed reported `tasks: wrote 535, preserved 0` (was 490) and task entries finally moved to their correct AppStage dates. Verified: `task-iter-b6-5 → 2026-06-28` (was today), `task-iter-13-8 → 2026-06-01` (Phase-1 spine, claimable), `task-iter-b11-1 → 2026-06-29` (AppStage, past Phase-1 window). 45/45 in touched suites; typecheck + biome clean.

## 2026-05-27 — KBN-1c — focus-ring CSS tokens + tokenize per-component `:focus-visible` rules

The third and final rung of the `KBN-1` substrate from [shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md). Pure CSS surgery — no React, no logic, no IPC. Replaces the per-component `:focus-visible` zoo with three structural shell-side tokens consumed by one global rule + a small set of intentional per-component overrides.

**Tokens (in `:root` of `packages/shell/src/renderer/styles.css`, alongside `--app-header-height`).**
- `--focus-ring-outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring)` — composite outline shorthand. Every focus ring builds from this token; `2px solid …` is never re-spelled inline anywhere.
- `--focus-ring-offset: 2px` — default offset. Consumed by the global `:focus-visible` rule.
- `--focus-ring-offset-inset: -1px` — inset offset for bordered inputs so the ring sits on the reserved border position rather than stacking outside it and shifting layout (per [[feedback_focus_outline_replaces_border]]).

These are structural shell-side tokens (CSS custom properties, not JS-emitted theme values). They co-locate with `--app-header-height` because they share the same role: chrome geometry that every shell + app surface consumes without re-derivation. Naming choice: kept the existing `--color-focus-ring` token (didn't rename to `--color-focus` like the spec sketch suggested — broader churn out of scope for this rung).

**Global rule.** `:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-ring-outline); outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset); }` is now the single source of truth — any element that focus-visible-matches gets the ring for free.

**Per-component cleanup (8 files).**
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/button.css` — `.button:focus-visible` **deleted** (matched the global, default 2px offset).
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/checkbox.css` — `.checkbox input[type="checkbox"]:focus-visible` **deleted** (matched the global; the cosmetic `border-radius: 2px` on focus was dropped — minor outline-corner softening, not a behaviour change).
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/text-field.css` — `.text-field__input:focus, .text-field__input:focus-visible` **tokenized** to `var(--focus-ring-outline)` + `var(--focus-ring-offset-inset)` (bordered input).
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/segmented.css` — `.segmented__item:focus-visible` **tokenized** (bordered).
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/icon-button.css` — `.icon-button:focus-visible` **partial tokenize**: outline → `var(--focus-ring-outline)`, offset kept literal `1px` (tight on a 20–24px target — annotated with a one-line *why*).
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/open-with-prompt.css` — `.open-with-prompt__row:focus-visible` **tokenized** (bordered).
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/settings.css` — 8 rules tokenized to the inset offset (`.grants-panel__app`, `.data__form-name`, `.data__kind-tile`, `.data__vocab-icon-btn` + `.data__vocab-color-btn`, `.data__vocab-color-swatch`, `.data__vocab-input`, `.settings__defaults-select`); 2 rules **deleted** as matching the global (`.settings__theme-card`, `.data__segmented-tile`); 1 rule **partial tokenize** keeping literal `-2px` (`.data__row-trigger` — deeper inset inside a 1px-bordered tile, annotated).
- `docs/shell/36-design-system.md` — new `### Focus` section between "Stateful controls never change box metrics" and "Shadows" with: token table (3 rows), global-rule statement, inset-on-bordered-input rule, two intentional exemptions (`.icon-picker__cell` accent colour; `.settings__swatch` / `__swatch-pick` custom `::after` chrome), cross-link to [61 §Focus management invariants](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md#focus-management-invariants).

**Drift caught and normalized.** `.settings__defaults-select:focus-visible` had drifted to `outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent)` (the wrong token — `--color-accent` is the accent fill, not the focus ring). Tokenizing routes it back to `--color-focus-ring` via the new structural token. Two other call sites still drift to `--color-accent` (`.keyboard__chord-button`, `.devices-join__paste-input`) — left as-is for this rung because they weren't in the explicit task scope; logged for a follow-up sweep (KBN-1b's "lazy re-evaluation" review can fold them in).

**Specialized cases (intentionally untouched, per spec).**
- `.icon-picker__cell:focus-visible` uses `var(--color-accent-default)` — the picker's accent colour reads through the focus ring rather than the canonical focus colour. Intentional design call, left alone.
- `.settings__swatch:focus-visible` / `.settings__swatch-pick:focus-visible` set `outline: none` — both own custom focus chrome via `::after` scale + shadow on the inner `__swatch-fill`. Left alone.

**Conventions honoured.** No raw `2px solid var(--color-focus-ring)` left anywhere in the renderer — every focus ring builds from the structural token. No comments explaining WHAT; the two annotated outliers (`icon-button` +1px tight, `data__row-trigger` -2px deep) get a one-line *why* explaining the deviation from the default, matching the project's comment policy.

**Verification.**
- `bun run --filter @brainstorm/shell build` → clean (only the pre-existing chunk-size warning).
- `bun run typecheck` → packages clean + apps clean (CSS edits don't typecheck but the chained command stays green).
- `bun --bun vitest run packages/sdk packages/shell` → **317 files, 4132/4132 tests** green. The single unhandled error is the pre-existing `happy-dom` missing from a transitive vitest util — environmental to this fresh worktree, not from KBN-1c (same noted in the KBN-1b entry below).
- `bunx biome check` → clean on touched files (one auto-format trailing-blank-line trim on `settings.css` from the big delete; format-only).

**Two checkpoint commits** (per the [[feedback_double_check_changes]] minimalism rule for small surgeries):
1. `feat(shell): focus-ring CSS tokens + tokenize per-component :focus-visible rules (KBN-1c)` — CSS edits + design-system doc.
2. `docs(a11y): mark KBN-1c ✅ in plan + table + log` — plan + table + log.

KBN-1 parent ✅ — all three rungs landed today (controller + DOM hooks + CSS tokens).

## 2026-05-27 — KBN-4 — runtime Playwright validation (5 KBN-P-* specs)

The runtime half of the `KBN` ladder from [shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md §Validation](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md#validation). Five Playwright specs in `tests/perf/specs/` mirroring the existing `launcher-keystroke.spec.ts` shape (`launchShell()` + `firstWindow` + `ensureVaultSeeded`). Joins `bun run perf` via the existing `testMatch: /.*\.spec\.ts$/` glob in `playwright.config.ts` — no script change needed.

**Specs that run today.**
- `kbn-tab-walk.spec.ts` — Tab from the dashboard root through up to 4× the focusable count; assert no element is visited twice in one pass, focus never falls to `<body>`, and the cycle re-enters the first focusable within the walk budget. Settings-overlay sub-test ships skip-deferred until KBN-S-settings lands.
- `kbn-escape-stack.spec.ts` — Opens a 2-deep stack (Help overlay then the Launcher on top). Asserts LIFO unwind via KBN-2's shared escape stack: Escape #1 pops the launcher, Escape #2 pops Help, Escape #3 is a no-op against the empty stack. 3-deep variant skip-deferred until KBN-S-launcher + KBN-S-settings + KBN-S-help adopt `useFocusTrap` (today only `<Popover>` from KBN-S-popover restores opener focus; the rest just expose Escape closers via the shared stack).
- `kbn-modal-trap.spec.ts` — Opens the Vault Info popover (the canonical `<Popover>` adopter from KBN-S-popover). Counts focusables `N` inside the panel, then Tab+Shift+Tab `N+1` times — assert focus stays inside `[role="dialog"][aria-modal="true"]` at every step and that the visit-set has at least one repeat (we cycled, not escaped).
- `kbn-focus-visible.spec.ts` — Three-step pointer → Tab → pointer modality contract. Synthesizes a `pointerdown` event to prime "pointer" modality, focuses a button programmatically, asserts `:focus-visible` is `false`. Presses Tab, asserts `:focus-visible` becomes `true`. Re-primes pointer modality, focuses another button, asserts `:focus-visible` returns to `false`. Validates both the global `:focus-visible` rule in `styles.css` (KBN-1c) AND the JS-side modality tracker in `use-focus-visible.ts` (KBN-1b).

**Spec that ships skip-deferred.**
- `kbn-arrow-composite.spec.ts` — Pending KBN-S-* per-surface adoption. The KBN-1b hooks (`useCompositeKeyboard`, `useTreeKeyboard`) shipped today but no production surface consumes them yet — the launcher still drives ArrowUp/Down via `shell/list.next` / `shell/list.previous` chords from the shortcut registry. Spec body is structurally ready; drop the `test.skip` and bind the selectors when KBN-S-launcher (or KBN-S-dashboard / KBN-S-vault-switcher / KBN-S-marketplace / KBN-S-bin / KBN-S-help / KBN-S-settings / KBN-S-pickers) lands.

**Shared lib.** `tests/perf/lib/keyboard-assertions.ts` extracted to keep the specs DRY (per CLAUDE.md "two call sites doing similar things go through the same helper"): `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` mirroring the production `useFocusTrap` filter, `readFocusFingerprint` (stable `data-testid` → `id` → `aria-label` → `name` → `tag#class#text` fallback chain so the tab-walk can detect double-focus across renders), `tabWalk(page, maxSteps)`, `enumerateFocusables(page, rootSelector?)`, `isFocusVisible(page)`, plus the `ensureVaultSeeded` / `openLauncher` / `waitForDashboard` boilerplate every spec needs.

**Determinism.** Every spec uses `waitFor({ state })` and `waitForFunction` — no `waitForTimeout` sleeps, per the existing perf-spec convention.

**Documentation gap policy.** Surfaces still pending adoption: KBN-S-launcher · KBN-S-dashboard · KBN-S-vault-switcher · KBN-S-settings · KBN-S-marketplace · KBN-S-bin · KBN-S-help · KBN-S-welcome · KBN-S-pickers · KBN-S-cap-prompt · KBN-S-lock-screen. Each surface's adoption adds tests today's skip-deferred specs validate; the spec scaffolding is in place so each adoption can drop a single `test.skip` and gain runtime coverage.

## 2026-05-27 — KBN-S-popover — shared `<Popover>` focus restore

First surface adoption of the `KBN-1`/`KBN-2` substrate. `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/popover.tsx` now consumes `useFocusTrap` from `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y` instead of the bare `useEscapeStackEntry` call landed earlier in `KBN-2`. The trap pushes onto the same module-scope escape stack so the renderer-wide LIFO unwinding from `installEscapeHandler` keeps working unchanged; in exchange the popover gains (1) focus-restoration to the opener on close, (2) Tab / Shift+Tab wrap inside the panel, (3) initial focus moved to the first focusable inside the panel on mount.

**Opener capture pattern.** The opener is captured at first render via a `useState` lazy initializer:

```tsx
const [opener] = useState<HTMLElement | null>(() =>
  typeof document === "undefined" ? null : (document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null) ?? null,
);
```

Lazy init runs once during the first render, synchronously, before any `useEffect` — including `useFocusTrap`'s own effect that moves focus into the panel. Passing `restoreFocusTo={opener}` explicitly (rather than relying on the hook's default `document.activeElement` capture) keeps the new `KBN-G-focus-trap-without-restore` guard from KBN-3 satisfied and makes the restoration target legible at the call site.

**Why this matters.** The four-panel object-menu drop, the cover-picker drop, the cheatsheet on Escape — every popover surface in the codebase was leaving focus on `<body>` in 100% repro, because the chord-registry `useShortcut("shell/popover.close")` migrated to `useEscapeStackEntry` in KBN-2 only handled the Escape contract, not the focus contract. One change in the shared primitive fixes every consumer in the renderer — matching the spec's leverage call-out ("one change fixes every popover call site in the codebase").

**Tests.** New jsdom file `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/popover.test.tsx` mounts the popover via a button-triggered harness and asserts:
1. Focus is restored to the opener button after Escape closes the popover (the canonical pattern).
2. A removed opener (yanked mid-popover via route change) doesn't throw and doesn't strand focus on the detached node — `useFocusTrap`'s `document.body.contains` guard absorbs the missing target.

The test installs `installEscapeHandler(getEscapeStack())` in `beforeEach` so the document-level Escape handler runs (production wires this once in `dashboard.tsx`).

**Numbers.** Full SDK + shell suite: **4154 / 4154** green. Workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean. No new dependencies. No bundle delta — Popover already imported from `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y`; this swaps one named export for another.

**Commits.** Single `feat(shell): KBN-S-popover focus restore via useFocusTrap` rolled with the plan + table + log update — small enough that the iteration ladder doesn't pay for splitting.

## 2026-05-27 — KBN-3 — four static CI guards (`KBN-G-*`)

The static-lint half of the `KBN` ladder from [shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md §Validation](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md#validation). Four pure TS-AST checkers in `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/`, same shape as `12.11`/`.12`/`.13`/`.14` + `0.11-keyboard` + `9.5.3-iframe-src`. **The structural CI gate inventory now stands at sixteen** — 12.2 / 12.9 / 12.10 / 12.11 / 12.12 / 12.13 / 12.14 / SH-30 / SH-31 / SH-32 / 0.11-keyboard / 9.5.3-iframe-src + the new **KBN-G-tabindex** / **KBN-G-roles** / **KBN-G-onclick-non-button** / **KBN-G-focus-trap-without-restore**. Each checker ships with a `KNOWN_VIOLATION_PATHS` snapshot per the SH-31/.32 mechanic — a violation in a file not in the snapshot fails the gate (new regressions are blocked), AND a snapshot-listed file with no live violation fails the gate too (stale entries force a real cleanup as call sites migrate).

**Why now.** The `KBN-1` substrate landed earlier today (controllers + DOM bindings + focus-ring tokens); `KBN-2` migrated the Escape stack onto it. The guards are the structural floor under both — without them an iteration can silently regress a positive `tabindex`, hand-roll a composite role and skip `useCompositeKeyboard`, glue `onClick` to a `<div>` with no keyboard contract, or use `useFocusTrap` without `restoreFocusTo`. All four are zero-or-low-snapshot today; locking the floor in now means the per-app `KBN-A-*` rungs land on a clean slate.

**Checkers.**

- `a11y-tabindex-check.ts` — `findPositiveTabindexes()`. Flags `tabIndex={N}` / `tabIndex="N"` JSX and `el.tabIndex = N` / `el.setAttribute("tabindex", "N")` JS where `N` is a positive integer literal (anything other than `0` / `-1`). Dynamic `tabIndex={x}` is opaque and passes (the value could be `0` / `-1` at runtime). Per-line escape hatch: `// kbn-tabindex-exempt`. Snapshot: **0 sites** today.
- `a11y-roles-check.ts` — `findRawCompositeRoles()`. Flags hand-written `role="listbox|grid|tree|tablist|toolbar|radiogroup"` (JSX literal + `el.role = "…"` + `setAttribute("role", "…")`) outside the SDK a11y subpath. Composite-keyboard roles must flow through `useCompositeKeyboard` / `useTreeKeyboard` / `useRegionNavigation`, which stamp `containerProps.role` along with the keyboard contract. Per-line escape hatch: `// kbn-roles-exempt`. Snapshot: **27 files** (apps + sdk + shell renderer). Biggest contributors: `apps/notes/src/editor/*` 7 files (link/mention/media/transclusion/inline-toolbar/block-embed/add-property menus), `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/*` 5 files (membership / data / appearance / devices-join / open-with-prompt), `packages/sdk/src/icon-picker/picker.tsx` 2 instances. Cleanup is to route each site through the SDK hook.
- `a11y-onclick-non-button-check.ts` — `findOnClickNonButton()`. Flags JSX `onClick={…}` on raw DOM elements (lowercase tags) outside the `INTERACTIVE_TAGS` set (`button|a|input|textarea|select|label|option|summary`) when the element carries none of `role` / `tabIndex` / `disabled` / `aria-disabled` / `contentEditable`. PascalCase tags (`<Button>`, `<MyClickable>`) are out of scope — the component owns its own a11y contract, mirroring `a11y-button-name-check`'s precedent. Per-line escape hatch: `// kbn-onclick-exempt`. Snapshot: **2 files** (`apps/files/src/ui/content-list.tsx`, `packages/shell/src/renderer/help/help-article.tsx`).
- `a11y-focus-trap-without-restore-check.ts` — `findFocusTrapsWithoutRestore()`. Flags `useFocusTrap({…})` call sites whose options object lacks `restoreFocusTo` (literal or shorthand property). Only fires in files that actually `import { useFocusTrap } from "@brainstorm/sdk/a11y"` (or the SDK-internal relative path) — a same-named local function elsewhere is out of scope. Conservative on opacity: an identifier argument (`useFocusTrap(opts)`) or an object with `{...spread}` passes (the spread could carry `restoreFocusTo`). Per-line escape hatch: `// kbn-trap-restore-exempt`. Snapshot: **0 sites** today — no production callers of `useFocusTrap` yet (the hook landed in KBN-1b), so the floor is locked at zero. KBN-S-popover and the per-app rungs will land call sites with `restoreFocusTo` from commit #1.

**MCP tool surface.** Each checker is wired into `tools/mcp-server/src/server.ts` as a `registerTool` entry: `a11y.find_positive_tabindex`, `a11y.find_raw_composite_roles`, `a11y.find_onclick_non_button`, `a11y.find_focus_traps_without_restore`. All four accept an optional `roots` array (default `['apps', 'packages/shell/src/renderer', 'packages/sdk/src']`) and return `{ ok, count, violations[] }`. A shared `walkSources(roots, opts)` helper lives at the top of `buildServer()` so each tool registration stays compact. The runtime CI guard is the vitest-driven repo-wide check in each test file — `bun run verify` and `bun run test` run them automatically (the test files live under `tools/mcp-server/tests/` and the workspace `vitest.config.ts` includes them).

**Tests.**

- `tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-tabindex-check.test.ts` — 17 tests: every JSX shape (`{N}` / `"N"` / lowercase `tabindex`), every JS shape (`el.tabIndex = N`, `setAttribute("tabindex", …)` string + numeric value), `0`/`-1` passes, dynamic-value pass, case-insensitive `setAttribute` name match, escape-hatch (on-line + above-line), reporting (path + 1-based line + value + excerpt), non-`.ts`/`.tsx` files skipped, repo-wide snapshot.
- `tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-roles-check.test.ts` — 15 tests: JSX literal + JSX expression-wrapped literal + every role in the set + non-composite roles pass + opaque `role={x}` pass + JS shapes (`el.role =`, `setAttribute("role", …)`) + non-composite JS pass, allowlist admits SDK a11y subpath (incl. absolute path) + rejects ordinary app source + no-flag inside the SDK a11y subpath, escape-hatch (on-line + above-line), reporting, non-`.ts`/`.tsx` files skipped, repo-wide snapshot.
- `tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-onclick-non-button-check.test.ts` — 14 tests: `<div onClick>` flagged + every interactive tag passes, opt-out by `role` (any value) + `tabIndex` (any value) + `disabled` + `aria-disabled` + `contentEditable`, PascalCase components pass, escape-hatch (on-line + above-line), reporting, non-`.tsx` files skipped, repo-wide snapshot.
- `tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-focus-trap-without-restore-check.test.ts` — 14 tests: missing-`restoreFocusTo` flagged + zero-arg flagged, `restoreFocusTo` property + shorthand pass, opaque `(opts)` pass + `{...rest}` spread pass, unrelated-module + same-named-local-function ignored, relative-path imports of the a11y subpath caught, escape-hatch (on-line + above-line), reporting, non-`.ts`/`.tsx` files skipped, repo-wide snapshot.

**Verification signals.**

- `bun --bun vitest run tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-tabindex-check.test.ts tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-roles-check.test.ts tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-onclick-non-button-check.test.ts tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-focus-trap-without-restore-check.test.ts` → **4 files, 60/60 tests** green.

## 2026-05-27 — KBN-2 — renderer-wide Escape stack (OQ-KBN-3 RESOLVED)

The single-handler half of the `KBN` substrate from [shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md §Escape stack](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md#escape-stack). One document-level `keydown` capture listener drains a renderer-wide LIFO of overlay closers; opening a popover / dialog / launcher / cheatsheet / dashboard context-menu / etc. pushes onto the stack; closing pops; `Escape` invokes the top-of-stack closer. When the stack is empty, the event continues propagating so the chord registry's existing `Escape` bindings (and the eventual app-side `app/escape`) keep working.

**OQ-KBN-3 RESOLVED:** renderer-only, per-window scope, no main-process round-trip. `getEscapeStack()` is a module-scope singleton — the shell and each sandboxed app each own a private stack. Per-window scope mirrors the rest of the focus model; a popover in window A must not swallow `Escape` in window B. No IPC, no cross-window coupling, latency unchanged.

**SDK additions (`@brainstorm/sdk/a11y`).**
- `escape-stack.ts` — `getEscapeStack()` (module-scope `createFocusTrapStack()` singleton reusing KBN-1a's pure stack); `installEscapeHandler(stack, { onEmptyStack? })` (capture-phase document listener; on non-empty stack, `preventDefault` + `stopPropagation` + `applyEscape`; on empty stack, optional callback + lets the event continue); `EscapeStackEntry` re-exports `FocusTrapEntry`.
- `use-escape-stack-entry.ts` — `useEscapeStackEntry({ onEscape, enabled?, label? })`. Pushes on mount via `useId()`-stable entry id; pops via the push-returned `off()` on unmount + when `enabled` flips true→false; re-pushes when `enabled` flips false→true. `onEscape` held in a ref so inline-arrow callers don't churn push/pop every render. StrictMode-safe: double-mount settles with exactly one entry.
- `use-focus-trap.ts` — now sources its module-scope stack from `getEscapeStack()` so trap pushes + ad-hoc closers share one LIFO; a focus-trapped dialog opened from inside a popover unwinds in the right order under one source of truth.

**Shell wiring.** `dashboard.tsx` adds one `useEffect(() => installEscapeHandler(getEscapeStack()), [])` next to the existing fullscreen / vault wiring; the same place `<LiveRegion />` was mounted in KBN-1b.

**Nine migration sites — all clean, no behavioural drift.**
1. `ui/popover.tsx` (shared dialog primitive) — `label: "popover"`.
2. `ui/icon-picker.tsx` — `label: "icon-picker"`.
3. `settings/settings.tsx` — `label: "settings"`.
4. `launcher/launcher.tsx` — drops `target: { kind: "scope", ref: panelRef }`, keeps `enabled: open`; `label: "launcher"`.
5. `marketplace/marketplace.tsx` — preserves the two-step Escape (clear selected listing first, close overlay on second press); `label: "marketplace"`.
6. `bin/bin.tsx` — `label: "bin"`.
7. `dashboard/icon-context-menu.tsx` — `label: "icon-context-menu"`.
8. `dashboard/window-switcher.tsx` — drops `target: scope`, keeps `enabled: open` (the switcher only registers while open); `label: "window-switcher"`.
9. `help/help.tsx` — `label: "help"`. Other `useShortcut("shell/help.search", …)` stays.

**Chord registry decision.** `shell/popover.close` chord entry stays in `default-chords.ts` purely as cheatsheet metadata ("Escape closes the popover" is still the user-visible behaviour) but no renderer component binds it via `useShortcut` anymore — the document-level handler owns delivery. JSDoc in `default-chords.ts` documents the new policy. `use-shortcut.ts`'s docstring example was rewritten to recommend `useEscapeStackEntry` for Escape on overlays.

**Tests.** New `escape-stack.test.tsx` (13 tests): hook push-on-mount / pop-on-unmount, LIFO ordering across nested mounts, out-of-order unmount preserves top, `enabled` flip false↔true repushes / pops, StrictMode double-mount settles with one entry, latest-callback-identity (ref-stabilize) check; handler routes Escape to top with `preventDefault` + `stopPropagation` (capture-phase blocks bubble-phase listeners), lets Escape continue on empty stack, `onEmptyStack` fires exactly once per Escape when empty + never when non-empty, ignores non-Escape keys, `uninstall` removes the listener, end-to-end hook + handler invocation. SDK a11y suite **152/152** (was 139 — +13); shell renderer suite **438/438**; shell build clean; workspace `tsc` clean on touched files; biome clean on touched files.

**Three commits per the iteration plan:** SDK module → shell wiring + 9-site migration → docs / plan / table / log + OQ-KBN-3 resolution.

## 2026-05-27 — KBN-1b — `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y` DOM bindings + shell live region

The DOM half of the `KBN-1` substrate — five React hooks on top of the KBN-1a reducers + a shell-mounted live region. Mirrors `B9.1b-ui` (the find-bar primitive's shell-injected chrome) for the live region; mirrors `find-bar.tsx` / `attach-find-bar.ts` for the React/DOM split where applicable. Same precedent of named exports, no defaults, enums for discriminators.

**Hooks.**
- `use-composite-keyboard.ts` — `useCompositeKeyboard({orientation, count, activeIndex, onActiveIndexChange, onActivate?, wrap?, columns?, pageSize?, disabled?, useAriaActiveDescendant?, typeahead?, getElementForIndex?})` → `{containerProps, getItemProps(i)}`. Frozen DOM-key → `CompositeKey` tables per orientation (`VERTICAL_KEYMAP` / `HORIZONTAL_KEYMAP` / `GRID_KEYMAP`); no raw `e.key` strings outside the keymap constants. Roving `tabindex` by default; `aria-activedescendant` opt-in for virtualized callers. Imperatively focuses `[data-composite-index]` on each active-index transition (falls through to `getElementForIndex` for callers whose items aren't in the DOM yet). `Activate` (Enter/Space) is observed by the hook before the reducer runs, since the reducer returns unchanged state on `CompositeKey.Activate` (documented asymmetry).
- `use-tree-keyboard.ts` — `useTreeKeyboard({nodes, activeId, onActiveIdChange, onToggle?, onActivate?, disabled?})` → `{containerProps, getNodeProps(node)}`. `role="tree"` on container, `role="treeitem"` + `aria-level` + `aria-expanded` (only on parents per the `hasChildren` flag / heuristic) + `aria-selected` on items. Imperatively focuses `[data-tree-node-id]` via a linear scan (`CSS.escape` isn't uniformly available in test envs).
- `use-focus-trap.ts` — `useFocusTrap({enabled, restoreFocusTo?, onEscape, initialFocus?, explicitInitialFocus?, openerLabel?})` → `{containerProps}`. Module-scope `createFocusTrapStack()` (one per renderer); KBN-2 will read this same instance for global Escape. Tab wraps inside the container; Shift+Tab wraps backward. Captures `document.activeElement` at enable-time for restore-on-close. StrictMode-safe (the entry id is `useId()`-stable; double-mount cycle pushes then pops then re-pushes cleanly). `InitialFocusMode` enum (`FirstFocusable` / `Container` / `Explicit`).
- `use-region-navigation.ts` — `useRegionNavigation({regions, activeRegionId?, onActiveRegionIdChange?, disabled?})`. Document-level capturing `F6` / `Shift+F6` keydown handler. First press with no active region lands on `regions[0]` (or `regions[length-1]` for Shift+F6); subsequent presses cycle via `regionNext` / `regionPrevious`. Focuses the matched region's `ref.current`. Cleanup removes the listener.
- `use-focus-visible.ts` — `useFocusVisible() → { isFocusVisible: boolean }`. Document-level capturing listeners for keydown / pointerdown / mousedown / touchstart; module-scope modality state shared across all subscribers. The last document-level installer cleans up when the subscriber set empties. Per spec §Focus invariants point 6.

**Helpers.**
- `typeahead-buffer.ts` — `createTypeaheadBuffer({getLabel, count, resetMs=500, now?})`. Pure: tracks the typed buffer + last-keystroke timestamp; prefix-matches via `getLabel`. Same-char repeats cycle through prefix-matching items starting from `indexHint + 1`. Wired into `useCompositeKeyboard` (the host's `typeahead` resolver is consulted; the buffer state lives in the helper).
- `live-region.tsx` — `<LiveRegion />` (one polite `role="status"` + one assertive `role="alert"`, both visually-hidden via `clip` + `position:absolute` etc.) and the imperative `announce(message, options?)`. Mounted once in `packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard.tsx` next to `<CapabilityPromptHost />` / `<OsHandoffPromptHost />`. Pre-mount calls queue into a 10-deep ring (oldest drops); flush runs on mount. Clear-then-write via `queueMicrotask` so repeated identical strings still announce.

**KBN-1a chores folded in.**
- `tree-keyboard.ts` — `TreeNode.hasChildren?: boolean` optional flag for lazy-loaded trees (the next-sibling-is-child heuristic still applies when the flag is `undefined`); `hasChildren()` consults the explicit flag first. +3 reducer tests covering the lazy case.
- `composite-keyboard.ts` + `tree-keyboard.ts` — JSDoc note above the `Activate` enum variant in each file explaining the hook-watches-key asymmetry (the reducer can't surface a side-channel from a no-op state transition).
- `focus-trap.ts` — JSDoc note above `applyEscape` warning that the host MUST remove its entry (via the unsubscribe from `push()`) before its `onEscape` returns, or before a recursive `applyEscape`, else `peek()` keeps returning the same top forever.

**Tests (next to each source file).**
- `use-composite-keyboard.test.tsx` 9 — tabindex stamp · ArrowDown advances + imperative focus · ArrowUp wraps · Home/End/PageDown/PageUp · Enter+Space → onActivate · typeahead resolver · `aria-activedescendant` mode · `aria-selected` mirroring · Grid orientation (ArrowDown = NextRow).
- `use-tree-keyboard.test.tsx` 7 — role + aria-expanded stamping · ArrowDown + focus move · ArrowLeft expanded-parent toggle · ArrowRight collapsed-parent toggle · lazy-tree (hasChildren=true) Collapse emits · Enter+Space → onActivate · Home/End.
- `use-focus-trap.test.tsx` 10 — initial focus first-focusable · Tab wraps · Shift+Tab wraps back · Escape → onEscape · unmount restores opener focus · disable pops the stack + restores · Container initial-focus mode · Explicit initial-focus mode · StrictMode double-mount stack count · nested traps sequential open + LIFO unwind via `applyEscape`.
- `use-region-navigation.test.tsx` 6 — first F6 lands on regions[0] · cycle through regions · F6 wraps last → first · Shift+F6 retreats from null → last · disabled=true ignores F6 · cleanup removes document listener.
- `use-focus-visible.test.tsx` 7 — starts pointer-modality · Tab → visible · pointerdown / mousedown / touchstart suppress · printable-char counts · F6 counts · programmatic focus retains keyboard modality · uninstall after last subscriber.
- `typeahead-buffer.test.ts` 10 — null on empty list · prefix match case-insensitive · extension within resetMs · reset window expiry · same-char cycle · no-match keeps buffer · `reset()` clears immediately · empty-char no-op · property: extension never matches earlier item · property: post-reset buffer length=1.
- `live-region.test.tsx` 8 — polite + assertive region shape · polite write · assertive write · pre-mount queue + flush · 10-deep ring · clear-then-write for repeated string · empty-string no-op · unmount + re-mount queue survival.
- `tree-keyboard.test.ts` +7 — three new `hasChildren` cases + format-driven re-counting brings the file from 14 to 21.

**Shell wiring.** `packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard.tsx` imports `LiveRegion` from `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y` and mounts it at the root, sibling to the other hosts. No other dashboard logic changes. `vitest.config.ts` gains the `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y` alias (positioned before the bare `@brainstorm/sdk` entry per the longer-prefix-first rule).

**Package wiring.** `packages/sdk/src/a11y/index.ts` re-exports the new hooks + `LiveRegion` + `announce` + `createTypeaheadBuffer` + helper types. NOT re-exported from `packages/sdk/src/index.ts` — consumers use the subpath, matching `./nav-history` / `./find-replace`. `packages/sdk/package.json` `exports` map already had `"./a11y"` from KBN-1a.

**Conventions honoured.** No raw `e.key` outside the local keymap constants (which are `Object.freeze`d and live next to the hook that uses them). `InitialFocusMode` is a TS string enum (no raw `"first-focusable"` literals). Named exports only; kebab-case files; React components / types `PascalCase`; functions / vars `camelCase`. No comments explaining WHAT; comments only when the WHY isn't obvious (the clear-then-write live-region invariant; the focus-trap module-scope-stack rationale; the Activate / re-entrancy notes are now on the reducer-side enums per the spec).

**Verification.**
- `bun --bun vitest run packages/sdk/src/a11y/` → 11 files, 135 tests, all green (was 4 files / 69+6 with happy-dom in the worktree).
- `bun --bun vitest run packages/sdk` → 84 files, **1132 tests** green. The single pre-existing red is `happy-dom` missing from one transitive vitest util — environmental to this worktree, not from KBN-1b.

Pentest surface (focus-trap is the only one that touches the global Escape contract — covered by the LIFO unwind test + the re-entrancy doc note; the rest are pure renderer-state mutations against the existing DOM contract).
