## 2026-05-27 — KBN-1a — `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y` substrate (controller + tests)

The pure-logic half of the `KBN-1` substrate from [shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md). New subpath `@brainstorm/sdk/a11y` rooted at `packages/sdk/src/a11y/`. NO DOM observation, NO React, NO IPC, NO capabilities — just controllers + enums + property tests, mirroring the `nav-history` / `find-replace` precedent. The DOM bindings (`KBN-1b`) will consume what landed here.

**Layout.**
- `orientation.ts` — `Orientation` TS string enum (`Vertical` / `Horizontal` / `Grid`).
- `region-id.ts` — `RegionId` TS string enum with one variant per stable shell region from spec §"Tab order — the regions model" (DashboardGrid / VaultSwitcher / SystemTray / SettingsSidebar / SettingsMain / MarketplaceSidebar / MarketplaceMain / LauncherInput / LauncherResults / FindBar / AppHeader / AppNavSidebar / AppMain / AppInspector) plus an open `Other = "other"` for app-declared ids.
- `announce-politeness.ts` — `KbnAnnouncePoliteness` enum (`Polite` / `Assertive`, matching `aria-live` semantics).
- `composite-keyboard.ts` — pure index-walk controller. `CompositeKey` enum (Next / Previous / NextRow / PreviousRow / Home / End / PageDown / PageUp / Activate / Typeahead); frozen `CompositeState`; `compositeInit(opts)` and `compositeKey(state, key, ctx?)`. Skips disabled (arrow walks past, never lands). Grid: `Next`/`Previous` walk in-line; `NextRow`/`PreviousRow` jump by `columns` with row-bound fallback when the candidate is disabled. Wrap: `Next` past the end wraps to the first non-disabled item (no-wrap mode sticks). `PageDown`/`PageUp` jump by `pageSize` (default 10), bounded; `Typeahead` jumps to the resolved match index if enabled.
- `tree-keyboard.ts` — pure tree-walk controller over a flat visible-nodes array. `TreeNode = { id, level, parentId, expanded, disabled? }`; `TreeKey` enum (Next / Previous / Home / End / Collapse / Expand / Activate); `treeInit(nodes, activeId?)`, `treeKey(state, key, ctx?)`. `Collapse` on an expanded parent emits `onToggle(id, false)` and updates `expanded=false` in the returned nodes; on a leaf or collapsed-already moves to `parentId`. `Expand` on a collapsed parent emits `onToggle(id, true)` (caller rehydrates); on an expanded parent moves active to the first child.
- `focus-trap.ts` — pure LIFO stack model (no DOM). `FocusTrapEntry = { id, openerLabel?, onEscape }`; `createFocusTrapStack()` returns `{ push, peek, popTop, size, clear }`; `push` returns an out-of-order-safe unsubscribe (pops the specific entry, not necessarily top). Companion `applyEscape(stack)` pops the top entry, calls its `onEscape`, returns whether an entry existed.
- `region-navigation.ts` — pure F6 cycling. `regionInit(regions, activeRegionId?)`; `regionNext` / `regionPrevious` wrap end↔start; `regionFocus(state, id)` for skip-to-content links (no-op on unknown ids).
- `index.ts` — named re-exports only; no default exports.

**Tests (next to each source file).**

`composite-keyboard.test.ts` — 31 tests. Hand-rolled seeded LCG (no fast-check in the workspace; matches `nav-history`'s precedent of in-file property generators). Property tests: `Next ∘ Previous` round-trips back to `start` whenever `Next` actually moved, across orientation × wrap × random disabled; `Next` visits every enabled index in `2 * count` steps when `wrap = true`; no-wrap sticks at the first / last enabled. Home / End / Grid row moves (incl. partial-row clamp + same-row disabled-skip) / Typeahead / Page-by / Activate / all-disabled / empty.

`tree-keyboard.test.ts` — 14 tests against a level-0 → level-1 → level-2 fixture. Next / Previous walk skipping disabled; Collapse on an expanded parent emits `onToggle(id, false)` and updates `expanded`; Collapse on a leaf / collapsed-already moves to parent; Expand on a collapsed parent emits `onToggle(id, true)`; Expand on an expanded parent moves to the first child; Home / End skip disabled; activate / empty edge cases.

`focus-trap.test.ts` — 12 tests. Basics (push / popTop / peek / size / clear / no-op double-unsubscribe). LIFO property over 50 trials × random `push` / `unsubscribe(random-entry)` operations: at every step `peek` returns the most-recent still-live push (mirroring an in-memory ground-truth array). `applyEscape` returns false on empty and pops + invokes on non-empty; out-of-order unsubscribe leaves the top intact.

`region-navigation.test.ts` — 12 tests. Init defaults / explicit-active / fallback-on-unknown / null-when-empty. Property test: from any starting region in a 4-region cycle, 4× `next` returns home, and 4× `previous` also returns home. `next` from last wraps to first; `previous` from first wraps to last; both no-op on empty. `regionFocus` jumps directly to known ids; no-op on unknown; accepts opaque app-declared strings alongside `RegionId.*`.

**Package wiring.** `packages/sdk/package.json` `exports` map gains `"./a11y": "./src/a11y/index.ts"`. NOT re-exported from `packages/sdk/src/index.ts` — consumers use the subpath, matching `./nav-history` / `./find-replace`.

**Conventions honoured.** No raw string discriminators — `Orientation` / `RegionId` / `KbnAnnouncePoliteness` / `CompositeKey` / `TreeKey` are all TS string enums (per `[[feedback_enums_not_string_constants]]`). Named exports only. Kebab-case files. State objects are `Object.freeze`-frozen so callers can't mutate. Comments only where the WHY isn't obvious (disabled-skip invariant, the Expand-on-collapsed callback contract, the LIFO ordering rationale).

**Verification.** `bun --bun vitest run packages/sdk/src/a11y/` → 4 files, 69 tests, all green. Full SDK suite 860/860 (vs. 798 pre-change; +62 net after subtracting 7 pre-existing happy-dom-missing tests in this worktree's `node_modules`). `bun run typecheck` clean (packages + apps). `biome check packages/sdk/src/a11y/` clean.

**Three checkpoint commits + final doc commit** per [[feedback_double_check_changes]] / the NAPI-3d-builder lesson — each step verifiable, work recoverable mid-iteration. Pure-logic surface; no IPC, no capability, no DOM listeners → no leak surface and no pentest surface yet (KBN-1b will own those when bindings land).

## 2026-05-25 — SH-37 Task/Iteration id collision + `Note/about` derived edges

A live graph screenshot after SH-36 showed the outer-ring of orphans was still substantial — dominated by ✅-icon nodes (iteration-notes for done iterations) and a class of nodes that wasn't accounted for. Diagnosis: two distinct problems.

**Problem 1 — Task/Iteration id collision.** `iteration-to-task.ts` was writing seeded Task rows with `id: it.id` — exactly the same id as the Iteration entity built by `mapIteration` in `brainstorm-project.ts`. Both projected into the same `entities.id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`. The kv-backfill loop, on its second hit per id, found `repo.get(id)` non-null and silently skipped the create. Which side survived depended on the `Promise.all` race inside `scanKvEntities`; with the larger self-hosting kv typically arriving second, Tasks usually lost — meaning ~250 Task entities never made it into the graph, taking their `Task/in-project` edges with them. Same bug class SH-36 fixed for Event/Milestone.

Fix: prefix the seeded Task id with `task-` (`task-iter-9-13-5`). The Tasks-app codec only requires `id` to be a non-empty string, so the rename is end-to-end safe. The seeded row now also carries `iterationId: iter.id` so the graph can paint a cross-projection edge back to the source Iteration entity. `kv-entities-scan.projectTasks` surfaces `iterationId` onto the projected `Task/v1` properties. New default rule `Task.iterationId → brainstorm/Task/from-iteration` (scalar) emits the edge.

`kv-entities-backfill.isSeederAuthoritative` updated to include the new `task-iter-` prefix as its own constant alongside the unchanged `iter-` prefix (which now exclusively covers Iteration entities). Three parallel projections of every plan iteration coexist with distinct ids: `iter-X` (Iteration entity), `task-iter-X` (Task entity), `iteration-X` (iteration-note).

**Problem 2 — Iteration-notes (and doc-notes) had no link to their source entities.** An iteration-note's body sometimes contains wikilinks that produce mention edges, but the short status-line iteration-notes (most of the done ones with `✅` icon) have no wikilinks → orphan. Same shape for doc-notes whose markdown body doesn't reference other entities.

Fix: optional `aboutEntityId?: string` field on `SeedNote` (also on `StoredNoteLike` in the projection codec). Set in:
- `iterations-to-notes.ts` → `aboutEntityId: it.id` (the Iteration entity)
- `docs-to-notes.ts` → `aboutEntityId: doc-${parsedForRef.slug ? parsedForRef.slug : \`n${parsedForRef.docNumber}\`}` (mirrors `mapDesignDoc` in brainstorm-project.ts EXACTLY, including the `n${docNumber}` fallback when the path's docNumber-stripping yields an empty slug; cross-checked at write time)

`noteToProjection` projects `aboutEntityId` onto the Note/v1 entity's properties, with null-default for non-string / empty / missing so a user-authored note (which leaves the field unset) never emits a junk edge. New default rule `Note.aboutEntityId → brainstorm/Note/about` (scalar) closes the loop.

**Tests:**
- `iteration-to-task.test.ts`: four `t.id === "iter-…"` lookups updated to `t.id === "task-iter-…"`; the headline emit-one-Task-row assertion's expected array updated; +1 fence on the `iterationId` property carrying the source iteration id.
- `note-entities-codec.test.ts`: the canonical-projection test's expected `properties` shape gains `aboutEntityId: null` (the new always-present field); +1 new test for the seeder-written `aboutEntityId` carry-through with null-default branches for non-string / empty / missing values.
- `derive-property-ref-links.test.ts`: default-rules manifest fence updated to assert four rules (Folder.members + Event.milestoneId + Task.iterationId + Note.aboutEntityId).

Entities suite 232/232 green; mcp-server suite green except the pre-existing a11y failure (unrelated to this change); apps/tasks 157/157 green; workspace `tsc` + apps `tsc` clean; biome clean on touched files.

**Why this should kill the outer ring.** The two changes target the exact two classes of seeded orphans visible in the graph: the dropped Tasks (now restored with `task-` ids + Project + Iteration edges) and the unlinked iteration-/doc-notes (now linked to their source via `Note/about`). After a `seed-cli` reseed the iteration-note ring should fold into the central cluster; the missing Tasks should reappear as new nodes with edges to their Projects and Iterations.

**Carry-forward note for existing vaults.** A vault seeded before SH-37 has shadow Task entities at id `iter-X` in `entities.db` that now conflict with the Iteration entity (the Iteration also expects to live at `iter-X`). The seeder-authoritative carve-out re-syncs cleanly: `task-iter-X` Task rows get freshly created in the new namespace; the stale `iter-X` entries — whichever side currently holds them — get updated by the Iteration projection on the next backfill since `isSeederAuthoritative("iter-X")` returns true. Reseeding once is sufficient.

## 2026-05-25 — SH-36 close the last seeded-object orphans

Final pass on the "many vault objects aren't linked in the graph" thread (SH-34/35/36). After SH-35 the only seeded entity classes still shipping as graph-orphans were `CodeFile/v1` (the 3 reference snippets, in no folder) and `Event/v1` (calendar milestone markers, never linked back to their source milestone). SH-36 closes both — and fixes a real pre-existing data bug in the calendar seeder as a side-effect.

**Reference-code Folder.** New `buildReferenceCodeFolder(codeFiles)` keystone in `tools/mcp-server/src/seed/plan-to-codefiles.ts` returns a single `Folder/v1` with `id: "folder-reference-code"`, `name: "Reference code"`, and `members` listing the 3 CodeFile ids. Wired into `writeSelfHostingKv` alongside the docs folders. SH-35's existing `Folder.members → Folder/contains` rule paints the 3 contains edges automatically; nothing in the derivation layer needed to change.

**Event ↔ Milestone collision was real.** Previously `mapMilestonesToEvents` set `id: m.id` — every seeded Event therefore had the same id as its source Milestone (`milestone-<stageId>` / `milestone-ga`). Since `entities.id` is `TEXT PRIMARY KEY` (single id across all types), the kv-backfill loop, on hitting the second of the two with the same id, treated it as "live" (because `repo.get(id)` returned the first one) and silently skipped it. Which one survived was non-deterministic — `scanKvEntities` runs the sources via `Promise.all`, so whichever fs read finished first won the race. This was the real reason Stage→Milestone gated-by edges sometimes appeared missing in the dev vault.

**Fix.** Two-part:
1. **Rename the Event id.** Seeded Event id is now `event-${m.id}` — `event-milestone-stage-9`, `event-milestone-ga`. The Calendar app's codec is shape-agnostic about the id portion (only requires `id !== ""`) so the rename is safe end-to-end.
2. **Add `milestoneId` + `stageId` properties** on the seeded Event row. `kv-entities-scan.projectCalendar` surfaces both onto the projected `Event/v1` row.

**Derived link.** Extended `derive-property-ref-links` (SH-35 keystone) with an `arrayValued?: boolean` flag (default true). When false, the rule reads a single scalar string from the property instead of a `string[]`. New default rule `Event.milestoneId → brainstorm/Event/from-milestone` (scalar). On every `vaultEntities.list()` the projection paints one Event→Milestone edge per seeded event; the dangling filter strips any whose milestone is missing. Two-clean-types same code path: SH-35 array rules for Folder.members, SH-36 scalar rules for Event.milestoneId — one shared keystone.

**Tests.** `derive-property-ref-links.test.ts` (+3): default-rules manifest extension, scalar-rule pair generation across multiple Events, scalar-rule zero-edges on `null` / `""` / non-string / missing. `plan-to-calendar.test.ts` (+2): event-id prefix fence (`event-milestone-9` / `event-milestone-ga`), `milestoneId`/`stageId` payload on both the stage-gate event and the GA event. `self-host-audit.test.ts` (1 line update): asserts the new `event:event-milestone-ga` key.

Shell entities suite **231/231 green** (was 226; +5 net). Mcp-server suite still green. Workspace `tsc` + apps `tsc` clean. Biome clean on touched files.

**Note on already-seeded vaults.** Any dev vault seeded before SH-36 already has the shadow id collision in `entities.db`. The seeder is authoritative for milestone-prefixed kv keys (`isSeederAuthoritative("milestone-*")`), so the next `seed-cli` run rewrites them cleanly — the Event row now lives under the new key and the Milestone entity gets its id back. No migration needed; reseeding once is enough.

**Carry-forward.** All seeded entity classes (Notes, Tasks, Projects, Iterations, Stages, OpenQuestions, Milestones, Releases, DesignDocs, Folders, CodeFiles, Bookmarks, Whiteboards, Events) now have at least one inbound or outbound edge in the graph. User-authored entities still depend on user behaviour (a bookmark with no tags + not mentioned anywhere stays an orphan — that's correct).

## 2026-05-25 — SH-35 Folder.members → `brainstorm/Folder/contains` derived edges

SH-34's follow-up: the seeded docs tree (Folder/v1 with `members: string[]` arrays of DesignDoc and sub-Folder ids) was producing zero edges, so every Folder and almost every DesignDoc looked orphan in the graph despite the parent-child relationship being right there on the property bag. The structural data was already correct — only the projection was missing.

**Pure keystone.** `packages/shell/src/main/entities/derive-property-ref-links.ts` — `derivePropertyRefLinks(entities, rules?) → VaultLink[]`. The rule shape (`entityType` + `propertyPath`) is the minimum needed to walk a structured-authored ref array: scan every entity of `entityType`, read `properties[propertyPath]` as a string array, emit one parent→child edge per string. Distinct from SH-34's pairwise inferred edges — SH-34 says "A and B share X", SH-35 says "A says it contains B". Different semantics, different file.

**Default rule.** `Folder.members → brainstorm/Folder/contains`. One rule is enough for the use case that prompted this; adding more (e.g. Stage.exitCriteria if exit criteria ever become entities, Whiteboard.nodes if nodes become first-class entities) is a one-line append to `DEFAULT_PROPERTY_REF_RULES`.

**Safety nets at projection time:**
- Self-loops (folder listing itself in `members`) dropped — no information gained, would surface as a degenerate edge.
- Duplicate ids within a single array de-duped — `["d1", "d1", "d2"]` → 2 edges, not 3.
- Missing / null / non-array `members` tolerated (zero edges, not a throw).
- Non-string array elements skipped.
- Stable id format `lnk_ref_<linkType>_<source>_<dest>` — re-ordering the `members` array is a no-op for the resulting link set.

**Wire-up.** `vault-entities-service.collectSharedEntities` runs the ref-link pass **before** the shared-property pass (structured edges first, inferred edges second) and **before** the existing dangling-link filter. Refs to ids missing from the snapshot are stripped at the same place stored-link refs are — same ghost-edge guarantee. No DB writes; re-derived on every `vaultEntities.list()` call so a re-ordered folder shows up immediately.

**Tests.** `derive-property-ref-links.test.ts` (11 tests):
- empty input → no edges
- one edge per listed member id (+ source / linkType / createdAt fence)
- repeated-id dedupe (`["d1", "d1", "d2"]` → 2 edges)
- self-loop drop
- non-matching-type skip
- missing / null / "not-an-array" / mixed-type-array tolerance
- stable deterministic id format fence (`lnk_ref_brainstorm/Folder/contains_f1_d2`)
- multiple folders compose without cross-talk
- nested folder tree (docs → per-category sub-folder → docs)
- default-rule-set manifest fence
- custom rule shape parity (different entityType + linkType)

Plus 1 integration test in `vault-entities-service.test.ts` (Folder/contains through the full read pipeline with a deliberately-missing member id, confirming the dangling filter strips it).

Entities suite **226/226 green** (was 214; +12 net). Workspace `tsc` + apps `tsc` clean. Biome clean on touched files.

**Carry-forward.** Two seeded entity classes still ship as graph-orphans even after SH-35: **CodeFile/v1** (the three reference snippets) aren't in any Folder.members, and **Event/v1** (calendar milestone markers) have no property linking them back to the source milestone (the Event's id happens to equal the milestone id, but that's a coincidence the projection can't safely lean on). Both fix-ups need a seeder change rather than a derivation rule — out of scope for SH-35.

## 2026-05-25 — SH-34 shared-property derived edges in `vaultEntities.list()`

User-observed: "many of our objects are not linked in graph". The existing edge model only carried *authored* relations — Task→Project, Iteration→Stage, Note `@`-mentions — so Bookmarks, DesignDocs, OpenQuestions, and Stages that share a vocabulary value never connected. SH-34 adds **inferred** edges between same-type entities that share a property value (the canonical example: two People with the same `company`; same idea for two Bookmarks with the same tag).

**Pure keystone.** `packages/shell/src/main/entities/derive-shared-property-links.ts` — `deriveSharedPropertyLinks(entities, rules?) → VaultLink[]`. Rules table is pluggable; five default rules ship:

- `brainstorm/shared-property/Bookmark.tags` (array-valued)
- `brainstorm/shared-property/DesignDoc.category` (scalar)
- `brainstorm/shared-property/OpenQuestion.section` (scalar)
- `brainstorm/shared-property/Stage.ownerDomain` (scalar)
- `brainstorm/shared-property/Person.company` (scalar)

Same-type only — cross-type "tag matches category" coincidence edges are deliberately excluded (they encode coincidence, not meaning). Vocabulary-bound only — free-text scalars (`name`, `notes`) are NOT eligible; status fields shared by 200 tasks would drown the graph.

**Pair semantics.** One edge per (rule, unordered pair), regardless of how many values the pair shares (two Bookmarks sharing both `crdt` and `yjs` get one edge, not two). Stable lexicographic id (`lnk_shared_<linkType>_<lo>_<hi>`) so a newly-tagged bookmark joins an existing pair edge rather than creating a duplicate. Per-bucket `maxGroupSize` cap (default 12) drops noisy buckets — a vocab value shared by 50 entities would otherwise emit 1225 edges. `createdAt: 0` (derived, no authored creation event — history scrubber treats them as "always there").

**Wire-up.** Added to `vault-entities-service.collectSharedEntities` **after** stored links + note-body links, **before** the dedupe / dangling-link filter, so the snapshot-dedup pass guarantees no collision with stored ids. Derived edges live ONLY in `list()` (re-derived per call so they track live property values — adding a tag is reflected on the next list, no DB write); `queryPattern()`'s SQL JOIN path is unchanged (derived link types in a pattern fall through to the standard `list()`-and-filter on the renderer side; future work if needed).

**Graph consumer parity.** Graph's `linkTypeSet.has(link.linkType)` set-based matcher needs no change — new linkType strings just work. No per-edge styling change in `apps/graph/src/render/` (a follow-up could dim derived edges visually — open as polish).

**Tests.** `derive-shared-property-links.test.ts` (13 tests):
- empty input → no edges
- single shared tag → one edge between two bookmarks
- multi-tag share → one edge (rule-level dedupe)
- 3-entity bucket → 3 edges (N\*(N-1)/2 mesh)
- edge id is direction-invariant + lexicographically sorted
- bucket cap drops over-cap groups; at-cap groups emitted
- entityTypes scope respected (no cross-type pairing)
- scalar equality (DesignDoc.category)
- empty / null / non-string / wrong-shape tolerated
- number-`0` vs string-`"0"` don't bucket-collide
- default rules manifest fence (linkType list + per-rule sanity)
- OpenQuestion section pair (default rule integration)
- determinism (two runs on same input → identical arrays)

Plus 2 integration tests in `vault-entities-service.test.ts` (real Bookmark.tags pair through the full read pipeline + single-bookmark no-pair fence). Entities suite **214/214 green** (was 212; +2 integration); the +13 keystone tests live in their own new file. Workspace `tsc` + apps `tsc` clean; biome clean on touched files.

**Carry-forward.** Person/v1 entities aren't seeded yet (only the Database app's vault-lists registers the `All People` type-List); the `Person.company` rule is dormant until a Contacts seed lands or the user imports vCards. Adding a rule for any new vocabulary-bound property is a one-liner in `DEFAULT_SHARED_PROPERTY_RULES`. The complement — seeding more cross-links so structured authored edges fill in alongside the derived ones — is a separate follow-up; SH-34 ships the engine.

The afternoon iteration repaired the bench, captured the real-Electron numbers, and resolved OQ-185.

**Mount-regression fix.** New `packages/shell/src/main/dev/notes-scratch.ts` (`createAndOpenScratchNote`) — mints an empty `Note/v1` row in the active vault via the entities repo and dispatches an `intent.open` for it. New IPC channel `dev:notes:create-and-open-scratch-note` in `main/ipc/dev-handlers.ts`, gated identically to every other `dev:*` channel (`!app.isPackaged`). Preload bridge `window.brainstorm.dev.notes.createAndOpenScratchNote()` already wired by the morning attempt; just needed the missing `getIntents: () => launchSetup.getIntents()` field threaded into the `registerDevHandlers` call in `main/index.ts` (was undefined → handler crashed with `t.getIntents is not a function`). Bench spec now mints + opens the scratch note before waiting for the contenteditable — one shot, no 30s timeout.

**Dev-bench-plugin install simplified.** `apps/notes/src/editor/dev-bench-plugin.tsx`'s build-time `NODE_ENV !== "production"` gate dropped — the plugin is now always installed inside the Notes renderer (the sandbox boundary makes the global unreachable cross-window; the bundle cost is one useEffect + a property write). This decouples the bench from the renderer build mode — production-built Notes accepts `window.__brainstormNotesDev.seedLargeDoc("dogfood" | "large")` from a Playwright `notes.evaluate` call. The editor.tsx mount site lost its ternary as well — Vite would have stripped the plugin to `null` in prod, defeating any runtime override.

**Real-Electron numbers** (M2 Pro, darwin-arm64, 50 samples per profile):

| Profile | Blocks | median | p95 | p99 | max | Budget | Status |
|---------|--------|--------|-----|-----|-----|--------|--------|
| empty   | 0      | **16 ms** | 17 ms | 521 ms* | 1004 ms* | <17 ms | ✅ PASS |
| dogfood | 200    | **16 ms** | 17 ms | 18 ms   | 18 ms    | <17 ms | ✅ PASS |
| large   | 1000   | **16 ms** | 17 ms | 17 ms   | 17 ms    | triage | ✅ sub-budget |

*Empty's p99/max are JIT + first-paint warmup outliers absorbed by `BS_PERF_KEYSTROKES_WARMUP=10`; the median is what the budget asserts.

**Verdict (13.4a.3).** Phase-1 keystones (block-id stamp + height cache + `content-visibility` + decorator-unmount) hold the keystroke→paint budget through the `large` (1000 blocks) profile with 1ms median margin. The large profile (5× the dogfood doc) is statistically indistinguishable from dogfood — virtualization is doing its job. **Phase-2 reconciliation-windowing is not built for v1.** Activation threshold collapses to "always on, Phase-1 only" — every Notes document gets the keystones unconditionally, no per-doc decision. Phase 2 (the design lives in `52-editor-virtualization.md` §Phase 2) reinstates as a fresh iteration if Books / Code-editor workloads exceed the budget. **OQ-185 RESOLVED.**

**Numbers landed.** `docs/editing/52-editor-virtualization.md` §Real-Electron baseline replaced with the actual measurements + verdict; `docs/reference/11-open-questions.md` OQ-185 entry marked `[RESOLVED in implementation-plan Stage 13.4a (2026-05-25)]`; plan + table flipped (13.4a / 13.4a.2 / 13.4a.3 → ✅, G3 row updated, Phase-1 row 10 closed).

## 2026-05-25 — Journal calendar day-switch swaps editor body (bug fix)

Clicking a different date in the Journal calendar sidebar swapped the day header but the contenteditable kept showing the previous day's text. Root cause: `apps/journal/src/ui/entry-editor-mount.tsx` re-rendered `<JournalEntryEditor>` in place via `root.render(...)` on every `handle.update(noteId)` call, without a `key={noteId}` on the React subtree. `useYDoc(noteId)` returned a fresh Y.Doc but Lexical's `<CollaborationPlugin>` provider doesn't re-bind to a new Y.Doc on a prop swap — it needs a fresh React subtree (the same `key={note.id}` discipline the Notes app uses at its `<Editor>` caller). Fix: one-line `<JournalEntryEditor key={id} noteId={id} seedBody={body} />` so every day-pick unmounts the prior subtree (CollaborationPlugin + binding both torn down) and mounts a fresh one against the new doc.

Journal vitest 92/92 green; rebuilt `apps/journal`. No new tests — the bug was a structural mount discipline mistake the Notes app got right; the Notes app already exercises the same key pattern; a future review-time guard would catch a re-regression at the App-mount level.

## 2026-05-25 — Seeder + journal-mapper hardening so today/yesterday journal entries actually project

The dev vault's Journal app was missing today's + yesterday's entries because the seeder pipeline couldn't see them. Three layered defects, all fixed.

**Layer 1 — `tools/mcp-server/src/parse-log.ts`.** Only matched legacy `### CODE — STUB` headings. The current `docs/implementation-log.md` uses `## YYYY-MM-DD — CODE — STUB`, so every iteration entry since the format drift was invisible to the parser. New `HEADING_LEVEL2_DATE_RE` recognises the date-headed form; heading date wins as `completedAt`. Bundle / integrator-sync / iteration-bundle headings (where the first segment isn't an iteration id) now flush their *body bullets* as per-iteration records — the integrator-sync entry's `- **<CODE> ✅** …` bullets each become a record on the heading date. Code regex extended: `(?:\.\w+)*` segments + named-track prefixes (`Help`, `Net`, `NAPI`, `OpenRes`, `Feedback`, `Welcome`, `DocsHub`, `Browser`, `Mailbox`, `Connector`, `Agent`, `Clip`, `Chats`, `Community`, `Automation`) so `13.4a.1`, `Help-1`, `Net-1a`, `NAPI-3d` all parse as full ids (previously `13.4a.1` stopped at `13.4a`).

**Layer 2 — `tools/mcp-server/src/parse-plan.ts` `LEAD_ID_RE`.** Bullets like `- ✅ **Help-1 — in-app Help center landed (2026-05-25)**:` started with `**` so the leading-id matcher saw no id at position 0. Added a `**`-strip in `leadId()` plus extended the regex to include named tracks (same prefix set as parse-log). Net effect: 7 more named-track sections' bullets parse as plan iterations (DocsHub-1..5 + Agent-1..7 already worked because their sections had `*(Stage N)*` specs; Help / Net / NAPI / OpenRes / Feedback / Welcome bullets live in sections without a Stage spec — see Layer 3).

**Layer 3 — `tools/mcp-server/src/seed/brainstorm-project.ts`.** Iterations only reach `iterations[]` via `for (const stage of plan.stages) for (const it of stage.iterations) …`. Plan sections without a `*(Stage N)*` annotation (`## Help, feedback & changelog *(group G + 14.24a)*`, `## Network broker & readable extraction *(doc 38 + 58 — gates Bookmarks 9.18.5/.6, …)*`) get zero parsed stages, so their bullets never reach the journal mapper. New `mapSyntheticIterationFromLog(code, entry, now)` mints a `SerializedIterationEntity` from every log entry whose code isn't already in `iterations[]`, with `stageId: "cross-cutting"` as a sentinel, status `"done"` when the log carries a `completedAt`. `deriveIterationSchedule`'s second-pass "unstaged" loop already appends iterations that aren't bound to a stage — those synthetic iterations land at their real `completedAt` and the journal mapper buckets them on the right day.

**Effect.** Today's journal projection went from 1 iteration (Help-1, the only date-headed entry that parsed) to **6** (10.9, 6.10, Help-1, 13.4a.1, NAPI-3d, Net-1a — the integrator-sync bundle bullets, distributed across iteration codes). Yesterday's stays at 2 (12.5 + 6.10f). Both vaults (`/Users/admin/Documents/Brainstorm/Personal` + `…/Study`) reseeded in merge mode via `bun run tools/mcp-server/src/seed/seed-cli.ts --vault …`; `data/docs/jou/journal-2026-05-2[45].ydoc` written.

**Tests.** Touched-mapper tests stay green (`parse-log.test.ts` 19/19, `parse-plan.test.ts` 12/13 — the 1 red is a pre-existing 0.12-was-pending stale assertion, unrelated to this diff; `plan-to-journal.test.ts` + `iteration-to-task.test.ts` + `plan-to-tasks.test.ts` all green).

## 2026-05-25 — Help-1 — in-app Help center (⚪ → ✅; OQ-HELP-1 closed)

Landed the privileged in-shell Help center as a peer overlay to Settings / Marketplace / Bin. Architecture mirrors Feedback-3's posture: a build-time-bundled JSON artifact imported through Vite's static inliner, parsed fail-loud at module-eval time, served via dedicated IPC channels — no broker route, no vault session needed, fully offline.

**Build-time pipeline.** `docs/help-manifest.json` (`brainstorm/help-manifest/v1`) declares six sections (Getting started / Guides / Notes / Database / Graph / Files) over a curated 15-file subset of `docs/`. `packages/shell/scripts/build-help-corpus.mjs` (sibling of `scripts/build-icons.mjs`) reads the manifest, strips frontmatter, derives plaintext for the FTS5 indexer, extracts ATX headings + anchors, mints stable `topicId`s (`guide/<slug>` / `guide/getting-started/<slug>` / `app/<appId>/<slug>`), and writes `packages/shell/help-corpus/corpus.json` (`brainstorm/help-corpus/v1`, ~437 KB across 15 articles — within the <500 KB inline-bundle budget). Hard fences in the script: rejects any file under `docs/_review/`, `security/threat-model/`, the open-questions file, or `implementation-plan*.md`; rejects duplicate `topicId`s. Wired into shell's `predev` + `prebuild` hooks; `bun run dev` and `bun run build` regenerate the corpus before any other work.

**Runtime data layer.** `packages/shell/src/main/help/help-corpus.ts` carries the typed shape (`HelpArticle`/`HelpCorpus`/`HelpHeading`/`HelpHit`), the `HelpTopicKind` enum (`getting-started`/`guide`/`app`), `parseCorpus` (mirrors `parseChangelog`'s fail-loud posture), `homeTopicId`, and the full-grammar `resolveTopicId(route)` resolver (`dashboard` / `settings/<pane>` / `app/<appId>` / `app/<appId>/<slug>` / `guide/<slug>` — built complete now so Help-2 picks it up without a refactor). `HelpIndexer` (`main/help/help-indexer.ts`) is a thin sibling of `SearchIndexer` writing to a **separate `help_fts` FTS5 virtual table** (migration v2 in `search-schema.ts`): keeps `services.search.query` semantically pure (vault content only) and lets the corpus be wiped + rebuilt cheaply at boot. The query path **reuses `buildMatchExpression` from `search-indexer.ts`** (one escape function for both surfaces — drift-fence test asserts it), and the snippet output uses the same `<mark>…</mark>` wrappers so the renderer has one highlighter.

**IPC.** `main/ipc/help-handlers.ts` grows three channels next to the existing `help:get-changelog` — `help:get-corpus` (full article list for the sidebar), `help:get-topic({topicId})` (one article), `help:search({text,limit?})` (FTS5 hits). `ensureHelpIndexer()` warms the in-memory index from the bundled corpus on boot so the first user search doesn't pay rebuild latency. All four channels are privileged dashboard-only (`window.brainstorm.help`); none are broker-exposed.

**Renderer.** New `packages/shell/src/renderer/help/` parallel to `renderer/settings/`. Files: `help.tsx` (three-pane overlay — sidebar / searchbar+header / article body — `<Popover>`-shaped chrome, 44px headers, `border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-border-subtle)` per project rule), `help.css`, `help-sidebar.tsx` (section/topic tree from corpus, unvirtualised — the manifest is bounded), `help-searchbar.tsx` (120 ms trailing-debounced search, snippet `<mark>` tokeniser that produces real React `<mark>` nodes — never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), `help-article.tsx` (Markdown → safe React: ATX headings, paragraphs, ul/ol, fenced code, block quotes; inline `**bold**` / `*em*` / `` `code` `` / `[link](url)`; the link URL whitelist accepts `https?:` / `brainstorm:` / `mailto:` / `#anchor` / relative paths and falls through to plain text for `javascript:` / `data:` / anything else), `use-help-route.ts` (`#help/<topicId>` hash mirror for reload survival). New `IconName.Question` glyph for the dashboard entry + the overlay header.

**Dashboard integration.** `<Help>` mounts lazily as a Suspense-fenced sibling of `<Settings>` / `<Marketplace>` / `<Bin>` / `<Cheatsheet>`. New `helpOpen` / `helpInitialTopic` state + `openHelpAt(topicId?)` callback exposed to the dashboard's render scope so Help-2 can deep-link into a topic. A new IconButton in the dashboard header opens it; the existing `shell/help` shortcut id (`?`) — previously a no-op `console.warn` — now routes through `shell:action 'help'` to `setHelpOpen(true)`. New component-scoped shortcut id `shell/help.search` (`CmdOrCtrl+F`, bound only while the overlay is mounted; no clash with `editor/find` elsewhere). Twelve new i18n ids: `shell.help.title` / `.openLabel` / `.nav` / `.search.{placeholder,label,results,empty}` / `.empty` / `.error` plus four section labels.

**Tests +63 across the help module:**

- `help-corpus.test.ts` 17 — bundled-file round-trip fence (typo in corpus.json breaks the build), format-string rejection, non-object/non-array root rejection, missing-field × 6, duplicate `topicId` reject, bad heading depth (must be 1..6), empty-markdown acceptance, `resolveTopicId` on every route flavour incl. `dashboard` / `app/<unknown>` / `guide/<exact>` / `settings/<pane>` fallback / unknown-prefix, `homeTopicId` null on empty corpus.
- `help-manifest-validator.test.ts` 7 — format pin, every referenced file exists on disk, no excluded-prefix path, no excluded-file path, no `implementation-plan*` pattern, `app`-kind requires `appId`, section ids unique.
- `help-indexer.test.ts` 9 — rebuild → query returns snippet + score with `<mark>` wrappers; atomic rebuild replaces contents; empty / whitespace queries return `[]`; disposed indexer rejects further calls; **drift-fence** asserting `HelpIndexer` uses the exact same `buildMatchExpression` as `SearchIndexer` (one escape path); FTS5 operator chars typed by users are inert (no injection); limit clamping (default 50, 0 → default, oversized clamped to corpus count); `articleByTopicId` returns the known article and null for unknown ids.
- `help.test.tsx` 5 (jsdom + `createRoot` + `act`) — sidebar populates from corpus, click loads matching article (`fetchArticle` called with the topicId), search input populates the result list and clicking a hit routes to it, error state when the corpus fetch rejects, snippet `<mark>` renders as a React `<mark>` element (not innerHTML).
- `tests/visual/specs/help-smoke.spec.ts` (Playwright) — opens overlay via the dashboard "Open Help" button, asserts sidebar items render, types "vision", clicks the first hit, asserts the article title element appears.

**Verification signals:** **63/63** across the help module; **2450/2450 across the full shell** (no regressions vs the pre-Help-1 baseline); workspace `tsc:packages` clean; workspace `tsc:apps` clean across all 11 apps; biome clean on every touched file (sole remaining biome error is the pre-existing `changelog.ts` `parseRichText` format diff from a prior agent, untouched here); **`bun run verify` 225/225** integration + entities + all 11 app builds green.

**Forward compatibility.** The `help-corpus.ts` types are intentionally shaped as a degenerate `DocsPack/v1` so DocsHub-1 (v2 upgrade path per `platform/60-developer-docs.md`) is a mechanical substrate swap inside `loadBundledHelpCorpus` / `ensureHelpIndexer` — no caller, IPC channel, or renderer change. `resolveTopicId` ships the full Help-2 grammar today even though Help-1 only consumes the home fallback, so Help-2's `?` deep-link path lands without revisiting the resolver.

**Files added:** `docs/help-manifest.json`, `packages/shell/scripts/build-help-corpus.mjs`, `packages/shell/help-corpus/corpus.json`, `packages/shell/src/main/help/help-corpus.ts` + `.test.ts`, `packages/shell/src/main/help/help-manifest-validator.test.ts`, `packages/shell/src/main/help/help-indexer.ts` + `.test.ts`, `packages/shell/src/renderer/help/{help,help-sidebar,help-searchbar,help-article}.tsx` + `help.css` + `use-help-route.ts` + `help.test.tsx`, `tests/visual/specs/help-smoke.spec.ts`.

## 2026-05-24 — 12.5 shell-half — RTL prep (logical CSS + `IconDirection.Inline` mirror + Playwright RTL smoke) (⚪ → 🟡; OQ-53 ✅)

The structural floor for right-to-left locales. Per [docs/platform/21-localization.md §242 "RTL is structural"](platform/21-localization.md) the v1 commitment is logical CSS everywhere + design-tokens that work in inline-start direction — this iteration lands the shell-side half of that commitment, leaves a deferred 12.5b slot for the apps-side CSS sweep, and resolves OQ-53 ("visual-regression vs runtime checks" — visual-regression on a shell smoke set wins).

**What landed.**

1. **Shell CSS swept to logical properties** — 29 rules across 13 files (`packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard.css`, `ui/toasts.css`, `ui/button.css`, `settings/{settings,sync-section,capability-prompt}.css`, `marketplace/marketplace.css`, `welcome/welcome.css`, `bin/bin.css`, `dashboard/{vault-switcher-popover,sync-status-chip,whats-new-release,icons-layer}.css`). `margin-left/-right` → `margin-inline-start/-end`; `padding-left/-right` → `padding-inline-start/-end` (or the `padding-inline:` shorthand where symmetric); `border-left/-right` → `border-inline-start/-end`; `text-align: left/right` → `text-align: start/end`; absolute-position `left/right: N` for inline-axis pinning → `inset-inline-start/-end: N` (or the `inset-inline: 0` shorthand for full-width pins). Each instance was read in context — sed-like blind swap would have miscarried the three platform-chrome reservations.

2. **Three platform-chrome lines KEPT physical with `PHYSICAL-AXIS INTENTIONAL` sentinel comments** in `dashboard.css`: macOS traffic-light inset (line 68), Windows window-controls inset (line 77), Linux WM-controls inset (line 85). OS-painted chrome doesn't mirror with the user's UI-locale direction (Apple HIG keeps traffic lights top-left in RTL macOS; same in Win/Linux), so these reservations would visually collide with the wrong chrome if we naïvely flipped them. The sentinel comments fence them so a future agent doing the 12.5b sweep doesn't "tidy" them. Same reasoning applies to `button.css` `left: 50%` + `translateX(-50%)` symmetric centring (the geometric centre is locale-invariant; both physical and logical pivots compute the same result for the centred-element case).

3. **`IconDirection` enum** on `@brainstorm/sdk/icon` (per [[feedback_enums_not_string_constants]]) — `Auto` (default, glyph stays bidirectional in both LTR + RTL) and `Inline` (glyph encodes inline-start ↔ inline-end direction and must mirror in RTL). New optional `direction?: IconDirection` prop on both:
   - the React `<Icon>` (`packages/sdk/src/icon/icon.tsx`) — stamps `data-icon-direction="inline"` on the rendered SVG (or `<svg>` shell for IconPack overrides) when `Inline`, omits the attribute otherwise.
   - the pure-DOM `createIconElement` twin (`packages/sdk/src/icon/create-icon-element.ts`) — sets `svg.dataset.iconDirection = "inline"` for the same case.
   Re-exported from `packages/sdk/src/icon/index.ts` so apps + the SDK can both reach it.

4. **Global RTL mirror rule** at two seams (shell renderer doesn't pull `app-theme.css`, sandboxed apps don't pull `styles.css` — both surfaces need their own copy):
   - `packages/shell/src/renderer/styles.css` — sits next to the existing `button { background: none; … }` UA-reset block.
   - `packages/sdk/src/app-theme.css` — sits just after the searchbar `@import` (the only allowed-before-first-rule position).
   Both install the identical `[dir="rtl"] [data-icon-direction="inline"] { transform: scaleX(-1); }`. Glyphs that don't carry inline-axis intent (Settings, Trash, Sun, Cube, …) are never stamped, so the rule scopes to inline-axis intent rather than all SVGs.

5. **Stamped at every directional-glyph call site**: `<NavButtons>` back/forward in `packages/sdk/src/nav-history/nav-buttons.tsx`, `createNavButtons` (pure-DOM twin) in `packages/sdk/src/nav-history/create-nav-buttons.ts`, `<FindBar>` prev/next match in `packages/sdk/src/find-replace/find-bar.tsx`. These are the only directional Phosphor glyphs in the SDK Icon registry today (`CaretLeft`/`CaretRight`); the shell Icon registry has none, so no shell call-site changes were needed.

**OQ-53 RESOLVED 2026-05-24** — visual-regression on a shell smoke set. `tests/visual/specs/rtl-shell-smoke.spec.ts` flips `<html dir="rtl">` on a freshly-launched, freshly-seeded shell **after** opening Settings, then asserts three structural invariants:
   - **Geometric mirroring of the Settings sidebar.** LTR baseline: `sidebar.left ≈ panel.left` (sidebar hugs inline-start = visual-left). After the flip: `sidebar.right ≈ panel.right` (sidebar hugs inline-start = visual-right in RTL) and `sidebar.left - panel.left > 50px` (sidebar is no longer flush against the panel's visual-left edge). This is the load-bearing proof that the `border-inline-start/-end` swaps actually behave as advertised — physical-property remnants would fail this fence.
   - **Computed transform on a stamped SVG.** Injects an SVG with `data-icon-direction="inline"` into the body and asserts `getComputedStyle(svg).transform === "matrix(-1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)"` (the resolved form of `scaleX(-1)`). A sibling SVG without the attribute resolves to `none` — the rule scope is correct (only stamped, inline-axis glyphs mirror; bidirectional glyphs stay identical).
   - **Structural survival.** `.settings__main` + `.settings__body` still render end-to-end after the flip — no overflow clipping or unmount regression. (We don't visual-diff per-pixel at v1; the geometry + computed-transform fences are the smoke set per OQ-53's tentative leaning. App-level visual diffs can be added in 12.5b if a regression slips.)

**Tests +6** on `packages/sdk/src/icon/icon.test.tsx` (was 8, now 14): default `<Icon>` omits the `data-icon-direction` attribute; `<Icon direction={IconDirection.Inline}>` stamps it to `"inline"`; `<Icon direction={IconDirection.Auto}>` does not stamp. Same three cases for the pure-DOM `createIconElement` twin (`dataset.iconDirection` undefined / `"inline"` / undefined). Plus the new Playwright spec on top.

**Build + test signals.** 14/14 icon suite (was 8), 83/83 across touched SDK suites (`packages/sdk/src/icon` + `nav-history` + `find-replace`), 239/239 across touched shell renderer suites (`packages/shell/src/renderer/ui` + `settings` + `dashboard`); `bun run typecheck` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean on touched files (4 latent format issues in unrelated CSS pre-existed on `main` and are not introduced by this iteration — confirmed via `git stash` round-trip: `dashboard/whats-new-release.css` font-family wrap, `dashboard/icons-layer.css` calc reflow, `sdk/app-theme.css` glass-class single-line preservation, `settings/settings.css` trailing newline — all latent, all out of this diff's footprint).

**Deferred to 12.5b** (apps-side CSS sweep, not blocking beta): the ~140 physical-axis CSS rules across `apps/*` stylesheets (`apps/notes/src/styles.css` 41, `calendar/src/styles.css` 23, `database/src/styles.css` 22, `files/src/styles.css` 14, `preview/src/styles.css` 9, `code-editor/src/styles.css` 9, `graph/src/styles.css` 7, `whiteboard/src/styles.css` 6, `tasks/src/styles.css` 5, `bookmarks/src/styles.css` 4, `journal/src/styles.css` 3) sweep to logical equivalents; apps-specific directional glyphs that should also stamp `IconDirection.Inline` (e.g. Journal's `setIcon(prev, JournalIcon.ChevronLeft)` day-stepper in `apps/journal/src/app.ts:535,548`). The contract (`IconDirection` enum + the `[dir="rtl"]` mirror rule in `app-theme.css`) is now in place — 12.5b is mechanical adoption. Two physical-axis lines (`margin-left` on line 1896 + `text-align: right` on line 2004) inside the **other agent's uncommitted 6.10f `.keyboard__*` block** in `settings.css` are explicitly out of scope here and will be picked up when that block lands.

## 2026-05-24 — 6.10f — platform-aware display + `Mod` round-trip (⚪ → ✅; closes 6.10 ladder)

Last rung of the 6.10 shortcut-hardening ladder. The display half was already plumbed by 6.10c/d/e (`formatChord(chord, mac)` consumed by `<Button shortcutId>` + cheatsheet + Settings → Keyboard). This iteration adds the round-trip half — a live rebinding surface that emits **`Mod`-tokenized canonical chords** so a binding made on macOS reads correctly on the same user's Windows install.

**What landed.** Five touch points.

1. **`packages/shell/src/renderer/shortcuts/chord-capture.ts`** — pure `captureChord(event) → { chord, isModifierOnly }`. Maps `event.code` (`KeyA`–`KeyZ`, `Digit0`–`Digit9`, `Numpad0`–`Numpad9`) for layout-invariance — a US `Cmd+K` rebound on AZERTY still records `Mod+K`. Semantic keys (`Enter`/`Escape`/`Tab`/`Backspace`/`Delete`/arrows/F-keys/`Space`) round-trip via `event.key`. Bare modifier presses return `isModifierOnly: true` so the capture surface stays armed. macOS `Cmd` (metaKey) maps to `Mod`; Windows/Linux `Ctrl` maps to `Mod`; the *other* primary modifier on the same platform stays distinct (`Ctrl` on macOS, `Meta` on Windows). Punctuation single-chars uppercase canonically. Multi-character non-semantic keys (`Process`, `Dead`) refuse rather than guess.

2. **`packages/shell/src/main/ipc/shortcuts-handlers.ts`** — privileged ipcMain surface (`shortcuts:list` / `shortcuts:set-override` / `shortcuts:reset-override` + push `shortcuts:bindings-changed`). Dashboard-only — apps already have the broker `shortcuts.register` for their own dynamic ids (6.10c); user-rebinding never goes through that channel because a sandboxed app rebinding shell chords on the user's behalf would be a privilege escalation. Defensive boundary rejects unknown ids, empty chords, bare-modifier chords (`Shift`/`Mod+Shift`), and conflicts (a different binding already using the same normalized chord) so a stale renderer can't end-run the renderer-side warning. Persists overrides into `brainstorm/ShortcutBindings/v1` via the existing `writeOverridesToEntity` path. **Fail-soft** — an entities.db write error logs but doesn't roll back the in-memory override (the session honours the user's intent per doc-24; the next successful write reconciles). New `SetOverrideErrorReason` enum (`UnknownId`/`NoRegistry`/`EmptyChord`/`BareModifier`/`Conflict`) — enums, not string constants, per [[feedback_enums_not_string_constants]].

3. **`packages/shell/src/preload/index.ts`** — `shortcuts` bridge mirroring the help/bin pattern (`list` / `setOverride` / `resetOverride` / `onBindingsChanged`). Result types re-declared at the preload boundary so the renderer never imports main code.

4. **`packages/shell/src/renderer/shortcuts/use-shortcut-bindings.ts`** — live snapshot hook (`useShortcutBindings()`). Fetches via the bridge on mount, re-fetches on every `shortcuts:bindings-changed` push, falls back to the renderer-side `defaultChordFor()` seed when no bridge is wired (cold-start / no-vault / stale-preload in dev). Exports `buildShortcutBindingsForTests()` so consumers exercise without a bridge.

5. **`packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/editable-chord.tsx`** — `<EditableChord>` interactive row + `KeyboardSection` rewrite. Three states — **idle** (chord tokens + Edit affordance + Reset chip when overridden + "Customized" pill), **capture** (capture target with `aria-label` + live keydown listener + conflict-aware Save / Cancel / Clear), **error** (the captured chord collides → surfaces the conflicting binding's translated label, disables Save, paints the capture frame red via `--color-state-error`). All chrome reads from design tokens — no hardcoded px / hex per [[feedback_use_design_system_not_ad_hoc]] + [[feedback_font_sizes_use_tokens]]; focus-outline rings replace borders (no sandwich, per [[feedback_focus_outline_replaces_border]]). Escape exits capture without staging. Bare-modifier press surfaces a quiet "Add a non-modifier key to finish the chord" hint, keeps the surface armed (matches `chord-capture.ts`'s `isModifierOnly`).

**Main-side wiring.** `packages/shell/src/main/index.ts` registers the new handler right before `registerBinHandlers` using the existing closure-over-`shortcutRegistry`/`getEntitiesRepoForActiveSession`/`dashboardWindow` pattern (the closures pick up the late-assigned registry at IPC time). `onVaultOpened` now pushes a final `shortcuts:bindings-changed` after `loadShortcutBindings()` + `loadInstalledAppShortcuts()` so the Settings panel + cheatsheet repaint when a vault opens with overrides — no manual refetch.

**Tests +56**:
- `chord-capture.test.ts` 19 (modifier-only presses; mac+pc Mod-tokenization grid; numpad-vs-digit distinction; macOS Ctrl as a separate modifier from Mod; semantic keys; punctuation; F-keys; IME refusal; round-trip with `normalizeChord` proving the macOS `Cmd+Shift+P` capture and Windows `Ctrl+Shift+P` capture both write `Mod+Shift+P` and both normalize equal to the doc-canonical `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+P`).
- `shortcuts-handlers.test.ts` 19 (channel registration; list payload contract; set-override happy path + persist into the entity row + broadcast; `null` = clear; Mod ↔ CmdOrCtrl normalize equivalence; unknown-id / empty / bare-modifier / conflict / malformed rejections; reset; broadcast skips on destroyed dashboard or no dashboard; fail-soft persistence with a throwing repo; null-repo path still lands the in-memory override + broadcasts).
- `editable-chord.test.tsx` 14 (find-conflict pure: normalize equivalence + null on no collision + self-exclusion + empty-chord; idle render + Reset visibility + Reset fires `onReset`; capture-mode mount + chord stage + Save fires `onSetOverride` with the Mod-tokenized chord; conflict disables Save + paints frame + surfaces conflicting label; bare-modifier keeps surface armed; Escape exits without staging; Clear sends null; Cancel returns to idle).
- `use-shortcut-bindings.test.tsx` 4 (seed fallback when no bridge; bridge resolution; re-fetch on `bindings-changed` push; `buildShortcutBindingsForTests` snapshot round-trip).

Plus a **Playwright spec** (`tests/visual/specs/keyboard-rebind.spec.ts`) exercising the real shell — IPC round-trip + conflict rejection + reset + capture-mode UI mount, both tests green on a freshly seeded vault (changelog popover dismissed via the existing `dashboard.setLastSeenChangelogVersion` bridge so the Settings click lands without interception).

Touched-suite green: chord-capture 19/19, shortcuts-handlers 19/19, editable-chord 14/14, use-shortcut-bindings 4/4. Full slice across renderer-shortcuts + renderer-settings + renderer-cheatsheet + main-shortcuts + shortcuts-handlers: **269/269**. Full main/ipc: **109/109**. Workspace `tsc:packages` + `typecheck:apps` clean; biome clean on touched files; shell build green.

**Closes 6.10.** The shortcut hardening ladder is complete — attach-at-create + layout-invariant matching (a), manifest→registry mirror with shell-collision rejection (b), dynamic IPC + cheatsheet aggregator (c), `<Button shortcutId>` + `aria-keyshortcuts` auto-stamp (d), cross-layer single-key suppression (e), and now the platform-aware display + `Mod` round-trip (f) — every promise the docs/24 keyboard contract made is now actually honoured by the registry/IPC/primitive layer. **Next on the shell row** (per [[feedback_serial_shell_then_apps]]): OpenRes-1c remaining slices (Privacy → Network egress panel — gated on Net-1, inline "Open with…", sticky app-vs-OS fork), Welcome-1/2, Help-1/2, App-lock surface 13.8.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.9c — soak harness fixes + boot instrumentation (⚪ → ✅; 10.9 + 10.9b stay 🟡)

Closes the three blockers the 10.9b smoke attempts surfaced on `main`. Five 15-minute attempts produced three real fixes that landed in `main` (harness argv `ee31b0c`, renderer Electron-inlining `66db417`+`b7c1ecb`) AND surfaced three defects 10.9c addresses here:

1. **Relay-cleanup race in `tests/soak/specs/10.9-ciphertext-only.spec.ts`.** The prior shape constructed the `RelayHandle` + both `LaunchResult`s OUTSIDE the `try`, so when `_electron.launch` threw (v3/v4/v5 all hit this), `finally` was never reached and the relay subprocess leaked across runs (v5 left PID 71905 behind). The fix declares `relay: RelayHandle | undefined` / `a: LaunchResult | undefined` / `b: LaunchResult | undefined` ABOVE the try, moves `launchRelay(...)` + both `launchShell(...)` calls INSIDE the try, and the `finally` block now `await a?.app.close().catch(() => {}) / b?.app.close().catch(() => {}) / relay?.stop().catch(() => {})` — every step is optional-chained on the handle, every step swallows its own errors so a teardown failure on one doesn't strand the others. Verified structurally in new `tests/soak/lib/launch-relay.test.ts` (5 vitest units): relay.stop runs when `_electron.launch` throws AFTER the relay is up; relay.stop runs on assertion failure inside the same try; relay.stop is NOT called when `launchRelay` itself throws (nothing to stop); relay.stop rejection does not mask the original assertion failure; happy-path teardown.

2. **Gate 4 made load-bearing in `tests/soak/lib/typing-load.ts`.** Previously the spec declared `keystrokeTimings: number[] = []` but `runTypingLoad` never wrote into it, so the spec computed `summarize(keystrokeTimings.length > 0 ? keystrokeTimings : [0]).median` — always `[0]` against a 17 ms budget = trivially `0 < 17`, the gate passed regardless of perf. The fix adds a required `keystrokeTimings: number[]` collector option (NOT optional — the spec MUST pass an array); `emitKeystroke` now wraps each `page.evaluate(... appendText ...)` in a `performance.now()` start/end pair and pushes the delta. The spec also fails-fast when `keystrokeTimings.length === 0` (`expect(keystrokeTimings.length, ...).toBeGreaterThan(0)`) rather than fall back to `[0]` — an empty series is itself a harness failure that should not be papered over. Verified in new `tests/soak/lib/typing-load.test.ts` (5 vitest units): pushes one elapsed-ms entry per successful appendText (length is non-zero, even, finite); two distinct caller-provided arrays do not share state; each elapsed value reflects the underlying evaluate delay (`ms >= delayMs - 1`); calls fire on both shellA and shellB each tick (|A - B| ≤ 1); canary text weaves into every 10th tick on both sides.

3. **Spec timeout raised 60 s → 300 s.** New `SHELL_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000` constant passed to both `launchShell({ timeoutMs })` and `firstWindow({ timeout })`. The v3/v4/v5 attempts hung at first-window creation; with the prior 60 s `_electron.launch` ceiling, a slow production cold-start was mis-classified as a hang — distinct from a real stall. The next attempt either succeeds outright (cold-start was simply slow on a stressed host) or stalls past 300 s — at which point the boot markers below pinpoint exactly where.

4. **Boot instrumentation in `packages/shell/src/main/index.ts`.** New module-level `BOOT_START = Date.now()` (captured at module load, after `__dirname` / `isDev` / `isMac` definitions) + `bootStage(stage: string)` helper that logs `[brainstorm/boot] <stage> <elapsed_ms>` through the existing `console.log` pipe (already wired into `attachWebContentsLogging` capture). Markers fire at eight load-bearing milestones between BOOT and dashboard window creation:
   - `[brainstorm/boot] vault-catalog-scanned <elapsed>` — inside `autoActivateDefaultVault`, immediately after `getDefaultVault().catch(...)` resolves (whether or not an entry exists).
   - `[brainstorm/boot] workers-spawned <elapsed>` — immediately after `workers = startWorkers(__dirname)` returns.
   - `[brainstorm/boot] auto-seed-{started,done,skipped} <elapsed>` — `started` fires once on entry to the `if (isDev && process.env.BRAINSTORM_AUTO_SEED !== "0")` branch; `done` fires once via a single `firstSeedDoneLogged` latch when the first `seedDemoApps` promise settles (success OR failure); `skipped` fires on the `else` branch (packaged build or `BRAINSTORM_AUTO_SEED=0`).
   - `[brainstorm/boot] vault-restored <elapsed>` — inside `autoActivateDefaultVault`, after the happy-path `activateVault(entry.id) + warmupLedger()`.
   - `[brainstorm/boot] vault-restored-none <elapsed>` — fires on the two no-restore paths (no default vault registered; restore threw + cleared the broken default).
   - `[brainstorm/boot] dashboard-window-creating <elapsed>` — immediately before `createDashboardWindow()` is called.
   - `[brainstorm/boot] dashboard-window-shown <elapsed>` — inside the dashboard window's `once("ready-to-show", ...)` listener.
   - `[brainstorm/boot] dashboard-renderer-domready <elapsed>` — `webContents.once("dom-ready", ...)` of the dashboard window.
   - `[brainstorm/boot] dashboard-renderer-paint <elapsed>` — `webContents.once("did-finish-load", ...)` of the dashboard window.

   The existing `BOOT shell-main marker=DEPLOYFIX-59069a1` log near the auto-seed branch stays in place; it now anchors the END of the synchronous setup (between auto-seed and dashboard-window-creating) rather than the start.

**No new default-grant capability.** All four fixes are harness-side or main-process logging only; no IPC surface, no broker service, no preload bridge change.

**Tests: +10 net** across 2 new files — `tests/soak/lib/launch-relay.test.ts` 5 + `tests/soak/lib/typing-load.test.ts` 5. Workspace `tsc:packages` is the same shape as baseline on touched files (the pre-existing `apps/*` and untouched-renderer errors are dep-resolution noise in this worktree, unchanged by 10.9c). Soak-tsconfig (`tests/soak/tsconfig.json`) clean. Biome clean on every touched + new file. Vitest `tests/soak/` 16/16 green (6 canary + 5 typing-load + 5 launch-relay).

**Status hand-off.** The receipt at `docs/_review/2026-05-23-10.9-g2-soak-smoke.md` records the five pre-10.9c attempts (v1 argv / v2 Electron-inlining / v3-v5 production cold-start hang). The next 10.9b soak run is manually triggered by the user and will either pass outright or stall at a specific `[brainstorm/boot] ...` milestone — at which point 10.9d fixes the underlying boot bug. 10.9 itself stays 🟡; 10.9b stays 🟡 until the formal 15-min smoke + 8 h soak both pass.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.9a — soak harness for the two-instance ciphertext-only E2E (⚪ → ✅, OQ-228/229/230/231/232/233 ✅; 10.9 itself stays 🟡 pending 10.9b run)

The fourth post-10.5 G2 slot ships the **harness** for the ciphertext-only soak. 10.9 splits into 10.9a (this iteration — harness only) and 10.9b (actually runs the three soak modes against the harness). The harness reuses the existing perf-harness primitives (`tests/perf/lib/launch-shell.ts`, `measure-paint`, `stats`) and stands up a parallel `tests/soak/` tree for the soak-specific helpers.

**Seven touch points.**

**1. `tests/soak/specs/10.9-ciphertext-only.spec.ts`** — the single Playwright spec. Three modes selected by `BS_SOAK_MIN=15|30|480` env var (default 15). Spawns a real `@brainstorm/relay-server` child via `launchRelay({auditLogPath})`, launches **two real `_electron.launch` shells** with isolated `--user-data-dir`s (NOT in-process — the in-process two-`VaultSession` proof already lives at `packages/shell/src/main/sync/new-device-join.test.ts`), pairs source→target via the existing `pairing.*` IPC bridge (`startAddDevice` → `scanPayload` → `confirmSas` on both sides — the bridge path, not the UI flow, since 10.5c's `pairing-live-e2e` already proves the UI), sets the same relay URL on both via `dev.setSyncRelay`, and runs `runTypingLoad({shellA, shellB, ...durationMs})` for the soak window. Asserts five binary gates: convergence (`compareStateVectors` returns `equal: true`), ciphertext-only (`searchCanariesInFile(auditLogPath, [CANARY_A, CANARY_B])` returns empty), no silent drops (audit count == sum of expected emits), perf floor (keystroke timing median <17ms — headroom over the 16ms editor budget for the encrypt+emit tax), memory slope (`regressionFromSamples(memSamples).slopeMbPerMinute < 1.0`).

**2. `playwright.soak.config.ts`** — repo-root soak Playwright config. `workers: 1`, `fullyParallel: false`, `retries: 0`, `timeout = max(2h, soakMinutes+30min in ms)` so the 8 h endurance mode bumps the ceiling inline rather than via a separate config. Reporter writes `tests/soak/results/<date>.json`; `outputDir: tests/soak/_artifacts`.

**3. `tests/soak/lib/launch-relay.ts`** — spawns `bun --bun --require <no-noble-probe.cjs> run packages/relay-server/bin/relay.ts --port <ephemeral> --audit-log-path <tmpfile>` via `node:child_process`. Waits for the port to be listening (TCP probe with 10 s deadline) before resolving, so the spec can immediately point shells at the relay URL. `stop()` SIGTERMs the child with a 2 s grace before SIGKILL — the `finally` block in the spec calls this even on assertion fail so the relay process never leaks across runs.

**4. `tests/soak/lib/canary-search.ts` + `canary-search.test.ts`** — pure `(auditLogPath, canaries) => CanaryMatch[]` scanner. Operates on raw `Uint8Array` so multibyte canaries survive any string-decode quirks; single linear scan via the `indexOfBytes` byte-needle search; handles overlapping matches by stepping from `at + 1` so duplicates are reported. **+6 vitest unit tests**: round-trip — finds a planted canary; false-positive resistance — random chunks don't match; hex-encoding edge case — string canary doesn't match its hex form (a separate fence the audit-log type-fence already enforces at compile time, this is just the runtime complement); multibyte canary (`üñîçødé-canary-Ω`) — UTF-8 sequences match byte-for-byte; empty log returns empty matches; large log (1 MB+) completes in <2 s.

**5. `tests/soak/lib/state-vector-compare.ts`** — exposes `getStateVector(page, entityId): Promise<Uint8Array>` + `compareStateVectors(pageA, pageB, entityId): Promise<{equal, hexA, hexB}>` so assertion failures print the divergence rather than an opaque byte mismatch. Calls into the renderer's `bs.dev.getStateVector` bridge (added below).

**6. `tests/soak/lib/typing-load.ts`** — keystroke-cadence generator. 5 Hz per side baseline (200ms per tick), every 10th tick emits the side's canary instead of a printable letter (so the canary lands ~once per 2 s of typing), every 30 s side A performs a structural edit (push onto a Y.Array, prune if >16 items). Drives writes through `bs.dev.appendText` / `bs.dev.structuralEdit` rather than reaching into the renderer's editor surface — keeps the harness deterministic and decoupled from each app's input handling.

**7. `tests/soak/lib/memory-sampler.ts`** — 60 s interval main-process RSS sampler via `ElectronApplication.evaluate(() => process.memoryUsage().rss)`. `regressionFromSamples(samples): MemoryRegression` does the linear least-squares fit and reports the slope in MB/min so the spec's threshold (`MEM_SLOPE_MB_PER_MIN = 1.0`) reads directly. Slope is on main-process RSS, not renderer V8 heap — main aggregates the storage worker + ydoc worker + broker, which is where a CRDT/sync leak would actually grow.

**Two infrastructure pieces** to make all of the above land cleanly:

**8. `tests/soak/lib/no-noble-probe.cjs`** — relay-process `--require` hook that patches `Module.prototype.require` to throw `RELAY_BLIND_VIOLATION` on any `@noble/*` resolve. CommonJS so it loads before any user module. The 12th structural CI fence at `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/relay-noble-import-check.ts` already enforces the same invariant **statically** on the relay-server source tree — this probe is the **runtime complement** so even if a dynamic / transitive edge slipped past the static scanner, the relay throws on first noble resolve. The audit log is already type-fenced against payload bytes at compile time (`packages/relay-server/src/audit-log.ts`); the canary grep is the third layer (defense-in-depth in three places: type-fence + canary-grep + no-noble-probe).

**9. `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/soak-handlers.ts`** — soak-only privileged IPC. Registered ONLY when `!app.isPackaged` AND `process.env.BRAINSTORM_SOAK_DEBUG === "1"`. Six handlers: `dev:soak:get-state-vector` (`Y.encodeStateVector(doc)` on a fresh load of the entity's `ydocStore` snapshot), `dev:soak:get-state-as-update`, `dev:soak:peek-entity-dek` (returns the entity's DEK bytes for the post-soak DEK-search defense-in-depth), `dev:soak:set-sync-relay` (calls `setSyncRelayConfig(vaultPath, ...)` so the harness wires the relay without going through Settings UI per OQ-232), `dev:soak:append-text` and `dev:soak:structural-edit` (mutate the Y.Doc on disk via `ydocStore.appendUpdate` AND emit through the encrypted wire path via `encryptAndEmit` against `getActiveRelay()?.currentPort()` so the relay child sees real ciphertext frames). The pipeline context is constructed inline; sequence numbers are tracked in-memory only for the soak run (the production `SeqTracker` wire-up is forward work per OQ-194's resolution — the soak counter starts at 0 each launch by design). Emit is best-effort: if `getActiveRelay()` returns null (vault has no `syncRelay` set), the local append still happens — keeps the harness usable for state-vector smoke without a relay. The crypto routing rule holds: `ed25519` verify goes through `verifySignature` from `main/credentials/identity.ts` (the only sanctioned entry point), no `@noble/*` import inside `ipc/`.

**Preload bridge.** `packages/shell/src/preload/index.ts` extends the existing `dev` object with `getStateVector` / `getStateAsUpdate` / `peekEntityDek` / `setSyncRelay` / `appendText` / `structuralEdit`. The renderer-side bridge is always exposed (matches the dev seeder + reseed bridge pattern); the main-process handler is what rejects in production. `Uint8Array` is sent over IPC as `number[]` (a `JSON.stringify`-safe shape) and reconstructed on the renderer.

**Scripts.** Root `package.json` adds `bun run soak` (chains `soak:build` + `playwright test --config=playwright.soak.config.ts`) and `bun run soak:build` (`@brainstorm/shell` build + `build:apps`). No relay-server build step needed — the CLI runs directly under Bun from source.

The harness deliverable is verified by: TS-compilation green (`bunx tsc --noEmit -p tests/soak/tsconfig.json`), workspace `tsc:packages` green, biome clean on every touched file, the 6 unit tests pass under vitest.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.8 — vault format frozen 1.0 + forward-only migration scaffold (⚪ → ✅, OQ-211/212/213/214/215/216/217 ✅)

The third post-10.5 G2 slot freezes the on-disk vault contract at `1.0` and ships the migration scaffold + the validation surface that future iterations will hang off. **Empty migration list at landing** by design — the freeze itself is the starting state; the runner, ordering invariant, on-disk preserve-and-write pattern, and backup-prompt seam all in place so the first real 1.0→1.1 migration is a content-only change.

**Five touch points + one new doc section.**

**1. `packages/shell/src/main/util/schema-version.ts`** — new `VaultFormatPreFreezeError` named error class + `assertVaultFormatNotPreFreeze(vaultFormat, minimumFormat)` guard. Refuses `< 1.0` with the explicit error class so the boot path fails-loud rather than guess at a migration shape that doesn't exist (there is no migration table that can carry a pre-freeze vault forward without ambiguity). Per OQ-215 the undocumented test-only env var `BRAINSTORM_ALLOW_PRE_FREEZE_VAULTS=1` downgrades the throw to a one-line `console.warn` so QA branches with long-lived pre-freeze test vaults stay openable. The existing `assertVaultFormatSupported` semantics changed: instead of rejecting any vault version strictly greater than the shell's supported format, it now compares **major-only** — `2.0` against `1.0` still throws `VaultFormatTooNew`, but `1.5` against `1.0` opens via preserve-and-ignore (the parsed JSON retains its unknown future-minor fields verbatim, the next atomic write keeps them intact). Major-version axis is reserved for wire-incompatible changes.

**2. `packages/shell/src/main/vault/vault-migrations.ts`** — new module owning the forward-only migration runner. `VaultMigration = {from, to, description, up}` shape; `VAULT_MIGRATIONS: readonly VaultMigration[] = []` (empty at 10.8); `migrateVaultToCurrent(vaultPath, parsedVaultJson)` walks the list, applies each matching `up`, rewrites `vault.json` per-step using a parse-mutate-stringify pattern that preserves unknown forward-compat keys verbatim (same shape `setSyncRelayConfig` / `rewriteVaultJsonAtRestMode` already use). Strict ordering invariant `assertVaultMigrationsOrdered` enforces both `compareDottedVersions(from, to) < 0` for every entry AND `previous.to === current.from` for every transition — a future list that skips a version (`1.0`→`1.1` then `1.2`→`1.3`) fails-loud at boot before any `up` runs. `promptBackupBeforeMigration(vaultPath, fromVersion, toVersion)` stub returns `true` immediately when `VAULT_MIGRATIONS` is empty (OQ-214 — the seam is in place so the first 1.0→1.1 migration activates the prompt as a single-file change). A throw from any `up` aborts the chain; partial progress (the format field at the previous step's `to` value) stays on disk so the next open re-enters the runner at the new step.

**3. `packages/shell/src/main/vault/vault.ts`** — `openVault` and `activateVault` both now call `assertVaultFormatNotPreFreeze` immediately after `assertVaultFormatSupported`, then `migrateVaultToCurrent` BEFORE the at-rest reconcile (no live session in flight, no IPC traffic, the migration runner has the file system to itself). The in-code constant `VAULT_FORMAT` (lived in `registry.ts`) renamed to `VAULT_FORMAT_VERSION = "1.0"` per the prompt's Option B: the on-disk `vault.json.format` field name is unchanged for backward compat — only the TS symbol moves so the constant name reflects what the value is (a freeze version).

**4. `packages/shell/src/main/vault/vault-validate.ts`** — new `validateVault(vaultPath, options): Promise<ValidationReport>` consistency checker. Per OQ-212 **warn-only at v1**, fire-and-forget after `openVault` succeeds (a freshly-broken vault stays openable in case the user wants to extract data before fixing). Six checks via `ValidationCheck` TS string enum (`EntityDekPresent` — every live entities.id has at least one entity_deks row, the 10.1 invariant; `EntityDekDangling` — every entity_deks.entity_id references an extant entity, the FK-row-stays-after-soft-delete case; `DeviceRecordsValid` — when `vault.json.syncRelay` is set, every signed add-device record on `brainstorm-VaultProperties`'s `meta.devices` Y.Array verifies via `verifyAddDeviceRecord`, an empty set is acceptable, the check **short-circuits** when `syncRelay` is absent so a local-only vault with no relay-side devices doesn't fire a noise warning; `SeqJsonReadable` — `<vault>/sync/seq.json` parses successfully or is absent, malformed JSON is non-fatal warning (the SeqTracker already tolerates corruption at runtime); `AtRestModeMatches` — re-uses `reconcileAtRestMode`'s four-outcome state machine (a recorded-encrypted vault opening into a plaintext driver can't reach this code path because `openVault` would have thrown; this check fires only on FirstStamp / UpgradeReady transitions); `OrphanYDocFile` — every `<id>.ydoc` under `<vault>/data/docs/<prefix>/` corresponds to a live or soft-deleted entities row, hard-deleted leftovers are flagged, the reserved vault-level doc ids `brainstorm-Dashboard` + `brainstorm-VaultProperties` are exempt by filename). `ValidationReport = {ok: boolean, warnings: ValidationWarning[]}`; each warning carries `{check: ValidationCheck, detail: string, fixable: boolean}`.

**5. `packages/shell/scripts/vault-validate.ts`** — new CLI surface per OQ-217 (CLI-only at v1; the IPC `shell.vault.validate` method lands when the Settings → Diagnostics pane is designed). Invoked as `bun --bun packages/shell/scripts/vault-validate.ts <vault-path>`; opens the vault's `entities.db` read-only, walks the docs dir, prints the report to stdout, exits 0 (warn-only per OQ-212).

**Fixture builders** — programmatic-fixture helpers in `packages/shell/src/main/vault/__fixtures__/build-vault.ts`: `freezeFixture` (canonical 1.0 baseline), `preFreezeFixture` (0.9), `futureMajorFixture` (2.0), `futureMinorFixture` (1.5), and `writeVaultJsonFixture(vaultPath, {override})` to materialise any shape on disk. No tarballs checked in — a freeze-shape change inside `vault.json` is caught by `tsc` here rather than via a stale fixture on disk.

**Doc** — `docs/foundations/28-vault-and-onboarding.md` adds a "Freeze surface inventory at 10.8" section enumerating every persisted shape covered by the 1.0 contract: (1) vault.json field table (required: `id`/`name`/`color`/`format`/`createdAt`; optional: `icon`/`identityPublicKey`/`identityFingerprint`/`credentialsBackend`/`atRestMode`/`syncRelay`) with explicit 2-space indent + trailing-newline convention. (2) Four SQLite DBs at `<vault>/data/<name>.db` with per-DB `_schema_version`; the per-DB schema bump is **not** a vault.json format bump per OQ-211 (componentVersions snapshot manifest rejected as churn-prone). (3) Yjs binary `'YDOC' || u32 version=1 || u32 snap_len || snapshot || (u32 update_len, update, u32 crc32(update))*` format. (4) Two reserved vault-level Y.Docs `brainstorm-Dashboard` + `brainstorm-VaultProperties`. (5) `<vault>/sync/seq.json` shape `{version, receive: {key → {highest, bitmapHex}}, send: {key → number}}`. (6) Attachments path-only reference (content-addressing owned by 9.10). (7) Per OQ-213 the per-app KV freeze covers only the path scheme + isolation invariants; per-app schemas evolve at the app's own pace. (8) Four keystore accounts `identity`/`master`/`device-x25519`/`device-ed25519` with naming `<vaultId>::<account>`; private keys never cross IPC. (9) Canonical-JSON ordering for signed add-device records (alphabetical, omit `sig` + `revokedAt`). (10) Explicit out-of-scope per OQ-216 for `apps/<app-id>/` bundle layouts + the relay-server audit log (both have their own contract owners).

**`SELECT *` audit pass** — swept across `packages/shell/src/main/storage/{entities,registry,ledger,search}-repo/*` + `main/capabilities/ledger.ts` looking for `SELECT *` in production code. Zero occurrences (only test files in `sqlite.test.ts` use the form). Forward-compat protection for future column-addition migrations holds — a future migration adding a column won't break a 1.0 reader's queries.

**OQ-211/212/213/214/215/216/217 confirmed RESOLVED** (filed pre-iteration in `3928be7`, no re-litigation): OQ-211 (componentVersions manifest rejected as churn-prone); OQ-212 (warn-only at v1; fire-and-forget after openVault); OQ-213 (per-app contract; freeze covers path + isolation only); OQ-214 (backup-on-migrate prompt seam in place; stub returns true when empty); OQ-215 (test-only undocumented env var); OQ-216 (app-bundle layout out of vault-format scope, app-install contract cross-referenced only); OQ-217 (CLI-only at v1; IPC method lands when Diagnostics pane is designed).

**No new default-grant capability** — the CLI is the only validate surface; IPC `shell.vault.validate` is forward iteration per OQ-217.

**Tests: +29 net** across 5 new test files + 2 modified.

- `packages/shell/src/main/vault/vault-migrations.test.ts` 15 — `VAULT_MIGRATIONS` empty-list contract + sorted; `assertVaultMigrationsOrdered` accepts empty list, accepts chained ordered list, rejects entry with non-strictly-greater `to`, rejects chain break (gap between previous.to and next.from), rejects backward (decreasing) entry; `migrateVaultToCurrent` returns `from === to === current` with empty applied[] on empty list, does NOT touch vault.json when no migrations apply, fails-loud when `format` is missing, fails-loud when `format` is non-string; with stub migrations: round-trip stub bumping format preserves unknown forward fields, idempotent re-run from current returns empty applied[], throw in `up` aborts chain with format at previous step; `promptBackupBeforeMigration` stub returns true when the list is empty.
