## 2026-05-23 — OpenRes-1c slice 4 — CR-1 sentinel routing fix + CR-2 prompt-host hardening (🟡 → 🟡, OQ-227 ✅)

The fourth OpenRes-1c slice closes both 🔴 beta-critical findings from `docs/_review/2026-05-23-iteration-bundle-findings.md`: CR-1 (the `__os__` sentinel-pin routing dropped on the floor in `dispatchExternalOpen`) and CR-2 (the unbounded `OsHandoffPromptHost.pending` Map with no dedup, no timeout, no cap). Three touch points + a sdk-types relocation + 10 tests.

**1. `packages/shell/src/main/intents/intents-bus.ts` — CR-1 sentinel routing.** When the user pinned "Open with system default" for a scheme/extension in Settings → Defaults (OpenRes-1c slice 2's surface), `defaultHandlers["open:scheme:https"]` stored the sentinel `OS_HANDOFF_APP_ID = "__os__"`. The next external `open` of that scheme hit `decideOpen` with `hasStoredDefault: true`, returned `OpenRung.StoredDefault`, the bus called `launchInto("__os__", ...)`, the orchestrator NotFound-threw, and the dispatch result was `handler-error` — the user's explicit OS pin **never reached `openExternal`**. Fix: the `OpenRung.StoredDefault` arm now branches on `storedDefaultAppId === OS_HANDOFF_APP_ID` and routes through a new `executeOsHandoff(target, uri)` helper — the shared chokepoint with the `OpenRung.OsHandoff` post-consent path. Skips the first-use prompt (the pin IS the consent) but respects a previously-Denied per-protocol consent ("never open in OS" beats a later "always open in OS" pin — clearing the pin in Settings is the one path to override Denied, not silent override). Dispatch result stamps `rung: OpenRung.OsHandoff` (NOT `StoredDefault`) so the slice-3 explainer surface reads "Opened with system default" rather than "Opened in __os__". The dangerous-scheme floor is unchanged: `decideOpen` short-circuits hard-block schemes to `Refused/DangerousScheme` before any rung resolution, so pinning OS for `javascript:` still refuses (regression-tested).

**2. `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/os-handoff-prompt.ts` — CR-2 hardening.** Three additions to the pure prompt host:

(a) **Per-signature dedup.** A second `request(signature, uri)` while one is in flight returns a promise that resolves to the same decision as the first call. The dashboard never sees two modals for one scheme; back-to-back link clicks resolve identically. Implementation: the in-memory state splits into two Maps — `bySignature: Map<string, Pending>` (the dedup key) and `byRequestId: Map<string, Pending>` (the reverse lookup `handleReply` needs). A `Pending` entry now carries `resolvers: Array<(decision) => void>` so a single dashboard reply / timeout / `setDashboard(null)` drain fans out to all waiting callers atomically — no closure-wrapping chain that could break under edge-case ordering.

(b) **60 s per-request timeout.** `PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` (OQ-227, 2026-05-23) — a wedged dashboard renderer can't leak resolve closures forever. `setTimeout` armed in `request()`, cleared in `handleReply` / `setDashboard(null)` drain / on its own firing. Timeout decision = `Cancel` (NOT `Deny` — preserves slice-1's "Cancel doesn't persist, re-prompts next time" invariant; the user's next attempt re-prompts cleanly).

(c) **Cap with newest-rejected.** `MAX_PENDING = 16` (OQ-227) — when the pending map is full, the incoming (newest) request resolves `Cancel` immediately rather than evicting an in-flight entry. Newest-rejected preserves the modal the user is actually looking at — evicting the visible one would lose user attention without recourse. Resolving (or timing out) a pending entry clears its slot so the next request succeeds normally.

**3. `packages/sdk-types/src/open-resolution.ts` — sentinel relocation.** `OS_HANDOFF_APP_ID = "__os__"` and `OS_HANDOFF_APP_LABEL = "Open with system default"` moved here from `defaults-catalog.ts`. The sentinel is part of the open-resolution contract (the IntentsBus reads it on every external `open` to decide whether to short-circuit to OS handoff) — not a defaults-catalog detail. `intents-bus.ts` imports the sentinel from `@brainstorm/sdk-types` directly. `defaults-catalog.ts` re-exports both for backward-compat (`export { OS_HANDOFF_APP_ID }`, `export { OS_HANDOFF_APP_LABEL }`) so any code that currently imports from the catalog keeps working — zero migration churn.

**OQ-227 RESOLVED 2026-05-23** (filed pre-iteration, pinned during the slice): `PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` + `MAX_PENDING = 16` + newest-rejected on overflow. 60 s is long enough that a deliberating user never hits it, short enough that a wedged dashboard renderer frees memory on the same scale as a tab reload. 16 is comfortably above any realistic concurrent open burst (launcher rate-limit is far tighter), bounded so a misbehaving caller can't OOM the resolver. Tune from soak data if the prompt becomes a hot path.

**No new default-grant capability.** The OS-handoff resolution path's capabilities (`system.open-external` for app callers; implicit grant for shell-source clicks) are unchanged from OpenRes-1b. CR-1 closes a *missing* path through an existing chokepoint, not a new one.

**Tests +10 across two files.** `intents-bus.test.ts` 44 → 48 (+4 new in a new `describe("IntentsBus — \`__os__\` sentinel pin routes through OS handoff")` block): (1) sentinel pin + granted consent → `openExternal` called once, `result.handled === true`, `result.rung === OsHandoff`, orchestrator NEVER called with the sentinel; (2) sentinel pin + denied consent → explained refusal, no `openExternal`, "blocked" message + `rung: OsHandoff`; (3) sentinel pin + no `openExternal` injected → fail-closed at the chokepoint ("OS handoff unavailable"), orchestrator still never called with the sentinel (the dangerous-stuck loop is the regression); (4) sentinel pin + `javascript:alert(1)` → `Refused/DangerousScheme` — no security bypass through the sentinel branch (the floor is in `decideOpen` before any rung resolution, but the regression test pins the property).

`os-handoff-prompt.test.ts` 7 → 13 (+6 new across three new `describe` blocks: dedup, timeout, cap): (1) per-signature dedup returns the same promise to both callers + dashboard sees one prompt; (2) sequential same-signature requests mint a fresh prompt after the first resolves; (3) 60 s fake-timer → Cancel; (4) reply before timeout disarms the timer (no double-resolution past 60 s); (5) cap rejects the newest request with Cancel when full + the in-flight 16 are untouched; (6) resolved entry frees its slot so the next request (distinct signature) succeeds normally. The existing "each `request` mints a unique requestId" test updated to use distinct signatures (same-signature requests now dedup by design — that's the contract).

**Workspace `tsc:packages` clean.** Biome clean on every touched file. `intents-bus.test.ts` 48/48, `os-handoff-prompt.test.ts` 13/13, `defaults-catalog.test.ts` 14/14 (sentinel-via-sdk-types re-export round-trips), `sdk-types` 206/206. A pre-existing typecheck error in `apps/code-editor/src/ui/code-pane.test.ts` (the `ObjectMenuContext` shape — unrelated 8.x refactor by parallel work) reproduces on the base branch with empty intersection to this iteration.

**Parallel-agent note.** The Stage 10.8 (vault format freeze) builder is running concurrently on a sibling branch; its code surface (vault.ts / vault-migrations / vault-validate / SQL-repos) has zero overlap with this slice's intents-bus + os-handoff-prompt + sdk-types open-resolution surfaces. The only file overlap is docs (plan.md / table.md / log.md / OQ.md); this iteration's entries are additive (new OQ-227 entry, new "Recent landings" entry, new "Open resolution" slice-4 marker) so the integrator can fast-forward both branches cleanly.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.7 — sync-status surface (⚪ → ✅, OQ-206/207/208/209/210 ✅)

The second post-10.5 G2 slot ships the live sync-state surface — dashboard chip + Settings → Sync drill-down — backed by a `SyncStatusStore` that aggregates `ActiveRelayOrchestrator` transport state, pipeline traffic ticks, `WebSocketRelayPort` drop counters, and persisted seq-tracker diagnostics. Five touch points.

**1. `packages/shell/src/main/sync/sync-status-store.ts`** — new `SyncStatusStore`. `SyncState` TS string enum (`LocalOnly`/`Syncing`/`Stale`/`Offline`/`Error`). State derivation is split — main handles `LocalOnly`/`Offline`/`Error` (transport-state shaped), the renderer derives `Syncing`/`Stale` against `Date.now()` against the `RECENT_TRAFFIC_MS = 5_000` / `STALE_AFTER_MS = 30_000` thresholds (OQ-208). The split keeps the renderer cheap (one shared 5s `setInterval` to re-derive Stale) and the main store timer-free for that axis. Per OQ-209 transient transport-Error folds into Offline for the first 1 second (`ERROR_STICKY_MS`), only paints Error if it lingers past the threshold; the orchestrator's state-event is observed via `activeRelay.on("state", …)`, an Error edge starts a 1-second sticky timer, expiring re-emits an immediate state-edge change so the chip flips Offline→Error without the user lifting a finger. Debounce: traffic ticks coalesce on a 500ms trailing timer; state-edges (transport transitions, vault-session swap, Error-sticky elapse) bypass debounce + fire immediately so the chip paints Offline the moment the wire drops. Snapshot shape: `state`, `transportState`, `relayUrl`, `connectionId` (null at v1; reserved), `lastInboundAtMs`, `lastOutboundAtMs`, `droppedSends`, `droppedInbound`, `seqStateBytes`, `pairKeyCount`. Privacy negative pin: the snapshot exposes only `seqStateBytes` + `pairKeyCount`, **never** the raw `(sender, entityId)` pair keys — sender pubkey is a device fingerprint, asserted by test (snapshot shape is exhaustively enumerated; no `pairs` / `senders` / `pairKeys` field).

**2. `packages/shell/src/main/sync/envelope-pipeline.ts`** — extended `PipelineContext` with optional `onSent?(frameBytes)` / `onReceived?(frameBytes)` callbacks. Wired in all six paths: `encryptAndEmit` / `emitWrapBootstrap` / `emitAwareness` fire `onSent` after a successful `relay.send(wire)`; `receiveAndApply` / `receiveWrapBootstrap` / `receiveAwareness` fire `onReceived` after a successful inner apply (`applyUpdate` / `onWrapAccepted` / `onAwarenessUpdate`). **Do NOT fire on throw paths** — revoked / EntityIdMismatch / sig-fail envelopes don't count as inbound traffic; existing `droppedInbound` counter on the transport surfaces those separately. Defaults are no-op so the dozens of existing pipeline test sites stay green without churn.

**3. `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/sync-status-handlers.ts`** — new `sync-status:snapshot` invoke channel + push channel; `registerSyncStatusHandlers({getDashboard, syncStatusStore})` mirrors `pairing:*` / `files-handles:*` pattern. The IPC handler is registered exactly once (the `ipcMain.handle` call is idempotency-guarded); the change-listener wire is rebindable so a session-switch + re-register swaps cleanly without double-pushing.

**4. `packages/shell/src/preload/index.ts`** — `window.brainstorm.syncStatus.{snapshot, on}` privileged dashboard bridge; `SyncState` + `SyncTransportState` re-exported as runtime enums. Apps don't see this surface — OQ-206 deferred app-side `sync.status:read` cap to v2 (apps see freshness indirectly via `entities` row `updated_at`).

**5. Renderer** — new `useSyncStatus()` hook (`packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard/use-sync-status.ts`) with a shared ~5s `setInterval` to re-derive `Stale` against `Date.now()`; pure `deriveSyncState(snap, now)` helper for tests. New `<SyncStatusChip>` (`packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard/sync-status-chip.tsx`) mounted in the dashboard header (icon + 1-word state label, `aria-live="polite"`, click opens popover) with OQ-210 quiet styling for `LocalOnly` (dim icon, no badge, but still visible for discoverability — the surface stays available before the user pairs a device). New `<SyncStatusPopover>` (quick read: relay host-only, relative-age `2s ago`/`3m ago`/`1h ago` inbound/outbound, dropped-sends row only when nonzero, seq diagnostic count + bytes; the LocalOnly variant hides the traffic rows entirely + shows "No relay configured"). New `<SyncSection>` Settings drill-down (full relay URL — clipped via the shared text-clamp pattern, transport-state, both dropped counters always shown including zero, seq diagnostic). `IconName.Cloud` + `IconName.CloudSlash` added to the registry; ~30 new i18n keys under `shell.dashboard.syncStatus.*` + `shell.settings.sync.*`. The chip + section consume `derivedState` from the hook, not `snapshot.state`, so the renderer-side stale flip actually applies.

**Main-side wiring** — `main/index.ts` lazy-imports `SyncStatusStore` after `installActiveRelay` runs so the singleton orchestrator is guaranteed installed; `registerSyncStatusHandlers` starts the store on register; `onActiveVaultSessionChanged` fires `notifyVaultSessionChanged()` which bypasses the 500ms coalesce timer + resets traffic counters so the chip paints LocalOnly/Offline shape immediately on vault open/close.

**OQ-206/207/208/209/210 confirmed RESOLVED** (filed pre-iteration, no re-litigation): OQ-206 (defer app-side cap to v2; apps see freshness via `entities` row `updated_at`), OQ-207 (aggregate-only at v1 — single-vault → single-transport → all entities share the wire state; per-entity drilldown deferred post-G2), OQ-208 (`STALE_AFTER_MS = 30_000`, configurable for soak tuning at 10.9), OQ-209 (Error sticky > 1 second; otherwise fold into Offline so transient reconnect noise doesn't look alarmist — the 500 ms traffic-tick debounce is one layer + the 1-second linger threshold is the second), OQ-210 (LocalOnly shown quietly, never hidden — a "Local only" pill is discoverability for users who later pair a device; quiet = subtle styling not a hidden state).

**No new default-grant capability.** The sync-status surface is shell-privileged: no broker route, no `sync.status:read` cap (deferred per OQ-206).

## 2026-05-23 — 10.6 — awareness encrypted under entity DEK, transient (⚪ → ✅, OQ-204/205 ✅)

The first post-10.5 G2 slot ships transient presence (cursor / selection / "alice is here") over the same blind relay as Yjs updates — same per-entity DEK, same XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, same Ed25519 sig-then-AEAD order, but a new `WireKind.Awareness` discriminator, an explicit kind guard on both seal and open, and a deliberate **skip** of the per-`(sender, entityId)` seq-tracker (y-protocols' `Awareness` clock-based dedup keyed on `clientID` is sufficient; routing awareness through the seq-tracker would (a) eat the counter on a class of frames it can't meaningfully reject and (b) tangle the awareness-frame lifetime with the Yjs-update frame lifetime in a way 10.7's sync-status surface would have to undo).

**Five touch points.**

(1) `packages/shell/src/main/sync/routing-header.ts` + `packages/relay-server/src/wire.ts` — added `Awareness = "awareness"` to both `WireKind` TS string enums. The relay's strict header-shape validator now routes awareness frames identically to entity frames (one-line enum addition on the relay side; the audit-log records `kind=awareness` so 10.9's ciphertext-only proof has a clean discriminator alongside `update` / `wrap-bootstrap` / `pairing`). The existing canonical-order property test in `routing-header.test.ts` auto-covers the new kind — no test churn needed.

(2) `packages/shell/src/main/sync/envelope-seal.ts` — new `sealAwarenessEnvelope` + `openAwarenessEnvelope` sibling to the Update / WrapBootstrap pairs. Same XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD under entity DEK as `sealUpdateEnvelope`, same AAD = `canonicalizeRoutingHeader(header)`, same Ed25519 sig-over-`canonicalHeaderBytes || ciphertext`. The defense-in-depth order on open mirrors `openUpdateEnvelope` AND adds the explicit kind guard the WrapBootstrap path already uses: (i) `header.kind === Awareness` first (refuse a sender that signed an Update header but routes it through this path), (ii) `frame.header.entityId === resolvedEntityId` (the 10.1/10.2/10.3a forward contract — no AEAD call before the row match), (iii) Ed25519 verify the signature over `canonicalHeaderBytes || ciphertext`, (iv) AEAD open with AAD = re-canonicalised header bytes. The seal layer accepts an empty payload — the dispose-broadcasts-`state=null` path emits a short awareness update whose encoded body has no minimum length.

(3) `packages/shell/src/main/sync/envelope-pipeline.ts` — new `emitAwareness(entityId, awarenessUpdate, ctx)` + `receiveAwareness(frame, ctx, onAwarenessUpdate)`. The emit path is structurally identical to `encryptAndEmit`: opens the DEK from `EntityDekStore`, mints a random 24-byte XChaCha nonce, builds the routing header with `kind=Awareness` + `seq=ctx.nextSeq(entityId)` (the seq is monotonic for **header debugging only** — the audit log + 10.7's sync-status panel see `seq=N` alongside Update frames, but the receive path deliberately does NOT call `seqTracker.accept`), seals via `sealAwarenessEnvelope`, sends through the relay, zeroes the DEK in `finally`. The receive path mirrors `receiveAndApply`: `decodeFrame` → `header.kind === Awareness` guard → `ctx.resolveEntity(...)` → `Unavailable` if not found → consult `ctx.isDeviceRevoked` **BEFORE** sig-verify (the 10.5c cheap path — a revoked-device awareness frame drops without touching the crypto layer) → open DEK keyed by the **resolved row id** (not the header-supplied id) → AEAD-open → hand plaintext awareness-update bytes + resolved entity id to the callback (the caller is the broadcaster, which feeds the bytes into `applyAwarenessUpdate(awareness, ...)`). DEK zeroed in `finally` even on parse/verify/decrypt error.

(4) `packages/shell/src/main/sync/awareness-broadcaster.ts` — new `AwarenessBroadcaster` class. Sender-side wrapper that owns per-entity `Awareness` instance pointers via a `() => Map<string, Awareness>` getter (so the broadcaster can refresh its registry across entity-doc lifecycle changes — entity docs come and go as apps mount/unmount), subscribes to `awareness.on('update', ...)` for outbound emission, and applies inbound updates via `applyAwarenessUpdate` with a unique-symbol `RemoteOrigin` marker so the same `update` listener that fans outbound emissions doesn't re-broadcast received frames in a tight loop. **OQ-204 invariants** wired exactly:
  - **50 ms trailing debounce per entity** (`AWARENESS_DEBOUNCE_MS`). Multiple `setLocalState` calls within the window batch into a single `encodeAwarenessUpdate(awareness, [clientIds...])` call → one envelope. A per-entity `Map<entityId, NodeJS.Timeout>` resets on each `update` event; on fire, the accumulated `(added, updated, removed)` clientID set goes into one encode-and-emit.
  - **~15 s heartbeat per entity** (`AWARENESS_HEARTBEAT_MS` = `outdatedTimeout / 2` = 15000 ms). A per-entity `setInterval` emits the current local state (under the local clientID) so peers refresh their `lastUpdated` and don't garbage-collect us at `outdatedTimeout = 30000 ms`. The y-protocols `Awareness` class already does an internal `_checkInterval` at 3s cadence that re-`setLocalState`s when local `lastUpdated > 15s` old — the broadcaster's explicit heartbeat is belt-and-suspenders: it ensures a peer receives our liveness signal even if our internal interval happens to coincide with a frame-drop on the relay.
  - **`setLocalState` is NEVER throttled.** Local `Awareness` always reflects the latest local cursor immediately; only the outbound envelope is rate-limited. Throttling `setLocalState` would break Yjs's clock invariant (the clock advances monotonically on every call; skipping one drops a tick and a future peer reconciliation would silently lose the update).
  - **`untrack(entityId)` AND `dispose()`** both broadcast a `state=null` update for the local clientID with bumped clock so peers cleanly drop our presence instead of waiting `outdatedTimeout = 30s`. Implementation: bump `awareness.meta.set(localId, {clock: prev+1, lastUpdated: now})`, then `encodeAwarenessUpdate(awareness, [localId], emptyStatesMap)` — y-protocols' `encodeAwarenessUpdate` reads state via `states.get(clientID) || null`, so an empty `states` map encodes the local state as null.
  - **DEK-missing graceful degradation.** If the outbound `emitAwareness` rejects with `Unavailable` (the entity has no DEK locally — possible during a 10.x retro-wrap miss), the broadcaster routes the error through `onEmitError` (default = `console.warn`). Awareness loss is non-fatal — the local `Awareness` continues to render local cursors; we just can't share them until the DEK lands. The local awareness state is **never** rolled back on a failed emit.
  - **Inbound `applyAwarenessUpdate` clock dedup** is y-protocols' responsibility. A stale frame (lower clock) is silently no-op'd by `applyAwarenessUpdate` itself; the broadcaster does not second-guess it.

(5) `packages/shell/package.json` — `y-protocols: "^1.0.6"` added as a direct shell dep. The editor package already had it transitively (`packages/editor/src/local-provider.ts`'s `Awareness` import); the 10.6 broadcaster lives in main-process code so the shell needs an explicit declaration.

**OQ-204 + OQ-205 confirmed RESOLVED** (filed pre-iteration; no re-litigation):
- **OQ-204 (awareness debounce default)**: 50 ms trailing debounce for user-driven updates (~20 Hz outbound), ~15 s heartbeat-only refresh rate (matches y-protocols `outdatedTimeout / 2`). Implementation lives in the broadcaster's `update` listener, never in `setLocalState` itself.
- **OQ-205 (future `entities.read.noPresence:<type>` capability)**: piggyback on `entities.read:<type>` at v1. Awareness is metadata *about* an entity (who's looking, where their cursor is); if an app already gets the plaintext entity bytes, awareness state is strictly less sensitive. A separate `sync.awareness:<type>` capability would force every Notes/Tasks/etc. manifest to declare a redundant cap and create incoherent product states ("app has read but not awareness"). The `entities.read` check the shell already does for the entity body covers awareness. Revisit only if a v2 "awareness-blind viewer app" cap proves coherent.

**No new default-grant capability.** Awareness rides the existing `entities.read:<type>` envelope.

**Tests: +19 net across 2 new files + 1 modified.**
- `packages/shell/src/main/sync/awareness-envelope.test.ts` — **9 tests**. Seal/open round-trip yields the original awareness-update bytes verbatim · seal refuses `Update` / `WrapBootstrap` / `Pairing` kinds (rejects all three in a single test loop) · open refuses non-Awareness header (caller cannot route an Update through this path) · `EntityIdMismatch` before verify when routed id != resolved id · sig verification fails before AEAD is invoked (spies on `dek` via a `Proxy` that throws on any property access — the test fails LOUDLY if AEAD-open is ever reached after sig-failure) · nonce length check rejects sub-24-byte nonces · AAD-pin: mutating `header.seq` after seal breaks open even with a verify-always spy · empty payload allowed (dispose-broadcasts-null case) · a frame claiming `kind=Awareness` with bogus inner bytes still round-trips at the seal layer (the seal layer guards crypto invariants; what's inside the plaintext is the y-protocols parser's concern).
- `packages/shell/src/main/sync/awareness-broadcaster.test.ts` — **9 tests**. Multiple `setLocalState` within the debounce window batch into one envelope · distinct entities maintain separate debounce timers · heartbeat fires at ~15s cadence even without state changes (fake timers advance `AWARENESS_HEARTBEAT_MS + 50`) · inbound `applyAwarenessUpdate` updates the local `Awareness.states` map without re-broadcast loop (the `RemoteOrigin` symbol marker suppresses the listener) · `dispose()` broadcasts a `state=null` update for each tracked entity (one envelope per entity, identified by entityId in `emit.mock.calls`) · stale inbound (lower clock) drops with no observable state change (apply newer then older — newer wins, older is no-op) · DEK-missing emit error routes to `onEmitError`; local `Awareness` keeps updating (the local state is untouched after the failed emit) · `untrack`-then-`retrack` rebuilds subscriptions cleanly (untrack broadcasts one null envelope, subsequent setLocalState on the un-tracked Awareness emits nothing, retrack with a fresh Awareness wires the new subscription) · `applyInbound` drops silently when the entity isn't tracked locally.
- `packages/shell/src/main/sync/new-device-join.test.ts` — **+1 test** (the new "awareness round-trips encrypted under the entity DEK" assertion). Two full `VaultSession`s; A1 mints DEK on a real `EntityDekStore` + B installs it via `wrapDekForRecipient` + `unwrapMemberWrap` + `EntityDeksRepository.create` (same install path as the existing 10.3b new-device-join demo). A1 builds an `AwarenessBroadcaster` tracking a local `Awareness`; B builds a receive-only broadcaster that wires its `applyInbound` to incoming frames via `receiveAwareness`. A1 calls `awarenessA.setLocalState({cursorLine: 42, user: "alice-the-canary"})`; after one debounce window (`AWARENESS_DEBOUNCE_MS + 30 ms`) B's `Awareness.getStates()` contains A1's clientID with the same `{cursorLine: 42, user: "alice-the-canary"}` payload — proves the full encrypt → relay → decrypt → apply path. The relay-observed frame body MUST NOT contain the plaintext canary "alice-the-canary" OR the field name "cursorLine" (ciphertext-only invariant on the awareness path, extending the existing 10.3b canary test that covered the Update path). Then A1's broadcaster `.dispose()` fires; after a microtask flush B's `Awareness.states.has(awarenessA.clientID) === false` — proves the dispose-broadcasts-null contract end-to-end.

**Workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean; biome clean on every new + touched file.** Vitest **packages/shell 2034/2034 green** when run in isolation (138 sync + 71 pairing + 81 vault + the rest); **`packages/relay-server` 22/22 green** (the new `WireKind.Awareness` enum entry on the relay side passes its existing strict-header-kind validator tests — the strict validator's `KIND_SET = new Set(Object.values(WireKind))` automatically accepts every enum member); **the 12th structural CI fence stays green** (`awareness-broadcaster.ts` is NOT a relay file — out of the `**/sync/**/*relay*.ts` scope of the fence; AND it contains zero `@noble/*` / credentials / envelope-seal imports anyway, so even if the fence were extended to scan it the audit would pass).

**Scope check vs the iteration prompt.**
- A. `WireKind.Awareness` (new entry) on both files ✅
- B. Seal/open primitives (`sealAwarenessEnvelope` + `openAwarenessEnvelope` with kind guard on seal AND open, same EntityIdMismatch-before-verify-before-AEAD order, AAD = canonical-routing-header bytes) ✅
- C. Pipeline orchestrator (`emitAwareness` + `receiveAwareness`, deliberately skipping `seqTracker.accept`, revoke-check before sig-verify, DEK zeroed in `finally`) ✅

**Decisions beyond the prompt.**
- Bundled the three E.3 new-device-join assertions into one `it` block instead of three. The setup cost (`VaultSession.create` + DEK install + broadcaster wiring) is ~2-3 seconds; running it three times tripled the test runtime for no separation-of-concerns benefit. The single combined test asserts all three contracts (round-trip apply, ciphertext-only canary, dispose-null cleanup) in sequence on the same harness. Net delivered tests = 19 (vs ~20 target); the broadcaster test file already covers each of the three sub-contracts in isolation against an in-memory `Awareness`.
- Used a `Proxy`-wrapped DEK in the "sig fails before AEAD" envelope test so the test fails LOUDLY (with a thrown error naming the property accessed) if AEAD-open is ever reached after sig-failure, rather than just asserting "the verify spy was called once". The Proxy approach extends the existing `verifyCallCount === 0`-style cheap-path proof from 10.5c.
- The dispose-broadcasts-null path mutates `awareness.meta` directly (bumps the local clientID's clock + lastUpdated) rather than calling `awareness.setLocalState(null)`. Rationale: `setLocalState(null)` *also* fires an `update` event with origin=`'local'`, which would be picked up by our own `update` listener and add the local clientID to the pending set just before we tear down. Mutating meta + calling `encodeAwarenessUpdate` directly emits one clean null-state envelope per entity, no listener-loop side effects.
- The broadcaster uses a unique-symbol `RemoteOrigin` (not a string) as the origin marker for `applyAwarenessUpdate`. Reference-identity match is robust against string-typo bugs (a future contributor copy-pasting `'remote'` as the origin elsewhere can't accidentally re-suppress the listener).
- Used a `() => Map<string, Awareness>` getter for `awarenessByEntity` instead of a static map. Awareness instances come and go across entity-doc lifecycle changes; passing a getter means the broadcaster always reads the live map without needing a separate register/unregister API.

**Anything not landed.**
- The renderer / app-host wire-up that connects each opened entity's `Awareness` to a singleton `AwarenessBroadcaster` is out-of-scope (this iteration ships the primitives; the wiring at the app-renderer boundary is a 10.6.1 / app-by-app follow-on that pairs with the editor binding work in 9.3.5 / B6).
- The shell-side `AwarenessBroadcaster` singleton + per-app cap check (`entities.read:<type>` per OQ-205) is also a follow-on — this iteration ships the broadcaster class; the broker registration + cap check + dashboard surface are 10.7's sync-status work + a 10.6.1 wiring slot.
- Awareness frames do not currently appear in the 10.7 sync-status surface (the panel is itself still ⚪). When 10.7 lands, the audit log's `kind=awareness` discriminator is already in place — no further wire-format work is needed.
- The `meta.devices` cross-device sync (so revokes made on A flip B's `isRevoked` predicate on B's end) remains the same `10.6+` follow-on noted in 10.5c's log; awareness frames from a revoked sender on A would only drop on A's side, not on B's, until that wiring lands.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.5c — live wire-up + revoke (⚪ → ✅, OQ-203 ✅, 10.5 trio complete)

The third and final 10.5 slot closes the loop. `setActiveVaultSession` now boots the live transport from `vault.json.syncRelay` via a new `ActiveRelayOrchestrator`; the QR pairing handshake completes end-to-end over the live relay; `meta.devices.revoke()` is enforced both at the verifier (sig-drop **BEFORE** sig-verify) AND on outbound wraps (wrap-skip on revoked devices), per OQ-203's "both" resolution.

**Three new modules + five touched.**

(1) `packages/shell/src/main/sync/active-relay.ts` — new `ActiveRelayOrchestrator` class. Single source of truth for the live transport's lifecycle. Relay-blind (matches the 12th-fence `**/sync/**/*relay*.ts` pattern; the fence's existing 21/21 tests still pass — `active-relay.ts` has zero `@noble/*` / credentials / envelope-seal imports). `onSessionChanged(session | null)` reads `vault.json.syncRelay` (via the injectable `readSyncRelayUrl` for tests) — absent ⇒ loopback (`LoopbackRelayPort.pair(1)` mints a single-port bus); present ⇒ `WebSocketRelayPort({url})` + `port.connect()`. The previous port (if any) is closed cleanly; subscriptions + frame listeners migrate to the replacement **BEFORE** the old port closes, so an inflight frame never slips through a listener-less gap. `reconfigure()` re-reads vault.json after a `setSyncRelayConfig` mutation and rebuilds the port — but only when the resolved transport actually changes (same `{kind, url}` ⇒ no port flap, no port build cost). Concurrent rebuilds are serialized so two rapid session changes don't race on the close/open sequence. `state(): {kind, port, syncRelayUrl?}` + a `state` event emitter feed 10.7's future sync-status panel. `dispose()` is idempotent. Module-level singleton via `installActiveRelay` / `getActiveRelay` / `disposeActiveRelay` — installed once in `main/index.ts` before `registerPairingHandlers` (the pairing handlers read the singleton on every IPC call). The `ActiveRelayKind` TS string enum (`Loopback` / `WebSocket`) avoids the string-literal-discriminator anti-pattern per CLAUDE.md.

(2) `packages/shell/src/main/pairing/pairing-frame.ts` — new pairing wire-frame codec. The outer wrapping matches `envelope-codec.ts` byte-for-byte (`u32-be(headerLen) || headerBytes || u16-be(sigLen=64) || sig || u32-be(bodyLen) || body`) so the relay's `peekRoutingHeader` routes a pairing frame identically to any other entity frame — no extra branches in the routing path. New `WireKind.Pairing` added to both `packages/shell/src/main/sync/routing-header.ts` AND `packages/relay-server/src/wire.ts` so the relay's strict header-shape validator accepts the new kind (without it the relay would have dropped pairing frames as malformed). Two JSON body shapes — `PairingFrameType.JoinRequest` (target → source: `deviceEd25519Pub` + `deviceX25519Pub` + `deviceLabel`, all base64url-encoded) and `PairingFrameType.SealedIdentity` (source → target: the `SealedSecret` JSON base64-wrapped + `sourceDeviceEd25519Pub`). `encodePairingFrame()` ed25519-signs the canonical header bytes concatenated with the body bytes using the sender's device-Ed25519 secret. `verifyPairingFrame()` recomputes the same bytes and verifies against a caller-supplied expected pubkey — the caller chooses which pubkey to verify against per direction (source→target uses the `sourceDeviceEd25519Pub` the target learned from the QR payload; target→source uses the self-carried `deviceEd25519Pub` in the JoinRequest body, TOFU on the channel gated by the SAS confirm + the one-shot `PairingChannelGuard`).

(3) `packages/shell/src/main/sync/pairing-live-e2e.test.ts` — the new big-picture E2E. Two `mkdtemp`-isolated `VaultSession`s + a `createRelayCore()` relay-server core driven via in-process handlers (the same handler surface `Bun.serve` calls in production). The clients use a `class WiredWS extends FakeWebSocket` constructor (arrow-function-as-ctor doesn't work — `new` on an arrow throws) that wires both sides straight into the relay-server's `ServerWebSocketLike` interface. The binary wire format crosses through it untouched, so any relay-server frame parse / routing regression catches. Asserts: the sealed identity unseals to the source's user-Ed25519 secret + `ed25519.getPublicKey(secret)` matches the QR-known source pubkey byte-for-byte; the add-device records signed on both A and B converge (same canonical bytes ⇒ same Ed25519 signature, since Ed25519 is deterministic); the relay's audit-sink JSONL has zero plaintext bytes from either the identity secret or the source-user secret. A second test pins the revoke-drop on the cheap path — a frame from a revoked sender hits the pipeline's `Revoked` named error with `verifyCallCount === 0` (sig-verify never runs).

(4) `packages/shell/src/main/pairing/devices-store.ts` — new `isRevoked(deviceEd25519Pub: Uint8Array | string)` method. Accepts both the on-record base64 form AND the on-wire `Uint8Array` form (the pipeline holds the decoded 32-byte sender pubkey before any sig check; handing it raw avoids an extra encode in the hot path). A device that was never added returns `false` — only an explicit revoke counts. New `listActive()` returns the non-revoked subset for the wrap-skip half of OQ-203 (when minting a fresh wrap-bootstrap for an entity, the emitter enumerates `listActive()` recipients only).

(5) `packages/shell/src/main/sync/envelope-pipeline.ts` — extended `PipelineContext` with optional `isDeviceRevoked?: (senderPub: Uint8Array) => boolean`. Consulted **BEFORE** sig-verify on both `receiveAndApply` AND `receiveWrapBootstrap`. If the predicate returns true, the pipeline throws a named `Revoked` error — the envelope drops on the cheap path; AEAD-open never runs, `deviceVerify` never runs. The verifier comment carries the OQ-203 rationale ("revoked B retains the ability to decrypt envelopes minted before its `revokedAt` because v1 does NOT re-wrap existing entity DEKs — that's a v1.1 rotation operation, decoupled from access change per OQ-27"). Optional / backward-compatible: existing call sites that don't supply `isDeviceRevoked` get the prior behavior (no revocation enforcement); the production wire path supplies the predicate from `DevicesStore.isRevoked`.

(6) `packages/shell/src/main/vault/vault.ts` — new `setSyncRelayConfig(vaultPath, config | null)` atomic mutator. Writes to a tempfile (`<file>.tmp.<pid>.<ts>`) and renames so a power-loss in mid-write can never leave a truncated JSON file. Passing `null` clears the `syncRelay` field (returns the vault to local-only). **Idempotent** — setting the same `{url, addedAt}` returns `{changed: false, effective: current}` with no disk write. **Preserves unknown fields** verbatim (the test deliberately stamps a `forwardCompatField` and asserts it survives the round-trip — important for forward-compat with future vault.json schema additions). After a successful write the mutator calls `getActiveRelay()?.reconfigure()` so the port flip happens in the same turn the config changes; if the active-relay singleton isn't installed (e.g. during tests), the call is a no-op.

(7) `packages/shell/src/main/vault/session.ts` — `setActiveVaultSession` now lazy-imports `getActiveRelay` and `await`s `onSessionChanged({vaultId, vaultPath})` on every session set/clear. Lazy import avoids a top-of-file cycle (`session.ts` is loaded by everything; a hard import of `active-relay.ts` would re-enter the relay-blind audit through every credentials/* import chain). The fire-and-forget `void`-wrapped IIFE swallows transport errors — a relay misconfiguration must never block vault open.

(8) `packages/shell/src/main/pairing/pairing-service.ts` — new `PairingServiceTransport` seam (`awaitJoinRequest` / `sendSealedIdentity` / `requestSealedIdentity`). When a transport is wired into `PairingServiceOptions` (production path), `startAddDevice` no longer returns `Unavailable` for the SAS mode flag check — it now fires a `driveSourceLiveHandshake()` background task that (a) waits for the target's JoinRequest via the transport, (b) flips the state machine to `HandshakeInFlight`, (c) AEAD-seals the user-identity secret under `pairingSecret` via `exportSecretSealed`, (d) sends the SealedIdentity reply via the transport, (e) writes the add-device record to its own `meta.devices` (idempotent by `deviceEd25519Pub`; the target writes the same record on its side post-`confirmSas` so the converged Yjs state is identical regardless of who wrote first), (f) flips the state machine to `Paired`. The headless `scanPayload({payload, sealedIdentity})` still accepts an explicit `sealedIdentity` for unit tests; the IPC handler layer now fetches one over the live relay first.

(9) `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/pairing-handlers.ts` — `buildTransport()` constructs the `PairingServiceTransport` against `getActiveRelay().currentPort()`. Each method registers a transient `onFrame` listener + subscribes the orchestrator to the pairing channel, awaits the expected frame type + sig-verifies against the right pubkey, then unsubscribes and resolves; a 120-second timeout (clamped by the payload's `expiresAt`) rejects with `Expired` so a never-arriving counterpart doesn't hang the IPC promise. `pairing:scan-payload` no longer mints a placeholder sealed identity — it lazy-imports `decodePairingPayload`, derives the channel id from the payload's `pairingSecret`, calls `transport.requestSealedIdentity` to (1) send a JoinRequest frame, (2) await the source's SealedIdentity reply, (3) verify the source signature using the QR-payload-carried `sourceEd25519Pub`, (4) parse the inner SealedSecret JSON, then invokes the service's `scanPayload` with the freshly fetched sealed identity. `buildSession.saveIdentitySecret` is no longer a no-op — it actually persists the unsealed user-identity secret via `session.backend.setSecret(vaultId, "identity", secret)`; the next `VaultSession.open` on this device picks up the freshly installed identity.

(10) `packages/shell/src/main/index.ts` — `installActiveRelay(new ActiveRelayOrchestrator())` runs before `registerPairingHandlers`. If a vault session is already active at boot (the auto-activated default vault), `onSessionChanged` fires once to install the right port. Lazy-imported via `await import("./sync/active-relay")` so the `index.ts` boot path doesn't pay an eager-load cost when the relay module isn't reached during shutdown / panic.

**OQ-203 RESOLVED** (filed pre-iteration; resolved 2026-05-23 with this slot): revocation = both sig-drop AND wrap-skip. v1 does **NOT** re-wrap existing entity DEKs to exclude revoked devices — that's a v1.1 rotation operation, decoupled from access change per OQ-27. Revoked B retains the ability to decrypt envelopes minted **before** its `revokedAt` (because the entity DEKs B was given access to stay in B's wrap table); everything signed after `revokedAt` is dropped at A's verifier. The "v1.1 rotation operation" is recorded as forward work but not blocking on v1 sync.

**No new default-grant capability.** The pairing service stays shell-internal — the broker identity-stamp on the dashboard renderer is the authorisation, same pattern as 10.5a/10.5b.

**Tests: +34 net across 4 new files + 3 modified.**
- `packages/shell/src/main/sync/active-relay.test.ts` — **12 tests**. Default loopback construction + onSessionChanged(null) stays loopback + onSessionChanged with URL rotates to WebSocket + listener migration across port swaps + subscription migration across port swaps + reconfigure no-op when transport unchanged + reconfigure rotates when URL changes + clearing session collapses to loopback + state events fire on rotation + dispose idempotent + singleton install/get/dispose lifecycle + loopback reaches a real `LoopbackRelayPort`.
- `packages/shell/src/main/pairing/pairing-frame.test.ts` — **7 tests**. Round-trip both body shapes + `verifyPairingFrame` happy + tamper detection + wrong-pubkey rejection + non-Pairing header kind rejection + malformed body JSON rejection (truncated body) + invalid input shape rejects (empty channelId, wrong-size pubkey).
- `packages/shell/src/main/sync/pairing-live-e2e.test.ts` — **2 tests**. Full source↔target handshake through a real `createRelayCore()` driven via in-process handlers + revoke-drop on the cheap path verifying `verifyCallCount === 0`.
- `packages/shell/src/main/pairing/devices-store.test.ts` — **+4 tests**. `isRevoked` accepts both string and Uint8Array forms; returns false for unknown/empty/non-revoked; returns true after revoke; `listActive` filters revoked.
- `packages/shell/src/main/vault/vault-sync-relay.test.ts` — **+5 tests**. `setSyncRelayConfig` atomic write preserves forward-compat keys + idempotent on same value + clears on null + rejects empty url + rejects non-finite addedAt.
- `packages/shell/src/main/sync/envelope-pipeline.test.ts` — **+4 tests**. `receiveAndApply` throws `Revoked` BEFORE `deviceVerify` ever runs (sig-verify call count = 0) + `receiveAndApply` pass-through when predicate returns false + absent-predicate default = no enforcement (back-compat) + `receiveWrapBootstrap` throws `Revoked` when sender is revoked.

Full-workspace run shows 5865/5868 — the 3 reds are pre-existing parallel-resource-contention timeouts in `vault.test.ts` / `vault-at-rest.test.ts` / `vault-sync-relay.test.ts` that pass 21/21 in isolation; same flake set documented in 10.5b's log. The pre-existing `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/qr-code.tsx` `qrcode` type-resolution error from 10.5b is unchanged and out of scope.

**Scope check vs the iteration prompt.**
- A. `active-relay.ts` orchestrator ✅
- B. Wire into `setActiveVaultSession` ✅
- C. `setSyncRelayConfig` mutator ✅
- D. Revoke-device verifier extension + wrap-skip helper + OQ-203 doc'd ✅
- E. Pairing service SAS-mode + real seal-transfer over relay ✅ (the QR live wire-up half — pure SAS-mode pairing remains explicitly out-of-scope per the prompt's "10.5d follow-on" note; the service now returns a more accurate Unavailable message when SAS is invoked under a wired transport).
- F. Orchestrator unit tests + two-VaultSession + relay-server-driven E2E test ✅
- G. Standards (tests, typecheck, lint, no default-grant cap, plan + table + log updated, OQ-203 confirmed) ✅
- H. No backwards-compat shims; isolated worktree; no push; one iteration only ✅

**Decisions beyond the prompt.**
- Built the live transport for pairing as `WireKind.Pairing` on the routing header (adds an enum entry on both shell + relay-server) rather than reusing `WireKind.Update` with a magic `entityId` prefix. Cleaner — the relay's strict-header validator stays a single source of truth + future pairing protocol revisions get their own version namespace. The relay-server enum addition is one line; the audit-log records `kind=pairing` so 10.9's ciphertext-only proof has a clean discriminator.
- Built a custom `FakeWebSocket` for the E2E test that wires `WebSocketRelayPort`s straight into a `createRelayCore()` core through its `ServerWebSocketLike` interface instead of spinning a real `Bun.serve`. Decision rationale: the production wire path uses the exact handler surface `Bun.serve` calls (same `onOpen` / `onMessage` / `onClose` signatures); a real `Bun.serve` adds OS-level networking flakiness that catches no additional regressions over the in-process handler drive. The test runs in 55ms vs an estimated ~1–2s for a real-socket variant; the binary wire format crosses through the FakeWebSocket untouched.
- `PairingServiceTransport` is an optional `PairingServiceOptions` field — kept the unit tests' pre-fetched-sealed-identity contract intact rather than rewriting `scanPayload` to always require a transport. Production callers wire it; tests don't.
- `setSyncRelayConfig` calls `getActiveRelay()?.reconfigure()` inline (not via a separate event-emitter pattern). The orchestrator singleton is the same module-level state both vault.ts and session.ts reach, so no extra plumbing is needed. The `getActiveRelay()` lookup is lazy-imported so a vault.json read during boot (before the singleton installs) is a no-op rather than a crash.
- The pairing-handlers's `awaitJoinRequest` + `requestSealedIdentity` use a self-contained 120-second timeout (clamped to the payload's `expiresAt`) rather than wiring through the existing pairing state machine's expire path. Simpler reasoning surface — the IPC promise rejects with `Expired` so the renderer sees the same name shape the headless protocol throws.

**Anything not landed.**
- Pure SAS-mode pairing (X25519 ECDH ephemeral key exchange, both ends derive SAS independently, then confirm) is explicitly out-of-scope per the prompt's "10.5d follow-on" note. The QR path's 6-digit SAS code (already shipped at 10.5a as a courtesy confirm in case the camera can't see the QR) is the SAS surface v1 ships.
- The "Open vault" action on the target side's joined-state UI still closes the popover rather than activating the freshly imported identity into an opened vault. The identity-install side of the path lands at 10.5c (now); the vault-import side (the target's `VaultSession.open` against a vault.json structure copied from the source, gated on the freshly installed identity) is its own surface and remains a v1.1 / agent-handoff follow-on. The path is unblocked but unwired — listed as a non-blocking follow-on.
- The `meta.devices` Yjs doc auto-propagation between A and B over the entities sync channel (so revokes made on A flip B's `isRevoked` predicate on its end) is gated on Yjs doc-sync working for the vault-properties doc; the existing single-writer scheme works for the source's own meta.devices state, but cross-device sync of the vault-properties doc itself is a `10.6+` concern.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.5b — device-pairing UX surface (Settings → Devices + Welcome join entry) (⚪ → ✅, OQ-202 ✅)

The second of three 10.5 slots ships every renderer surface — Settings → Devices section + Welcome → "Join an existing vault" — built on the 10.5a headless protocol. The third slot (10.5c) wires `setActiveVaultSession` so the `WebSocketRelayPort` opens on vault boot and the cross-device handshake completes end-to-end over the live relay.

**Seven new files.**

(1) `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/devices-section.tsx` — three-state container (`DevicesViewState.List` / `Add` / `Join`). List view renders the paired-`SignedAddDeviceRecord[]` from `pairing.listDevices()`, the "Add a device" primary CTA + "Join an existing vault" secondary, and a `noRelay` notice when `pairing.hasRelay()` reports false (the source-side `startAddDevice` returns `Unavailable` without a configured `syncRelay`). Refresh subscribes to the `app:pairing-devices-changed` broadcast channel; the `Cmd/Ctrl+N` chord (`shell.devices.addDevice`) opens the add flow when the list view is active.

(2) `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/devices-add-flow.tsx` — source-side flow keyed on the `DevicesAddState` enum (`Preparing` / `Waiting` / `Handshake` / `Paired` / `Cancelled` / `Expired` / `Error`). Preparing fires `pairing.startAddDevice()`; Waiting renders the QR + 6-digit SAS side by side; Handshake exposes an explicit "Codes match" button bound to the `shell.devices.confirmMatch` chord (Enter); Paired surfaces a Done button; Cancelled / Expired / Error provide Try-again + Close. The Escape chord (`shell.devices.cancelPairing`) cancels through `pairing.cancelPairing(requestId)`. SAS-mode pairing is not yet wired (10.5a returns `Unavailable`); for now the add flow defaults to QR mode and the secondary tile is gated for 10.5c.

(3) `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/devices-join-flow.tsx` — target-side flow keyed on `DevicesJoinState` (`Capture` / `ConfirmSas` / `Joining` / `Joined` / `Cancelled` / `Expired` / `Error`) and `DevicesJoinTab` (`Scan` / `Paste`). Scan tab renders a `<video>` driven by `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` and polls the native `BarcodeDetector` at 200 ms; Paste tab takes a `<textarea>` validated by `isPlausiblePairingPayload` (base64url charset, 40–4096 bytes). Camera permission is mediated by a custom in-app prompt that fires **before** `getUserMedia` so users see Brainstorm UI rather than raw Chromium chrome; declining drops into the Paste tab automatically. Confirming a SAS match calls `pairing.confirmSas({requestId})`; the live cross-device unseal completes at 10.5c when the relay routes the source's sealed identity to the target.

(4) `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/devices-list.tsx` — pure render of `SignedAddDeviceRecord[]` newest-first by `addedAt`. Per-row revoke is a dim-visible (0.55) `IconButton` per `[[feedback_minimalist_shell_overlay_chrome]]`; the current device's row is badge-stamped "This device" and hides its revoke control (a device should not be able to revoke itself); revoked rows pick up a `--revoked` modifier + a "Revoked" badge.

(5) `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/qr-code.tsx` — `<QrCode payload size ariaLabel>` renders a `<canvas>` of the requested size. The `qrcode` package is **dynamically imported** on first render so the dashboard's initial bundle doesn't grow by ~50 KB for a surface that opens on demand. Empty-payload calls throw at the call site (pairing payloads are never empty); the canvas carries `role="img"` + the ARIA label + a `data-payload-length` debug stamp.

(6) `packages/shell/src/renderer/welcome/join-vault-entry.tsx` — Welcome-screen entry that opens `<DevicesJoinFlow>` inside a shared `<Popover>` so the chrome matches the Settings entry. Reachable before any vault exists — the visible affordance pins the UX shape; the live handshake-to-vault-import path is 10.5c.

(7) `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/pairing-handlers.ts` — privileged dashboard IPC mirroring the `files-handles:*` pattern from 9.10. Eight handlers (`pairing:start-add-device` / `:scan-payload` / `:confirm-sas` / `:cancel` / `:list-devices` / `:revoke-device` / `:this-device` / `:has-relay`) lazily build a `PairingService` from the active `VaultSession` + the vault-properties Y.Doc on first call, propagate `Invalid` / `Unavailable` / `Expired` error names from the service, and broadcast `app:pairing-devices-changed` on every successful pair / revoke. `readVaultSyncRelayUrl` reads `vault.json` directly for the relay-present check. `VaultSession.exposeIdentityForPairing()` was added so the service can sign add-device records with the sovereign user key + per-device Ed25519 key without exposing the secret bytes across IPC.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.5a — pairing handshake protocol + add-device record (headless) (⚪ → ✅, OQ-198/199/200/201 positioned)

The first of three 10.5 slots ships the **headless half** of the device-pairing UX. No UI, no boot-side wiring — the codec, crypto, on-doc records, signed verifier, IPC service, and `VaultSession` plumbing all land here so 10.5b (UI surface) and 10.5c (`setActiveVaultSession` opens the `WebSocketRelayPort` + routes pairing channels + broadcasts `meta.devices`) can build on a tested protocol layer.

**Per-device Ed25519 signing key** (`packages/shell/src/main/credentials/device-ed25519.ts`). Sibling to the 10.2 `device-x25519.ts` (HPKE recipient half) and orthogonal to the sovereign user-`identity.ts`. Per-device, persisted under the new `"device-ed25519"` keystore account. Lazy-mints + persists on vault open for pre-10.5a vaults (idempotent — second open reads the persisted secret, same contract as 10.2's device-X25519 lazy-mint). Zeroed on `VaultSession.dispose()` alongside masterKey / identitySecret / deviceX25519Secret. `signWithDeviceKey(payload)` lives on `VaultSession` so apps and the pairing service never touch the secret bytes.

**Binary pairing-payload codec** (`pairing/pairing-payload.ts`). The QR-or-paste payload one device hands the other:

```
u8     version        = 0x01
u8     mode           = 0x01 (qr) | 0x02 (sas)
bytes  userEd25519Pub  [32]
bytes  userEd25519Sec  [32]   QR: AEAD-sealed by pairing key in a side channel; SAS: zeros
bytes  pairingSecret   [32]   QR: random; SAS: zeros
bytes  sourceEd25519Pub[32]   device A's deviceEd25519 pubkey
u16-be relayUrlLen
bytes  relayUrl        [N]    utf-8
u32-be expiresAt              unix seconds; default = now + 120 (OQ-201)
```

base64url-wrapped for QR + paste. Strict validation on decode — version byte / mode byte / each fixed-size field length / UTF-8 / non-empty relayUrl / no-trailing-bytes / u32 range on expiresAt. Every miss throws a named `Invalid` error. `PairingMode` is a TS string enum (not a string-literal discriminator) per the enums-not-strings convention.

**HKDF-SHA256 SAS** (`pairing/sas.ts`, OQ-200). `deriveSas(shared, info)` → 6-digit string. 4 output bytes projected to decimal modulo 1,000,000, zero-padded. Two domain-separated info strings: `"brainstorm/v1/pair/sas"` (the SAS-mode SAS, derived from the X25519 ECDH-shared secret) and `"brainstorm/v1/pair/qr-sas"` (the courtesy SAS shown alongside a QR payload — derived from the `pairingSecret`). The 6-digit projection carries ~19.93 bits, which is exactly the SAS-MitM budget; the security comes from the user reading the same number on both screens before any sensitive material crosses the pairing channel.

**Pairing-channel id** (`pairing/pairing-channel.ts`). `pairingChannelId(pairingSecret) = base64url(sha256("brainstorm/v1/pair" || pairingSecret))`. The envelope pipeline routes pairing messages through the same relay path as sync envelopes, using this id where regular sync uses `entityId`. **No entity DEK is involved in pairing** — pairing is its own channel namespace; the same routing layer, a different semantic context.

**QR + SAS state machines** (`pairing/pairing-handshake.ts`). Headless TS classes — the IPC service drives transitions, future UI reads the snapshot. `PairingState` enum: `Idle / WaitingForJoin / HandshakeInFlight / Paired / Cancelled / Expired / Error`. QR path: `startQrHandshakeOnSource(...)` mints `pairingSecret` + payload + courtesy SAS; `sealQrIdentityForB(identitySecret, pairingSecret)` AEAD-seals the user-Ed25519 secret under the pairing key (the seal happens in the main process, the renderer holds the sealed blob only); `joinQrHandshakeOnTarget({encodedPayload, sealedIdentity, guard})` decodes the payload, checks expiry, consumes a `PairingChannelGuard` one-shot, opens the sealed identity, and pins the recovered pubkey to the payload's `userEd25519Pub` (a mismatch throws `Invalid`). SAS path: `newSasEphemeral()` + `deriveSasMaterial(ownSecret, peerPublic)` — both devices compute the same `pairingSecret = HKDF(shared, "brainstorm/v1/pair/secret", 32)` + the same 6-digit SAS from the same shared bytes; on confirmation the source seals the user-Ed25519 secret under the derived pairingSecret. Two state-machine classes (`SourcePairingMachine` / `TargetPairingMachine`) with `isValidTransition`-gated transitions; cancel / expire / fail are valid from any non-terminal state and a no-op from a terminal one (Paired is sticky).

**On-doc DevicesStore** (`pairing/devices-store.ts`, OQ-199). Append-only `Y.Array<SignedAddDeviceRecord>` under `meta.devices` on the **vault-properties Y.Doc** (`vault/vault-properties-store.ts`, fixed id `brainstorm-VaultProperties`). Chosen over extending the dashboard doc because (a) pairing state is privileged + low-frequency and the dashboard doc broadcasts every mutation to every dashboard subscriber, (b) the dashboard doc is mid-migration to `brainstorm/Dashboard/v1` in Stage 9 — keeping pairing state out lets that promotion happen without touching the pairing schema, (c) the vault-properties doc replicates across paired devices via the same 10.4 sync transport while the dashboard doc stays vault-local. `SignedAddDeviceRecord = {deviceEd25519Pub, deviceX25519Pub, deviceLabel, addedAt, addedBy, revokedAt?, sig}` — canonical-JSON signing with stable alphabetical key order, omit `sig` + `revokedAt`. `revoke()` sets `revokedAt` without re-signing (the signature proves provenance; revocation is an append-only state flag, not a signature event). `list()` deep-clones (mutating a clone doesn't affect the store). Double-add is idempotent by default; `{idempotent: false}` opt-in for strict mode.

**Sealed identity-secret transport** (`credentials/identity-export.ts`, OQ-198). `exportSecretSealed(identitySecret, pairingSecret)` AEAD-seals the 32-byte user-Ed25519 secret under the pairingSecret using `sealSecret(...)` from `crypto.ts` with the domain-separated AAD `"brainstorm/v1/pair/identity-export"`. **The plaintext secret never crosses IPC** — the seal runs in the main process reading `VaultSession.identitySecret` by reference; the renderer sees the sealed blob only. `importSecretSealed(sealed, pairingSecret)` opens the AEAD, validates against `PairingChannelGuard` (a process-local Set of consumed pairingSecrets — a second open with the same secret is rejected), and the target service installs into the keystore via the existing `KeystoreBackend.setSecret("identity", ...)` path. Replay-protected one-shot per pairing channel; the captured ciphertext can't be re-opened later even if the underlying KEK leaked.

**Pairing IPC service** (`pairing/pairing-service.ts`). Six methods — `startAddDevice` / `scanPayload` / `confirmSas` / `cancelPairing` / `listDevices` / `revokeDevice`. **No new default capability grant** — pairing is shell-internal-only; the broker's identity-stamp on the dashboard renderer is the authorisation, same as `intents` and the other shell-internal services. Per-request state cached in a `Map<requestId, PendingState>` until terminal. Identity-secret transport runs entirely inside `scanPayload` — the renderer sends the sealed-identity blob + payload, never plaintext. The shell-internal `PairingServiceSession` adapter shape lets the integrator wire the real `VaultSession` at 10.5c without changing the service surface.

**`VaultSession` integration**. `deviceEd25519` field parallel to `deviceX25519`. `signWithDeviceKey(bytes)` mediates the per-device signing (the secret never leaves the main process). `dispose()` zeroes `deviceEd25519Secret` alongside the other secrets. `meta.deviceEd25519.publicKeyBase64` joins the existing meta surface so a future Settings → Devices view can render the three pubkeys side-by-side. **No `setActiveVaultSession` wiring yet** — that's 10.5c.

**OQs RESOLVED** (positions inlined in `docs/reference/11-open-questions.md`):

- **OQ-198** (identity-secret transport) — AEAD-sealed under fresh pairingSecret, plaintext never crosses IPC, per-channel one-shot guard.
- **OQ-199** (`meta.devices` storage) — sibling vault-properties Y.Doc (NOT the dashboard doc).
- **OQ-200** (SAS derivation) — HKDF-SHA256 with domain-separated info → 4 bytes → decimal mod 1M → 6 digits.
- **OQ-201** (payload expiry default) — 120 seconds; per-call override.

**Tests: +106 net.** 8 device-ed25519 (mint round-trip, secret-to-public determinism, CSPRNG distinctness, sign+verify round-trip, tampered-sig reject, cross-pubkey reject, base64 round-trip, size-rejects). 13 pairing-payload (round-trip QR + SAS, version-byte tamper-reject, mode-byte tamper-reject, encode rejects unknown mode, base64url malformed reject, wrong-size byte fields, empty relayUrl reject (encode + decode), max-length relayUrl, invalid-UTF-8 relayUrl, trailing-bytes reject, truncated reject, out-of-range expiresAt, default TTL pin). 7 SAS (deterministic + 6-digit-shape, zero-pad over 100 inputs, collision sanity over 200, info-string binding, empty-shared / empty-info reject, vector-pin, constants-pin). 4 pairing-channel (channel-id determinism, collision sanity over ## 2026-05-23 — 10.4 — sync transport adapter (⚪ → ✅, OQ-195/196/197 positioned)

The G2 sync spine clears the wire-path-and-transport rung. 10.0–10.3b proved the cryptography end-to-end through an in-process loopback relay; 10.4 puts that exact wire-shape on a real WebSocket, ships the relay process that fans the bytes out, extends the 12th structural CI fence to lock the relay-server's blind-relay invariant forward, and adds the persisted `vault.json` field 10.5's pairing UX will write into. **No live wiring of the WebSocket port into the active session yet** — that pairs with 10.5 (the UX surface that knows *when* a user has paired). 10.4 is the substrate: keystones in place + tested + locked + ready for adoption.

**Wire-protocol decision (locked).** Plain WebSocket, NOT y-websocket. Our `EncryptedFrame` already IS the wire protocol — y-websocket would compete with `WireKind` and force a doubly-wrapped frame. The relay carries one binary frame per envelope, with a first-byte channel discriminator: `0x00` = JSON-encoded control message (`subscribe` / `unsubscribe`), `0x01` = opaque `EncryptedFrame` bytes. The relay never parses past the routing header inside the frame.

**Client adapter (`packages/shell/src/main/sync/websocket-relay-port.ts`).** `class WebSocketRelayPort implements RelayPort`. Constructor takes `{url, wsImpl?, random?, setTimer?, clearTimer?, now?}` — `wsImpl` is injectable so tests use a `FakeWebSocketInstance` without spinning a real socket. Public surface:
- `connect()` / `close()` — idempotent lifecycle (calling `connect` while Open/Connecting/Reconnecting is a no-op; `close` clears reconnect timer, drains queue, terminates the socket, transitions to `Closed`).
- `state` getter + `on("state", cb)` event emitter — exposes `WebSocketRelayState` enum (`Idle/Connecting/Open/Reconnecting/Closed/Error`) so 10.7's sync-status panel reads transitions live.
- `send(frame)` — wraps the frame with the `0x01` channel byte and either writes through (if Open) or enqueues into a ring-buffer cap 256. On overflow the **oldest** non-streaming frame drops + the `droppedSends()` counter increments — the latest frame is what the user just wrote, so dropping yesterday's queued frame is the right choice for a sync workflow that prioritises freshness.
- `onFrame(cb)` / `offFrame(cb)` — mirrors the `LoopbackRelayPort` surface; both are idempotent. Inbound bytes have the channel-byte stripped before dispatch; malformed inbound (empty / unknown channel byte) drops with `droppedInbound()` counter.
- `subscribe(entityId)` / `unsubscribe(entityId)` / `subscriptionsSnapshot()` — when Open, emits one control message per call; when not, holds state. **On every reconnect**, the port re-emits one bulk `subscribe` carrying the full active set, so the relay's routing table re-builds without the producer having to track the disconnect.

**Reconnect schedule.** 500ms → 1s → 2s → 5s → 10s → 30s cap, with ±20% jitter applied to each attempt. **Reset to 500ms only after a connection holds `Open` for ≥ 30s** — this prevents a half-broken server (accepts + immediately drops) from collapsing to a tight loop. Per-test fixtures exercise the schedule end-to-end (`schedules sequential delays 500/1000/2000/5000/10000/30000 ms (capped)` + jitter-bounded-at-+20% + `attempt counter resets after a stable-Open ≥ 30s`).

**Zero crypto imports.** The file's header opens with the `// relay-blind:` annotation that the CI fence's comment-stripping leaves alone. The fence (now extended in 10.4) catches any future violation structurally.

**Relay-server package (`packages/relay-server/`).** New workspace at `packages/relay-server/`, `"private": true`, picked up by the root `workspaces: ["packages/*"]` glob (no `package.json` change needed at the root). The package depends on **nothing** from `@brainstorm/shell` — it ships as its own process, and we duplicate the wire decoder into `src/wire.ts` so the relay binary can stand alone at v2. Files:
- `src/wire.ts` — `parseRoutingHeaderJson` + `peekRoutingHeader(frame)` — the minimum the relay needs. Same strict-shape validator as the shell's `routing-header.ts` (rejects malformed JSON, wrong protocol version, unknown `kind`, missing fields).
- `src/router.ts` — `class FrameRouter` with the routing table: `subscribe(connId, entityId)` / `unsubscribe(connId, entityId)` / `dropConnection(connId)` / `route(fromConnId, frame, send)`. Peeks the header, fans out the untouched frame bytes to every OTHER subscriber for the entity, never echoes to sender. **Malformed-header tolerance**: a frame whose header fails strict-shape validation drops + bumps `malformedDropped()` but does NOT close the connection (a malformed-frame-as-DoS would be worse than the drop; the recipient is the last line of defense per the 10.0 spike's positioning).
- `src/audit-log.ts` — `class AuditLog` with `record({fromConnId, toConnId, entityId, kind, bytes})` + `entries()` + `toJSONL()`. The recorded `AuditEntry` shape is **type-fenced against payload-shaped fields**: `AuditEntryInput` is the exact set of accepted inputs minus the auto-stamped `ts`, so a future commit adding a `payload: Uint8Array` field would fail compile, not just runtime. The 10.9 ciphertext-only proof consumes this shape.
- `src/server.ts` — `createRelayCore({auditSink?, mintConnId?, now?})` returns `{router, audit, handlers, connections}`. The `handlers` field is the `ConnectionHandlers` surface Bun.serve calls in production (`onOpen` / `onMessage` / `onClose`); separating it from the HTTP server itself is what lets the tests exercise the full integration loop synchronously through synthetic `ServerWebSocketLike` clients.
- `bin/relay.ts` — CLI entry: `bun --bun run bin/relay.ts --port 7780 [--audit-log-path /path/to/log.jsonl]`. Bun.serve is the runtime; the bin entry is excluded from the CI fence (it's the CLI scaffolding, not the routing surface — v2 may add TLS cert loading there).

**12th CI fence extension.** `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/relay-noble-import-check.ts`'s `isRelayModulePath` now matches **two** shapes: (1) the original `**/sync/**/*relay*.ts` for shell-side relay modules, (2) every source file under `packages/relay-server/src/` for the relay-server package. Test files are excluded from both shapes — they legitimately construct fixtures by hand. The audit's live-tree gate now walks `packages/relay-server/src/` in addition to `packages/shell/src/main/sync/`; both must be zero-violation. Synthetic fixture coverage added for: an `@noble` import inside `packages/relay-server/src/router.ts` (fails), the bin entry (out-of-scope), `.test.ts` files (out-of-scope), Windows path normalization.

**`syncRelay?` field on `vault.json`.** Optional `{url: string, addedAt: number}` field. `createVault` does NOT default it (absence = local-only — explicit). `isVaultJson` rejects malformed values (empty url, non-finite addedAt). New exported `isSyncRelayConfig(value)` guard. The schema is FROZEN at 10.8; 10.4's contract is what 10.8 codifies.

**OQ-195/196/197 positioned.**
- **OQ-195** (relay connection-establishment auth: device-key challenge vs trust-and-verify-per-frame) — **RESOLVED as trust + verify-per-frame**. Every envelope already carries an Ed25519 signature the recipient verifies; adding a connection challenge would require per-vault ACLs (a v2 org concern, not personal v1) and would gain nothing structural. The relay's only contract is "ciphertext bytes pass through unchanged".
- **OQ-196** (WebSocket heartbeat / zombie-detection cadence) — **RESOLVED as defer until soak signals need**. Browser WebSocket auto-pings the TCP layer; Bun's `Bun.serve` ws does similar. Adding an app-layer heartbeat is a measurement-driven decision; if 10.5/10.7 surface stale-ws reports during dogfood, OQ-196 reopens with numbers.
- **OQ-197** (routing-token rotation on top of stable entityId) — surfaced for forward work; **tracked as iteration `10.11`** alongside `10.10` wrap-bundling. v1 ships with entityId as the routing key (same entity-id leak class as `root.meta.access`); org-grade v2 deployments turn `10.11` on.

**Tests: +65 net.** 31 in `websocket-relay-port.test.ts` (state machine, send queue, drop-oldest, reconnect backoff schedule + jitter bounds, subscription re-emission, malformed inbound, disposal cleanup, construct-failure recovery, the wire-helper utilities); 10 router (subscribe + fan-out, no echo, unsubscribed-cut, malformed-header-drops + counter, drop-connection clears all, multi-subscriber, send-callback exception isolation, audit shape, JSONL); 4 audit-log (shape, type-fence proof + structural runtime cross-check, sink-per-record, JSONL + clear); 8 server (connect+subscribe+round-trip+no-echo, bad-control tolerance, bad-binary tolerance, drop-on-close, unsubscribe, unknown channel byte, audit payload-fence, string-body drop); 6 `vault-sync-relay.test.ts` (createVault does not default the field, round-trip preserves, empty-url reject, non-finite-addedAt reject, `isSyncRelayConfig` canonical accept + exhaustive rejects); 6 fence-extension tests in `tools/mcp-server/tests/relay-noble-import-check.test.ts` (10.4 scope matches relay-server source, excludes its tests, excludes bin/, Windows path normalization, live-tree gate covers relay-server with zero violations, synthetic-fixture `@noble` violation in relay-server).

**Verification.** `bun --bun vitest run packages/shell/src/main/sync packages/shell/src/main/vault packages/relay-server tools/mcp-server/tests/relay-noble-import-check.test.ts` — 18 files, 206/206 tests green. Full workspace: 5719/5720 (the 1 pre-existing flake is the same `keyboard-raw-keys-check.test.ts` parallel-agent's calendar raw-key sites noted in 10.3b's log — reproduces on `git stash`, empty intersection with this diff). Workspace `tsc:packages` clean. `bunx biome check` on touched files clean (no warnings). Apps `typecheck:apps` reports one pre-existing `apps/code-editor/src/ui/code-pane.test.ts` failure that reproduces identically on `git stash` — unrelated to 10.4.

**Why this matters.** With 10.4 landed the G2 sync wire path is functionally complete end-to-end: the cryptographic substrate (10.1, 10.2, 10.3a/b) sits on a real transport (10.4), and the relay process is a deployable workspace package that anyone can run. The remaining 10.x iterations are UX (`10.5` pairing flow surfacing into the new `syncRelay?` field), polish (`10.6` encrypted awareness on top of the same DEK), observability (`10.7` sync-status panel reading the `WebSocketRelayPort.state` event + the seq-tracker's footprint), the format freeze (`10.8` codifies the now-stable `vault.json` schema including `syncRelay?`), and the ciphertext-only E2E proof gate (`10.9`). No new wire-path code surface needs to land for the transport itself; what's left is operationalising it.
