## 2026-05-23 — 10.3b — wrap-bootstrap envelope + per-(sender, entityId) seq-tracker + two-`VaultSession` new-device-join E2E (⚪ → ✅, OQ-194 ✅)

The second half of Stage 10.3 closes the G2 sync wire-path loop: a paired device can now be admitted, given the entity DEK over the blind relay, and apply CRDT updates under the same DEK with replay protection. 10.3a slice 1 shipped the `Update` envelope spine; 10.3b adds the `WrapBootstrap` kind that lets a new device receive the DEK in the first place, plus the per-(sender, entityId) seq-tracker every receiver runs to drop replayed frames. The canonical E2E test exercises two real `VaultSession` instances (separate vault dirs + keystores + `entities.db`), so the demo is end-to-end real shell code paths, not a unit-test mockup.

**Seq-tracker.** New module at `packages/shell/src/main/sync/seq-tracker.ts` — `SeqTracker` keyed on `(sender pubkey base64, entityId)` pairs. Receive state per pair = `{ highest: number, bitmap: BigInt }`; the BigInt is a 64-bit cumulative window (bit `n` set means `highest - n` was already accepted). `accept()` returns the `SeqAcceptance` enum (`Fresh` / `Duplicate` / `OutOfWindow`); a seq more than `windowBits - 1` behind `highest` is rejected as `OutOfWindow` (conservative: too old to dedupe authoritatively). Send state per pair = a monotonic counter; `nextSeq()` returns +1 each call and persists. Writes are serialised through a chained Promise so concurrent `accept`/`nextSeq` cannot interleave-clobber. Persistence is one JSON file at `<vault>/sync/seq.json` (pattern after `window/session-state.ts` — the project's existing simple-KV idiom; no SQLite needed for state this small). Reopen reloads receive + send state so a vault re-open does not restart the send counter at zero. Malformed on-disk JSON is logged + treated as empty — the wire path stays available; at worst one window of frames re-replay. **15 tests** cover Fresh-then-Duplicate, gap-then-late-arrival inside window, gap-of-128 still rejects N=0 but accepts N=129, distinct (sender, entityId) pairs are independent, persistence round-trip across `dispose()` + `open()`, custom `windowBits=8` boundary, malformed JSON tolerated, concurrent-acceptance consistency.

**WrapBootstrap envelope.** Sibling primitives in `envelope-seal.ts` — `sealWrapBootstrapEnvelope` / `openWrapBootstrapEnvelope` carry `MemberWrapPayload` JSON as the inner payload. The wrap is already HPKE-sealed under the recipient device's X25519 pubkey (10.2), so a second AEAD layer keyed by the DEK would be redundant — the DEK is exactly what the wrap is delivering, so it cannot also wrap itself. The routing-header Ed25519 sig over `canonicalHeaderBytes || payload` is the integrity surface: it binds the wrap to sender pubkey, routed entity id, seq, nonce, ts, and `kind`. Same `EntityIdMismatch`-before-verify ordering as the Update path; same `header.kind === WrapBootstrap` guard on both seal and open so a caller cannot route an Update payload through this seal path and skip the AEAD layer. **9 tests** cover round-trip, kind-guard on seal + open, EntityIdMismatch-before-verify, sig + payload tamper, malformed-JSON / non-wrap-JSON payload reject, encode→decode→open through the wire codec.

**Pipeline orchestrators.** `envelope-pipeline.ts` gains `emitWrapBootstrap(entityId, wrap, ctx)` and `receiveWrapBootstrap(frame, ctx, onWrapAccepted)`. The receive callback hands the parsed `MemberWrapPayload` + resolved entity id to `onWrapAccepted` — the actual HPKE unseal of the inner DEK happens at the call site (via `VaultSession.unwrapMemberWrap`) because the X25519 secret never leaves the main process. **4 tests** cover emit → receive round-trip, Invalid on Update-kind, Unavailable on unknown entity, plaintext-DEK-absent-from-wire.

**CR-14 inline.** `RelayPort` gains `offFrame(cb)` + `LoopbackRelayPort.offFrame` impl, per the iteration-bundle review finding. 10.3b's E2E test swaps a wrap-handler for an update-handler mid-test; `offFrame` is what makes that clean. CR-3 / CR-8 / CR-10 / CR-11 from the same review stay forward work.

**Two-`VaultSession` E2E.** `new-device-join.test.ts` is the canonical demo. Device A1 owns vault A's entity with a real `EntityDekStore`-minted DEK; Device A2 is a separate `VaultSession` (separate vault dir + keystore + `entities.db` + X25519 keypair). Wire: A1 builds a `MemberWrapPayload` addressed to A2's device pubkey via `wrapDekForRecipient` → emits `WrapBootstrap` through the loopback relay → A2 receives + verifies sig + parses the wrap + calls `session.unwrapMemberWrap` to get the DEK + persists a fresh `entity_deks` row + stamps the entity row's `dek_id` → A1 emits a regular `Update` under the DEK → A2 receives + opens + applies → A2's `Y.Doc` converges to A1's text. Assertions: the converged CRDT body matches, the blind relay's observed frame bodies contain no plaintext DEK byte sequence (verified by raw-hex-substring scan over the wire bytes) and no plaintext CRDT text content (the wire body after AEAD is ciphertext indistinguishable from random), replay protection — re-`accept` of A1's `seq=0` frame returns `Duplicate`. **2 tests**: the full join + a focused `offFrame` cleanup test.

**OQ-194 RESOLVED.** Per-(sender, entityId) granularity is the smallest replay-window unit that gives a correct one-shot dup-drop without coupling unrelated entities' replay state. At 10k entities × 3 devices = ~30k rows the JSON KV is fine; SQLite handles 30k–100k rows trivially for the day we promote storage. 10.7's sync-status surface lists the seq state footprint as a diagnostic; re-evaluate only if a 100k-entity / 10-device scaling pass at G(GA) flags table size. Marked `*[RESOLVED in implementation-plan Stage 10.3b]*` in `11-open-questions.md`.

**Verification.** `bun --bun vitest run packages/shell/src/main/sync packages/shell/src/main/credentials packages/shell/src/main/vault tools/mcp-server/tests/relay-noble-import-check.test.ts` 22/22 files, 238/238 tests green (was 206 → +32). Full workspace 5654/5655 tests green (one pre-existing unrelated parallel-agent failure in `keyboard-raw-keys-check.test.ts` — reproduces on stash, empty intersection with this diff). `bun run typecheck:packages` clean. `bunx biome check` on touched files = 3 pre-existing `noNonNullAssertion` warnings in `envelope-seal.test.ts` from the 10.3a slice 1 land — not in 10.3b scope. Apps `typecheck:apps` reports one pre-existing `apps/code-editor/src/ui/code-pane.test.ts` failure that reproduces identically on `git stash` — unrelated to 10.3b.

**Why this matters.** With 10.3b landed the G2 sync wire path is functionally complete for the single-shared-vault multi-device case: a new device joining a vault gets the DEK over the blind relay (in HPKE-sealed form, addressed only to it), then participates in the encrypted-update stream with replay protection. The remaining 10.x iterations (`10.4`–`10.9`) are transport (swap the LoopbackRelayPort for `y-websocket`) + UX (`10.5` device-pair flow) + observability (`10.7` sync-status panel surfacing the seq state footprint) + the format freeze (`10.8`) + the two-instance ciphertext-only E2E gate (`10.9`). No new code surface needs to land for the wire path itself; what's left is operationalising it.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.3a slice 1 — sync wire format + envelope seal/pipeline + 12th structural CI gate (⚪ → 🟡, OQ-191/192/193 ✅)

The G2 sync spine starts here. Slice 1 of 10.3a ships the pure keystones every wire path downstream consumes — codec, seal/open primitives, the `EntityDekStore`-integrated pipeline orchestrator, the in-process loopback relay, and the 12th structural CI gate that locks the blind-relay invariant at the project level. Slice 2 (entity-wraps installer at entity.create + retro-wrap + ydoc-worker integration) pairs with the live wire path's first cut.

**Integrator merge.** Two agents authored 10.3a slice 1 in parallel — both implementations were uncommitted when the conflict surfaced. The merge kept the build that already integrated with the 10.1 `EntityDekStore` and reused `XCHACHA_KEY_BYTES` / `base64ToBytes` / `bytesToBase64` from `../credentials/crypto` (no second copy of the AEAD constants); on top of that the merge took the dev-MCP `sync.relay_noble_import_check` audit + 15 fence-audit tests (the alternative implementation had an inline fence inside `envelope-pipeline.test.ts` only; lifting it to a project-level audit is the structural win). Net change vs. main: 10 new files under `packages/shell/src/main/sync/`, 1 new audit + test in `tools/mcp-server/`, +53 net tests.

**The wire layout** mirrors the 10.0 spike byte-for-byte so reviewers can diff:

```
u32-be(headerLen) || canonicalHeaderBytes(routingHeader)
  || u16-be(sigLen=64) || sig
  || u32-be(ctLen) || ciphertext
```

The `canonicalizeRoutingHeader` helper emits a **pinned key order** (`v|kind|entityId|sender|seq|nonce|ts`) so byte-equality across producer / consumer / relay survives any JS field-construction-order difference. The pinned bytes feed both the AEAD AAD AND the Ed25519 signature — a relay that re-orders header keys at the JSON layer would silently break verify before any AAD work. The encode path's invariant is pinned by a property test in `routing-header.test.ts` (`emits pinned key order regardless of input insertion order`).

**The seal / open primitives** (`envelope-seal.ts`) follow a load-bearing order of checks on `openUpdateEnvelope`:
1. `frame.header.entityId === resolvedEntityId` — the **10.1 / 10.2 forward contract** ("AAD recomputed from resolved entity row id, never caller-supplied"). A receiver that resolves the entity from its row before opening can never decrypt under a different DEK than the row authors. The mismatch throws a named `EntityIdMismatch` error so downstream audit can distinguish "wrong row" from "tampered crypto".
2. Ed25519 verify the signature over `canonicalHeaderBytes || ciphertext`. A relay-forged envelope fails here without ever touching the AEAD path — and a tampered header is rejected before the DEK is even looked at.
3. AEAD open under the per-entity DEK with AAD = re-canonicalised header bytes. The DEK only lives for one envelope: `encryptAndEmit` / `receiveAndApply` in `envelope-pipeline.ts` opens it from `EntityDekStore.open()` per call, uses it once, and zeroes the plaintext in `finally`. There is no DEK cache.

Tested by `envelope-seal.test.ts`: seal/open round-trip + wrong-DEK rejection (Poly1305 catches) + single-byte ciphertext flip + header.kind flip (AAD-bound: open under a re-encoded frame whose header was mutated AFTER the original seal fails the AEAD) + flipped sig fails verify BEFORE AEAD reaches for the DEK (asserted via spy) + flipped sender pubkey fails verify + AAD recomputed from frame.header (caller-supplied header has zero effect) + `EntityIdMismatch` thrown BEFORE verify when routed id ≠ resolved id + seal returning a non-64-byte sig is rejected at emit time + encode → decode → open path also resists wire-side ciphertext byte flips + wrong-size DEK is rejected on both seal and open.

**The pipeline** (`envelope-pipeline.ts`) ties seal/open to the `EntityDekStore` + a `RelayPort` + a per-entity sequence counter. Per OQ-191 (resolved 2026-05-23) every envelope carries a fresh random 24-byte XChaCha nonce — no counter, no birthday-bound concern at v1 device counts; the property test `1000-envelope property run: no nonce collisions` pins the structural absence of the constant-nonce hazard. Per OQ-193 (resolved 2026-05-23) v1 emits one envelope per Y.Doc `transact` boundary — the test `one Y.Doc transact -> exactly one envelope on the wire` runs a doc.transact with two text inserts and asserts the wire saw exactly one frame; two consecutive transacts produce two frames. The pipeline also throws a named `Unavailable` error on `encryptAndEmit` for an entity with no DEK row (a Stage-10.x retro-wrap miss); the wire path never silently skips rows.

**The blind relay** (`relay-port.ts` → `LoopbackRelayPort.pair(N)`) has **zero crypto imports**. Each port re-broadcasts to every OTHER port on `send`, with a defensive Uint8Array copy so a downstream listener mutating the buffer can't see the sender's writes (or vice versa). The relay has no per-port state besides the port set — no entity index, no sender pubkey, no nonces. The file's own header documents the rule prose-only, scanned-but-not-imported.

**The 12th structural CI gate** (`tools/mcp-server/src/tools/relay-noble-import-check.ts`) is the project-level fence the spike asserted prose-only. Pure `(files) → violations`. Scope: every `**/sync/**/*relay*.ts` file (matches `relay-port.ts`; auto-matches `y-websocket-relay.ts` when 10.4 lands; test files excluded — they need the crypto for fixtures). Forbidden patterns:
- `import … from "@noble/<anything>"` + the `require(…)` form + side-effect `import "@noble/…"`,
- `import … from "./envelope-seal"` / `./envelope-crypto` / any `*envelope-seal*` / `*envelope-crypto*` sibling — pattern-matched so a rename can't bypass.

Comments mentioning the rule are stripped before matching, so the relay file's own header doc doesn't false-positive. Exposed via dev-MCP `sync.relay_noble_import_check` (full surface: scanned-count + violation count + per-violation `{ path, line, excerpt, kind }`). The workspace vitest gate `tools/mcp-server/tests/relay-noble-import-check.test.ts` runs the audit against the live tree on every commit + carries synthetic-fixture units for every forbidden import shape + the comment-stripping safe-cases.

**Verification.** `bun --bun vitest run packages/shell/src/main/sync tools/mcp-server/tests/relay-noble-import-check.test.ts` **53/53** green. `bun run typecheck:packages` exit 0. Pre-existing `apps/code-editor` tsc miss is unrelated (reproduces identically via `git stash`). Pre-existing `apps/tasks` + `apps/calendar` raw-key violations (from a different parallel-agent's work) also reproduce on stash and are not in 10.3a scope.

**FakeDekStore type fix (incidental).** The parallel agent's `envelope-pipeline.test.ts` originally typed its `FakeDekStore` as `Pick<EntityDekStore, …>`; TS `Pick<>` over a class with TS-private (`#`) fields drags every private member along (they're nominal), so the picked type was inhabit-able only by the real class. Re-typed as a structural `DekStoreSurface` interface + a single `as unknown as EntityDekStore` widen at the makeCtx boundary; `Omit<Partial<PipelineContext>, "dekStore">` strips the field from the spread to avoid re-introducing the collision. No behaviour change.

**Slice 2 deferred.**
1. Entity-wraps installer: append one `MemberWrapPayload` (from the 10.2 schema) per recipient device to `doc.meta.wraps` at entity.create + retro-wrap pass over existing entities. The wrap is HPKE-sealed under each recipient's X25519 pubkey; the receiver finds its wrap on doc-load and unwraps the DEK through `VaultSession.unwrapMemberWrap` (the 10.2 wire is ready, the installer wiring is the missing half).
2. ydoc-worker integration: install `sealUpdate` on every Y.Doc `transact` + `openUpdate` on every incoming relay frame so plaintext DEK + plaintext Yjs updates **never cross IPC**. This is the integration that lets the renderer never see the DEK; the loopback relay already proves the API surface, the swap to the worker is one wire-up.

Both pair with the live wire path's first cut (10.3a slice 2) — separating them now keeps the slice scope tight; the keystone surfaces here are durable.

**Why this matters.** G2 sync is the binding-clock item on the beta roadmap, and 10.3a is the spine rung that turns the 10.0 spike from a proof into production code. With slice 1 landed, every byte the relay sees is opaque ciphertext; every header field is bound into the AEAD; every receiver verifies a sig before touching the AEAD; the relay has zero crypto imports and the audit pins it that way structurally. The next builder to add `y-websocket-relay.ts` will inherit the fence automatically.

## 2026-05-23 — 9.8.7 — Files move/copy/drag-drop persisted + cross-app `intent.move` (◑ → ✅, OQ-121 ✅)

The first of the four Files-app preview-drop conversions SH-31 flagged for "ship or rewrite". Drag-drop *looked* like it worked since 9.8.2b — the in-memory mirror repainted, then the next `vaultEntities.list` refresh silently reverted everything to disk state. This iteration makes the move real (it writes through), adds the copy gesture, and elevates `intent.move` from doc to live wire. Any app can now dispatch `moveEntity(rt, { entityIds, toFolderId, fromFolderId })` and the file manager handles it identically to a user drag.

**The persistence flip.** `useFilesStore.moveIds` used to call `tree.move` and stop there. Now it kicks off `services.entities.update` for both the source and destination folder as fire-and-forget background promises. The optimistic in-memory tree repaints first (instant UX); on persist success the next `vaultEntities.list` broadcast confirms the new state; on persist *failure* the next broadcast reverts the optimistic in-memory state so a transient error is self-healing rather than silently divergent. One `entities.update` per affected folder = one Yjs transaction per folder, exactly the "atomic per folder, not across folders" rule in design 30 §Performance. Same shape for `copyIds` (dest-only persist, since membership-add doesn't touch the source).

The plumbing lives in one module-scope helper:

```ts
async function persistFolderMembers(tree: FolderTree, folderId: string): Promise<void> {
  const runtime = typeof window !== "undefined" ? window.brainstorm : undefined;
  const update = runtime?.services?.entities?.update;
  if (!update) return;                              // standalone-dev / preview-build
  const folder = tree.get(folderId);
  if (!folder) return;
  try {
    await update.call(runtime?.services?.entities, folderId, { members: [...readMembers(folder)] });
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn(`[files] entities.update(${folderId}.members) failed:`, error);
  }
}
```

`readMembers(folder)` reads live state from the already-mutated `tree`, so a quick second move on the same folder always persists the *latest* members rather than a stale capture. The `runtime?.services?.entities?.update` chain plus the rejection-swallow with console-warn is the same shape every other Files-app broker call uses (matches `uploadFiles`, `quickLookEntity`, etc.).

**Copy via alt-drag.** Holding Alt (macOS Option) at drop time switches the gesture from move to copy. `FolderTree.copy(destId, ids, now?)` lands alongside `move` with the same cycle guard (`wouldCycle` short-circuits at `CYCLE_DEPTH_LIMIT = 32`) and an idempotent semantic — ids already in `dest.members` get silently skipped (`copiedIds: []`, no notify). The result type is `CopyResult = { ok: true; copiedIds: string[] } | { ok: false; reason: "cycle" | "missing-dest" | "missing-entity" }`, intentionally lacking the move-only failure modes. Multi-membership is the documented default per design 30, so the entity becomes a member of both folders — no deep clone, no recursive walk. Drop handlers in both `content-list.tsx` and `sidebar-tree.tsx` got the same change: `event.altKey` at drop time routes to `copyIds`; `onDragOver` toggles `e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = e.altKey ? "copy" : "move"` so the OS cursor reflects the active modality before the user commits.

**`intent.move` as a cross-app verb.** The `INTENT_VERBS` namespace in `packages/shell/src/main/apps/manifest.ts` grows from 9 to 10 verbs (`"move"` joining `open` / `insert` / `share` / `convert` / `export` / `import` / `process` / `compose` / `quick-look`). The Files manifest declares the new caps (`entities.write:brainstorm/Folder/v1` per the OQ-121 leaning, `intents.dispatch:move` for outbound dispatch) plus an `intent.move` *receiver* registration without an `entityType` field — the wildcard "any object can be moved" semantic. New typed SDK helper in `packages/sdk/src/open-entity.ts`:

```ts
export type MoveEntityTarget = {
  entityIds: readonly string[];
  toFolderId: string;
  fromFolderId?: string;
  copy?: boolean;        // membership-add instead of remove-and-add. Default false.
};
export async function moveEntity(rt: OpenCapableRuntime, target: MoveEntityTarget): Promise<boolean>
```

The helper clones `entityIds` on the way out so a caller passing a mutable array doesn't have its array leak through the dispatcher, returns `false` on empty input / no dispatcher / throwing dispatcher (no exceptions escape — matches the `openEntity` / `quickLookEntity` contract callers already rely on), and stamps the cap hint `intents.dispatch:move` through the runtime proxy at the same layer as `:open` / `:quick-look` (per [[project_intents_dispatch_cap_scope]] — the scope is load-bearing for the broker's cap check). On the receiving side, `useFilesStore`'s existing `runtime.on("intent")` listener now branches on `verb === "move"` and routes the payload to a new module-scope `handleMoveIntent(payload, tree)`. The handler is the cross-app trust boundary, so it's paranoid about every field: filters non-string entries from `entityIds`, no-ops on missing `fromFolderId` (for moves) / `toFolderId` / empty `entityIds`, swallows cycle / missing-entity rejections silently. The `copy: true` branch skips the `fromFolderId` requirement entirely (membership-add doesn't touch the source). On success the same `persistFolderMembers` fire-and-forget pair runs — an `intent.move` dispatched from Notes is byte-identical to a user drag on disk.

**OQ-121 closes on the leaning.** "`intent.move` capability requirements" had a tentative position in `11-open-questions.md` that `entities.write:brainstorm/Folder/v1` suffices since moving = editing source/dest Folder `members[]`. This iteration commits — no new capability invented, just the scoped Folder write the manifest declares.

**Tests (+22, mix of pure logic + cross-app contract).**

- `FolderTree.copy` (+7 in `folder-tree.test.ts`): membership-add to dest without removing from source; idempotent re-copy of the same id (no duplicate, no notify); cycle guard on copying an ancestor into its descendant; missing-dest / missing-entity rejection; 100-entity bulk copy is atomic w.r.t. listeners (one notify) and the source folder stays unchanged.
- `moveEntity` SDK (+7 in `packages/sdk/src/open-entity.test.ts`): correct verb + payload routing; `copy: true` omits `fromFolderId`; falsy `copy` is omitted from the payload (no `copy: false` noise); no-dispatcher / empty-`entityIds` / empty-`toFolderId` short-circuit to `false`; throwing dispatcher swallowed with a `console.warn`; `entityIds` cloned (the dispatched payload doesn't alias the caller's array).
- `handleMoveIntent` (+8 in new `apps/files/tests/move-intent.test.ts`): happy-path persists both folders with the right `(folderId, { members })` shape; cycle rejection persists nothing; missing `entityIds` / `fromFolderId` / `toFolderId` / empty-`entityIds` all no-op cleanly; non-string entries in `entityIds` get filtered defensively (cross-app payload trust boundary); `copy: true` persists dest only and doesn't require `fromFolderId`; missing `services.entities.update` is a silent no-op (preview-build path); a rejected `entities.update` is swallowed with a warn (the next vault snapshot reverts).

**Verification.** `bun --bun vitest run apps/files packages/sdk` **1107/1107** green (was 1085, +22 net). `apps/files` **175/175** (was 164, +11); `packages/sdk` **+7** in `open-entity.test.ts`; `folder-tree` suite **33/33** (was 26, +7). Workspace `bun run typecheck:packages` exit 0. Apps tsc: pre-existing tsc miss in `apps/code-editor/src/ui/code-pane.test.ts` reproduces identically via `git stash` (not introduced here). Biome clean on all touched files (a pre-existing virtualizer-deps warning in `content-list.tsx` is unrelated; same `git stash` test). Manifest pipeline: `bun --bun vitest run apps/files/tests/manifest.test.ts packages/shell/src/main/apps` **113/113** green — the new `"move"` verb + the new Files-manifest cap + the receiver registration all pass the install-time validator.

**What's deferred.** Notes/Tasks/etc. don't yet *originate* `moveEntity` dispatches — the SDK helper exists, but no caller is wired. That's a follow-on per-app integration (each app gets a "move to folder…" affordance somewhere in its UI), out of scope for this iteration's "make the Files preview real" goal. The receiver works today regardless of how the dispatch is wired upstream.

**Why this matters.** Drag-drop was the most visible illusion in the Files app — the user saw their reorganization happen, then walk back on the next idle tick. With this landing, file management actually persists, and the cross-app `intent.move` is the long-promised "any app can ask the file manager to organize this" primitive (Notes can offer "move this attachment to Archive/", Tasks can drop a completed entity into Done/, etc.). The first ◑ in the Files preview-drop ladder flips ✅; three left (9.8.8 / .9 / .10).

## 2026-05-23 — OpenRes-1c slice 2 — Settings → Defaults extended to URL schemes + file extensions (🟡 → 🟡, slice landed)

The second of OpenRes-1c's UI slices. Settings → Default apps used to list only object-type targets; now it carries three sections (object types, URL schemes, file extensions), each rendering the same `<select>` row pattern against the same dashboard `defaultHandlers` map. The IntentsBus already reads pins by `osHandoffSignature` (`open:scheme:https`, `open:ext:pdf`), so the bus is unchanged — this iteration is purely the surface + the pure builder that fed it.

**The OS-handoff sentinel — the load-bearing piece.** Scheme + extension rows include a fixed pick `"Open with system default"` (app id `"__os__"` = `OS_HANDOFF_APP_ID`), always sorted LAST so it reads as the fallback choice. Distinct from the OS-handoff allow/deny **consent memory** (the prompt's sticky choice from slice 1) — this is a **hard pin** the user makes explicitly: "always open `https:` in the system browser". The bus's existing default-handler lookup already detects the sentinel via the same map lookup; the renderer's `<DefaultsAppOption>` is the only site that does sentinel-aware label substitution so no section paints the raw string.

**Files (the keystones).**

- `packages/shell/src/main/storage/registry-repo/openers-repo.ts` — new `listDistinctTargets(targetKind: OpenerTargetKind) → string[]` method. Single SQL `SELECT DISTINCT target … ORDER BY target ASC`. Dedupes when N apps register the same scheme/ext (e.g. browser + notes both claim `https`); the catalog wants one row per scheme regardless of who claims it.
- `packages/shell/src/main/intents/defaults-catalog.ts` — `DefaultsCatalog` grows `schemes: DefaultsSchemeEntry[]` + `extensions: DefaultsExtensionEntry[]` arrays alongside the existing `entries` (back-compat: emits empty arrays when the new inputs are omitted). New `OS_HANDOFF_APP_ID` + `OS_HANDOFF_APP_LABEL` constants and `DefaultsTargetKind` enum. `buildDefaultsCatalog` accepts four new optional inputs (`schemes`, `extensions`, `capableAppsForScheme`, `capableAppsForExtension`); a shared `buildSignatureEntry` helper does the sort + OS-handoff append + pin-lookup once for both scheme and extension paths. Pin signature uses `osHandoffSignature(OsHandoffSignatureKind.Scheme | .Ext, target)` so the bus reads the same pin via `resolveDefaultHandler(verb, signature)`.
- `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/dashboard-handlers.ts` — `dashboard:defaults-catalog` IPC handler now also feeds `schemes: openersRepo.listDistinctTargets(Scheme)`, `extensions: openersRepo.listDistinctTargets(Extension)`, plus the per-target capable-apps lookups via `openersRepo.listForTarget`.
- `packages/shell/src/preload/index.ts` — `DefaultsCatalog` interface grows `schemes` + `extensions`; new `DefaultsSchemeEntry` + `DefaultsExtensionEntry` + `OS_HANDOFF_APP_ID` re-exports. `setDefaultHandler` parameter renamed `entityType → signature` (wire-compatible — the IPC handler treats it as an opaque string).

## 2026-05-23 — B5.10 — Properties usage index (lazy property + dictionary-item counts; Settings → Data pills) (🟡 → ✅)

The shell half of B5.10 — the clipboard wire-format / paste-rebind keystone landed earlier as B5.10(a); this iteration ships the long-deferred usage index + the Settings UI consumer. Until today, Settings → Data was a flat list with no signal which property was carrying weight across the vault and which was leftover from an old experiment; deleting one was a guess. This lands the lazy index that answers "how many objects actually use this" and surfaces it on every property row + every vocabulary item.

**The pure keystone.** `packages/shell/src/main/properties/usage-index.ts` — five small exports, zero Electron / IO deps.

- `computePropertyUsage(entities)` — `propertyKey → count` of entities whose `properties[propertyKey]` carries a non-empty value. `false` / `0` count as values (they carry meaning in boolean / number columns); `null`, `undefined`, `""`, `[]`, `{}` do not.
- `computeDictionaryUsage(entities, propertyDefs, dictionaries)` — `dictionaryItemId → count` of entities citing that specific item through any vocabulary-backed property. Keyed by **item** id, not dictionary id, so the Vocabulary editor inside the constructor can render a per-item "used by N" pill next to each label. Multi-select arrays collapse to one credit per (entity, item) pair (`["red","red","blue"]` still credits `red:+1, blue:+1`). Archived items never receive credit (so an item-archive doesn't ghost a count back from older entities still holding the id).
- `computeDictionaryTotalsFromItems(entities, propertyDefs, dictionaries)` — derived per-dictionary aggregate, de-duped per entity (a MultiSelect with two items from the same dictionary still counts as one). Provided so consumers don't naïvely sum per-item counts and double-count.
- `class UsageIndex` — the lazy + invalidating cache. Holds the latest `UsageCounts` snapshot; starts dirty; `invalidate()` flips dirty; `snapshot()` returns cached when clean, otherwise runs one recompute that concurrent in-flight callers share (no thundering herd on a paste / import burst). Reader failures (entities read throws, catalog read throws) resolve to the frozen `EMPTY_USAGE_COUNTS` rather than reject — the broadcaster can't have a rejected promise leaking past `await`.

**Broadcast composition.** `properties-handlers.ts` grows a `PropertiesBroadcastSnapshot` type — `{ properties, dictionaries, usage }` — distinct from the store-level `PropertiesSnapshot` (which stays usage-free so the broker `properties.list()` proxy serves apps the same shape they've always seen). The handler now composes by calling `store.snapshot()` + `usageIndex.snapshot()`; the privileged `properties:snapshot` IPC channel carries the composed shape, the renderer-side `usePropertiesSnapshot()` returns it with `usage` typed in.

The handler exports a new `republishPropertiesSnapshot()` function — the entities-mutation broadcasters call it whenever entity state changes. Three call sites in `main/index.ts`:
1. the storage-envelope wrap (legacy kv-write of a `Note/Task/etc.` row),
2. the entities-service mutation wrap (`entities.create | update | delete` over `entities.db`),
3. `registerBinHandlers` → `afterMutation` (Restore / Purge).

Each call invalidates the cache + re-pushes the composed snapshot to the dashboard window. Properties-store changes (a property edit) also republish, because adding a new vocabulary item flips which item ids count as "live" — a recompute is required even though the entity graph hasn't moved.

**Session lifetime.** One `UsageIndex` per active vault session. `main/index.ts` adds a `usageIndex` slot next to `searchIndexer`; `swapUsageIndex()` runs inside the existing `onVaultOpened` chain (after `swapSearchIndexer`). On vault switch the old index is dropped (entity refs no longer apply); the new one starts dirty so the first read in the new session triggers exactly one recompute — no eager scan on swap. `PropertiesStore` is pre-opened so the catalog reader can stay synchronous (one `.snapshot()` call) — without this, the recompute would need a two-step async dance every time, and the dashboard renderer hits this path every time it opens Settings → Data.

**Settings → Data UI.** The renderer half threads `propertyUsage` + `dictionaryUsage` from the broadcast into the existing component tree without restructuring.

- `<DataSection>` reads both maps off the snapshot (falls back to a module-stable frozen `EMPTY_USAGE_MAP` while the first broadcast is in flight so `useMemo` deps don't churn).
- `<PropertiesPanel>` / `<VirtualizedPropertyList>` forward `propertyUsage` to each `<PropertyRow>` via the `usageCount` prop.
- `<PropertyRow>` renders a new `<UsagePill count kind="property" />` to the right of the kind badge — compact numeric chip (22px min-width, tabular-nums, 18px tall pill), `pointer-events:none` so it never steals the row click. `count === 0` short-circuits to `null` so the row chrome stays still on properties no one uses yet.
- `<PropertyConstructor>` forwards `dictionaryUsage` into `<VocabularyEditor>`, which adds the same `<UsagePill count kind="dictionary-item" />` next to each vocabulary item's label input — so a user editing the Status vocabulary sees that "Done" has 47 entities while "Wontfix" has 0 before deciding what to archive.
- `<PropertyRow>` delete-confirm grows a usage warning sentence (`shell.settings.data.properties.deleteConfirm.usageNote` — "Currently used by N object(s) — those values will become orphan rows.") appended to the body when count > 0, so deleting a load-bearing property is an *informed* choice. The same chip chrome lives at one place in CSS (`.data__usage-pill`) used by both render sites — the per-property and per-vocabulary-item pills are byte-identical.

**Tests (+18 in `usage-index.test.ts`, shell suite 1714/1715, was 1697).**

- `computePropertyUsage` (5): non-empty value counting; falsy primitives count (`false`, `0`); empty inputs; non-object payload (defensive); nested-empty object treated as no-value.
- `computeDictionaryUsage` (5): per-item credit with multi-value arrays + repeated-tag de-dupe; archived items skipped; unknown ids (stale references after an item delete) skipped; no vocabulary-bound properties → `{}`; no dictionaries → `{}`.
- `computeDictionaryTotalsFromItems` (2): multi-tag collapse within a single dictionary; empty dictionaries.
- `computeUsageCounts` (1): composite emits both halves with matching numbers.
- `UsageIndex` (5): caches until invalidated; concurrent in-flight callers share one recompute; entities-reader-throws → empty snapshot; catalog-reader-throws → empty snapshot; recover-after-failure via `invalidate()`.

**Verification.** `bun --bun vitest run packages/shell/src/main/properties` 60/60 green (was 42). `bun --bun vitest run packages/shell` **1714/1715** — the 1 failure is `vault-at-rest.test.ts > createVault stamps atRestMode=plaintext` timing out at 5s on Argon2id (pre-existing flake, reproduces identically on `git stash` without these changes; not addressed in this iteration). Workspace `bun run typecheck` (packages + apps) exit 0. `bunx biome check` clean on 8 touched files: `usage-index.ts`, `usage-index.test.ts`, `properties-handlers.ts`, `main/index.ts`, `preload/index.ts`, `data-section.tsx`, `settings.css`, `i18n/t.ts`.

**What's deferred.** The same pattern surfaces at three more places once they're built: Notes property-pane (per-note property usage drill-down — out of scope for B5.10), Database column-header (count next to a column name — folds into the per-column inspector at 9.12.x), Theme-editor token-usage (a parallel `index:token-usage`). The forward shape stays this lazy-invalidate + composed-broadcast pattern.

**Why this matters.** The vault-level property catalog has been a black box from the moment VP-2 landed — the user could see the list but not the weight. With this signal a user can confidently prune. It's also the first concrete consumer of the entity broadcast spine: the same `republishPropertiesSnapshot` plumbing is the template for any future "count things from entities" affordance.

## 2026-05-23 — 9.14.5 — Tasks inline property edits + edit popover (⚪ → ✅)

The Tasks app was a flat checklist — only the completion toggle did anything; chips, name, project, dates were all display-only. Direct user complaint ("i can only complete tasks but i cant change their properties or move them so i just see a todo list"). This iteration makes every visible property editable in place + adds an edit popover for changing several at once.

**The keystones.**

- `apps/tasks/src/ui/task-row.ts` — chips became real `<button class="task-row__chip task-row__chip--editable">` rendered for *all* fields including unset ones. Empty chips paint a dim dashed "Priority" / "Schedule" / "Inbox" affordance that fades in on row hover (so they don't crowd the populated state but stay reachable). Click each → calls the matching `onPickX(task, anchor)` callback with the chip element as the anchor. Name became a click-to-rename: `<button class="task-row__name-label">` swaps to `<input class="task-row__name-input">` on click; Enter commits the trimmed value, Escape cancels, blur commits; unchanged value short-circuits the patch. Double-click on the name host opens the new Edit popover. New `TaskRowProps` fields: `onPickPriority`, `onPickDate`, `onPickProject`, `onRenameTask`, `onOpenEdit` — added to `RowEditHandlers` in `surface-view.ts` so search + surface rows both wire them.
- `apps/tasks/src/app.ts` — adds `onPickPriority` (anchored menu via `openAnchoredMenu` with the 5 levels + the current one disabled as a marker), `onPickProject` (Inbox + every project, current disabled), `onPickDate` (small free-floating panel with `<input type="date">` × 2 + Clear/Apply, anchored at the chip via the same viewport-clamp/outside-mousedown/Escape pattern as `openAnchoredMenu`; **NOT** the shell glass popover — keeps it close to the chip), `onRenameTask` (single patchTask call), `onOpenEdit` (opens the compose-form-in-edit-mode popover). The Edit popover persists every field at once through the same patchTask path the inline chips use; notes-removal uses an `{notes: _omit, ...rest}` destructure to satisfy `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`. Object menu's `extraItems` gains an "Edit…" entry (between Pin and Remove) — uses the SDK's already-existing `extraItems` hook + `TaskMenuResolver` gained an optional `extraItems` field; no SDK change.
- `apps/tasks/src/ui/compose-view.ts` — full rewrite. `buildComposeForm({mode: {kind:"create",defaultProjectId} | {kind:"edit",task}, projects, onSubmit, onCancel})` serves both modes via a discriminator. Edit-mode prefills name + project + priority + scheduled + due + notes; create-mode seeds with defaults. Submit button label switches Create→Save. `formatDateInputValue` / `parseDateInput` exported for the inline date-chip popover to reuse.
- `apps/tasks/src/logic/compose-task.ts` — `ComposeTaskInput` learned `priority?: Priority`; `composeTask` threads it through (`input.priority ?? Priority.None`) so the create popover's "set priority during creation" is byte-identical to the inline chip path.
- `apps/tasks/src/ui/targeted-row-update.ts` — focus-restoration extended for the four new focusable controls (name label + priority/date/project chips) so toggling completion while focused on a chip doesn't drop focus.
- `apps/tasks/src/styles.css` — `.task-row__chip--editable` (cursor, hover border-accent, focus outline), `[data-empty="true"]` (dashed border, faded, opacity-0 until row hover), `.task-row__name-label` / `.task-row__name-input` (the swap), `.tasks-date-popover` (fixed-position glass panel + field/input/actions/btn variants), `.tasks-compose__textarea` / `.tasks-compose__row` (notes + 2-up dates in the edit form). All token-driven; no raw hex.
- `apps/tasks/src/i18n/t.ts` — +20 new keys (`tasks.row.chip.*`, `tasks.row.menu.*`, `tasks.row.date.*`, `tasks.compose.{title.edit,priority/scheduled/due/notes,save}`, `tasks.menu.edit`).

Empty-chip affordance for priority + date + project; click fires the corresponding `onPickX` with the row's task and the chip as anchor (cross-checks the anchor wire so the menu opens at the right point); project chip shows the project name when populated + omits when `showProjectChip:false`. Inline rename: click swaps to input prefilled with current name; Enter dispatches `onRenameTask` with the trimmed value; Escape cancels (no callback + input removed); blur commits but unchanged value skips the callback; double-click on the name host fires `onOpenEdit`.

## 2026-05-23 — 9.12.16-UI — Database Contacts import slice 1 (vCard / CSV via Files-host) (◑ → ✅ slice 1)

The G2 fan-out Database tail. The 9.12.16 keystones (`contact-import.ts` parser, `contact-import-plan.ts` dedupe + commit-plan, `import-registry.ts` generic per-type mapper registry) shipped earlier as pure-logic primitives; this iteration wires them to the Files-host service + an in-app UI so a user can right-click their People list and import a vCard / CSV from disk. **Slice 1 ships the foundation + the happy-path end-to-end with a count-only confirmation** — per-row preview-and-override grid is slice 2 polish (toggle Create→Skip per row, edit the merged property bag, see the existing-row diff inline).

**The mirror-of-9.17.8b pattern.** Where Whiteboard 9.17.8b ran the Files-host save flow through a tagged `SaveDisposition`, this iteration runs the **read** flow through a tagged `PickAndParseResult` (5 branches: `Cancelled | NoMapper | Failed | EmptyParse | Ready`). Same shape, same caller ergonomics — the UI switch covers every terminal state, no try/catch needed at the call site, never throws. The disposition pattern is now the cross-app idiom for both directions of the Files-host integration; the third consumer (Files app drag-export, future Books/Bookmarks import) drops in trivially.

**Files (the keystones).**

- `apps/database/src/logic/import-orchestrator.ts` (new, ~190 lines). `pickAndParseImport(files, {mappers, existing, title?, filterName?})` runs the pipeline: `requestOpen({filters})` → first handle's `displayName` → extension lookup against the caller-provided mapper list → `services.files.read(handle)` → UTF-8 decode (`{fatal:false}`) → `runImport(mapper, filename, text, existing)` → if `drafts.length === 0` then `EmptyParse`, else `Ready`. Five disposition kinds carry the exact context the caller needs (filename + extension on `NoMapper`, error on `Failed`, the full ImportRun on `EmptyParse` / `Ready`). `extensionOf` strips the lowercased tail after the last `.`; dotfiles + bare-trailing-dot fall to `""` → `NoMapper` (explicit beats clever for a surface that writes the vault). `activeImportMappers()` convenience snapshot walks the registry for the known extensions and dedupes by reference so a mapper serving multiple extensions surfaces once.
- `apps/database/src/ui/import-flow.ts` (new, ~220 lines). `runImportFlow(host, opts)` orchestrates the full pipeline including UI: pick → parse → confirmation modal → commit. Dispatches by disposition (silent on Cancelled; "Unsupported file type: .xml" on NoMapper; "Couldn't read foo.vcf: EPERM" on Failed with console.warn for the runtime error log; "Nothing to import" on EmptyParse). On Ready, opens a native `<dialog>`-based confirmation modal (focus trap + Escape + backdrop click handling for free) showing summary text + Cancel / Import buttons; on Import, runs `commitImportRun(commands, entities, targetType)` — per-command try/catch so one bad row doesn't kill the batch; partial-success surfaces in the toast as "Imported 8 of 12 (4 failed)". `summaryText` formats "3 new · 2 merge · 1 skip" (suppresses zero counts, returns "Nothing to import" for the all-zero case which also disables the Import button).
- `apps/database/src/app.ts` — calls `registerBuiltInImportMappers()` at module top-level (previously only fired from tests; the contacts mapper was unreachable from runtime). Adds the `files?` surface to the local `BrainstormRuntime` type (narrowed `requestOpen` + `read`). New `buildHeaderExtraItems(state, list)` returns an `extraItem` for the active list's object menu — "Import contacts (vCard / CSV)…" — gated on (a) the list targeting `PERSON_TYPE` AND (b) both `services.files` + `services.entities` being reachable. Graceful no-show otherwise; this is the established "hide when unbound" pattern from the 9.17.8b export side.
- `apps/database/manifest.json` — adds `"files.read"` capability (non-default; install-time grant; revoke leaves the rest of the app functional).
- `apps/database/src/styles.css` — `.db-import-modal` chrome (panel + backdrop + actions row + Cancel / Import buttons). Native `<dialog>` keeps the DOM small; the slice-2 per-row grid will swap to a richer shell-popover surface when the column layout demands it.

**Tests (+25, apps/database 319/319 green, workspace 5455/5455 green).**

- `apps/database/src/logic/import-orchestrator.test.ts` (+16). Every disposition kind on its own test: Ready happy path (2-row vCard parses + plans, run.commands ready to commit); Cancelled when picker returns `[]` (read NEVER called); NoMapper × 4 cases (unsupported extension, no-extension-at-all, dotfile leading-dot, bare-trailing-dot — each rejects without read); Failed when `services.files.read` rejects (error round-trips through the result); EmptyParse on a CSV with only a header row (the file is well-formed; the disposition says so). Case-insensitive extension match (`CONTACTS.VCF` resolves). **Dedupe-against-existing-rows** surfaces the Merge verdict — the load-bearing planImport contract under the dedupe-on-re-import behavior. requestOpen receives the dedupe-sorted `["csv", "vcf"]` extension list + `multi:false`. exactOptionalPropertyTypes title omit-vs-include fence. filterName overrides the default "Import" label. activeImportMappers convenience: returns contacts after register, empty pre-register, dedupes per-mapper-not-per-extension.
- `apps/database/src/ui/import-flow.test.ts` (+9). commitImportRun: dispatches create commands with host targetType (not a per-command type — contract fence); dispatches update commands; **per-command failure isolation** (one rejecting update doesn't kill the two surrounding creates); merge-without-update-method counts as failed (defense-in-depth for a future shell binding without update); empty-list no-op; targetType-not-overridden contract fence (commands don't carry the type; mapper-knowing-target is the contract). summaryText: zero-suppression ("5 new" not "5 new · 0 merge · 0 skip"); "Nothing to import" for the all-zero case (used to disable the Import CTA).

**What's deferred and why.** Per-row preview-and-override grid (slice 2) wants its own column layout + per-row toggle UI; punting until the v1 happy path is dogfooded against a real seed vault. Manifest test for `files.read` not added — apps/database doesn't have a manifest.test.ts harness today; the structural shell-level validator runs at install and catches drift in production. No PNG / icon / cover handling in commit — the commit path writes the canonical Person properties (name / email / phone / company / role / birthday) the parser surfaces; image attachments would need the chunked-upload 9.10a flow as a follow-up.

**Verification.** apps/database `tsc --noEmit` clean (the `import type` runtime trap). Workspace `tsc --noEmit` carries 1 pre-existing red from **untracked** parallel HPKE work in `packages/shell/src/main/credentials/hpke.test.ts` — empty intersection with this diff. `biome check --fix` clean on touched files (6 formatter rewraps — long object-spread blocks + style consolidation). **apps/database 319/319 green** (was 294 — +25 new + 0 regressions); **workspace 5455/5455 green** (was 5424 — +31 net incl. parallel HPKE tests landing alongside my +25). No flakes this run.

**Why this matters.** The Files-host integration now has both directions covered with the same disposition pattern (`pickAndParseImport` + `requestSaveBytes`). With Database 9.12.16 done, the remaining G2 fan-out items are the BP-block set (Tasks 9.14.3, Calendar 9.15.3, Bookmarks 9.18.4, Whiteboard 9.17.4/.7) — all gated on the 9.5.x install-flow source loader for app-contributed BP blocks. The dispositions + the orchestrator-takes-service pattern also unlock the Books app's EPUB / PDF import (when that ladder lights up) and the future Files-app drag-export. **Next natural pull**: Bookmarks 9.18.2b (Notes paste-URL → embedded-bookmark) is the smallest in-process BP-block-adjacent piece; or OpenRes-1c remaining UI slices (Settings → Defaults scheme/ext, "Why did this open here?" explainer) for shell-side breadth.

## 2026-05-23 — 10.2 — member-wraps schema + HPKE base mode + device X25519 keypair (G2 spine, ⚪ → ✅)

Clears the G2-spine rung that gates `10.3` Yjs envelope encryption: defines the on-doc shape of an entity's member wraps, lands the RFC 9180 HPKE base-mode crypto that mints them, and adds the device-side X25519 keypair the wrap addresses. Like 10.1, this is a primitive-shipping iteration — wire-path consumption is 10.3.

**The keystones.**

- `packages/shell/src/main/credentials/device-x25519.ts` (new module, 65 lines). Per-vault X25519 keypair, **orthogonal to the Ed25519 identity** (signing vs encryption stays separated; the well-known pitfalls of reusing curve material across primitives stay off the menu). API mirrors `identity.ts` for grep parity: `generateDeviceX25519`, `publicKeyFromSecret`, `publicKeyToBase64`/`publicKeyFromBase64`, `X25519_{SECRET,PUBLIC}_BYTES`. Persisted via the keystore under a new `device-x25519` account (the `KeystoreAccount` union widens from `identity|master|recovery` to `identity|master|device-x25519|recovery` — backends are generic, no per-backend wiring needed). +5 tests (sizes, deterministic derive, CSPRNG separation, base64 round-trip, boundary rejects).
- `packages/shell/src/main/credentials/hpke.ts` (new module, ~170 lines). RFC 9180 base mode (`sealBase`/`openBase`) on noble primitives. **Cipher suite pinned for v1**: DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) `kem_id=0x0020`, HKDF-SHA256 `kdf_id=0x0001`, ChaCha20-Poly1305 `aead_id=0x0003`. Single-shot only (the PSK + auth modes + multi-shot context machinery from RFC 9180 §5/§6 are out of scope — member wraps encapsulate a 32-byte DEK, nothing benefits from a long-lived AEAD context). Module structure: `encap`/`decap` for DHKEM, `keyScheduleBase` for the base-mode key schedule, `labeledExtract`/`labeledExpand` for the RFC's labeled HKDF, and `i2osp`/`utf8`/`concat` byte helpers. `SealBaseOptions.ephemeralSecret` lets tests pin the ephemeral key for the RFC test vector check — production callers omit it and get a fresh CSPRNG keypair every call. +9 tests including **RFC 9180 A.2.1 sequence-0 byte-for-byte vector** (info, skEm, pkRm, expected enc + ct all match — any regression in `extract`/`expand` labels, suite-id bytes, or `concat()` ordering is caught loudly).
- `packages/shell/src/main/credentials/member-wraps.ts` (new module, ~190 lines). The on-doc schema + the wrap/unwrap glue: `MemberWrapPayload = {v: 1, alg: "hpke-x25519-hkdf-sha256-chacha20poly1305-v1", recipientPubB64, encB64, ctB64}` (plain JSON inside a Y.Array — the wrap is opaque ciphertext, never edits in place, so no nested Y types are needed; a rotation appends a new wrap and revokes the old). Stored at `doc.getMap("brainstorm.meta").get("wraps")` — namespaced top-level key avoids collision with app types (Lexical uses `root`, CodeMirror its own). `getEntityMetaMap`/`getWrapsArray` are idempotent get-or-create. `wrapDekForRecipient(dek, recipientPub, entityId)` calls HPKE seal with **info = `brainstorm/entity-wrap/v1`** (binding name + version into the key schedule) and **AAD = `brainstorm/entity-wrap/v1:` || UTF-8(entityId)** (domain-separated prefix mirroring `ENTITY_DEK_AAD_PREFIX`; a wrap minted for entity X cannot be replayed against entity Y). `unwrapDekForRecipient` is the inverse. Read API: `listWraps` (skips entries that fail `isMemberWrapPayload` — forward-compat: a future schema bump can land on an older client without crashing the codec) + `findWrapForRecipient(doc, recipientPub)` (returns the wrap addressed to this device, or null). +16 tests (HPKE round-trip × 9 covering AAD binding / wrong-device-secret / tampered ct / tampered enc / per-wrap fresh enc / empty-id reject / wrong-size DEK reject + Y.Doc codec × 7 covering meta-map idempotency / list order / find-by-recipient / `Y.encodeStateAsUpdate` round-trip + state-vector exchange / payload-guard accept-reject / forward-compat skip).
- `packages/shell/src/main/vault/session.ts` — wires device X25519 into the session lifecycle. `create()` generates + persists alongside identity + master. `open()` fetches all three in parallel; if `device-x25519` is missing (pre-10.2 vault), **lazy-mints + persists** — idempotent (the next open reads the persisted key). New session API: `deviceX25519.{publicKey, publicKeyBase64}` (read-only handle for the wrap path) + `unwrapMemberWrap(wrap, entityId)` (encapsulates the secret; never crosses IPC). `dispose()` zeros the X25519 secret alongside the master key + identity secret. `VaultSessionMeta` gains `deviceX25519: {publicKeyBase64}` so UIs can render the device-pub fingerprint if needed (no consumer yet — Stage 10.5 pairing UX). +5 session tests covering provisioning, open recovery, pre-10.2 lazy-mint idempotency, `unwrapMemberWrap` round-trip, disposed-unwrap throws.

**Forward contract for 10.3.** The wire path MUST resolve the wrap with `findWrapForRecipient(doc, session.deviceX25519.publicKey)` and call `session.unwrapMemberWrap(wrap, resolvedEntityId)` — **`resolvedEntityId` from the row, never the caller-supplied id**. This mirrors the 10.1 forward pin: a Y.Doc pointer-swap attack cannot re-introduce the DEK-swap vector because the AAD recompute uses the canonical id. The unwrap module re-binds the entity id via `entityWrapAad(entityId)` so a wrong id fails closed on AEAD verification (exact same shape as `entity-dek-store.open`).

**Spike's static-static ECDH** is now superseded by HPKE; the spike's `experiments/sync-spike-10.0/src/crypto.ts` keeps the older shape as documentation but **production code uses the HPKE path** going forward. The 32-byte ephemeral pubkey budgeted in the spike envelope (`senderX25519Pub`) maps directly to HPKE's `enc` slot — no envelope-size impact.

**Ladder boundary**. Like 10.1, this iteration ships the primitives (mints the secret, defines the codec) but does **not** yet wire entity-create or the retro-wrap pass to write wraps into Y.Docs. That pairs with 10.3's encrypted-envelope wire path since both touch the Y.Doc lifecycle (loading the entity doc, applying one update, persisting the snapshot). Doing it earlier would build two parallel doc-write paths and then collapse them.

**Tests (+35, full shell suite 1696/1696 green).** `device-x25519.test.ts` 5/5; `hpke.test.ts` 9/9 (incl. RFC 9180 A.2.1 vector); `member-wraps.test.ts` 16/16; `session.test.ts` 25/25 (5 new). Vault + credentials subtree 153/153 green (was 118). Workspace `tsc:packages` clean. Biome clean on touched files (auto-formatted: import order in `session.ts` + `hpke.test.ts`; long-line rewrap in `hpke.ts`; redundant parens in `member-wraps.test.ts`).

**Verification.** `bun --bun vitest run packages/shell/src/main/credentials packages/shell/src/main/vault` 153/153 green. `bun --bun vitest run packages/shell` 1696/1696 green. `bun run typecheck:packages` clean (apps tsc unchanged — the one pre-existing apps/code-editor red is from another untracked iteration). `bun run lint` workspace-wide reports the pre-existing 1331-error backlog; on the 9 touched files it's clean post-format.

**Why this matters.** With member-wraps schema + HPKE wrap path landed, **10.3 is fully unblocked**: the Yjs envelope encryption can pull DEKs out of the on-doc wraps for any device the user has paired (v1: just this device), bind ciphertext to entity id via AAD, and round-trip through the blind relay without the relay ever seeing a key. The spike-positioned forward-secrecy property (per-wrap ephemeral key) is now structurally present — compromise of one wrap's ephemeral key affects only that wrap, no other. The audit surface is also tighter: HPKE base mode is RFC-9180-pinned to a single suite and the test vector pin will fail loudly on any future regression to the labeled-extract / labeled-expand machinery.

Picks up the Whiteboard 9.10-gated tail with the same `Save as JSON/SVG/PNG` shape Graph just landed at 9.13.13b. **The headline keystone** is the SDK extraction: per [[extract-to-sdk-at-copy-two]] + the CLAUDE.md DRY rule ("two call sites doing similar things go through the same helper"), the pure file-save helpers (`textToBytes`, `svgToPng`, `suggestedFilename`, `requestSaveBytes` orchestrator) moved out of `apps/graph/src/logic/graph-export.ts` into the new `@brainstorm/sdk/export-file` subpath — both apps now import from the SDK, no third app pays the duplication cost. The new orchestrator returns a tagged `SaveDisposition { Saved | Cancelled | Failed }` so the call site stays a switch, not three try/catch branches.

**Files (the keystones).**

- `packages/sdk/src/export-file/index.ts` (new module, ~180 lines + 220-line test). Surface: `textToBytes(text) → Uint8Array` (UTF-8 via a hoisted `TextEncoder`); `svgToPng(svg, {scale?}) → Promise<Uint8Array>` (renderer-side: SVG blob → `<img>` decode → 2×-scaled `<canvas>` → `toBlob("image/png")`; `URL.revokeObjectURL` in `finally` so even decode-failure leaks zero blob URLs; scale clamped to [1, 8] — under 1 defeats the hi-DPI intent, over 8 risks jank without quality gain); `suggestedFilename(stem, ext, {defaultStem?})` (FS-hostile char strip — `/\:*?"<>|` + ASCII whitespace controls fold to `_`; 96-char stem cap; caller-overridable `defaultStem` so Whiteboard can say "board" while Graph says "graph"); `requestSaveBytes(files, {suggestedName, filters, title?, encode})` returning `{kind: Saved, handle} | {kind: Cancelled} | {kind: Failed, error}` — never throws, every error collapses to the Failed disposition; `failureDetail(error)` (Error.message ?? String() — hoisted so the menu rows don't repeat the ternary); `SaveDispositionKind` enum; `SaveFileService`/`SaveFileTarget`/`SaveFileFilter` types (narrowed slice of `@brainstorm/sdk-types::FilesService` — apps don't need the full surface to wire one menu row).
- `packages/sdk/package.json` — adds `"./export-file": "./src/export-file/index.ts"` export. `vitest.config.ts` — adds the matching alias.
- `apps/graph/src/logic/graph-export.ts` — drops the local copies of the 5 helpers; keeps the Graph-specific `EXPORT_EXTENSIONS`/`EXPORT_MIMES` tables (they key off `GraphExportFormat` enum). Doc-header updated to point at the SDK module.

Net: the try/catch + early-return-on-null pattern collapses to a single `switch (result.kind)` — fewer branches, same behavior. Status-pill warn + console.warn for failures unchanged.
- `apps/graph/src/logic/graph-export.test.ts` — drops the 7 pure-helper tests that moved to the SDK suite (textToBytes, suggestedFilename × 4, table-coverage stays since it's domain-specific).
- `apps/whiteboard/src/storage/runtime.ts` — narrowed `FilesService` type added (`requestSave` + `write` only); `WhiteboardBrainstorm.services` gains the optional `files?: FilesService` slot.
- `apps/whiteboard/src/app.ts` — imports the SDK helpers; extends `buildExportMenu` with 3 new Save-as rows (JSON, SVG, PNG). ## 2026-05-23 — 9.13.13b — Graph export-to-file + PNG raster (G2 fan-out) (⚪ → ✅)

Picks up the last 9.10-gated tail in the Graph app. The Export menu now carries five `Save as …` rows alongside the existing `Copy as …` ones — JSON, DOT, GraphML, SVG (text-encoder path) + PNG (raster path) — each pumping bytes through `services.files.requestSave` → `services.files.write`. Cancellation is data (`requestSave → null` = silent no-op); failures surface through the status pill + console warn (the runtime error log is the dogfood signal). `Save as …` rows hide entirely when `services.files` isn't bound (standalone-dev, preview build, non-Electron host) — same graceful-no-show pattern Files-app uploads already use.

**Files (the keystones).**

- `apps/graph/src/logic/graph-export.ts` — new pure helpers below the existing text encoders: `EXPORT_EXTENSIONS` / `EXPORT_MIMES` tables (5 entries each: `json` / `dot` / `graphml` / `svg` / `png`), `textToBytes` (UTF-8 encode via `TextEncoder`, the byte format `files.write` accepts), `svgToPng` (renderer-side raster: SVG blob → `<img>` decode → 2×-scaled `<canvas>` → `toBlob("image/png")` → `Uint8Array`; scale clamped to `[1, 8]`; `URL.revokeObjectURL` in a `finally` so even decode-failure leaks zero blob URLs), `suggestedFilename` (filesystem-hostile-char strip: `/`, `\`, `:`, `*`, `?`, `"`, `<`, `>`, `|`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t` all fold to `_`; 96-char stem cap so an extreme-long graph name doesn't blow past common filesystem ceilings; falls back to `"graph"` when input is null / empty / whitespace).
- `apps/graph/src/app.ts` — `makeExportMenu` extended with the 5 save rows (only enumerated when `getRuntime()?.services?.files` is reachable). New `saveExportAsFile(state, kind, encode)` orchestrator: encoder is a thunk so the (potentially expensive) PNG raster only fires *after* the user commits in the picker; `requestSave({title, suggestedName, filters: [{name, extensions: [ext]}]})` follows the established Files-host pattern with format-specific filter list. Local `BrainstormRuntime` type narrowed to add the `files` surface (only `requestSave` + `write` — the two methods the export flow actually uses; the full `FilesService` shape lives in `@brainstorm/sdk-types`).
- `apps/graph/src/i18n/manifest.ts` — 9 new keys: `export.saveJson` / `…Dot` / `…Graphml` / `…Svg` / `…Png` + `export.saveDialogTitle` + `export.saved` + `export.saveFailed` + `export.saveUnavailable`. The Copy-and-Save split is deliberate — both surfaces stay available for users who prefer clipboard handoff to another tool over file save.
- `apps/graph/manifest.json` — adds `"files.write"` to capabilities (non-default; user approves at install or via Settings → Security; revoke keeps the clipboard "Copy as X" rows functional).

**Tests (+10, apps/graph 247/247 green, workspace 5365/5365 green).**

- `apps/graph/src/logic/graph-export.test.ts` (+9): `EXPORT_EXTENSIONS` covers every format the menu exposes (drift fence — a `Save as PNG…` click would land in the dialog with no default extension if the table desynced); `EXPORT_MIMES` parity; extension lookup round-trips the `GraphExportFormat` enum (rename-of-enum-without-table-update fence); `textToBytes` produces UTF-8 bytes (round-trips through `TextDecoder` on mixed Cyrillic + emoji — `"Привет"` + `"👋"` — so non-Latin labels in saved DOT/GraphML survive byte-level); `textToBytes` on empty input → zero-length array (not null/undefined); `suggestedFilename` composes `<graph-name>.<ext>` when clean; falls back to `graph.<ext>` for null/undefined/empty/whitespace; replaces filesystem-hostile chars with underscore; caps the stem at 96 chars.

No worker offload — measured-cost-threshold first: typical graphs (a few hundred nodes) raster in single-digit ms on a modern machine, well below the main-thread budget; if a 10k-node graph eventually hits the 16ms paint budget, swap to `OffscreenCanvas` + worker (the encoder thunk already shields the call site).

## 2026-05-23 — B6.4a — Notes `!@` transclusion lands (G2 fan-out) (🟡 → ✅)

The last open Notes-app G2 fan-out rung closes: typing `!@` in a note opens a typeahead popover that produces a block-level `TransclusionNode` carrying a live reference to another vault entity. Two `BlockEmbedNode`-shaped persisted fields (`entityId`, `entityType`, `label`) under a distinct discriminator (`type: "transclusion"`) + a distinct clipboard flag (`data-lexical-transclusion="true"`) — so paste round-trips don't conflate embed with transclusion and a freshly-imported document with foreign transclusion nodes paints a recognisable chrome card even before the live body-preview renderer ships.

**Scope (the contract).** Persisted shape is the load-bearing part — the renderer can be upgraded freely as long as `{type: "transclusion", version: 1, entityId, entityType, label}` stays stable. Walker edges (shell + app sides) emit `NoteReferenceKind.Transclusion` / `ReferenceKind.Transclusion` so downstream consumers (Graph paints transclusion edges; backlinks panel surfaces incoming transclusions; the future entities-service indexer at Stage 9.3 folds both walkers into one pass) see the new relationship kind without touching their render paths.

**Files (the keystones).**

- `apps/notes/src/editor/nodes/transclusion-node.tsx` — `TransclusionNode extends DecoratorNode<JSX.Element>`. Block-level (`isInline(): false`), keyboard-selectable. Same hostile-body hardening as `BlockEmbedNode`: `MAX_FIELD_LEN = 1024` per persisted field; `STRIP_FORMAT_CONTROLS_RE` strips ASCII C0 controls (U+0000-001F minus tab/LF/CR) + zero-width chars (U+200B-200F) + bidi overrides (U+202A-202E) + isolate variants (U+2066-2069) uniformly through `clampField` so every label / id / type comes out clean regardless of provenance (Trojan-Source / homoglyph defense). `entityIdToUriSegment` defangs `#` / `?` / `/` truncation in the `brainstorm://entity/<id>` href (the `brainstorm:` prefix already defangs `javascript:` / `data:` scheme injection — browser parses the whole URL as scheme `brainstorm`). Clipboard `exportDOM` emits a 3-element inline card (icon-box span with the `↪` glyph + body span with title + subtitle) — paste into Word / Gmail / Docs surfaces a visible card not a bare bold link; XSS regression-fence (`querySelector("script, img, svg, iframe, object, embed") === null`). `importDOM` matches the exact stamp `data-lexical-transclusion="true"` (not just presence; `="false"` and `=""` and plain `<a>` all reject) and rejects empty `data-entity-id` outright. Renderer v1 paints icon + title + "Transcluded {type}" subtitle; the live read-only inline body preview is B6.4b follow-up (needs YDoc resolution + depth-budgeted nested editor mount; the persisted shape is forward-compatible). Clicking the card dispatches `intents.open` through the shared `dispatchOpenEntity` so navigation travels the same path as launcher / right-click / Mod+K / mention chip.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/transclusion-typeahead-plugin.tsx` — `<TransclusionTypeaheadPlugin currentNoteId={…}>`. Mirrors `MentionTypeaheadPlugin` for the popover chrome + anchored-popover behavior + ArrowUp / ArrowDown / Enter / Esc routing through Lexical commands. Trigger detection runs against the single anchor TextNode via `detectTransclusionTrigger` (B6.4a(a) keystone, start-of-line / post-whitespace only — `note!@x` and `a@b!@c` never trigger). Picker queries `vaultEntities.list()` once per open. `applyTransclusionInsertion` splices `!@<query>` out of its TextNode via `splitText` + replaces the middle segment with a `TransclusionNode`, then ensures a fresh paragraph after the node for the caret to land in. Cycle/depth guard: v1 calls `resolveTransclusionTarget(host, target, () => [])` which catches `Self` (host==target). The deeper multi-hop check stays open — needs the YDoc-resolution edge map that B6.4b's nested renderer will already build, so wiring it now would be wasted work. The exclude-set on the picker results pre-filters the host so a Self-rejected row never appears (defense in depth + better UX than a dead-end pick).
- `packages/shell/src/main/entities/extract-note-references.ts` + `apps/notes/src/editor/extract-references.ts` — both walkers add a `TRANSCLUSION_NODE_TYPE` branch emitting `NoteReferenceKind.Transclusion` / `ReferenceKind.Transclusion`. Schema is **protocol** — the discriminator string + persisted-field names are what both walkers agree on, what's written to disk in the Y.Doc-backed body, and what the future Stage 9.3 indexer will read. Don't rename `entityId` / `entityType` / `label` without updating both walkers AND the node.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/notes-nodes.ts` — registers `TransclusionNode` in `NOTES_ADDITIONAL_NODES` so the live editor surface, the headless migration planter (`store/migrate-body.ts`) and any future serialization tool all see the same class. Drift = a planter missing TransclusionNode would throw on `parseEditorState` of a body containing one, fall back to the rebuild path, and silently strip the transclusion.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/editor.tsx` — mounts `<TransclusionTypeaheadPlugin currentNoteId={noteId} />` alongside `<MentionTypeaheadPlugin>` and `<BlockEmbedPickerPlugin>`.
- `apps/notes/src/styles.css` — `.notes__transclusion-host` (block margin), `.notes__transclusion-card` (36×36 icon slot — smaller than the BlockEmbed 56×56 so a transclusion reads as "live reference to elsewhere" not "generic preview"), `.notes__transclusion-card-icon` + `…-icon-glyph` + `…-icon-fallback`, `.notes__transclusion-card-body` / `…-title` / `…-type`, plus the popover chrome (`.notes__transclusion-menu`, `…-empty`, `…-row`, `…-row--active`, `…-row-name`, `…-row-type`) mirroring `.notes__mention-menu` family for consistency.
- `apps/notes/src/i18n/t.ts` — 9 new keys under `notes.transclusion.*` (region, empty, noResults, cycleHint / depthHint / selfHint for the not-yet-wired multi-hop verdict UI, untitled, typeUnknown, subtitle).

**Tests (+27, 499/499 apps/notes green, 5350/5350 workspace green).**

- `apps/notes/src/editor/nodes/transclusion-node.test.ts` (+10): JSON round-trip + `isInline`/`isKeyboardSelectable` invariants, `getTextContent` does not leak `brainstorm://` URI (screen readers / search index / markdown export want the label), `importJSON` clamps oversize fields (2048→1024) + strips bidi-override / zero-width controls from every field uniformly (the literal `"before‮​evil"` round-trips as `"beforeevil"`), `exportDOM` emits an `<a>` with the load-bearing flag + URL-encoded href for ids containing `#`/`/`/`?` + 3-element card chrome + no `<script>`/`<iframe>`/`<svg>`/etc, `importDOM` round-trips an exported anchor + rejects flag values other than `"true"` + rejects empty entityId.
- `packages/shell/src/main/entities/extract-note-references.test.ts` (+3): Transclusion edge surfaces from a properly-shaped serialised body, **Embed + Transclusion of the same entity stay distinct refs** (downstream Graph paints both edge types — they're different relationship kinds), malformed transclusions with missing/blank `entityId` drop silently.

## 2026-05-22 — OQ-CT-1 resolved → standalone Contacts app, shared `Person/v1` space (Stage 9.23 unblocked)

Closes the last "Tentative leaning: None yet" row in the G0 decision-queue table. **OQ-CT-1** asked whether the post-beta Contacts app should fold into a curated Database view over `Person/v1`, or ship as a standalone app. Position taken: **standalone app, mirroring the Tasks pattern** — a dedicated convenience UI for the daily-use case (people lookup, vCard import, relationship browsing), with the Database `All People` type-List staying as the power-user surface for ad-hoc gallery / board / kanban-by-tag / company-grouping cuts. The two surfaces share one `Person/v1` entity space through the canonical type registry; no data fork, no parallel schema, no per-app HTML — just a different UI over the same rows, exactly like Tasks vs Database `By Priority` board.

**What it unlocks.** The `9.23.1–9.23.5` ladder was previously gated as "Provisional ladder — do not build" because OQ-CT-1 could collapse the whole app to zero. With the position taken, the ladder is **buildable**: 9.23.1 scaffolds over the existing 9.12.13 `Person/v1` (no new type), 9.23.1.5 ships a preview over the curated People List, 9.23.2 reuses `@brainstorm/sdk/property-ui` for cells (the Notes+Database property-renderer), 9.23.3 wires relationship links + the 9.15.5 recurrence engine for birthdays, 9.23.4 rides the 9.12.16 vCard/CSV import keystones, 9.23.5 wires the Mailbox auto-resolution. **OQ-CT-2** (the `Org/v1` + `Person→Org` typed-link timing) remains open as scoped — answerable inside the 9.23 design pass, not a separate gate.

**Why this shape and not the other.** Two reasons surfaced in the position call:

  1. **The Tasks precedent works.** Tasks is a standalone app whose UI is the convenient daily-use surface for a vault-wide entity type; Database can still show those same tasks in a board, calendar, or timeline view by predicate. Contacts wants the same shape — a dedicated convenience UI for the common case, Database co-existing for power-user cuts. Folding Contacts into Database would mean the common case (open the app, see your people) requires the user to construct a view by predicate first, which is the wrong default for the daily-use action.
  2. **Schema ownership decouples from app ownership.** `Person/v1` is owned by the canonical type registry (same place Database, the seed, and the import pipeline already read it from). The Contacts app declares `entityTypes: [Person/v1]` in its manifest but does NOT redefine the shape. Result: a user who doesn't want the Contacts app can delete it — the data, the Database `All People` view, the 9.12.13(b) seeded `Birthdays` view, the vCard import path all persist. **The Contacts app is the convenience UI, not the schema authority.**

**Coupling to OQ-DASH-1** (the unpin-still-referenced-List concern) **dissolves under this shape**: the dashboard "Contacts" tile (whether app-icon-pinned or a `PinnedList: All People` preset) routes Person opens through the Contacts app's `intent.open(Person)` handler — same per-type routing as any other type-owned app. Unpinning the seeded List does NOT affect the app; they're independent surfaces over the same data.

**Touched.** `docs/reference/11-open-questions.md` (OQ-CT-1 entry — RESOLVED + position inlined), `docs/implementation-plan.md` (Stage 9.23 section — drop the "Provisional ladder — do not build" caveat, refresh the ladder to consume the resolved position). No code in this iteration — it's a structural position call that unblocks an already-scoped ladder.

**G0/G2 status check.** With OQ-CT-1 resolved, the G0 decision-queue's four burn-down rows now stand: #1 (OQ-10/26/27/28/29 sync) ✅, #2 (OQ-185 virtualization) — needs real-Electron measurement against the 9.3.5.N5 fixture, **G3 not G0 gate** in the updated roadmap (it's a 13.4a precondition, planned not reactive), #3 (OQ-12/OQ-8 BlockEmbedNode/frame) ✅, #4 (OQ-CT-1) ✅. **G0 is closed.** Contacts itself stays post-beta scope.
