449/449 notes tests green. 4689/4689 workspace tests green; the lone `Errors=1` from full-suite is the documented pre-existing apps/preview teardown flake (passes 178/178 in isolation, byte-identical to its pre-N4 shape, not a regression). Workspace `tsc` clean, `bunx tsc -p apps/notes/tsconfig.json` clean, biome clean on touched files, `apps/notes` build clean. Commits `5f1c81b` (builder) + `b78b11d` (integrator).

## 2026-05-20 — 9.3.5.N3 — Notes Lexical-yjs selection / IME / autosave parity (⚪ → ✅)

Rung 1 of the G1 critical-path spine after G0 cleared (10.0 sync spike + 9.10 files service landed earlier today). N2 promoted `<EditorYjs>` to THE Notes editor and dropped the body silo; N3 closes the parity gap so a user typing under the Yjs transport gets the same selection / undo / autosave behaviour the legacy editor gave. Four sub-pieces, one builder commit + one integrator fix.

### Sub-piece 1 — HistoryPlugin → Yjs UndoManager (verify-already-wired)

The N1 hand-off note flagged `HistoryPlugin` as "N3-deferred" because under collab Lexical's UndoManager double-applies with Yjs's. Reading `@lexical/yjs` 0.21's `CollaborationPlugin` shows it already mounts `createUndoManager(binding, binding.root.getSharedType())` inside `useYjsHistory` and registers `UNDO_COMMAND` / `REDO_COMMAND` — adding `HistoryPlugin` would have stacked two undo stacks. The right move is to **document the deliberate omission** so a future contributor doesn't try to add it; doc-comments in `packages/editor/src/editor.tsx` + `apps/notes/src/editor/editor.tsx` spell out the decision. The N3 test (`editor.test.tsx › Yjs UndoManager wiring`) asserts both commands have handlers registered on a fresh editor (proves wire-up without subscribing a second observer — no leak path introduced).

### Sub-piece 2 — Title seeding via `shouldBootstrap`-compatible initializer

Lexical 0.21's `CollaborationPlugin` forbids `editorState` and instead owns bootstrap behind its `root._xmlText._length === 0` gate. N1 explicitly punted title seeding to N3 because the previous `makeInitialState` path bypassed the CRDT. The N3 design: pass an `(editor: LexicalEditor) => void` closure via `<CollaborationPlugin initialEditorState>` so the seeder runs **once on the first attach to an empty root** — never on a replica that's already been seeded.

What landed:
- `packages/editor/src/editor.tsx` — `<BrainstormEditor>` accepts a new optional `initialEditorState?: InitialEditorStateType` prop, spread onto `<CollaborationPlugin>`. Additive; existing callers unchanged (prop identity preserved when undefined).
- `apps/notes/src/editor/seed-title.ts` (new) — `makeNoteBootstrap(storedTitle)`: trim → empty TitleNode (TitlePlugin's RootNode transform fills the "root.firstChild is a TitleNode" invariant) or TitleNode bearing the trimmed title + a trailing paragraph. Re-entrancy guard (`!root.isEmpty()`) on the closure itself so a misuse can't double-seed even if called inside an active editor.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/seed-title.test.ts` (new) — 4 pure tests (headless Lexical: empty / whitespace-only / present / re-entrant idempotent).
- Remote-replica idempotency test in `editor.test.tsx`: a second resolver pre-applies the encoded state from the first-seeder doc, mounts a fresh `<Editor>`, asserts the seeded title appears exactly once (a `body.toString().split(...).length - 1` count).

### Sub-piece 3 — AutosavePlugin first-real-interaction gate regression-fenced

The [[project_notes_autosave_swallows_first_edit]] invariant: AutosavePlugin must arm on real `KEY_DOWN`/`PASTE`/`CUT`/`DROP`, not on commit order. N2 reported the existing test stayed green through the transport swap; N3 adds an **explicit Yjs-transport-level** test that opens an editor, applies a programmatic `Y.Doc` mutation, asserts `onChange` does NOT fire over the 200 ms debounce window — then synthesizes a `KEY_DOWN` and asserts a save DOES fire. The original `autosave-plugin.test.tsx` is unchanged; the new test sits on top as a regression fence for the rewritten transport path.

### Sub-piece 4 — Body-derived sidebar / search snippet restoration

N2's paydown removed `StoredNote.body`'s role as the body-of-record (it now lives in the Y.Doc), which broke the sidebar list cards' body-snippet fallback when `title` is empty + the local-search fallback when matching body substrings. N3 restores both by **denormalising a length-capped plain-text snippet** back onto `StoredNote.body` on every autosave commit (gated by the first-real-interaction guard above, so the mount-settle echo doesn't re-fire). Cold-cache rows (notes never opened in this session) still show title-only — a N4 vault-open precompute would walk every doc and write the snippet once.

What landed:
- `apps/notes/src/logic/body-to-snippet.ts` (new) — pure `bodyToSnippet(body: Y.XmlText, maxChars): string`: reads `body.toString()` (the inline string content; collapses block-shape markers but keeps typed runs + mention labels), pipes through the shared clip helper. Cold-cache assumption documented (caller must hold a resolved doc).
- `apps/notes/src/logic/body-to-snippet.test.ts` (new) — 7 pure tests (empty / whitespace / collapse / cap with ellipsis / exact-cap no-ellipsis / custom max / Y.Doc encode-as-update round-trip to a fresh replica).
- `apps/notes/src/app.tsx` — `onBodyChange` denormalises `clipPlainText(extractPlainText(body))` onto `StoredNote.body` only when changed.

### Sub-piece 5 — Selection / IME parity (the rung's headline)

The first four sub-pieces + the existing Lexical-yjs binding give the parity. IME / real selection mechanics aren't testable in jsdom; the **mechanical proxy** N3 pins is **DOM node identity preservation on a remote update** — a precondition for any in-place selection or composition state to survive. `editor.test.tsx › selection / IME parity proxy`: mount editor, capture the contenteditable element, apply a no-op encoded remote update, re-query the element, assert it's the same node (a remount would invalidate the identity). Manual IME smoke on the running shell is the qualitative complement.

### Integrator fix on top — bootstrap closure stability (BLOCKER) + clip-plain-text DRY

The parallel review pass (4 reviewers, all clean except code-review) surfaced one BLOCKER on the builder commit:

**Identity instability:** `useMemo(() => makeNoteBootstrap(storedTitle), [storedTitle])` in `apps/notes/src/editor/editor.tsx` rebuilt the seeder closure whenever `storedTitle` changed, but `<CollaborationPlugin>` lists `initialEditorState` in its `useYjsCollaboration` effect deps. Combined with `storedTitle={note.title}` flowing through every title autosave's denormalisation — the user types in TitleNode → autosave fires → `update(noteId, {title})` → prop updates → memo rebuilds → effect tears down (disconnect provider, remove observers/listeners) and reconnects mid-typing. The seeder is idempotent so it's a perf + correctness churn, not a wrong-state, but it's the exact "silently fatal in apps/*" trap class.

**Fix:** the seeder only ever fires on the first empty-doc attach, so the initial-mount `storedTitle` is the only value that matters → `useRef`-once captures it for the life of the component instance. The caller's `key={noteId}` remount discipline gets a fresh seeder per note switch. **Regression-fenced** by a new test that re-renders with a changed `storedTitle` and asserts contenteditable host node identity is preserved (a tear-down would have replaced it).

**Also DRY'd** the whitespace-collapse + slice + ellipsis primitive across three sites — `app.tsx`'s `clipSnippet`, `body-to-snippet.ts`'s inline pass, `notes-list.tsx`'s `displayTitle` — plus a duplicate cap constant (`TITLE_FALLBACK_MAX` vs `DEFAULT_SNIPPET_LENGTH`). Extracted to `apps/notes/src/logic/clip-plain-text.ts` (`clipPlainText` + `DEFAULT_SNIPPET_LENGTH`) with 9 pure tests; idempotent on already-collapsed input so callers fed by `extractPlainText` don't double-pay. Three is the hard ceiling per CLAUDE.md §DRY; left at three was a rejection bar.

### Other review findings (deferred, not blockers)

Performance review (clean against documented budgets) flagged two latent issues to fold into the **N5 perf hand-off** rather than N3:
1. `bodyToSnippet` materialises the full `Y.XmlText` then slices — O(content) regardless of cap. Not wired into a hot path yet (only `clipPlainText` is fed from `extractPlainText`), so it's a future cliff for the N4/N5 caller, not a current regression.
2. `onBodyChange` walks `SerializedEditorState` twice per commit (`extractTitle` then `extractPlainText`). Pre-existing — N3 didn't regress it but didn't fix it either. A single combined walker would halve per-autosave allocation on large notes. Belongs in the 13.4a virtualization arc.

Security / memory-leak passes were both clean: no new IPC / capability / dependency / observer / timer / closure-retention; pure-renderer Notes-internal change.

### N4 hand-off

- **Snippet precompute migration.** The body-snippet path covers fresh + edited notes; a one-shot vault-open migration could walk every note's Y.Doc once and write the snippet into `StoredNote.body` to close the cold-cache gap. The pure `bodyToSnippet(body)` helper is already there for the caller.
- **`StoredNote.body` field type narrowing.** N3 always writes a `string` snippet. N4 can drop the union to `string` after the migration normalises any remaining legacy `SerializedEditorState` rows.
- **Bootstrap extension point.** `makeNoteBootstrap` only seeds a TitleNode today; per-app / per-type body templates (Journal date stub, Bookmark URL preview) plug into the same `<BrainstormEditor initialEditorState>` slot.

### Build + test signals

Workspace `tsc` clean. `bunx tsc -p apps/notes/tsconfig.json` clean. `apps/notes` 436/436 green; full workspace 4678/4679 green (the 1 red is a pre-existing `apps/preview` flake — passes 178/178 in isolation). `apps/notes` build clean. Biome clean on every touched file. Commits: `db35dfb` (builder) + `7791dee` (integrator fix).

## 2026-05-20 — 9.8.5 — Files create-flow upload via `files.requestOpen` (◑ → ✅)

The real half of the Files create-flow ◑: the `New ▾ → New file` entry no longer creates a synthetic `Untitled.txt` placeholder; it opens the OS picker via the **9.10** broker (`services.files.requestOpen({ multi: true })`), reads each picked file via `services.files.read`, and creates one `brainstorm/File/v1` per file with real `name` / `mime` / `size` / SHA-256 `hash`. Manifest declares `files.read` (non-default cap, install-time grant per the 9.10 contract).

**Why now:** 9.10 (Files host service broker half) landed in `044e096` and explicitly unblocks 9.8.5. The ◑ debt is "no `◑` in a v1 release build" (Legend policy + SH-31 audit), so converting now keeps the queue honest. Persistence boundary: `entities.create` write + `attachments/` blob copy (doc 42 §9.8.5) fold in at the Stage 9.3 entities-service swap — the `File/v1` *wire shape* (`name`/`mime`/`size`/`hash`) is what's durable today, not the mirror-only row.

**What landed:**
- `apps/files/manifest.json` — adds `files.read` to `capabilities` (manifest validator only checks the cap string against `CAPABILITY_PATTERN`; no allowlist, so the new cap installs cleanly; default-grants unchanged — the user approves at install).
- `apps/files/src/logic/upload.ts` *(new)* — four pure helpers, DOM-free + testable without jsdom: `mimeFromName` (compact typed extension→MIME map, default `application/octet-stream`), `splitName` (stem + dotted-ext; `.bashrc` is stem-only, the dotfile invariant), `collisionName` (insert ` (N)` *between* stem and ext so the MIME hint survives the rename — the Files-folder collision semantic), `sha256Hex` (Web Crypto `subtle.digest`; copies into a fresh `ArrayBuffer` so a `SharedArrayBuffer`-backed view still satisfies `BufferSource` under `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` — the strict-TS app-tsc gate the workspace tsc would NOT have caught, per [[feedback_app_tsc_not_gated_import_type_trap]]).
- `apps/files/src/types/runtime.ts` — adds a minimal `files?` shape (just `requestOpen` + `read`) under `services`, mirroring the local-shape pattern `VaultEntityShape` / `BrainstormRuntime` already uses (sdk-types stays the canonical surface, but the app declares only what it consumes).
- `apps/files/src/i18n.ts` — four new keys: `upload.dialogTitle`, `upload.filterAny`, `upload.unavailable`, `upload.readFailed` (every user-visible string wraps `t(key)` per the convention, [[feedback_keyboard_and_i18n]]).
- `apps/files/src/store/use-files-store.ts` — replaces the synthetic `newFile` (`tree.createFile({mime: "text/plain", size: 0})` + immediate rename-mode) with `uploadFiles`: `requestOpen` → for each handle → `read` → `mimeFromName` + `sha256Hex` → `tree.createFile({name,mime,size,hash})` → selection-set to the created ids. **Cancellation is data, not error** (`requestOpen` → `[]` → no-op; preserves the 9.10 picker-as-data semantic). **Missing `services.files`** (non-Electron / preview path) is a graceful no-op + a `console.warn` (lands in the runtime error log so absent-cap is observable). Name collisions in the active folder rename to `stem (N).ext` via `collisionName`. The exported store keeps `newFile` as a **back-compat alias** for `uploadFiles` so `app.tsx`'s `onNewFile={store.newFile}` keeps working — no renderer churn.
- `apps/files/src/logic/upload.test.ts` *(new)* — 12 unit tests over the four pure helpers (every fallback branch + the two FIPS-180-2 SHA-256 reference vectors so the digest is byte-exact under both Node and jsdom Web Crypto).
- `apps/files/tests/upload-store.test.tsx` *(new)* — 5 store-integration tests under jsdom + a vi.fn-stamped `window.brainstorm.services.files`: (a) two-file picker mock → two `File/v1` entities with the right `name`/`mime`/`size`/`hash` + `requestOpen({multi:true})` + localised title; (b) double-upload of `report.pdf` → second one is `report (2).pdf`; (c) cancelled picker `[]` → no entity created, `read` never called; (d) missing `services.files` → no entity, no throw; (e) `newFile === uploadFiles` (the back-compat alias pin).
- `apps/files/tests/manifest.test.ts` — +1 test pinning the new `files.read` cap.

**Decisions made:**
1. **MIME from extension, not bytes.** A bytes-sniffer adds a dep + worker; extension is exhaustive enough for v1 + matches what the file's *creator* asserted (the MIME hint is later overrideable via inspector). Default `application/octet-stream` preserves bytes verbatim.
2. **SHA-256, not BLAKE3.** Web Crypto already exposes SHA-256; BLAKE3 would need a polyfill. Hashing happens once on upload, not on every read, so the throughput delta is irrelevant. Doc 42 §9.8.5 just says "hash" — no algorithm prescribed.
3. **`newFile` alias kept.** App.tsx wires `onNewFile={store.newFile}`; renaming would churn the test snapshot + cross-app docs. The semantic of "New file" *is* the upload picker now (per doc 42 / doc 41 §New File (upload)); the identifier preserves the call-graph.
4. **No `attachments/` blob copy yet.** That belongs at the entities-service write seam (Stage 9.3) — the in-memory mirror is the *transitional* persistence. Calling it out here so a future 9.3 iteration knows where to fold the byte-store half.

**Deferred (still pending):**
- `entities.create` write path (Stage 9.3): the `File/v1` row currently lives only in the in-memory `FolderTree` mirror; vault-reopen drops it. The wire shape (`File/v1` with `name`/`mime`/`size`/`hash`) is the durable part.
- `attachments/` blob store (doc 42 §9.8.5): the bytes read via `services.files.read` are hashed + sized but not written to a vault-resident blob path. The handle itself is shell-scoped (the registry rebuilds on shell restart), so the bytes are *literally* only in the picker pass — the next read would need a fresh `requestOpen`.
- Aggregator menu via `intents.suggest({verb: "compose"})` (doc 42 §9.8.5 Tasks): the cross-app "New ▾" composer entries (e.g. New Note, New Task) ride 7.5+9.4 — not in this rung's scope.

**Build + test signals:** workspace `tsc` clean, `bunx tsc -p apps/files/tsconfig.json` clean, `apps/files` 147/147 green (18 test files). +17 over the 4609 N2 baseline → 4626 total.

## 2026-05-20 — 9.3.5.N2 — body-primary data model: 9.3.5.B reconciled + Notes silo dropped

Two-part iteration: **(a)** reconcile the 9.3.5.B universal-body keystone with the `@lexical/yjs` binding shape N1 surfaced as a design ambiguity, then **(b)** collapse the Notes silo onto the reconciled contract. Both halves were unsafe to do separately — the silo collapse depends on `useUniversalBody(doc)` returning the same root the editor writes to.

### Part (a) — 9.3.5.B contract amended

The N1 discovery: `@lexical/yjs` 0.21's `createBinding` hardcodes `doc.get('root', XmlText)` — a `Y.XmlText` named `"root"` — while 9.3.5.B's `UNIVERSAL_BODY_FRAGMENT_NAME = "body"` and `getUniversalBody(doc): Y.XmlFragment` named the body differently *and* typed it differently. N1 left both root types coexisting (the editor wrote to `root`/XmlText, `useUniversalBody(doc)` materialised an unused `body`/XmlFragment) and explicitly punted the reconciliation to N2.

**User decision (made before N2 kicked off):** amend B to match Lexical's convention. Cost is zero — no production data exists on either name yet — and forking `@lexical/yjs` for a custom fragment name would be a sizeable patch with ongoing maintenance for a load-bearing dep. The universal-body invariants (universal / lazy / not-a-property) survive the type change unchanged — Yjs encodes nothing for an untouched `Y.XmlText` root, and `@lexical/yjs`'s `shouldBootstrap` also writes nothing for an empty doc, so the lazy-zero-bytes property test still passes structurally on the new type (32-iteration loop, `Y.encodeStateAsUpdate` size equality with `clientID` held fixed across each pair).

**What landed (Part a):**
- `packages/sdk-types/src/universal-body.ts` — `UNIVERSAL_BODY_FRAGMENT_NAME = "root" as const` (was `"body"`); doc-comment rewritten to explain the WHY: the well-known name `@lexical/yjs` binds to, carrying the universal body via Lexical's own root preserves the lazy invariant and avoids a fork. `UniversalBodyFragmentName` stays the inferred `typeof` shape.
- `packages/sdk-types/src/universal-body.test.ts` — value pin (`"root"`) + type-literal pin updated; the structural shape of the test is unchanged.
- `packages/sdk-types/src/index.ts` — re-export comment updated to describe the new shape (`Y.XmlText` root named `"root"`, the well-known `@lexical/yjs` binding name).
- `packages/react-yjs/src/universal-body.ts` — return type `Y.XmlText` (was `XmlFragment`); body switches from `doc.getXmlFragment(NAME)` to `doc.get(NAME, Y.XmlText)`; `useUniversalBody(doc)` delegates to `useYText(body)` instead of `useYXmlFragment(fragment)`. `Y.XmlText extends Y.Text` so the existing `useYText` hook accepts the XmlText without further change.
- `packages/react-yjs/src/universal-body.test.tsx` — all six tests switched from `Y.XmlFragment` / `doc.getXmlFragment("body")` / `new Y.XmlElement("p")` to `Y.XmlText` / `doc.get("root", Y.XmlText)` / `body.insert(0, "…")`. **Lazy-zero-bytes property test stays load-bearing** (32-iteration property, clientID held fixed): an unused `Y.XmlText` named `"root"` produces zero encoded bytes — what `@lexical/yjs` relies on for empty docs to be empty on disk.
- `packages/react-yjs/src/{hooks,stores,resolver}.test.ts` — the B-era migration that swept these onto `UNIVERSAL_BODY_FRAGMENT_NAME` is intentionally reverted onto literal names (`"t"` for `Y.Text` round-tripping sites; `"frag"` for the one `Y.XmlFragment` site). These tests assert generic `Y.Text` / `Y.XmlFragment` round-tripping — NOT universal-body semantics — and the convenience of sharing the constant no longer fits: `Y.Text` named `"root"` and `Y.XmlText` named `"root"` are different types under the same Yjs root key, which would conflict if mixed. The reversal makes the *semantic* intent of each test obvious (this is generic Y.Text behaviour; the universal body has its own dedicated tests).
- `docs/data/21-objects-and-collections.md §Universal rich-text body` — Decision text amended to the new shape (`Y.XmlText` named `"root"`, the well-known `@lexical/yjs` binding name) with an explicit "retired in 9.3.5.N2 after the @lexical/yjs binding shape was confirmed" note. The "no migration impact" decision had a stale `getYFragment`/`applyDoc` reference that was actually the universal-body name — corrected to the current 9.3.2b transport names (`loadDoc`/`applyDoc`). No migration block: nothing in production exists on either name.

### Part (b) — Notes silo collapse

With the contract reconciled, the N1-era transport flag + parallel `<EditorYjs>` surface + legacy `<Editor>` (local-only) composer all become dead code. They were the N1 scaffold for the two-name coexistence; with one name and one type, there's one editor.

**What landed (Part b):**
- **Deleted:** `apps/notes/src/editor/transport-flag.ts` + `transport-flag.test.ts` (5 tests). The flag had no remaining purpose.
- **Deleted:** the legacy `apps/notes/src/editor/editor.tsx` (the local-only `LexicalComposer`-with-`editorState` composer that hydrated from `SerializedEditorState`). No other code path reached it after the flag was gone — `app.tsx` was the only importer.
- **Renamed + promoted:** `apps/notes/src/editor/editor-yjs.tsx` → `apps/notes/src/editor/editor.tsx`. The renamed file is now THE Notes editor (the name reflects reality — there's only one editor surface now). `EditorProps` lives here. The `initialBody: SerializedEditorState | string` prop was dropped (the universal body owns its own initial state via the `@lexical/yjs` bootstrap); `storedTitle` is retained as a `string` prop for N3's shouldBootstrap-compatible title-seeding command.
- **Renamed + rewritten:** `apps/notes/src/editor/editor-yjs.test.tsx` → `apps/notes/src/editor/editor.test.tsx`. The N1 design-ambiguity coexistence test was retired (the ambiguity no longer exists); three new tests were added pinning the N2 properties:
    1. *the universal body is actually written to* — after `@lexical/yjs`'s `shouldBootstrap`, `getUniversalBody(doc).length > 0` (was always 0 in N1 — the editor wrote elsewhere). **This is the load-bearing confirmation that N2's body-primary data model is real, not a name change.**
    2. *body survives a Y.Doc round-trip* — `encodeStateAsUpdate(writer)` → `applyUpdate(fresh)` → `getUniversalBody(reader).toString()` equals `writer`'s, end-to-end through the editor (bootstrap + binding produce the encoded state, not the test).
    3. *no parallel `body` root coexists* — `doc.share.has("body")` is `false`, confirming the prior contract's stray fragment is gone.
- The MentionNode persisted-shape protocol stayed unchanged ([[feedback_mention_persisted_protocol]]). A fresh round-trip test under the new transport pins `exportJSON`/`importJSON` field names verbatim against accidental drift.
- `apps/notes/src/app.tsx` — the transport ternary is gone (single `<Editor>` mount); the `bodyEqual` helper + body-write in `onBodyChange` are gone (the body lives in Y.Doc; only `title` is denormalised back into the StoredNote for the sidebar list). `AutosavePlugin`'s `onChange` callback signature is unchanged — `app.tsx` just stopped using the body half.
- `apps/notes/src/store/runtime.ts` — typed-comment refresh away from the N1-era `NotesTransport.YjsUniversalBody` reference.
- `StoredNote.body` field retained read-only as a grace-period legacy field. `parseStoredNote` still normalises it on load (so an existing kv blob doesn't crash), but the editor never writes to it. The cost: sidebar previews + local-substring search degrade to **title-only** matching for now — `notes-list.tsx` calls `extractPlainText(note.body)`, which returns `""` for an empty body, and the title-match branch above it carries the bulk of the cases. The proper restoration (a Y.Doc-walking body→text helper, or a FTS index feeder reading from the body) belongs to a later rung; flagged in the N3 hand-off.
- `AutosavePlugin` survives unchanged — its `userTouchedRef` first-real-interaction gate ([[project_notes_autosave_swallows_first_edit]]) is exactly what the new transport needs to avoid the mount/settle echo bumping `updatedAt`; the bug it prevents is identical on both transports.

### What's NOT in N2 (handed off to N3)

- **HistoryPlugin vs Yjs UndoManager.** The N1-era `HistoryPlugin` is still not mounted on the Yjs path. Yjs UndoManager owns undo/redo under `CollaborationPlugin`; stacking Lexical history on top double-applies. The proper N3 work is wiring a `Y.UndoManager` over the universal-body XmlText with the existing keyboard chords (`Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z`).
- **Title seeding via `shouldBootstrap`.** A fresh note opens with Lexical's empty doc; the existing `storedTitle` prop is unused. The N3 task is a `shouldBootstrap`-compatible initializer command that seeds a TitleNode + paragraph into the universal body the first time it's bootstrapped, mirroring the legacy `makeInitialState`'s `seedTitleAnd(text)` shape. `CollaborationPlugin` forbids passing an `editorState`, so this must run inside the binding's first commit.
- **AutosavePlugin dedupe** on the new transport (per N1's hand-off note). The plugin works correctly today (the existing `editor.test.tsx` and `autosave-plugin.test.tsx` are both green), but the first-edit cycle on a freshly-bootstrapped Y.Doc has not been spot-checked end-to-end — the prior dedupe rule was geared to a `SerializedEditorState`-stringify comparison, and a real-world Yjs commit cycle might surface a corner case (a hydration commit from a remote replica that the plugin should NOT treat as an interaction).
- **Body-derived sidebar/search snippet restoration.** Either a Y.Doc-walking body→plain-text helper (cheap per-note, expensive at scale) or a FTS index feeder reading from the body (cheap at scale, requires the feeder). The current title-only sidebar/search is acceptable as a grace-period regression; the proper restoration belongs to a search-index rung.

## 2026-05-20 — 9.3.5.N1 — Notes editor onto the Lexical-yjs transport, behind a flag

Composed the three Stage-9.1/.2/.B keystones (`useYDoc(entityId)` resolver, `<BrainstormEditor>`, `useUniversalBody(doc)`) into a Notes-side `<EditorYjs>` surface that mirrors the existing `<Editor>` prop signature exactly. App.tsx switches between them on a single explicit flag (`NotesTransport` enum read from `import.meta.env.VITE_NOTES_EDITOR_TRANSPORT`, default `LegacySilo`, override `YjsUniversalBody`). The flag is a temporary scaffold — it goes away when N2 collapses the silo.

**What landed:**
- `apps/notes/src/editor/transport-flag.ts` — `NotesTransport` string enum (`legacy-silo` / `yjs-universal-body`) + `getNotesTransport()` (reads `import.meta.env.VITE_NOTES_EDITOR_TRANSPORT` once at module init) + `setNotesTransportForTest()` (test-scoped override). Enum, not raw string literals, per CLAUDE.md §No raw string literals as discriminators.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/editor-yjs.tsx` — `<EditorYjs>` mounts `<BrainstormEditor>` from `@brainstorm/editor` over `useYDoc(noteId)` and threads the existing Notes plugin tree as `children`. Same `EditorProps` signature, same `NoteContextProvider`, same `editorTheme`. `useUniversalBody(doc)` is composed in as a change-signal hook (per the 9.3.5.B contract).
- `apps/notes/src/app.tsx` — mount-site branches on `getNotesTransport()`: `YjsUniversalBody` mounts `<EditorYjs>`, `LegacySilo` mounts the unchanged `<Editor>`. No other code paths touched on the legacy branch.
- `apps/notes/src/main.tsx` — `<YDocProvider resolver={getBrainstorm()?.ydoc?.resolve ?? null}>` wraps the app tree. The provider is optional: shells lacking `runtime.ydoc` (older / preview drops) skip it entirely; `useYDoc(entityId)` on the YJS path throws with a clear message if no provider is installed, which is correct since the YJS path needs it.
- `apps/notes/src/store/runtime.ts` — types the optional `ydoc.resolve: YDocResolver` field already exposed by the app preload at 9.3.2b (was untyped on the Notes side until now).
- `apps/notes/package.json` — adds `@brainstorm/editor` + `@brainstorm/react-yjs` + `yjs` workspace deps. Build green; lockfile regenerated.
- `packages/editor/src/editor.tsx` — additive extension: `<BrainstormEditor>` now accepts `additionalNodes?: ReadonlyArray<Klass<LexicalNode>>` (appended to `BASELINE_NODES` only when present, so `config.nodes` identity is preserved for existing callers) + `children?: ReactNode` (mounted inside the `LexicalComposer` after the baseline plugin set, so Notes' Title / Slash / TurnInto / Tables / Toggle / Embed / Columns / Mention / BlockEmbedPicker / LinkMarkup / Find / Autosave / BlockGutter / BlockSelection / InlineToolbar / Marquee / Media / context-menu / hint / Backlinks / AddPropertyMenu / CheckList / HorizontalRule / MarkdownShortcut / TabIndentation plugins all compose inside the Yjs binding without forking the editor package). `packages/editor/src/config.ts` widens `nodes` to `ReadonlyArray<Klass<LexicalNode>>` so additional-node arrays type-check.

**Design ambiguity surfaced (load-bearing for N2 — not a unilateral fix here):**
`@lexical/yjs` 0.21's `createBinding` **hardcodes** its root as `doc.get('root', XmlText)` — a `Y.XmlText` named `"root"`. The just-landed 9.3.5.B universal-body keystone defines body as `doc.getXmlFragment("body")` — a `Y.XmlFragment` named `"body"`. Both names AND types differ. Today's `<BrainstormEditor>` (and therefore N1's `<EditorYjs>`) writes to `root`/XmlText; `useUniversalBody(doc)` materialises the `body`/XmlFragment but the editor doesn't write into it, so it stays empty (the 9.3.5.B lazy-zero-bytes invariant survives unchanged). The third editor-yjs test pins this coexistence structurally. **The reconciliation is the architectural call gating N2 and the cross-app universal-body editor surface (Tasks / Bookmarks workflows)**: either fork `@lexical/yjs` to accept a custom fragment name (sizeable patch, ongoing maintenance), or amend the universal-body contract from `XmlFragment` named `"body"` to `XmlText` named `"root"` (changes doc 21 §Universal rich-text body + the just-landed `UNIVERSAL_BODY_FRAGMENT_NAME` constant). Both options retain the lazy-zero-bytes property; neither is unilateral N1 scope.

**Plugins confirmed parity (mounted on the YJS path through `<EditorYjs>`):** Title / Slash / TurnInto / Tables / Toggle / Embed / Columns / Mention / BlockEmbedPicker / LinkMarkup / Find / Autosave (dual-write — silo persists alongside Yjs; N2 drops the silo write) / BlockGutter / BlockSelection / InlineToolbar / Marquee / Media (drop+inspector) / context-menu / EmptyParagraphHint / Backlinks / AddPropertyMenu / CheckList / HorizontalRule / MarkdownShortcut / TabIndentation.

**Plugins N3-deferred:**
- `HistoryPlugin` — Yjs UndoManager owns undo/redo under collab; stacking Lexical history on top double-applies (the package doc on `<BrainstormEditor>` is explicit about this).
- `ListPlugin` + `LinkPlugin` — already mounted by `<BrainstormEditor>`'s baseline tree; would double-register if added by the child plugin set.
- `makeInitialState` / title seeding from `storedTitle` — collab owns initial bootstrap (the package doc explicitly forbids `editorState`). The Yjs-path editor opens with Lexical's empty doc; title-seed-from-`storedTitle` needs a `shouldBootstrap`-compatible initializer command, which lands at N3.

**Behind the flag-off branch:** byte-identical to today's path. Legacy `<Editor>` mount is unchanged; no edits to the legacy autosave, init, or codec paths. The only legacy-path code-adjacent change is the `<YDocProvider>` wrap at `main.tsx`, which short-circuits on shells without `runtime.ydoc` and is a no-op for the `<Editor>`-only path. The 411 existing notes tests all stay green, untouched.

**Tests (+9 new):**
- `apps/notes/src/editor/transport-flag.test.ts` (5) — enum wire-format pin (the two strings appear in CI / dev `.env` files; changing them silently unpins the flag), default `LegacySilo` baseline, override to `YjsUniversalBody`, override to `LegacySilo`, override null-reset.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/editor-yjs.test.tsx` (4) — `<EditorYjs>` mounts a `[contenteditable=true]` element and Lexical's binding installs `doc.share.has("root")` + `doc.get("root", XmlText) instanceof XmlText` inside the resolver-minted doc; two `<EditorYjs>` instances on the same `noteId` resolve to the same doc (refcounted by the YDocResolver core); the design-ambiguity test pins the `root`/XmlText vs `body`/XmlFragment coexistence; bootstrap-smoke pins that the binding actually ran inside the resolver's doc (a different doc would have left `share.has("root")` false).

**Verification status:**
- `bun --bun vitest run apps/notes` → 412/412 green (411 unchanged + 9 new — the +9 already includes the 4 added editor-yjs cases; the legacy AutosavePlugin + Editor + everything else stay green untouched).
- `bun --bun vitest run` (workspace) → 4611/4611 green across 465 files.
- `bun run typecheck` → clean.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit -p apps/notes/tsconfig.json` → clean (per CLAUDE.md "type-only import" trap discipline; the workspace gate doesn't cover `apps/*` and Vite strips type-only imports).
- `biome check` on touched files → clean (workspace baseline of 123 pre-existing diagnostics on `main` unchanged — 4 fewer than the 127 baseline before this iteration, owing to auto-formatting on touched files).
- `bun run --filter @brainstorm-app/notes build` → green.

**OQ-resolved:** none (per the brief — N1 doesn't resolve an OQ). The design ambiguity above will surface as a new OQ when N2's design lands.



Shipped the **shared contract** for the universal `body` `Y.XmlFragment` every entity carries (per [docs/data/21 §Universal rich-text body](data/21-objects-and-collections.md), user directive 2026-05-15). Pure contract iteration — no Notes editor swap (that's N1), no per-app surfacing (that's the workflow rungs). The point is that N1–N5 (and every future per-app body editor) can `import { UNIVERSAL_BODY_FRAGMENT_NAME, getUniversalBody, useUniversalBody }` from one place instead of hand-typing `"body"` at each call site.

**What landed:**
- `packages/sdk-types/src/universal-body.ts` — `UNIVERSAL_BODY_FRAGMENT_NAME = "body" as const` + `UniversalBodyFragmentName` literal-type alias; re-exported from `packages/sdk-types/src/index.ts`. The doc-comment carries the WHY (the universal / lazy / not-a-property invariants from doc 21).
- `packages/react-yjs/src/universal-body.ts` — `getUniversalBody(doc: Doc): XmlFragment` (one-line wrapper around `doc.getXmlFragment(UNIVERSAL_BODY_FRAGMENT_NAME)` so a typo is impossible) + `useUniversalBody(doc: Doc): XmlFragment` (React hook that delegates to the existing `useYXmlFragment(doc, …)`, mirroring the hook pattern); both re-exported from `packages/react-yjs/src/index.ts`. `@brainstorm/sdk-types` added as a `workspace:*` dependency on `@brainstorm/react-yjs` (it's a runtime value, not a type-only import — guarding against the [[feedback_app_tsc_not_gated_import_type_trap]] pattern at the package level).

**Tests:** +13 new across 2 files (32 if you count the migrated existing tests that now exercise the constant), `bun --bun vitest run packages/react-yjs/src/ packages/sdk-types/src/` green 30/30 stress runs:
- `packages/sdk-types/src/universal-body.test.ts` (2) — value pin (`"body"`) + type pin (the round-trip through `UniversalBodyFragmentName` proves the string-literal type, not `string`).
- `packages/react-yjs/src/universal-body.test.tsx` (6) — identity (Yjs caches by name → same fragment instance through both call sites and direct `doc.getXmlFragment` access), universality (callable on 10 mock docs with arbitrary other state), **lazy-zero-bytes property test** (32-iteration loop: `Y.encodeStateAsUpdate(baseline).length === Y.encodeStateAsUpdate(observed).length` with `clientID` held fixed across each pair so the VarUint encoding is byte-stable — pins the load-bearing "an unused body is zero storage" claim from doc 21 structurally, not as a vibes claim), monotone-write-size invariant (only a real body insert inflates encoded bytes; the property-write→body-write deltas both increase the encoded length), roundtrip (`Y.encodeStateAsUpdate` after a `<p>`-insert applies cleanly into a fresh doc + reproduces the same `XmlFragment.toJSON()` / nodeName), `useUniversalBody` hook (jsdom React render — returned fragment is identity-stable across renders and the component re-renders on body mutation).
- Existing fragment-name sites migrated to the constant: `packages/react-yjs/src/resolver.test.ts` (14 sites — all the `getText("body")` instances in the snapshot/edit/refcount/dispose/cross-window-convergence suites), `packages/react-yjs/src/stores.test.ts:10/126`, `packages/react-yjs/src/hooks.test.tsx:43/83` (Y.Text-named "body" and Y.XmlFragment-named "body" both grep'able through the constant now; the migration is conservative — only sites that name the universal-body root, not unrelated `"body"` strings in CSS / Settings copy / layout tests).

`packages/shell/src/main/entities/kv-entities-backfill.ts:96` — the `"body"` here is a **kv-row property key in a projection comparison** (`["name", "title", "icon", "body"]`), not the Yjs fragment name. Left alone (conservative-migration discipline).

**Out-of-scope finds (flagged, not migrated):** `packages/shell/src/preload/app-preload.ts:261` has `getYFragment: async (entityId, propertyPath = "body")` — the default of `"body"` here is the same universal-body convention this iteration centralises, but the brief explicitly scoped the migration to the listed test sites. Worth folding into the constant on the next 9.3.2b touch (single-line change). Other `getText("body")` sites in `packages/shell/src/workers/ydoc/ydoc.test.ts` and `packages/shell/src/main/storage/ydoc-store.test.ts` are also unmigrated for the same reason — they use `"body"` as a generic Y.Text name for transport / persistence tests, not specifically the universal body.

**Ambiguity surfaced:** the design doc reference `getYFragment(entityId, "body")` (doc 21 §Universal rich-text body) is the **preload bridge's** entity-id-taking helper (already implemented in `app-preload.ts:261`), distinct from this iteration's `Doc`-taking `getUniversalBody(doc)`. They're complementary — the preload form resolves through the YDoc resolver, the doc form is the leaf that names the fragment. N1 will compose them: `editor` calls `useUniversalBody(useYDoc(entityId))` once the resolver is wired through. No ambiguity needs surfacing past this entry — the doc-21 wording was about the fragment name, which both forms agree on.

`bun run typecheck` clean. `bun --bun vitest run packages/react-yjs/src/ packages/sdk-types/src/` green (248 tests across 21 files including 32 in the touched / migrated files). `biome check` clean on every touched file (pre-existing 479 repo-wide diagnostics on `main` unchanged — confirmed by stashed-baseline run). No new dependency. No OQ resolved (OQ-DM-1 is already resolved). The N1–N5 chain is now unblocked at the contract level.

## 2026-05-20 — 0.11 — three new dev-MCP audit tools

Shipped the three per-PR / per-stage audit tools the `0.11` iteration in [`docs/implementation-plan.md`](implementation-plan.md) gated on, all in `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/`:

**`audit.stage_boundary`** — `(stageId) → { snapshot, baseline, drift }`. Pure helpers in `stage-boundary-audit.ts` snapshot a stage's iteration counts by status, the resolved + open OQ counts (matching `Stage N` mentions in `where` / `section` / `body` / `resolution`, with a word-boundary regex so `Stage 3` doesn't false-match `Stage 30`), the preview-drop tail (`Partial` iterations whose body carries a `gate:` / `BLOCKED:` marker per the SH-31 pattern), and the heading + status. `stage-boundary-baselines.ts` pins the **10 Stage 0–7 floors** (0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 5b / 6 / 7a / 7b) as a frozen record; `diffBaseline` reports drift kinds (`StatusRegressed` / `DoneCountRegressed` / `ResolvedOQCountRegressed` / `NoBaseline` / `Ok`). The doc-stated "stages-0-7 audits replay as baselines" rule is now a structural assertion: a stage whose `Done`-count or `Resolved`-OQ-count drops below the 2026-05-20 floor fails the suite, not the next audit doc. **First live finding:** all 10 baselines hold today (zero drift); Stage 0 reports 8/11 done — the residual 3 are 0.11 (this iteration, closing now), 0.12 (next), and the 0.10 sub-iteration nested under the same `Done` bullet (counted as `Pending` because the per-section bullet for 0.10.1's nested entries hasn't been split out yet — design note, not a regression).

**`capability.diff`** — `(beforeRef, afterRef) → { added, removed, narrowed, widened, byApp }`. Pure helpers in `capability-diff.ts`: `parseCapability` (kept symmetric with `main/capabilities/ledger.ts`'s same-name helper), `compareScopeBreadth` (`null` ↔ `*` are equal breadth per the ledger match rule; specifics are narrower; two distinct specifics are non-comparable → fall through to added+removed), `diffCapabilitySurface` (collapses single-scope-per-side `(app, cap)` changes into narrow/widen; multi-scope-on-one-side stays in added+removed). The MCP-tool wrapper spawns `git show <ref>:apps/<id>/manifest.json` for every app via `readAppManifestsAtRef`; `--local` compares the uncommitted working tree against a ref. The "did this PR silently add a new IPC surface?" review-time question is now answerable from the dev-MCP without a reviewer remembering to grep manifests. **First live finding:** across `HEAD~10..HEAD`, the **only** capability surface change is `io.brainstorm.files` adding `entities.read:*` — exactly commit `8893181` ("files: grant entities.read:* (was vault-entities.list — wrong cap id)"). The tool surfaces the audit trail clean.

**`keyboard.find_raw_keys`** — `(files) → KeyboardViolation[]`. Pure TS-AST walk in `keyboard-raw-keys-check.ts` (mirrors 12.9 `type-import-check`): flags `event.<key|code|keyCode|which>` access on identifiers named `event` / `e` / `ev` / `evt` in value positions (comparisons, method chains, args, switch discriminants), plus raw `addEventListener("keydown"|"keyup"|"keypress", …)` calls outside the shortcut-registry allowlist (`renderer/shortcuts/**`, `sdk/src/shortcut/**`, `sdk/src/find-replace/**`, `sdk/src/popover/**`, `sdk/src/object-menu/**`, per-app `*shortcuts.ts` / `keyboard/**`). Escape hatch: `// keyboard-exempt` on or above the line — pairs with the SH-32 orphan-exempts audit so the gate's authority can't erode. Modifier predicates (`event.shiftKey` / `metaKey` / `ctrlKey` / `altKey`) are intentionally **not** flagged (chord-parsing reads them; they're not raw keys). Repo-wide CI guard uses the SH-31 / SH-32 `KNOWN_VIOLATION_PATHS` pattern: pre-existing raw-key sites snapshotted, new sites fail, stale snapshot entries (sites later migrated) also fail. **First live finding:** **31 raw-key sites across 11 files** in the live repo — biggest cluster `apps/database/src/app.ts` (14 sites, the largest pre-React imperative renderer), then `apps/database/src/ui/view-settings.ts` (4), `apps/notes/src/editor/nodes/equation-node.tsx` (3), `apps/files/src/ui/content-list.tsx` + `apps/notes/src/editor/link-markup-plugin.tsx` (2 each), and one each in `apps/code-editor/src/demo/dataset.ts` (a `Map.set(e.key, e)` over an iterator entry — non-keyboard false-positive class documented in the test rig), `apps/database/src/react/{board,gallery,grid,list}-view.tsx` (one each, inline rename), and `packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard/window-strip.tsx` (a `keydown` dismiss of an open context menu — legitimately not chord-matching). The latter three classes become Stage-9 migration tickets when the React rebuild touches them; the dataset false-positive stays in the snapshot until the Map iteration is refactored.

**Wiring + tests + signals:**
- `server.ts` registers all three tools (`audit.stage_boundary`, `capability.diff`, `keyboard.find_raw_keys`) alongside the existing audit / coverage / orchestration tool set.
- **+74 tests in 3 new test files:** `keyboard-raw-keys-check.test.ts` 20 (synthetic AST cases + repo-wide guard with stale-snapshot pairing), `capability-diff.test.ts` 23 (parseCapability/formatCapability round-trip, compareScopeBreadth all six branches, manifestsToSurfaces malformed-tolerance, the four diff classes end-to-end, byApp rollup, identical-snapshot no-op), `stage-boundary-audit.test.ts` 31 (counting helpers, preview-drop detection, OQ-stage matching including substring rejection, snapshotStage roll-up, every `BaselineDriftKind`, `baselineFor` over all 10 stages, fixture-locking + live-repo baseline pinning).
- mcp-server suite: **422 → 496** (+74), all 40 files green; workspace `tsc` clean; biome lint clean on every new file.
- The 0.11 inventory adds the **eleventh structural CI gate** (12.2 / 12.9 / 12.10 / 12.11 / 12.12 / 12.13 / 12.14 / SH-30 / SH-31 / SH-32 / **0.11-keyboard**). The keyboard guard inherits the `KNOWN_*` snapshot pattern so it locks in forward without forcing a 31-site migration in this iteration.

**Why this iteration mattered:** The audit doc tradition in `docs/_review/` was prose-only; a stage's "did Done iterations stay done" check was a vibes review. This pins it. Same for the capability surface — until now, a PR adding `intents.dispatch:open` to an app's manifest got a reviewer's "looks fine" with no structural anchor. Now `capability.diff HEAD~1 HEAD` is a literal one-line PR-template addition. The keyboard guard is the harshest gate of the three — it would have caught the equation-node + database-app raw-key leaks during 9.12.x landing if it had existed, and it now blocks every future leak past the day-one chord-parser modules.

## 2026-05-20 — 9.10 — Files host service (broker half) + `files.read` / `files.write` caps + Settings revoke panel

Closed the half of Stage 9.10 the registry keystone landed for: the `files` broker service every app uses to open / save / read / write user-chosen files, with the privileged Settings → Security "Open files" panel as the user's kill switch. **Apps still never see filesystem paths** — the registry mints opaque tokens, this service is the single gate that swaps token → path inside the trusted main process. Five downstream tails are now unblocked (per the plan): 9.13.13b (Graph export-to-file), 9.17.8b (Whiteboard export-to-file), Database 9.12.16-UI (CSV / vCard import dialog), Books 9.21.2 (EPUB reader file import), Files 9.8.5 (create-flow upload path).

**What landed:**
- `packages/shell/src/main/files/files-service.ts` — broker service handler with seven methods: `requestOpen` (returns `FileHandle[]`; cancellation is `[]`, NOT a thrown denial — the broker would otherwise audit a user-cancelled picker), `requestSave` (returns `FileHandle | null`; same cancellation discipline), `read` ({ base64 } reply, capped at `MAX_WRITE_BYTES` — symmetric ceiling with write, 9.10a lifts both via streaming), `write` (`decodeWriteData` rejection paths map to `Invalid`, never throw into the FS), `watch` + `unwatch` (`node:fs.watch` underneath, broadcast via `app:files-watch` channel to every window of the owning app, `MAX_WATCHES_PER_APP = 128` ceiling so a misbehaving app can't exhaust `inotify`), `handleFromIntent` (the cross-app pass-through — the producing app attaches its token to an intent payload, the receiver's `handleFromIntent` call hits the registry's shell-internal `resolveAny`, a fresh read-only handle is minted scoped to the receiver who never sees the source token / source app id / path). Every method is fail-closed on cross-app handle theft (registry `resolve` returns `null`, handler maps to `Invalid`); injected `showOpenDialog`/`showSaveDialog`/`readFile`/`writeFile`/`watchFile` so the unit tests don't hit real disk or real pickers.
- `packages/shell/src/main/files/file-handle-registry.ts` — extended the 9.10(a) keystone with `resolveAny(token)` (shell-internal lookup that doesn't require knowing the owning app — used only by `handleFromIntent` so the receiver can't enumerate other apps' tokens) and `onChange(listener)` (notify on every mint / revoke, idempotent unsubscribe, throwing listeners survive). The Settings panel + the broadcast subscribe through it; mints are notified once, idempotent re-mints are not (no spurious churn).
- `packages/shell/src/main/vault/session.ts` — `VaultSession.fileHandles` (new readonly `FileHandleRegistry` instance — one per active vault session, in-memory only by design; a vault close drops every handle, apps re-pick on next launch). The handle registry is per-vault because cross-vault token leakage would be a security boundary breach.
- `packages/shell/src/main/capabilities/default-grants.ts` — `files.read` / `files.write` added to the **shell**'s grant set (the Settings panel + future shell-side import flows need them) but **NOT** to `DEFAULT_APP_CAPABILITIES` — apps declare them in the manifest and the user approves at install. This is the load-bearing security split.
- `packages/shell/src/main/index.ts` — wires the service into the broker on top of the existing covers / blocks registrations. `showOpenDialog` / `showSaveDialog` parent on `dashboardWindow` when available so the picker is modal to the right window; `emitWatch` fans into `launcher.windowsFor(appId)` so a cross-app subscription leak isn't possible at the IPC layer either.
- `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/files-handles-handlers.ts` — privileged `files-handles:list` / `files-handles:revoke` ipcMain handlers + the `app:files-handles-changed` broadcast channel. The dashboard renderer is the only renderer wired to these (apps go through the broker). The list payload carries the absolute path so the user can see what they're revoking — that's the whole point of the panel. The change-broadcast wiring resubscribes on every `setActiveVaultSession` so the panel stays live across vault switches.
- `packages/shell/src/preload/index.ts` — `brainstorm.filesHandles.{list,revoke,on}` surface exposed to the dashboard renderer; mirrors the `covers` / `ledger` shape.
- `packages/shell/src/preload/app-preload.ts` — `app:files-watch` listener fans per-subscription events to the right per-app callback; `runtime.services.files.watch` overlay returns a `Subscription` that registers/deregisters the callback + sends the unwatch envelope (the SDK default proxy alone cannot do this — broker is request/reply).
- `packages/sdk/src/runtime.ts` — replaced the throw-Unavailable placeholder with a real `filesProxy(bridge)` that stamps `["files.read"]` on read-side methods and `["files.write"]` on write-side methods (cap hints carry the scoped capability per [[project_intents_dispatch_cap_scope]]).
- `packages/sdk-types/src/index.ts` — `FilesService` interface refreshed (typed `FileDialogFilter`, `FileWatchEventKind` enum so the wire string isn't a raw literal, `handleFromIntent`, `requestOpen` returns `readonly FileHandle[]`, `watch` returns `Promise<Subscription>`). `FileHandle` shape unchanged so existing call sites stay valid.
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/file-handles-panel.tsx` — new Settings → Security "Open files" section (positioned below GrantsPanel — same row chrome). Per row: app icon · filename (with the full path on hover via `title`) · mode badge (read-only / read & write) · relative-time stamp · destructive Revoke button with confirm. Subscribes to `app:files-handles-changed` so a sibling-app mint refreshes the list without polling. Every label is `t()`-wrapped (15 new i18n keys); revoke uses the shared `<confirm>` modal + `Button` primitive.
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/i18n/t.ts` — 15 keys under `shell.settings.files.*` (section title, empty state, mode labels, relative-time templates with singular variants, revoke + confirm strings).
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/settings.css` — `.files-handles-panel` rules (token-only, no new colours).
- `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/settings.tsx` — added the section under `SecurityBody`.

**Tests:** +33 new tests across 4 files, **4520/4520 green** (up from 4488):
- `packages/shell/src/main/files/files-service.test.ts` 22 — every method, cancellation-as-data, cross-app handle scoping fail-closed (read / write / watch / unwatch all return `Invalid` for another app's token), `decodeWriteData` rejection mapping (non-binary / over-ceiling), read-only handle write rejection, watch subscribe → emit → unwatch closes underlying watcher (idempotent on second call), cross-app unwatch is a fail-closed no-op (doesn't kill the owner's watcher), `MAX_WATCHES_PER_APP` ceiling, `handleFromIntent` mints read-only scoped to receiver + idempotent re-call + returns `null` for unknown / revoked source token, no-vault-session → `Unavailable` for every read/write/watch/handleFromIntent path, unknown method → `Invalid`, defensive `normalizeOpenDialog` swallows bad app input. Electron is mocked; FS + dialogs + watcher factory all injected so the suite is pure.

## 2026-05-20 — 10.0 — sync de-risk spike (per-entity DEK + blind relay)

Throwaway two-instance prototype in [`experiments/sync-spike-10.0/`](../experiments/sync-spike-10.0) proving the v1 sync invariant: **per-entity DEK + encrypted Yjs update envelopes over a blind relay that sees ciphertext only**. The proof is the audit document `docs/_review/2026-05-20-10.0-sync-spike.md`; the code is supporting evidence and will be deleted (or referenced as a reproducible test fixture) once 10.1–10.9 land.

**What was built:** two Node clients (Alice's device + Bob's device, same sovereign user, different Ed25519 device keys + X25519 wrap keys) and one in-process blind relay. The relay module imports nothing from `@noble/*`, holds no key material, and parses only the routing header — the **blind-relay property is structural**, asserted at the end of every run by reading `relay.ts` and rejecting any `import` of `@noble/*` or `./crypto`. Wire envelopes are length-prefixed `(headerJSON || Ed25519-sig || XChaCha20-Poly1305-ciphertext)` frames; AEAD AAD = the header bytes; per-sender monotonic `seq` for replay protection. Member-wraps use static-static X25519 ECDH + HKDF-SHA-256 + AEAD (spike-grade; the proof doc forces the 10.2 swap to HPKE-RFC 9180, same envelope shape). The documented edit sequence — Alice creates → types "Hi", pairs Bob via signed `add-device` record + `kind=wrap` envelope addressed to Bob's X25519 pubkey + `kind=snapshot` envelope; both clients then issue concurrent `kind=update` envelopes that converge via Yjs CRDT — runs end-to-end and prints the relay's full byte log.

**What was learned, what positions fell out.** OQ-10 / OQ-26: **QR-primary + SAS-code fallback** (a 6-digit code can't carry 32 bytes of entropy, so the code path is an authenticated DH with a short authentication string the user matches — not a duplicate of QR-as-UX). OQ-27: **rotation envelope shape decouples cryptographically from access change** (one signed `kind=rotation` record + fresh `kind=wrap` per remaining member; v1 ships the shape, v2 wires the policy). OQ-28: **only org spaces route through the org relay** (the spike's routing model has no enforcement surface for "force personal entities through org relay" — and shouldn't, per the account-less floor; the implication forced into the open is that the **client-side per-entity relay-routing table is identity-level state that must be backed up alongside the user-Ed25519 key**). OQ-29: **permanently visible in `root.meta.access`, append-only** (`revokedAt` field, never deletion; the access record is inside the entity Y.Doc so it's encrypted at rest and per-entity-visible, not centrally readable until v2's server-readable spaces). All five OQs now marked `*[RESOLVED in implementation-plan Stage 10.0]*` in [`11-open-questions.md`](reference/11-open-questions.md). The spike also surfaced two non-blocking 10.x followups: **10.10 wrap+snapshot bundling** (a freshly-paired device pays 2 envelopes per accessible entity to bootstrap — 20k envelopes on a 10k-entity vault) and **10.11 routing-token rotation** (hash of `(entityId || epoch)` to mitigate the entity-id + sender-pubkey side-channel; matters in v2 multi-user, deferrable in v1 single-user). Confirmed the structural-blindness invariant becomes a CI rule on the production relay module (the spike's step-7 assertion encodes the same lint) — recorded in the audit doc as a 10.4 addition.

**Files shipped (all outside `packages/*` / `apps/*`):**
- `experiments/sync-spike-10.0/` — `package.json` + `README.md` + `tsconfig.json` + `.gitignore` + `src/{wire,crypto,relay,client,spike}.ts`.
- `docs/_review/2026-05-20-10.0-sync-spike.md` — the primary deliverable: positions on the five OQs, the ciphertext-only proof transcript (1 wrap + 1 snapshot + 2 concurrent updates routed through the relay; final convergent title "Hi!?"), the side-channel enumeration (entity-id / sender-pubkey / sizes / timing / subscribe-set leaked; content / structure / member-set / awareness not), the final DEK+wrap shape, what the spike rules out, and the 10.1–10.9 revisions.
- `docs/implementation-plan.md` — 10.0 ⚪ → ✅; status snapshot Infrastructure cell updated; OQ-10/26/27/28/29 strike-through in the burn-down list.
- `docs/implementation-plan-table.md` — Sync row bumped; "Last updated" → 2026-05-20.

## 2026-05-19 — 9.4.1 — `BlockEmbedNode` + `/embed` snapshot card

Shipped the bridge node from [`docs/editing/15-embedding-and-composition.md`](editing/15-embedding-and-composition.md): a block-level Lexical `DecoratorNode` carrying `{blockId, entityId, entityType, label}` — the cross-app "embed any vault object as a preview card inside another document" primitive the user asked for. v1 ships the **shell fallback card path** only (`io.brainstorm.shell/entity-card/v1` — entity-icon at 56×56 + live title + reverse-DNS type tail), which works for every vault object today *without* needing the B9.4.4/B9.5 BP-block iframe; when a providing app contributes a real BP block for `blockId`, the persisted node lights up the live mount and the on-disk shape doesn't change.

**Files shipped:**
- `apps/notes/src/editor/nodes/block-embed-node.tsx` + `.test.ts` — node + `BlockEmbedView` React renderer (uses `entityIconsSnapshot` / `entityTitlesSnapshot` so the card stays live with renames + icon changes; click → `brainstorm://entity/<id>` via the editor's existing link interceptor).
- `apps/notes/src/editor/embed-insert.ts` + `.test.ts` — pure `applyEmbedInsertion(editor, paragraphKey, insertion)` mirroring `applyMentionInsertion`; root-append fallback on stale key.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/embed-picker-store.ts` + `block-embed-picker-plugin.tsx` — `addPropertyStore`-shaped pub-sub + popover plugin (search input + filtered `vaultEntities.list()`, ArrowUp/Down/Enter/Esc through Lexical's command stack), opened by the slash command's `run`.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/commands.tsx` — new `block.embed.entity` `BlockCommand` + `openEmbedPicker(editor)` helper that reads the empty paragraph's key + bounding rect and opens the store.
- `apps/notes/src/editor/editor.tsx` — `BlockEmbedNode` registered in the nodes array (after `PageRefNode`); `BlockEmbedPickerPlugin` mounted (after `MentionTypeaheadPlugin`).
- `apps/notes/src/i18n/t.ts` — 9 new keys (`notes.command.embed.label/.description`, `notes.embed.menu.region/.results/.search/.placeholder/.empty/.noResults`, `notes.embed.untitled`, `notes.embed.typeUnknown`).
- `apps/notes/src/styles.css` — `.notes__embed-host` / `.notes__embed-card` (card chrome) + `.notes__embed-menu*` (picker chrome, mirrors `.notes__link-markup-menu`).
- `packages/shell/src/main/entities/extract-note-references.ts` + `.test.ts` — added `BLOCK_EMBED_NODE_TYPE` + `NoteReferenceKind.Embed`; walker now emits an edge per `BlockEmbedNode` (3 new tests: snapshot, mention+embed of same entity stay distinct, missing-id guard).
- `apps/notes/src/editor/extract-references.ts` — apps-side walker mirrored; on-disk JSON protocol stays in sync.

**Why a separate node from `PageRefNode`?** `PageRefNode` is a single-line link row (icon + title); `BlockEmbedNode` is a framed block card with a 56×56 entity icon — for image entities that *is* the thumbnail (per [[feedback_per_object_icons_everywhere]]), for whiteboard/database/note it's the type's glyph at preview size. Different UX role: ref says "follow this link", embed says "here is content from elsewhere". The data shape also differs — embed carries `blockId` for the future BP-frame routing the design doc anchors on (doc-15 §The bridge).

**Why the slash command + picker now, not later?** Doc-15's "fallback card" + a working `/embed` insertion is the whole user-visible feature; shipping the bare node without a way to insert it would be theatre. The picker is ~200 lines mirroring the established mention-typeahead pattern and Settles the UX shape (icon + title + type label, anchored popover, vaultEntities.list once per open) so it doesn't have to be relitigated when the real BP-block path lands. The Graph-edge emission was bundled because the walker is in scope (extract-note-references already walks every note body) and the alternative is shipping a known backlinks gap.

**Live-transclusion (B6.4a) and BP-iframe (B9.4.4/B9.5) stay ⚪.** Those swap the snapshot card for a live mount, but they consume the *same persisted node* — no migration when they land.

Shell→app-transform chain proven sound; only the live Electron renderer bridge is uncovered (now unmasked + DIAG-instrumented). **Design-system pass ✅ (2026-05-16, parallel design agent)** — shared `<Spinner>` loader primitive + `<Button loading>` (aria-busy, size-held, decorative spinner) + glossy Glass/Primary/Destructive button fills (shared `--gloss-from/--to` tokens, `::before/::after` shine) + app-icon polish + 11 app `icon.svg` re-pad; canonical async/busy-state spec added to [36-design-system.md §Async loading & busy state](shell/36-design-system.md#async-loading--busy-state); +10 spinner/button tests. **B6.6 universal open resolver ✅** — bus resolves a bare `open` id→`{type,mime}` (`main/intents/entity-target.ts`) + unions the previously-dead `openers` registry into the `open`-verb handler set; id-only clicks reach the type-specific opener, MIME falls back to its viewer (Preview reachable for free); `suggest()` async; +15 tests. **B6.7 handler-side completeness ✅** — Preview now actually receives intents (replaced a never-exposed `intents.onOpen` shim with the real handshake + `runtime.on("intent")` two-path delivery), Files & Graph gained running-app `runtime.on("intent")` subscribers, Graph node-focus implemented via pure `focusNodeTransform`; +17 tests. **B6.8 shared SDK open primitive ✅** — `openEntity`/`quickLookEntity` in `@brainstorm/sdk` collapse the 6-copy open-dispatch DRY violation; Database/Graph/Files/Calendar migrated (Journal = B6.8a, no SDK dep yet); +7 tests. **B6.9 end-to-end open/quick-look correctness ✅ (2026-05-16)** — affordance audit fixed three live defects behind B6.6–B6.8: `quick-look` was undeliverable (every non-`open` verb null'd in `launchContextFor`; its id→MIME resolution never ran) so Database/Files Quick Look fell back to a toast and Preview never opened; `@`-mention chips (a `<span>`) were dropped by the link-only click interceptor so mention-click navigation was dead; Notes/Journal were the last hand-rolled dispatches. Notes + Journal route through SDK `openEntity` (Journal took the dep — B6.8a closed). +9 tests. **Files 9.8.2b read half ✅** — pure `buildVaultFileTree` keystone renders the real vault with `Folder/v1` nesting; vault is the only source in shell (no demo bleed, honest empty state); write-through deferred (Database-write-half posture); +6 tests. **8.T Storybook design-system gallery ✅ (tooling, ahead of Stage 8)** — Storybook 8.6 (React-Vite) at root `.storybook/`;
