## Stage 2 — Identity, credentials, at-rest encryption (✅)

### 2.1 — ✅

✅. `@napi-rs/keyring` wired with a `KeyringBackend` (lazy-loaded so Vitest under Bun doesn't fail loading the addon). `pickKeystore()` selects between keyring / passphrase / insecure; `skipKeyring` flag lets tests exercise the fallback chain on platforms where the real keychain *would* succeed. Backend recorded as `credentialsBackend` in `vault.json`.

### 2.2 — ✅

✅. `VaultSession.create()` generates Ed25519 identity + 32-byte master key via `@noble/curves` + `@noble/hashes/sha2`. Stores both in the keystore under `brainstorm.<vault-id>.{identity,master}`. Writes public key (base64) + fingerprint (`ed25519:<16hex>`) + `credentialsBackend` to `vault.json`. Active session wired into the main process via `setActiveVaultSession`.

### 2.3 — ✅

✅. `PassphraseBackend` derives a wrap key via Argon2id (configurable cost; defaults to OWASP profile) and wraps each Tier-1 item with XChaCha20-Poly1305 + fresh nonce. Persisted wrap file records KDF params so old vaults stay openable when defaults change. Verifier blob detects wrong passphrases on open. Tests use a light KDF profile to stay fast.

### 2.4 — ✅

✅. `CredentialStore` at `<vault>/shell/credentials.json`. Each row XChaCha20-Poly1305-encrypted under the vault master key with fresh nonce. AAD binds ciphertext to `(app, key)` so moving a sealed value between keys fails to decrypt. Per-app keyspace isolation enforced at the API layer (`list(app)` only returns the caller's keys). 64 KiB hard cap per value (OQ-116). Encryption library deferral noted (no SQLite in Stage 2 — encrypted JSON file is sufficient).

### 2.5 — ✅

✅. IPC handlers `credentials:{list,get,set,delete}` registered alongside `vaults:session`. Master key stays in the main process — no worker hop. Preload exposes `window.brainstorm.credentials.{list,get,set,delete}` (and `window.brainstorm.vaults.session()` for the dashboard).

### 2.6 — ✅

✅. Dashboard now renders a "Security" panel showing the active backend (`macOS Keychain` / `Windows Credential Manager` / `Linux Secret Service` / `Passphrase` / `Insecure (dev mode)`) and the identity fingerprint. Insecure mode renders an explicit warning in `--color-state-warning`.

### 2.7 — ✅

✅. `VaultSession.open()` loads identity + master from the keystore; verifies the loaded public key matches `vault.json` (rejects on mismatch). `setActiveVaultSession` replaces any prior session, calling its `dispose()` which zeroes the master key + identity-secret buffers and disposes the passphrase wrap key.

### 2.8 — ✅

✅. `BRAINSTORM_DEV_INSECURE_CREDENTIALS=1` selects the `InsecureBackend` (plaintext on-disk JSON file with a `DEV MODE — DO NOT USE FOR REAL DATA` warning baked into the file). Dashboard banner makes the active backend visible to the user.

## Stage 3 — Local data substrate (SQLite + Yjs persistence) (✅ — encryption-at-rest deferred to 3b)

### 3.1 — ✅

✅. Runtime-agnostic SQLite abstraction at `packages/shell/src/main/storage/sqlite.ts` (interface: `prepare/run/get/all`, `exec`, `pragma`, `transaction`, `close`). Lazy driver pick: `bun:sqlite` under Bun, `better-sqlite3` under Electron's Node. Default `open()` enables WAL + `foreign_keys=ON` + `synchronous=NORMAL`. Per-DB encryption-key derivation deferred to Stage 3b; the abstraction's shape is what the driver swap plugs into.

### 3.2 — ✅

✅. Migration runner at `storage/migrations.ts` reuses the generic `runMigrations<Context>` from Stage 0.8 with a SQLite-flavored wrapper that (a) writes a `_schema_version` row per applied migration, (b) wraps each up-step in a transaction (atomic on failure), (c) rejects async migration bodies.

### 3.3 — ✅

✅. `ledger.db` v1 — `capabilities` table with `(app_id, capability, scope, granted_at, granted_via in ('install','runtime'), revoked_at)`. Soft-delete via `revoked_at IS NULL`. Indexes for active-grant lookup per `(app_id, capability)` and per `(app_id)`. Rows added in Stage 4.

### 3.4 — ✅

✅. `registry.db` v1 — `apps`, `openers` (target-kind discriminator avoids the expression-in-PK SQLite restriction), `blocks`, `entity_types` (with `schema_url` + optional `schema_inline` for OQ-2 hybrid), `custom_node_types`, `widgets`. Foreign-keyed to `apps(id)` with `ON DELETE CASCADE` where appropriate.

### 3.5 — ✅

✅. `entities.db` v1 — `entities` (properties as JSON; `dek_id` placeholder for Stage 10 encryption), `links` (FK-enforced; soft-deleted), `change_log` (autoincrement seq + change_kind enum). Selective property indexes will be added lazily by the entities service (Stage 9).

### 3.6 — ✅

✅. `search.db` v1 — FTS5 virtual tables `entity_fts(entity_id UNINDEXED, type UNINDEXED, title, body)` and `file_fts(file_handle_id UNINDEXED, filename, content_excerpt)`. Tokenizer `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`. Vector column deferred to Stage 11.

### 3.7 — ✅

✅. `YDocStore` at `storage/ydoc-store.ts`. File format: `'YDOC' magic | uint32 version | uint32 snap_len | snapshot bytes | tail entries`. Each tail entry: `uint32 len | bytes | uint32 crc32`. Files sharded by 3-char id prefix under `<vault>/data/docs/<prefix>/<id>.ydoc`. Encryption deferred to Stage 10 (wraps both snapshot + each tail entry under the entity DEK).

### 3.8 — ydoc worker

✅. **ydoc worker** (`src/workers/ydoc/index.ts`) — `utilityProcess.fork` target. Methods: `load`, `applyUpdate`, `snapshot`, `close`, `recover`. In-memory `Map<vaultPath::entityId, Y.Doc>` cache; lazy load on first touch. Wired into `startWorkers()` alongside the storage worker. Build registers `workers/ydoc` as a second main-build entry.

### 3.9 — ✅

✅. Compaction at the threshold of 256 KiB tail (configurable via `compactThresholdBytes`). `appendAndMaybeCompact()` does the append-then-conditionally-compact dance and reports whether compaction ran. `writeSnapshot()` atomically replaces the file via `<file>.tmp` + `rename`.

### 3.10 — ✅

✅. Recovery is built into `load()`: per-update CRC-32 mismatch or truncated final entry causes the load to stop at the last good update and surface `truncatedTail: true`. The `recover` worker method reports this without applying anything — useful for a recovery-pass sweep on shell startup. (The startup sweep itself wires in when the entities service comes online in Stage 9; the building blocks are ready.)

## Stage 4 — Capability ledger + IPC broker enforcement (✅ — 4.6/4.7 deferred to Stage 5)

### 4.1 — Default-minimum grants

✅. `CapabilityLedger` at `packages/shell/src/main/capabilities/ledger.ts` — CRUD on the `capabilities` table from Stage 3.3. Methods: `grant` (idempotent), `revoke`, `revokeAllFor`, `listActive`, `has` (with wildcard scope match), `historyFor`. Throws `LedgerUnavailableError` on SQL failure so the broker can fail closed. **Default-minimum grants** live in `default-grants.ts`: per-app set (`storage.kv`, `intents.dispatch:open`, `credentials.read:self`, `credentials.write:self`) + shell set (broad wildcard scopes for the dashboard renderer). `applyDefaultAppGrants(ledger, appId)` and `applyShellGrants(ledger)` are idempotent helpers.

### 4.2 — ✅ (foundation)

✅ (foundation). `RendererIdentityRegistry` at `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/renderer-identity.ts` — `Map<WebContents.id → appId>`. The `verify(claimedApp, source)` method is wired into the broker as `verifyAppIdentity`. `registerDashboard(reg, webContentsId)` tags the dashboard renderer as `"shell"`. Stage 5 calls `register(webContentsId, appId)` when each app renderer is created.

### 4.3 — ✅

✅. Broker enforcement updated: `checkCapability` is called with the envelope's app + service + method + declared caps. The wiring callsite (in Stage 5's main-process startup) iterates over declared caps and verifies each via `ledger.has(app, cap)`. Anything throwing returns `Unavailable` (see 4.8).

### 4.4 — per-app

✅. Per-app pending queue at the broker level. `maxPendingPerApp` (default 256 per docs/12) bounds in-flight requests per app id. Overflow drops the oldest non-streaming request and rejects it with `Unavailable: "request dropped due to per-app backpressure"`. The check is **per-app**: one misbehaving app cannot starve other apps' queues. Streaming subscriptions (for live entity updates) bypass the cap and apply producer-side backpressure instead — that machinery lands with the entities service in Stage 9.

### 4.5 — ✅

✅. Audit log `AuditEventKind` extended with `capability.grant`, `capability.revoke`, `ipc.denied`. The broker exposes an `onDenied(event)` callback so the main-process startup wires audit-log writes without coupling the broker to the vault session.

### 4.8 — ✅

✅. End-to-end test at `capabilities/enforcement.test.ts`: closes the ledger DB (proxy for corruption / unavailability), dispatches a capability-protected call, asserts the broker returns `Unavailable` (NEVER approval). Covers the full broker → CapabilityLedger → SQLite path including the `LedgerUnavailableError` → `Unavailable` mapping.

## Stage 5 — App SDK v1 surface + manifest + install (✅ — UI deferred to Stage 5b)

### 5.1 — ✅

✅. Manifest validator at `packages/shell/src/main/apps/manifest.ts` — hand-written (no Zod runtime dep). Validates `id`, `version`, `sdk`, `entry`, `capabilities`, `registrations` (openers / blocks / entityTypes / widgets), `shortcuts`, `menus`, `layouts`. Hybrid entity-type rule per OQ-2. `diffCapabilities` helper for update flows.

### 5.2 — AppInstaller

✅. **AppInstaller** (`apps/installer.ts`) reads + validates manifest, copies the bundle to `<vault>/apps/<id>/<version>/`, computes a deterministic SHA-256 over sorted contents, applies default-minimum + manifest-requested grants via the ledger. Pure orchestration — SQL lives in the new `storage/registry-repo/` repos (per Stage 5 repo-pattern decision).

### 5.3 — ✅

✅. Update flow diffs capabilities (`added` / `removed` / `unchanged`); revokes the removed; grants the added (programmatic — UI gate is Stage 5b). Atomic via the registry-db `transaction(...)` wrapper.

### 5.4 — ✅

✅. Uninstall flips `apps.uninstalled_at`, marks introduced entity_types orphaned (OQ-3), drops openers/blocks/widgets registrations, revokes every live grant via `ledger.revokeAllFor`. Bundle stays on disk for forensic recovery; `vacuumBundles()` is the separate cleanup step.

### 5.5 — AppLauncher

✅. **AppLauncher** at `apps/launcher.ts` — sandboxed `BrowserWindow` per app (OQ-4 (b)) via injectable factory; identity stamped via `additionalArguments` (`--brainstorm-app-id=...`, `--brainstorm-handshake=<base64>`); WebContents id registered in the renderer-identity registry. `closeApp(id)` cleans up windows + identity on uninstall.

### 5.6 — `@brainstorm/sdk`

✅. **`@brainstorm/sdk`** runtime — `buildRuntime({ handshake, bridge })` marshals every `brainstorm.services.<service>.<method>(...)` call into a broker envelope via a `Bridge`. Storage / credentials / identity / ui surfaces wired. Entities / files / intents throw `Unavailable` with pointers to their landing stages (9 / 9 / 7).

### 5.7 — ✅

✅. `LifecycleEmitter` exposes `ready`, `suspend`, `resume`, `intent`, `capability-changed`, `close`. `buildRuntimeWithEmitter` returns the emitter alongside the runtime so the preload (or tests) can dispatch events into the app. Throwing handlers don't break sibling handlers.

### 5.8 — ✅

✅. Structured error classes `CapabilityDenied`, `NotFound`, `Conflict`, `Unavailable`, `Invalid`. `makeSdkError(kind, message, detail)` reconstructs the right subclass from a wire reply. Unknown kinds fall through to a generic `Error` with the kind as the `name`.

### 5.9 — `@brainstorm/sdk-types`

✅. **`@brainstorm/sdk-types`** ships the full type surface: `AppRuntime`, `AppHandshake`, `LaunchContext`, `LifecycleEvent`, `EntitiesService`, `StorageService`, `FilesService`, `CredentialsService`, `IntentsService`, `IdentityService`, `UiService`, `CapabilitiesService`, `Intent`, `IntentResult`, `Entity`, `EntityQuery`, `PropertyPredicate`, `LinkPredicate`, `StructuredError`. Type-only, zero runtime.

### 5.10 — Wiring closed (Stage 4 inheritance):

✅. `EntityFallback` React component at `packages/shell/src/renderer/fallback/entity-fallback.tsx`. Renders type label + reason headline + primary-fields card (driven by schema display hints; falls back to top-3 string-valued top-level props). Optional "Pick a handler" button hook for Stage 7's intents picker.

**Wiring closed (Stage 4 inheritance):**
- `BrokerContext` at `main/runtime/broker-context.ts` is the cross-cutting glue. Owns the `RendererIdentityRegistry`. Closures pass `verifyAppIdentity` + `checkCapability` + `onDenied` into the broker once at startup; the closures read from `getActiveVaultSession()?.capabilityLedger()` on every call. Caches the resolved ledger per session; invalidates on vault switch.
- `startWorkers()` constructs the BrokerContext and wires it into the broker.
- `main/index.ts` registers the dashboard's WebContents id as the shell identity on creation; unregisters on close.
- `vault-handlers` calls `warmupBroker()` after every vault create / open / activate to hot-load the ledger before the first IPC call lands.
- `broker:dispatch` `ipcMain` handler at `ipc/broker-handler.ts` is the single channel app preloads talk on. The app preload (`preload/app-preload.ts`) decodes the handshake from `additionalArguments`, builds the SDK runtime via `buildRuntime({ handshake, bridge })`, and exposes it via `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("brainstorm", runtime)`.

**Deferred to Stage 5b:**
- **4.6 capability-prompt modal** — `capabilities.request(cap, reason)` UI in the dashboard renderer.
- **4.7 ledger grants panel** — Settings → Security view of every app's live grants with per-grant revoke.
- An interactive **install dialog** that wraps the programmatic `AppInstaller` flow with a user-facing capability review.
- The capability service stubs in the SDK runtime — they exist but `list()` returns empty / `request()` round-trips to a service that doesn't exist yet. Stage 5b wires real handlers.

## Stage 6 — Window manager, system menu, keyboard shortcuts (✅ — 6.7/6.9 deferred)

### 6.1 — WindowManager

✅. **WindowManager** at `main/window/window-manager.ts` tracks `(appId, windowId)` and persists placements to `session.json` with debounced writes. Duck-typed `TrackedWindow` interface — testable without Electron. `move`/`resize`/`close` events update snapshots; close also captures a synchronous final snapshot so a quit-during-debounce doesn't lose state.

### 6.2 — ✅

✅. `monitor.ts` derives a stable `mon_v1:<hash>` id from `(workArea x/y/width/height + scaleFactor)`. `resolvePlacement()` falls back to the primary monitor when the remembered one is gone, and `clampToMonitor()` recentres windows that ended up fully offscreen.

### 6.3 — ✅

✅. `planRestore(targets)` reads `session.json`, applies the monitor resolver, returns `RestoreHint[]` describing where to position each re-opened window. `lastSessionTargets()` returns the `(appId, windowId)` pairs that were open at last close — caller decides which to re-launch (opt-in setting wires in alongside Stage 5b's settings UI).

### 6.4 — MenuComposer

✅. **MenuComposer** (`main/menu/menu-composer.ts`) is a pure function: input `(platform, focused-app menus, focused-app shortcuts, overrideAccelerator)` → output ordered `TopLevelMenu[]`. Top-level order is `Brainstorm` (mac) / `File` / `Edit` / `View` / `<app menus>` / `Window` / `Help`. Apps cannot override shell-owned top-level menus. Menu-item ids are namespaced `<owner>/<action>` so dispatch can resolve them. Accelerators resolve `override → manifest.shortcut → shortcut-registration default`.

### 6.5 — MenuRouter

✅. **MenuRouter** (`main/menu/menu-dispatch.ts`) routes shell ids to in-process handlers and app ids to a `sendToFocusedApp` callback on the private `menu:invoke` channel (avoids the broker — trusted shell→app dispatch). Returns a `DispatchResult` describing what happened so callers can log / instrument.

### 6.6 — ShortcutRegistry

✅. **ShortcutRegistry** (`main/shortcuts/shortcut-registry.ts`) holds the two layers (shell + app). Default shell set ships baked in (`launcher`, `settings`, `new`, `switch-window`, `close-window`, `quit`, `cheatsheet`, `help`). Apps register/unregister via their manifest. Conflict detection canonicalizes chords (`normalizeChord` collapses modifier synonyms like `Cmd`/`Command`/`Meta` → `cmd` and reorders modifiers alphabetically so `B+Cmd` matches `Cmd+B`).

### 6.8 — The UI itself

✅ (logic). `ShortcutRegistry.overrideOne` / `resetOverride` / `conflicts()` / `findByChord()` provide everything the rebinding UI needs. `bindings-store.ts` persists overrides. **The UI itself** moves to Stage 5b alongside the Settings panel.

✅. **DashboardStore** (`main/dashboard/dashboard-store.ts`) wraps a Yjs doc with typed get/set for wallpaper / icons / widgets. Persists via `YDocStore` (one file per entity, sharded by id-prefix) at `<vault>/data/docs/bra/brainstorm-Dashboard.ydoc`. Lazy-instantiated on `VaultSession.dashboardStore()`. Will migrate to `brainstorm/Dashboard/v1` entity when Stage 9 entities service ships — the on-disk shape is forward-compatible.

Interim "Pin app…" picker enumerates installed apps via `apps:list-installed`.

✅. **Launcher palette** (`renderer/launcher/`) — opened by `⌘ Space` / `Ctrl+Space` delivered via per-window `webContents.on("before-input-event")` (not Electron's `globalShortcut.register`, which was capturing the chord OS-wide and breaking macOS input-source switching — fixed 2026-05-11). Plain list (no fancy-menus until Stage 8). Substring matching against label + subtitle in a pure `filterResults()` helper. ArrowUp/Down navigates; Enter launches; Escape closes. Apps source wired; intents/entities/files placeholders for Stages 7.5 / 9 / 11.

### 7.5 — What's in:

✅ PARTIAL (Stage 7b). Intents bus foundation landed. **What's in:** `intents` table added to `registry.db` (migration v2); `IntentsRepository` with `findHandlers({verb, entityType?, mime?, format?, kind?, blockId?})` matching NULL discriminators as wildcards; manifest validator extended for `registrations.intents` with the curated verb namespace (`open|insert|share|convert|export|import|process|compose|quick-look`); `AppInstaller.install/update/uninstall` writes and clears intent registrations alongside openers/blocks/widgets; **`IntentsBus`** in `main/intents/intents-bus.ts` with `suggest()` + `dispatch()` (handler selection: same-source-app wins, then primary, then first; `open` verb routes via `LaunchOrchestrator.launch({launch: {reason: "open-entity", entityId}})`; other verbs return structured `no-delivery-channel` until the `runtime:lifecycle` push channel lands); broker service handler registered in `index.ts` against `launchSetup.getIntents()`; SDK `intentsProxy` replaces the placeholder (`runtime.services.intents.dispatch(...)` now works). **What's deferred:** the four-mode navigation resolver and route-aware focus-existing per [37-cross-app-navigation.md](shell/37-cross-app-navigation.md) (full plumbing is a Stage 8 commitment per that doc's phasing); delivery for non-`open` verbs needs the `runtime:lifecycle` IPC push channel. **Tests:** +22 (intents-repo 4, intents-bus 6, intents-service 5, manifest validation 5, installer expansion 2). 503 tests total, all green; lint clean; main bundle 23.84 KB brotli.

### 7.6 — Manifest registration hot-reload

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **Closes 7.6's remaining piece — re-apply an installed app's manifest registrations without an uninstall/reinstall or a shell restart.** 7.5 landed the manifest validator + `AppInstaller.install/update/uninstall` writing/clearing registrations; the gap was a runtime *refresh* so a dev iterating on `apps/<app>/manifest.json`'s `registrations` doesn't have to pay the dev seeder's full uninstall+reinstall (which churns grants and is boot-gated per [[apps_build_separately_from_shell]]). **What landed:** `AppInstaller.refreshRegistrations(appId)` (+ `RefreshResult`) — looks up the active app record, re-reads + validates `manifest.json` from the **already-installed** bundle dir, guards the manifest id matches the installed app, then in one registry transaction `clearLookupRegistrations` + `writeRegistrations` (the exact registration half of `update()`). Deliberately narrow: no bundle copy, no version bump, no install-dir churn, and **no capability re-grant/revoke** — manifest `capabilities` are a user-consent surface, not a dev knob. The live `IntentsBus` reads the registry repo on every `suggest`/`dispatch` (no cache — established at 7.5), so a refreshed registration is picked up on the next dispatch with zero restart. Dev-only `dev/refresh-app-registrations.ts` (mirrors `seed-demo-apps.ts`'s active-session → registry/ledger → `AppInstaller` wiring; guards empty appId / no session) behind a `dev:refresh-app-registrations` IPC (registered only when `!app.isPackaged`, alongside `dev:seed-demo-apps`) + `window.brainstorm.dev.refreshAppRegistrations(appId)` (+ `DevRefreshResult`). **Tests:** +3 `installer.test.ts` (not-installed → typed error; a changed installed manifest's blocks/intents replace the old set with the apps row + version + `uninstalled_at` untouched — proving it's a refresh, not an update; renamed-manifest id-mismatch rejected — empty `registrations` used to isolate the id guard from the namespacing validator). 18 installer tests + 159 across the apps/dev/ipc regression suites green; `bun run typecheck` clean (only the 5 pre-existing unrelated `react-dom/client` errors); `biome` clean on all touched files. No new dependency, no OQ gated it. Advances Stage 7b — widgets (7.3) + pin-to-dashboard (7.13) remain.

### 7.7 — Notifications host service

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **`services.ui.notify({title, body?, kind?})` — an app hands the shell a structured message; the shell owns presentation.** The SDK `uiProxy.notify` already stamped `["notifications.post"]` on the envelope, but **no `ui` broker service existed** (registered services were storage/ydoc/intents/vault-entities/properties/search) — so every `ui.notify` call failed at the broker. This wires the missing half. **What landed:** (a) `main/ui/notify-host.ts` — a **pure** `UiNotifyHost` (no Electron imports, mirrors `CapabilityPromptHost`): holds an optional dashboard sender, `post()` forwards on the `ui:notify` channel and returns `false` (best-effort, not an app-visible error) when no renderer is attached; `normalizeNotification(appId, raw)` validates shape (title required non-empty → else `Invalid`; body optional, empty dropped; title/body clamped to 200/1000 chars with an ellipsis rather than rejected), `coerceKind` defaults an unknown/absent kind to `info`; module singleton via `getUiNotifyHost`/`resetUiNotifyHost`. (b) `main/ui/ui-service.ts` — thin `ServiceHandler`: `notify` → normalise (stamping the **broker-verified `envelope.app`**, never a client-supplied source) → `host.post`; unknown method (incl. the not-yet-implemented `openWindow`/`closeWindow`) → `Invalid`, consistent with every other service. (c) `index.ts` registers `"ui"` and binds the host's dashboard sender on dashboard-window create + clears it on `closed`, alongside `promptHost`. (d) preload exposes `notifications.on(cb)` on the `ui:notify` channel (mirrors `capabilityPrompt.on`/`mainErrors.on`); `renderer/ui/notification-bridge.ts` installs once at boot (next to `installErrorBridge`) and pushes the message through the existing `ToastHost` the shell's own surfaces use, via a defensive `toToastKind` (unknown kind → `Info`, never a dropped toast). **Capability:** `notifications.post` is pattern-valid (`CAPABILITY_PATTERN`) and deliberately **not** added to default-minimum grants — per security/09 §Capabilities the default set is `storage.kv`/`intents.dispatch:open`/credentials-self/own-window only; an app that wants to post notifications declares `notifications.post` in its manifest and the user grants it like any capability (no inference). Broker enforcement is unchanged — the handler assumes an authorised caller and only validates shape. New **OQ-NOTIF-1** logged: should `notifications.post` become a default-minimum grant (parity with `search.read`'s "benign, universal UX" argument) or stay user-granted — left user-granted for now, revisit if first-party apps find the prompt friction outweighs the consent value. No new dependency. **Tests:** +25 — `notify-host.test.ts` 14 (validation matrix incl. clamp/empty-body-drop/kind-coercion, post with/without sender, detach, singleton), `ui-service.test.ts` 4 (forward+app-stamp, Invalid on bad payload, Invalid on unknown method), `notification-bridge.test.ts` 7 (kind→ToastKind incl. degrade). 95 tests across the new + regression suites (ipc/sdk-runtime/search-service) green; `tsc --noEmit` clean (only the 5 pre-existing unrelated `react-dom/client` errors); `biome` clean on all touched files. Closes the notifications half of Stage 7b; tray (7.8) + widgets (7.3) + manifest hot-reload (7.6) + pin-to-dashboard (7.13) remain.

### 7.8 — Tray API

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **`services.ui.tray.publish/clear` — a `tray.publish`-granted app contributes a section to the single shell-owned OS tray.** Extends the `ui` broker service stood up in 7.7. **Design position (v1):** there is **one** shell-owned `Tray`; an app publishes a *section* (a header + its items) and the shell composes the final native menu from every publisher ("apps publish a subset; the shell composes" per 04-shell/33). Clicking an item with an `intent` routes through the **existing `IntentsBus`** attributed to the publishing app (`getIntentsSync().dispatch(intent, {app})`) — the tray reuses the curated-verb path rather than inventing an app-callback channel, so 7.8 has **zero dependency on the still-deferred `runtime:lifecycle` push**. Renders **OS-native** (`Tray` + `Menu`) — the avoid-blocking minimum; the `fancy-menus` app-rendered tray (doc 33 §Tray menu, a Stage-8 dep) is the later upgrade, logged as **OQ-TRAY-1**. **What landed:** (a) `sdk-types` — `TrayMenuItem`/`TraySpec`/`TrayService`, `UiService` gains `tray: TrayService`. (b) SDK `uiProxy.tray = { publish, clear }` → broker methods `ui/tray.publish` + `ui/tray.clear`, both stamping `["tray.publish"]`. (c) `main/ui/tray-host.ts` — **pure** `TrayHost` (no Electron, mirrors `notify-host`/`CapabilityPromptHost`): insertion-ordered per-app sections, `publish`/`clear`/`reset`, `compose()` → a plain-data `ComposedTray` (`null` when no publisher, so the icon is torn down not left empty), validation throws `Invalid` (object/non-empty-items/≤24-items/id+label required/intent shape/enabled-coerce/label-clamp-80/tooltip-clamp-120), single-publisher tooltip names the tray else the product name; module singleton. (d) `ui-service.ts` grows `tray.publish`/`tray.clear` cases (stamp the broker-verified `envelope.app`; bad spec → `Invalid`; unknown method still `Invalid`). (e) `index.ts` renders the pure model into a real `Tray`: created on first publish, `setContextMenu(Menu.buildFromTemplate(...))` rebuilt on every change (header → disabled item, separator → separator, item → `{label, enabled, click→IntentsBus.dispatch}`), destroyed when the last publisher clears + on `before-quit`; macOS uses a template image. **Capability:** `tray.publish` is documented in security/09 and stays **explicit (not default-minimum)** — appearing in the system tray is exactly the kind of surface that warrants user consent; an app declares it in its manifest. **Tests:** +25 — `tray-host.test.ts` 18 (validation matrix, compose ordering/headers/separators, re-publish-moves-to-end, tooltip resolution, change-emit + clear-unknown-no-emit + reset-idempotent, singleton), `ui-service.test.ts` extended +3 tray (publish under app, Invalid spec, clear) and refactored to a shared `handlerWith` helper. 104 tests across the new + regression suites (ipc/sdk-runtime/ui) green; `bun run typecheck` clean (only the 5 pre-existing unrelated `react-dom/client` errors); `biome` clean on all touched files. No new dependency. **OQ-TRAY-1** logged (OS-native now → fancy-menus when the Stage-8 dep lands; per-app-icon vs. one-shared-tray revisit). Advances Stage 7b — widgets (7.3), manifest hot-reload (7.6), pin-to-dashboard (7.13) remain.

### 7.13 — Pin any object to the dashboard

✅ DONE (2026-05-18). **Any object can be pinned to the dashboard; the pin shows the object's own icon with a small opener-app badge, drags + reorders in the same grid as app icons, and survives rename / re-icon / delete.** `DashboardIconKind` already declared `"entity"`/`"view"` but `activateIcon` warned-and-no-op'd for them and nothing could create one. **What landed, five layers:**

- **Contract** — `sdk-types`: `DashboardService` (`pin`/`unpin`/`isPinned`, all `{ entityId }`) + `PinResolution` (`label`/`icon`/`appId`/`missing`); added to `AppRuntime.services`. The pin persists **only** the entity id — every presentation field is live-resolved, so a rename/re-icon/delete is reflected without the app re-pinning.
- **Live shell resolution** — `main/dashboard/pin-resolver.ts` (pure; injected `getEntity` + `resolveOpenerApp`) maps each entity pin → its current title (shared new `entities/derive-title.ts`, also adopted by the search collector — DRY, the two title derivations can no longer drift), its own `properties.icon` via the one shared `parseIcon` (malformed → null, never throws), the current opener app (Settings→Defaults override → registered opener → first `open` intent handler, mirroring the defaults-catalog precedence so badge and open never disagree), and `missing: true` for a vanished target. `ipc/dashboard-handlers.ts` enriches the snapshot (skips the registry/entities reads entirely when there are no entity pins — the common app-icons-only case stays cheap) on the `dashboard:snapshot` read **and** the subscribe push; `republishDashboardSnapshot()` re-pushes on every `entities` create/update/delete so a rename/delete/restore reflects with no user action.
- **`services.dashboard` broker verb** — `main/dashboard/dashboard-service.ts`: deterministic icon id `pin_<entityId>` (idempotent pin, O(1) unpin/isPinned, no "find an icon that happens to target this"), best-effort label seed (overridden live on read), first-free-cell row-major placement; new **`dashboard.pin` default-minimum capability** (same rationale as `covers.write`/`properties.write`: every first-party app's object menu uses it; unscoped; stores no cross-app data) added to `DEFAULT_APP_CAPABILITIES` + `SHELL_CAPABILITIES`; registered on the broker in `index.ts`.
- **Composite tile + activation** — `renderer/dashboard/icons-layer.tsx` `PinTile`: the object's own `<EntityIcon>` with a small bottom-right opener-app `<AppIcon>` badge, greyed-tombstone state when `missing`, label from the live resolution; identical drag/reorder/persist path as app icons (zero change to the grid math). `dashboard.tsx` `activateIcon` now dispatches `intent.open` for entity/view (the one open path → IntentsBus focus-existing), falls back to launching the resolved opener app, and no-ops a tombstone. Context menu relabels remove → "Remove pin" for pins.
- **Shared object-menu convention** — new headless `@brainstorm/sdk/object-menu` (`buildObjectMenuItems` + `isObjectPinned`): the one cross-app contract for an object's context menu — fixed order **Open → Pin/Unpin → app `extraItems` → Remove**, capability-gated Pin toggle, localisable labels, `onRemove` opt-in (apps without a confirm affordance omit Remove rather than ship an unconfirmed delete). It returns descriptors; apps render through their own menu chrome (no forked menu styling). First adopter: the **Database app** via one delegated `contextmenu` over the stable stage body (covers every view kind — grid/list/gallery/board/calendar/timeline — in a single integration point). Documented as the standing convention in [docs/shell/37 §Object menu](shell/37-cross-app-navigation.md).

**OQ-DASH-1 resolved** (adopts the tentative leaning): activation = the one open path so focus-existing comes for free (a Mod-click new-window is deferred to the Stage-8 `<Link>` modes, inherited then, not hand-rolled now); unpin is pure dashboard state and never touches the object; a deleted/binned target is a greyed tombstone with explicit "Remove pin", never auto-removed (a Bin restore re-lights it in place). The two specific blocked cases stay pending as thin presets over this primitive — 9.12.13(c) `PinnedList` Contacts, 9.19.2 `PinnedShellSurface` Bin.

**Scope note:** the Database adoption wires **Open + Pin/Unpin** (the headline ask). **Remove** is a first-class slot in the SDK contract + doc but is *not* wired into Database here — the app has no shared confirm affordance and the workflow bar forbids shipping an unconfirmed destructive delete; it lands per-app when the app gains a confirm surface.

**Tests:** +12 shell (`pin-resolver.test.ts` 7 — skip app/view, title/icon/badge derivation, title→name→id fallback, malformed-icon degrade, tombstone, no-opener; `dashboard-service.test.ts` 5+ — idempotent pin, dashboard-state-only unpin, distinct cells, no-session→false, repo-unavailable still pins, Invalid matrix), +10 SDK `object-menu.test.ts` (order, pin↔unpin label, capability gate incl. scoped grant, extra-before-destructive, localisation, pin invokes surface; `isObjectPinned` passthrough + safe-default). Workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean; `apps/database` app-tsc clean; new tests green.

**Stage 7a wired or pending wire-in:**

- **AppLauncher → LaunchOrchestrator** wiring (`main/runtime/launch-setup.ts`): rebuilds per session-id so windows belonging to the previous vault close on switch. The `apps:launch` IPC handler routes the dashboard's launch requests through it.
- **Shell shortcuts** (`main/runtime/shortcut-setup.ts`): per-window `webContents.on("before-input-event", ...)` delivery — fires only when a Brainstorm window has OS focus, so well-known OS chords like macOS `Cmd+Space` (input-source switcher / Spotlight) keep working when Brainstorm is in the background. On fire, the action id minus the `shell/` prefix is forwarded over `shell:action`. The `?`-only "Help" shortcut is intentionally not deliverable (re-evaluate with the cheat-sheet UI).
- **Dashboard IPC** (`main/ipc/dashboard-handlers.ts`): `snapshot` + `upsert-icon` + `move-icon` + `remove-icon` + `set-wallpaper` + `upsert-widget` + `remove-widget`. Subscribes the dashboard renderer to the DashboardStore's snapshot stream on first call; pushes every update via `dashboard:snapshot`.
- **Drive-by**: ledger-handlers.ts inline `SELECT` replaced with `AppsRepository.listActive()` so it follows the repository pattern.

## Stage 9 — Rich text, Block Protocol, first-party apps

### Platform — rich text, Block Protocol, host services

#### 9.1 — `packages/react-yjs` — React ⇄ Yjs binding

✅ DONE (2026-05-15). **`packages/react-yjs` — React ⇄ Yjs binding.** The five hooks per [13 §State management](shell/13-frontend-stack.md), built so all CRDT/batching logic is framework-free and unit-testable without a renderer. (a) `subscription.ts` — `createYStore` microtask-coalesced subscription store: ref-counted lazy bind/unbind (idle docs carry no observer), `getSnapshot()` referentially stable until a real change (satisfies `useSyncExternalStore`), N synchronous Yjs mutations → one notify per microtask, `equals`-gated recompute, `flush()` for sync teardown/tests, resync-on-first-bind; `shallowMapEquals` so a rebuilt Y.Map snapshot is "unchanged" when entries are. (b) `stores.ts` — typed builders `yTextStore` / `yMapStore` (shallow-equal) / `yMapKeyStore` (single key, ignores siblings) / `yDocStore` / `yXmlFragmentStore` (monotonic version change-signal — structural snapshots would be expensive + identity-unstable; editors bind the live object). (c) `awareness.ts` — `AwarenessLike` *structural* interface (no `y-protocols` dependency — keeps the React binding decoupled from transport) + `awarenessStore` (`{clientID, local, states}`, version-stable). (d) `hooks.tsx` — thin `useSyncExternalStore` wrappers `useYText` / `useYMap` (whole-map | single-key overloads) / `useYXmlFragment` / `useYDoc` / `useAwareness`. (e) `provider.tsx` — `<YDocProvider>` injects the `entityId → Y.Doc` resolver; `useYDoc(doc)` works today (used by `@brainstorm/editor` 9.2), `useYDoc(entityId)` throws a Stage-9.3 pointer until the SDK installs the resolver (avoid-blocking-on-deps: pure hooks ship now, entity resolution wires at 9.3). Read-only by construction — mutations flow through the SDK's `entities.update`. Package gains `react` (optional peer) + `yjs` (peer) per the `@brainstorm/sdk` pattern. **No OQs blocked** (OQ-9 full-replica + OQ-18 worker-canonical already resolved; the IPC sync transport is the existing renderer↔ydoc-worker bridge, transparent to these hooks). **Tests:** +25 across 4 files — `subscription.test.ts` 11 (coalescing, flush, equals-gating, snapshot stability, ref-count bind/unbind, resync, dispose, post-unsubscribe no-notify, `shallowMapEquals`), `stores.test.ts` 6 (real in-memory Y.Doc: transaction coalescing, shallow-stable map, single-key isolation, version bumps, **two-replica CRDT round-trip convergence over 200 seeded ops**, deep fragment mutation), `awareness.test.ts` 3 (structural fake — snapshot, microtask-once, null clear), `hooks.test.tsx` 5 (first jsdom render test in the repo: every hook end-to-end via `react-dom/client` + async `act`, both `useYDoc` paths incl. provider release-on-unmount + the Stage-9.3 throw via an error boundary). **2456 tests pass across 212 files** (+27 net). `tsc --noEmit` clean; `biome check` clean across all new files. #### 9.3.1 — The real entities service comes online (CRUD + query, capability-gated)

✅ DONE (2026-05-15). **The real entities service comes online (CRUD + query, capability-gated).** (a) `main/storage/entities-repo/entities-repo.ts` — `EntitiesRepository` over `entities.db` (the Stage-3 `entities`/`links`/`change_log` tables, previously unused): `create`/`get`/`update` (shallow property merge + `change_log` version bump)/`softDelete` (cascades to incident links)/`query`/`putLink`/`deleteLink`/`linksFrom`. `query` compiles `EntityQuery` → SQL: `type`/`spaceId` (scalar|array, empty-array short-circuits), `text` (lowercased `LIKE` over the JSON blob), `orderBy` (`updatedAt`/`createdAt`/property), `limit`, a recursive `PropertyPredicate` compiler (`$eq`/`$contains`/`$gt`/`$lt`/`$exists`/`$and`/`$or` → `json_extract`), and a `LinkPredicate` `EXISTS` sub-query. Property keys in JSON paths (which can't be bound params) are validated against a strict charset → `Invalid` on anything unsafe (SQL-injection closed); values are always bound. Soft-delete filtered on every read; corrupt property blobs degrade to `{}` rather than failing a query. All SQL stays in the repo (Stage-5 repository pattern). (b) `main/entities/entities-service.ts` — `makeEntitiesServiceHandler`, broker service `"entities"`. `create` stamps `createdBy = envelope.app`. Per-type capability enforcement against the per-vault ledger (`entities.read:<type>` / `entities.write:<type>`, `*`-scope matches any): reads **silently filter** rows whose type the app can't read (per docs/apps/08 + docs/security/09 — surfacing existence is itself information), writes throw `Denied`. Because the type isn't known until a row is fetched, the per-call broker gate is intentionally `caps: []` and the handler is the sole authority; a `LedgerUnavailableError` / no-vault fails closed as `Unavailable`. (c) `sdk/runtime.ts` — `entitiesPlaceholder()` replaced by `entitiesProxy(bridge)` matching the `EntitiesService` sdk-type (`get`/`query`/`create`/`update`/`delete` over the bridge; `subscribe` is a no-op default the preload overrides via the existing `app:vault-entities-changed` IPC). (d) `main/index.ts` — registered on the broker beside the `vault-entities` preview (which keeps running — apps migrate off the per-app-KV aggregator onto this **per-iteration**, avoid-blocking; not a flag day), with the same successful-mutation → staleness-broadcast + search-reindex wrap the storage handler uses. **Tests:** +17 across 2 files — `entities-repo.test.ts` (real `bun:sqlite` via `DataStores`: CRUD, merge + change-version, soft-delete cascade + idempotency, every query facet + every predicate operator, link `EXISTS`, unsafe-key rejection, corrupt-blob tolerance), `entities-service.test.ts` (createdBy stamp, read-filter + write-`Denied` per type, missing-id `Invalid`, idempotent delete, unknown method `Invalid`, no-vault + `LedgerUnavailableError` → `Unavailable` fail-closed). Existing `runtime.test.ts` placeholder assertion updated (entities is now a live proxy; `files` stays the placeholder). **2495 tests pass across 219 files** (+17). `tsc --noEmit` clean; `biome check` clean. `test:coverage` 0% repo-wide is the pre-existing `bun --bun vitest` environmental issue (see 9.1 note), not a regression.

#### 9.3.2 — `createYDocResolver` — the renderer-side Y.Doc replica resolver core

✅ DONE (2026-05-15, resolver core). **`createYDocResolver` — the renderer-side Y.Doc replica resolver core.** Pure + transport-injected (mirrors how 9.1's subscription core landed before its consumers): `packages/react-yjs/src/resolver.ts` produces a `YDocResolver` compatible with 9.1's `<YDocProvider>`. (a) `resolve(entityId)` is **synchronous** (the `<YDocProvider>` contract) so it returns an empty `Y.Doc` immediately and hydrates it from the canonical snapshot **asynchronously** — the 9.1 hooks re-render when it lands; `whenLoaded(entityId)` is the await point `getYFragment`/`getYText` will use. (b) **Echo-suppression**: canonical-applied updates carry a `REMOTE_ORIGIN` symbol so the outbound `doc.on("update")` observer never ships them back as local edits (the classic Yjs-provider feedback-loop bug, structurally prevented). (c) **Refcount**: N consumers of the same entity share one replica + one `load`; `release()` is per-handle idempotent; the canonical handle is freed (`transport.release`) only on the last release; re-resolving after full release re-opens. (d) **Transport-injected** `YDocTransport { load / persist / release / onRemote? }` — the IPC plumbing is a parameter, so the core is exhaustively tested without IPC/React and is unaffected by how 9.3.2b wires it. `onRemote` (live inbound) is optional and **absent in 9.3.2** — a failed/empty load leaves a usable offline-from-canonical replica (OQ-9). **Tests:** +9 in `resolver.test.ts` (snapshot hydration w/o echo, local-edit→persist, inbound-apply w/o echo, refcount share+single-load, last-release-frees, per-handle idempotent release, dispose, failed-load offline replica, no-`onRemote` transport, `vi.fn` release-exactly-once). **2504 tests pass across 220 files** (+9). `tsc`/`biome` clean.

#### 9.3.2b — The rich-text Y.Doc transport — `useYDoc(entityId)` works end-to-end

✅ DONE (2026-05-15). **The rich-text Y.Doc transport — `useYDoc(entityId)` works end-to-end.** (a) `entities-service.ts` gains `loadDoc` / `applyDoc` / `closeDoc`, gated by the **same per-type ledger check** as the property CRUD (`loadDoc` needs `entities.read:<type>`, `applyDoc` needs `entities.write:<type>`; `closeDoc` ungated idempotent cleanup; no-vault / not-wired → `Unavailable`; missing entity → `Invalid`). No new app-callable service or privileged channel — the entities service is already the per-type capability authority and proxies the `ydoc` worker in-process (`main/index.ts` injects `getVaultPath` + a `ydoc(method,args)` invoker that calls the registered `ydoc` broker handler with a synthetic shell envelope). (b) `sdk-types` `EntitiesService` gains `loadDoc`/`applyDoc`/`closeDoc` — **base64 strings only, no yjs types cross the boundary** so sdk-types stays yjs-free; `sdk` `entitiesProxy` implements them. (c) `app-preload.ts` builds a `YDocTransport` over those (atob/btoa — sandboxed preload has no Buffer), feeds it to the tested **`createYDocResolver`** core (9.3.2), and exposes `window.brainstorm.ydoc = { resolve, getYFragment, getYText }` — `resolve` is the `<YDocProvider resolver=…>` value (release-managed via `useYDoc`); `getYFragment`/`getYText` resolve+await-snapshot then hand back the live CRDT type. `@brainstorm/react-yjs` added as a shell dep (pure core, no React pulled). **Tests:** +3 `entities-service.test.ts` (loadDoc read-gated + missing→Invalid + Denied; applyDoc write-gated; closeDoc idempotent+ungated; not-wired→Unavailable; ydoc invoker called with right args). **2526 tests across 223 files.** `tsc`/`biome` clean. Live cross-window inbound convergence (`onRemote` — needs a ydoc-worker→renderer broadcast) remains **9.3.2c**; single-writer-per-entity (the dominant case) works now. This closes the 9.1/9.2 editor seam — Notes' real Lexical-over-Yjs editing + the per-app store migrations that need rich text are unblocked.

#### 9.3.2c — Live cross-window inbound convergence

✅ DONE (2026-05-15). **Live cross-window inbound convergence.** Two windows editing the same entity now converge without reload. (a) `entities-service` keeps a refcounted `${vaultPath}::${entityId} → app` subscriber map: `loadDoc` registers *after* the read gate + a successful worker load, `closeDoc` releases (refcounted — intra-app windows share one renderer/Y.Doc per OQ-4 (b)), `applyDoc` fans the just-applied delta to every *other* subscriber app (originator excluded — its own renderer already has the edit). (b) New `main/entities/ydoc-remote-broadcast.ts` (`APP_YDOC_REMOTE_CHANNEL` + `deliverYDocUpdateToApps`) mirrors `vault-entities-broadcast` but is payload-bearing: it must carry the Yjs delta because the resolver's `onRemote(apply)` contract is delta-shaped and a full-snapshot re-load per remote keystroke is a live-editing anti-pattern. **Security envelope held at the source, not the channel:** `targetApps` is only ever the read-gated, replica-holding subset the service computed, and delivery is a strict subset of that (empty list → nothing) — no new authorization surface. (c) `app-preload.ts` implements `ydocTransport.onRemote` over a single `app:ydoc-remote` listener + a per-entity sink map; the resolver applies inbound updates with `REMOTE_ORIGIN` so they are not echoed back through `persist`. **Tests:** +10 — react-yjs resolver cross-window convergence + detach-stops-delivery (echo-suppression asserted), entities-service fan-out/originator-exclusion/refcounted-unsubscribe, new `ydoc-remote-broadcast.test.ts` (targetApps filter, skip destroyed, fail-closed empty, resilient send). **2598 tests across 233 files.** `tsc` clean; `biome` clean (also cleared 2 pre-existing mcp-server lint nits + the new import ordering). No OQ gated it. This completes the 9.3.2 ladder — collaborative multi-window editing on the shared object space is live.

#### 9.3.2d — `docSubscribers` lifetime hardening

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **`docSubscribers` subscriber-map lifetime hardening — closes the chores-convergence item from the 9.3.2c security / pentest / memory-leak passes.** The refcounted `${vaultPath}::${entityId} → app` map was service-lifetime and only shrank on an explicit `closeDoc`, so (a) a renderer that crashed / closed without `closeDoc` left its `app → count` row forever, and (b) a vault switch/close orphaned every entry (the old `vaultPath`-embedded subKeys can never match the new vault's fresh `loadDoc`s). Both are bounded-safe (no misdelivery — post-switch subKey differs and `deliverYDocUpdateToApps` already skips `isDestroyed()` windows; no new disclosure — a stale app already holds the gated plaintext replica), so this is hardening, not a bug fix. (a) **Renderer-death prune:** `deliverYDocUpdateToApps` now returns the subset of `targetApps` with **no live window** (an app with ≥1 non-destroyed window is live even if a sibling window died); `applyDoc`'s fan-out deletes those from the subscriber map and drops the subKey when it empties — the dead app's refcount can no longer leak for the service lifetime. (b) **Vault-change clear:** the handler tracks `lastVaultPath` (via the already-injected `getVaultPath`) and `docSubscribers.clear()`s the first envelope it observes the active vault path change (incl. → `null` on close); the initial `undefined → first path` transition is a no-op clear of the empty map. No new capability surface, no new IPC channel, no new dep (return-value widen + an internal counter only). **Tests:** +10 — `ydoc-remote-broadcast.test.ts` (return `[]` all-live, app with no window, app whose only window is destroyed, one-live-one-destroyed → not pruned, empty `targetApps`); `entities-service.test.ts` (applyDoc prunes a dead subscriber so a later applyDoc no longer targets it; vault switch → no cross-vault fan-out; vault close (`null`) clears + Unavailable + re-open starts empty). **2925 tests across 272 files** (+10; the single failure is a pre-existing, unrelated `apps/files/tests/i18n.test.ts` from an uncommitted edit that deleted the `…footer.runtimeReady` key — not touched by this entities-only change). `tsc --noEmit` clean; `biome check` clean on all touched files. No OQ gated it. Closes the 9.3.2 ladder's deferred hardening rung.

#### 9.22.3 — Tasks + Notes inline search bars

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **The user-facing payoff of the 9.22 engine inside the two text-heaviest apps — type to filter your own objects by relevance, not recency.** Both apps now carry a persistent inline search bar that queries the shell's vault-wide FTS5 index via `services.search.query` (capability `search.read`, a default-minimum grant) and re-projects the app's *own* in-memory entities down to the matched id set, in the index's rank order. **Shared keystone:** new `@brainstorm/sdk` `orderByHitRank(items, hits, idOf)` — the rank-projection every searching app needs (Tasks/Notes now, Database/Calendar later): keeps only items whose id is a hit, in hit order, deduped, skipping hits the app's list doesn't currently hold (sibling-app / since-deleted ids); pure, input-non-mutating, 7 SDK tests. Written once so the dedupe/ordering edge cases aren't re-derived per app (CLAUDE.md DRY — 2 uses today with a third imminent). **Tasks (vanilla TS):** the search input lives in `index.html` *outside* the re-rendered content slot (a persistent `.tasks-content-col`), so the app's full-replace render loop never steals input focus mid-type — the recurring trap with imperative re-render. New pure `logic/search-results.ts` (`taskSearchFromHits` = `orderByHitRank`; `localTaskMatch` name/notes scan), `ui/surface-view.ts` grows `renderSearchView` + an extracted shared `renderTaskList` (DRY with `renderSection` — a search row is byte-identical to a surface row), `app.ts` wires a 150 ms-debounced query with a monotonic stale-token guard (a slow earlier keystroke can't clobber a newer result), Escape-to-clear + `Cmd/Ctrl+F` focus via two new `ActionId`s (no raw `e.key`), results derived from live `state.tasks` at render so toggling a task while searching updates the row with no re-query. **Notes (React):** `store/search-results.ts` (`noteSearchOrder` / `localNoteOrder` over title + `extractPlainText(body)`), `NotesList` gained an optional `order` (render exactly these ids in rank order vs. the default recency sort) + `emptyLabel`, `app.tsx` adds the sidebar search field with the same debounce/stale-guard/Escape/`Mod+F` shape (element-scoped `matchesActionChord` for Escape so it doesn't fight the editor's other Escape bindings), `searchOrder` is `useMemo`'d off the live `notes` map so an edit while searching is reflected without a re-query. **No-search-service degrade (preview / older shells):** both fall back to a local substring scan so the bar is never dead. Manifests already declare `search.read` (default grant — no new capability surface); no new IPC, no new dependency. Chrome is shared tokens only (`--color-*`/`--space-*`/`--radius-*`), decorative SVGs `aria-hidden`, inputs `aria-label`led, every string `t()`-wrapped, the clear affordance never doubles a glyph into label text. **Tests:** +7 SDK `search-filter.test.ts`, +6 `apps/tasks/src/logic/search-results.test.ts`, +5 `apps/notes/src/store/search-results.test.ts`. 418 tests across the tasks/notes/sdk suites green; `@brainstorm-app/tasks` + `@brainstorm-app/notes` builds green; app-tsc clean on every touched file in both apps (the 6 `'id' specified more than once` are the repo-wide test-fixture spread idiom, identical across the existing logic tests); workspace `typecheck` clean except the 5 pre-existing unrelated `react-dom/client` errors; `biome` clean on all touched files. No OQ gated it; **OQ-SR-1** untouched (query path unchanged). This closes the 9.22 ladder except 9.22.5's deliberately-deferred body→Y.Doc reindex note.

#### 9.22.4 — Settings → Search index panel

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **A diagnostic + manual-maintenance surface for the vault-wide lexical index — the user-visible payoff of the 9.22 engine.** The index is self-healing (rebuilt on every launch + after every entities write, per `search-indexer.ts`), so this panel is honest about that: it *reports* health and offers a manual rebuild for when a user wants to force one, rather than implying the index needs babysitting. **What landed:** (a) `SearchIndexer.stats()` — pure aggregate queries (no full scan): `total`, `byType` (per-type counts, busiest-first, ties broken by type name), `lastIndexedAt` (newest sidecar `updated_at`), `bytes` (`page_count × page_size`, wrapped in a try/catch + a driver-shape-tolerant `readPragmaNumber` so an encrypted-at-rest DB or a pragma-shy driver degrades to 0, never blanks the panel). (b) The indexable predicate was inlined in `rebuild()` only; extracted to exported `isIndexable` + `pickIndexable` and `rebuild()` now routes through it — so the panel's "indexed vs. available" coverage can't drift from what a rebuild actually writes (DRY, the 3-use rule applied at 2 with a correctness reason). (c) `search-handlers.ts` gained `search:stats` + `search:reindex` privileged IPC (same shell-trust model as the launcher's `search:query` — apps never reindex); `registerSearchHandlers` now takes a `{getIndexer, reindex, getAvailableCount}` deps object. `getAvailableCount` runs the *same* `collectIndexableEntities` + `pickIndexable` the rebuild path uses, so coverage is a true estimate of source-vs-index, and `null` (no session / scan threw) renders as "—" not a misleading 0%. Each half of the report degrades independently. (d) New **Settings → Search index** section (own `SettingsSection.Search` enum member + nav entry, `IconName.Search`) — a 4-card stat grid (indexed / coverage-with-bar / last-indexed / size), a `Reindex now` Glass button with an in-flight `Reindexing…` state + success toast, and a by-type breakdown with proportional bars. Chrome is all existing tokens + the shared `Button`/`Icon`/`pushToast`/`settings__*` primitives — zero hardcoded colours/sizes; the coverage bar is `aria-hidden` (the % and "X of Y indexable" sub-line already carry the value for assistive tech — no redundant focus stop). Affected suites: 51 search/format/ipc tests green; 49 `main/ipc` green. `bun run typecheck` clean for every touched file (the 5 pre-existing `react-dom/client` errors in unrelated `packages/sdk/src/property-ui/*.test.tsx` are byte-identical pre/post — proven by a stash baseline — and out of scope); `biome check` clean on all 12 touched files. #### 9.22.5 — Broaden the search indexer past Notes

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **Cross-app full-text search now actually covers every app, not just Notes.** User-reported: global search returned no Task hits. Root cause: `collect-indexable.ts` hard-scanned only `io.brainstorm.notes/kv.json` `note:` rows, but since 9.3.5.x Tasks/Bookmarks/Calendar/Whiteboard/Notes all persist to `entities.db` — none of those non-Note types were ever fed to FTS5. The reindex *trigger* was already correct (`index.ts` fires `rebuildSearchIndex()` on entities `create/update/delete`); the only gap was the collector's source. ""` and `body` = rich-text `extractNoteBodyText(properties.body)` ⧺ every other top-level **primitive string** property value (so a Task's `description`, a Bookmark's `url`, an Event's `location` are findable with no per-type allowlist to maintain), clamped to a 100k-char per-entity cap; objects/arrays are never `JSON.stringify`'d into the row. #### 9.17.6b — Whiteboard edge-label authoring

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **Connectors can now carry a label, authored in place.** `WhiteboardEdge.label` was already modelled + persisted (codec) + drawn, but (a) there was no way for a user to set one and (b) the label was positioned at the naive chord midpoint `(from+to)/2`, so on bent (bezier/step) edges it floated off the line. **What landed:** (a) `logic/edge-path.ts` refactored so the `d`-builders and a new pure `edgePathMidpoint(kind, from, fromSide, to, toSide)` share one geometry source — extracted `bezierControlPoints` + `stepPolyline` (the `d`-string builders now consume them too, so output is byte-identical — proven by the 11 pre-existing edge-path tests still green). Midpoint = bezier curve at `t=0.5` (de Casteljau on the real control points), step = the point at half the elbow polyline's **arc length** (not vertex count, so a long mid-segment doesn't skew it), straight = segment midpoint; degenerate `from==to` anchors at the point, never `NaN`. This is the long-term keystone that survives the 9.17.5 Pixi swap exactly like `edgePath` (same rationale, now shared). (b) `app.ts` — every edge group gets a wide **invisible hit-path** (`stroke:transparent; stroke-width:16; pointer-events:stroke`) so the 2 px visible line is a comfortable double-click target; the label bg/text now anchor at `edgePathMidpoint`. Double-click an edge → `beginEditEdgeLabel`: sets `state.editingEdgeId`, repaints so `paintEdges` renders an SVG `<foreignObject>` `<input>` centred on the midpoint, then focuses+selects it and binds commit/cancel via the shortcut registry (`ActionId.CommitEdit`/`CancelEdit`, element-scoped `{target,allowInTyping}` — no raw `e.key`, mirrors the node `beginEdit` split). Commit on blur/Enter; Escape cancels; an empty value clears the label back to `null`; one `repository.saveEdge(edge)` per commit (never per keystroke), `updatedAt` bumped. (c) i18n keys (`whiteboard.edge.label.aria` / `.placeholder`); styles use tokens only (`--accent`/`--bg`/`--text`/`--radius-sm`/`--text-size-xs`/`--space-xs`), foreignObject input re-enables `pointer-events` inside the `pointer-events:none` edge SVG. **Keyboard path:** double-click edge → type → Enter commit / Esc cancel. **Discoverability:** the text cursor over the fat hit-path on hover. **Tests:** +5 `edge-path.test.ts` (`edgePathMidpoint`: straight exact, bezier symmetric→centre, bezier bows off-chord when both handles same side, step on-polyline at half arc length, degenerate finite) — 16 edge-path tests total; 162 whiteboard tests across 13 files green; `@brainstorm-app/whiteboard` build green (17.13 KB gz); app-tsc clean on `app.ts` + `edge-path.ts`; `biome` clean. No new dependency, no OQ gated it. **Remaining 9.17 connector polish → 9.17.6c:** step-path obstacle routing (route the elbow around intervening node rectangles) — deliberately scoped out so this lands as a complete, tested increment rather than two half-features; the `stepPolyline` keystone it will extend is now isolated and tested.

#### 9.17.6c — Whiteboard obstacle-aware step routing

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **Step connectors now leave/enter their handles with a clearance stub and route their elbow clear of the two endpoint node boxes** — fixing the most visible step-path defect (a connector slicing straight back across the node it just left, or the corner overlapping a node). Builds directly on the `stepPolyline` keystone isolated in 9.17.6b. **What landed (all pure, in `logic/edge-path.ts`):** (a) `stepPolylineAvoiding(from, fromSide, to, toSide, obstacles?, clearance?)` — the path goes straight out of each handle by `DEFAULT_STEP_CLEARANCE` (18px) along its normal to a *stub point*, then connects the two stubs with the elbow (X-first / Y-first) whose middle segments don't cross either inflated endpoint box; if **both** simple elbows are blocked (handles facing into a gap with a box between), a deterministic detour routes around the obstacles' union bbox + clearance. (b) `segIntersectsRect` — exact axis-aligned segment↔rect overlap (step segments are always H or V; a border graze is *not* a hit, so a stub leaving its own node edge doesn't self-trip). (c) `polylinePathD` (shared `M…L…` builder) + `polylineMidpoint` exported, so the Step renderer's path string **and** its 9.17.6b label both derive from the *same* routed polyline — they can't disagree. **Key correctness fix found via the failing test (reproduce-first):** the obstacle check must exempt the stub segments — the handle sits on the node's boundary, so a handle→stub segment always "touches" the inflated box; including it flagged every elbow as blocked and forced a needless detour. Now only the inter-stub route is tested. **Scope (v1):** the two endpoint boxes only — full scene-wide visibility-graph avoidance stays a later rung (noted); this is deterministic, allocation-light, pure, and survives the 9.17.5 Pixi swap unchanged (same rationale as `edgePath`). **`app.ts`:** the Step branch builds `pts = stepPolylineAvoiding(from, …, [sourceRect, destRect])`, `d = polylinePathD(pts)`, `mid = polylineMidpoint(pts)`; bezier/straight keep the analytic helpers. `EdgePathKind` promoted from a type-only to a value import (it's now switched on at runtime — guards the [[app-tsc-not-gated / import-type trap]]). **Tests:** +8 `edge-path.test.ts` (`segIntersectsRect` cross/graze/vertical; `polylinePathD`; `stepPolylineAvoiding` stub-clearance, endpoint-box-clear, both-blocked-detour-stays-clear, no-obstacle clean elbow) — 24 edge-path tests; 170 whiteboard tests across 13 files green; `@brainstorm-app/whiteboard` build green; app-tsc clean on `app.ts` + `edge-path.ts`; `biome` clean. No new dependency, no OQ gated it. Closes the 9.17 connector-polish track; **9.17.5** (Pixi renderer swap mirroring Graph 9.13.5) is the remaining Whiteboard rung.

#### Database Filter v2.1b — nested filter groups

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **The Database filter model is now an arbitrarily deep AND/OR tree (`A AND (B OR C)`), and a nested filter authored elsewhere / synced in round-trips losslessly instead of being silently flattened.** `filter-builder.ts`'s comment had explicitly deferred this as "v2.1b". **What landed (pure keystone):** `FilterDraft` gains an **additive** optional `groups?: FilterDraft[]` — a draft with no `groups` is byte-for-byte the old flat draft, so every persisted view + existing call site round-trips with **zero migration** (the 18 pre-existing flat tests pass unchanged, proving it). `draftToFilterNode` recurses: rule-children ∪ recursively-compiled sub-group children, declaration order; incomplete rules and groups that compile to nothing are pruned, and a group left with no surviving children compiles to `null` (an empty group never silently filters everything out). `filterNodeToDraft` recurses too — group children now reconstruct into `groups` (previously **dropped**, so a re-opened nested filter was a lie — a real correctness fix). New pure helpers: `countDraftRules` / `isDraftEmpty` (whole-tree, complete-rules-only) + `describeGroup` (`(2 rules · ANY)` / `(empty group)`, using the group's *own* join word). **Renderer (throwaway menu chain, per the module's own guidance):** `openFilterMenu` lists each sub-group as a row opening `openFilterGroupMenu` (its rules with delete · group-op toggle · add-rule-to-group · remove-group); a new "Add nested group" action appends a group defaulting to the **opposite** join (the reason to nest is almost always `… AND (x OR y)`); the property→operator chain takes an optional `groupIndex` so an added rule lands in the targeted sub-group; every commit rebuilds the whole draft immutably so `commitFilterDraft` stays the single write path. The model + converters handle **any depth**; the throwaway chain authors one nesting level (tractable until fancy-menus exposes the full tree). **Tests:** +8 `apps/database/tests/filter-builder.test.ts` (flat byte-identical; `A AND (B OR C)` compile; empty/all-incomplete sub-group pruned; only-empty-groups → null; 3-level node→draft→node fixpoint; non-flattening reconstruction; `countDraftRules`/`isDraftEmpty` tree-walk; `describeGroup`) — 26 filter tests; 230 Database tests across the suite green; `@brainstorm-app/database` build green; **app-tsc added zero new errors** (27 with/without my changes via a stash baseline — the 27 are the pre-existing unrelated `ListSource`/`list.source` drift documented at 9.3.5.1b, out of scope); `biome` clean on touched files. No new dependency, no OQ gated it. Closes the Filter v2.x track; remaining Database work is the 9.12.16 import UI slice + 9.12.13(c) dashboard PinnedList.

#### 9.13.10a — Graph history reveal modes

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **The history scrubber gains the three documented reveal curves (Strict / Eased / Recent), user-selectable and persisted.** The scrubber UI (play/pause/speed/drag/date/count) already shipped in 9.13.1.x, and `scene.ts` already had a single hardcoded Eased linear-window alpha; this lands the missing *behaviour*. **Pure keystone:** `scene.ts` exports `computeRevealAlpha(createdAt, cutoffAt, reveal, easeWindowMs, recentWindowMs)` — `cutoffAt===null` ⇒ 1 (history off); **Strict** = hard step (`delta>=0?1:0`); **Eased** = the long-standing centred linear window (formula byte-unchanged, so every existing scene/alpha test stays green — back-compat proven); **Recent** = not-yet-created→0, fully lit for the trailing `recentWindowMs` after it appears, then a linear fade to `RECENT_FLOOR_ALPHA` (0.15, never 0 — "Recent" *dims* history, the cutoff *hides* it) over the next window: a comet tail that keeps the settled graph legible while fresh edits pop. `computeAlpha` is now a thin wrapper; `SceneOptions` gains `reveal` + `recentWindowMs` (defaults `Eased` / 7 d, so `DEFAULT_SCENE_OPTIONS` callers — incl. tests — are unaffected). **Wiring:** app-local `GraphSettings` gains `reveal` (rides the existing `graph:state` persistence — `PersistedState.version` 5→6, `CURRENT_PERSISTED_VERSION` bumped in lockstep; `applyPersistedState` defaults legacy payloads to Eased via the established `?? state.settings` migration-tolerant pattern, and `shouldRestorePersisted` already accepts any sane version so nothing is discarded). `sceneOptionsFrom` threads `reveal`+`recentWindowMs`; a new `#reveal-btn` in the scrubber chrome cycles Strict→Eased→Recent (mirrors the sibling `#speed-btn` exactly — `dataset.bound` guard, label refresh, `reconcileScene`+`schedulePersist`); label is a literal like its siblings (the Graph app has no i18n manifest yet — folds into `t()` when it gets one, noted). **Tests:** +5 `scene.test.ts` `computeRevealAlpha` (history-off all modes; Strict step; Eased centred-window unchanged; Recent fresh→1 / comet-tail half-fade / floor-clamp / never-0; every mode ∈ [0,1]) — 19 scene tests; 152 graph tests across the suite green; `persisted-version.test` green at v6 (it loops `1..CURRENT`, no hardcoded literal); `@brainstorm-app/graph` build green; app-tsc clean on `scene.ts`/`app.ts`/`persisted-version.ts` (the lone pre-existing unrelated `app.ts:2113 === "1"` SDK-version error is byte-identical, out of scope per 9.13.5a); `biome` clean. #### 9.13.10b — OQ-GR-3: legacy `created_at` backfill

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **Resolves OQ-GR-3 (the long-open blocker on 9.13.10) — legacy graph rows with a missing `created_at` no longer pile at the 1970 epoch and wreck the history scrubber the 9.13.10a reveal modes ride.** Implements the OQ's tentative-leaning **option (c)**. New pure `apps/graph/src/logic/history-backfill.ts` `backfillCreatedAt(graph)`: a link's ts = `MAX(link.createdAt, source_entity.createdAt)` (an edge can't predate the node it leaves; a missing link ts inherits its source's — "the edge appeared around when the source did"); an entity, or a link whose source is itself timeless / absent, with no usable ts falls back to the **minimum known timestamp** across the whole graph, so a legacy element shows near frame 0 instead of dragging the scrubber bounds back to the epoch. "Usable" = positive finite (real vault ts ≈ 1.7e12; legacy gaps are 0 / NaN / negative). **Pure** (returns a fresh `InMemoryGraph`, never mutates — verified by a `structuredClone` snapshot test), **idempotent** (a real ts is only ever pushed later, never rewritten on a second pass — `backfill(backfill(g))` deep-equals `backfill(g)`), and **degenerate-safe** (empty / all-timeless graph → no-op, no NaN/throw). Wired at the single seam where the vault snapshot becomes the graph (`app.ts` `loadVaultEntities`: `state.db = backfillCreatedAt(vaultSnapshotToInMemoryGraph(snapshot))`) so every reveal mode + the scrubber bounds are correct for upgraded vaults. The pre-entities-service in-memory model has no SQL `UPDATE`/audit-log surface, so this is the in-memory pass; the keystone survives the Stage 9.3 swap (the same rule becomes the server-side one-shot `UPDATE` + audit row-count when the entities service lands). **Tests:** +10 `history-backfill.test.ts` (fully-timestamped untouched; timeless link inherits source; MAX never moves a real ts earlier; later-than-source kept; timeless entity → floor; timeless/absent source → floor transitively; idempotent; no input mutation; empty + all-zero degrade). 162 graph tests across the suite green; `@brainstorm-app/graph` build green; app-tsc clean on `app.ts`/`history-backfill.ts` (the lone pre-existing unrelated `app.ts:2113` SDK-version error is byte-identical, out of scope per 9.13.5a); `biome` clean. No new dependency. **OQ-GR-3 marked RESOLVED** in the ledger (option c). **Split:** the typed `HistoryAnimationState`/graph-view wiring + the `entities.subscribe({historyForPatternId})` bucketed event stream are the remaining **9.13.10c** slice — kept separate so the OQ-resolving backfill lands as a complete, tested increment.

#### 9.20.7a — Audio inspector ID3 enrichment

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). **A sound file's Quick Look now shows its track metadata (Title / Artist / Album / Genre / Year) like Finder, not just duration + format.** The 9.20.3 audio renderer header had flagged ID3 as a "9.20.7 inspector rung" TODO; this lands it. New pure `apps/preview/src/logic/id3.ts` `parseId3(bytes)` — a bounds-checked ID3 reader built to the same discipline as the existing `exif.ts` (9.20.2): the 10-byte ID3v2 header (`ID3`, major-version gate 2/3/4, syncsafe tag size), an **entry-capped** frame walk (≤256, stops at a padding run), text frames for the mapped ids (TIT2/TPE1/TALB/TCON/TYER/TDRC + the v2.2 3-char TT2/TP1/TAL/TCO/TYE), per-frame text-encoding byte honoured (0 latin1 / 1 UTF-16+BOM / 2 UTF-16BE / 3 UTF-8) via `TextDecoder`, v2.3 plain-32 vs v2.4 syncsafe frame sizes both handled; every offset validated against the buffer and **any** structural problem degrades to `{}` (a corrupt MP3 must never wedge the previewer). When no v2 tag is present it falls back to the **ID3v1 128-byte trailer**; v2 wins when both exist. `formatId3Pairs` emits present fields only in display order (mirrors `formatExifPairs`). #### B7.1a — OQ-COV-1 resolved + cover-colour normalization keystone (B7.2 gate)

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). The plan gates B7.2/B7.3 on **OQ-COV-1**; this resolves it (adopting the tentative leaning, with the concrete decision-(3) wire encoding pinned) and lands the one pure-SDK keystone the resolution requires — the rest of B7.2 (picker UI, upload, `brainstorm://cover/` protocol, Settings library) is shell-main + renderer-ui work that rides Stage 9.3 and is currently locked under a large parallel in-flight change, so this iteration is **deliberately scoped to the clean zone** (`packages/sdk` + `docs`), touching zero files in the in-flight set.

**OQ-COV-1 resolution** (recorded in [reference/11-open-questions.md](reference/11-open-questions.md), [foundations/50-object-covers.md](foundations/50-object-covers.md) §Shape, the B7-ladder plan intro): (1) **storage = both** — `properties.cover` is the data (reserved universal property, sibling to `icon`/`body`, zero BP/schema change), the `cover` chrome cell is its layout-driven placement; (2) **precedence** `view.coverProperty → properties.cover → id-seeded gradient`, an explicit view "none" suppresses the band for that view only (no fall-through); (3) **theme-awareness** — `CoverKind.Color` is a theme-token `var(--token)` reference by default (the `--token` shorthand normalised), an absolute literal the explicit escape hatch; validated to a *single* token or *single* colour shape — never multiple tokens / `var(--x, …)` fallback / arbitrary CSS — because it is interpolated into an inline `style`. The curated gradient set stays a theme-neutral key by design (content, not chrome).

**Keystone.** `normalizeCoverColor(value): {css, themed} | null` in `@brainstorm/sdk/entity-cover` — `--x`/`var(--x)` → `{css:"var(--x)", themed:true}`; an allow-listed literal *shape* (hex 3/4/6/8, `rgb()/hsl()/hwb()/oklch()/oklab()/lab()/lch()/color()` with a `;{}:`-free charset, or a ≤30-char letters-only keyword) → `{css, themed:false}`; everything else (multi-token, `var()` fallback arg, `url(...)`, `;`/`{`/`}`, >64 chars, non-string) → `null`. `resolveCoverBackground`'s `Color` branch now routes through it: unrecognised/unsafe degrades to the id-seeded gradient instead of interpolating attacker-controlled text into an inline `style` — closing an injection vector B7.1 left open (it passed `cover.value` verbatim). Single keystone, so `<EntityCover>` + `createEntityCoverElement` inherit the fix with no change. **Security note (per Standard 3):** the new surface is user-controlled colour data reaching an inline `style`; the strict shape allow-list (deny-by-default, no escape characters possible in any accepted form) is the mitigation, covered by adversarial tests.

**Tests:** +4 net in `packages/sdk/src/entity-cover.test.ts` (24 total) — a `normalizeCoverColor` block (token shorthand/`var()`/whitespace normalisation; every literal shape; rejection of non-string/empty/over-long/`red; } body{…}`/`url(...)`/`var(--x, red)`/multi-token/`expression(...)`/`{}`) + a `resolveCoverBackground` adversarial case (each evil value → exact id-seeded gradient). `bun run typecheck` clean (0 errors); `bunx biome check` clean on touched files.

**Suite:** `Tests 3464 passed` with **+4 from this work and 0 new failures**. #### B7.1b — Per-view cover resolution keystone (OQ-COV-1 decision 2)

✅ DONE (2026-05-18). B7.1a landed OQ-COV-1's decision-(3) keystone; this lands the symmetric **decision-(2)** one — the typed primitive for the per-view precedence `view.coverProperty → properties.cover → id-seeded gradient` *and* the explicit per-view "no band". Without it, B7.3's cross-app adoption would re-implement that rule per app — exactly the rejected anti-pattern the per-object-covers-everywhere invariant forbids (one resolver, not per-app logic). Same constraint as B7.1a: apps + shell-main + renderer-ui are locked under a large parallel in-flight change, so this is **deliberately scoped to the clean zone** (`packages/sdk` + `docs`), touching zero in-flight files.

**What landed** (`@brainstorm/sdk/entity-cover`): `ViewCoverMode` enum (`Inherit` / `Property` / `None`) + `CoverViewSource` union + `resolveCoverForView(subject, source = Inherit)` returning `ResolvedCoverForView` (= `ResolvedCover | { kind: Suppressed }`). `CoverRenderKind` gains `Suppressed` — the one outcome `resolveCoverBackground` can't produce: an explicit per-view "no cover" → the consumer omits the band *for that view only* (never the id-seeded gradient — "none" means *no band*; the object still shows its own cover everywhere else). `Inherit` delegates to `resolveCoverBackground` (id-seeded gradient when the object has no cover); `Property` reads the cover from `properties[key]` and, if that slot isn't a well-formed cover, still yields the id-seeded gradient (never a broken square, never `Suppressed`). `parseCover(raw)` was extracted from `coverOf` (which is now a thin wrapper over it) so the arbitrary-per-view-key validation reuses the exact same guard — DRY, one validator. Enums throughout (no string discriminators).

#### 8.2 — Layout resolver (per `(entity, context)` scope-precedence pick)

✅ DONE (2026-05-18). The pure resolver that, given a render request and the candidate `brainstorm/Layout/v1` entities, picks the winner by doc-27 §Resolution's layered precedence — the natural next clean-zone rung on the 8.1 contract (apps + shell-main + renderer-ui still locked under the parallel in-flight change). No blocking OQ (same gating analysis as 8.1; OQ-90 gates 8.4).

**What landed** (`packages/sdk/src/layout-resolver.ts`, pure — no DOM/dep, subpath-exported `@brainstorm/sdk/layout-resolver` + parallel vitest alias, the entity-cover precedent): `resolveLayout(target, candidates, fallbacks)` → `LayoutResolution` (discriminated by `LayoutResolveSource` enum: `Scope`/`AppDefault`/`ShellFallback`/`None` — provenance the form-designer's "revert to app default" needs). Algorithm faithful to the doc: keep candidates whose `scope` matches the target *and* whose `context` is the requested one or `null` (any); winner = lowest scope rank (`entity > list(=collection) > type > user > org`), then context-specific over any-context at equal scope, then highest `updatedAt` (most-recent-modified), then earliest-listed (stable); on no match → `appDefault` → `shellFallback` → `None`. `app-default`/`shell-fallback` are separate fallback inputs, **not** scope-precedence entries (per the doc's pseudocode), so they never out-rank a real scoped match. `scopeMatches` matches each `Scope` kind against its target dimension and never matches when that dimension is absent (an `org` scope with no `orgId`); multi-typed objects match a `type` scope for *any* of their types. Frozen `SCOPE_PRECEDENCE` exported so callers/tests don't re-encode the chain. **`Scope` reused verbatim** — `list` *is* the doc's "collection" tier (the same membership-overlay mechanism PropertySchema uses) — no parallel scope type.

**8.1 contract refinement (the resolver required it):** `LayoutDef.context` widened `LayoutContext` → `LayoutContext | null`, where `null` is the **any-context wildcard** the doc mandates ("context == C OR context == null"). `validateLayout` updated to accept `null` (only a non-null non-member context is `InvalidContext`); +1 test. Faithful to doc 27 §Resolution, not scope creep — the resolver cannot honour the doc without it; recorded here as an explicit 8.1 adjustment.

✅ DONE (2026-05-15). **Enabling step: the aggregator also surfaces `entities.db` (authoritative + deduped).** `vault-entities-service` gained `aggregateSharedEntities` — after the per-app kv aggregators it reads the real `entities.db` (via an injected structural `SharedEntitiesRepo`, the cached `open("entities")` repo wired in `main/index.ts`) and unions its live entities + outgoing links into the snapshot. **`entities.db` is authoritative**: any kv-derived entity/link with the same id is dropped in favour of the shared-store row, so an app mid-migration never double-renders. #### 9.3.5.3 — Tasks app migrated onto the shared entities service

Manifest already granted the `entities.read/write:brainstorm/{Task,Project}/v1` caps.
