A new shell-side `backfillKvIntoEntities(vaultPath, repo, now?)` (`kv-entities-backfill.ts`) projects every recognised kv blob and writes missing rows + stable-id links into the real store via `EntitiesRepository`: **boot-independent** (wired into `onVaultOpened` driven by `onActiveVaultSessionChanged` in `index.ts`, the same mechanism the search-indexer swap uses — runs *before* `swapSearchIndexer()` and before any app's first `list()`; not dev-gated, no app launch/seed required), **idempotent** (keyed on the stable entity id — present ⇒ skip; links `INSERT OR REPLACE`), **no-clobber** (an existing `entities.db` row is never overwritten — a post-bridge edit through the entities service always wins), **fault-isolated** (scan throw / bad row / storage error logs and bails, never rejects vault-open). Documented edge semantics preserved (dangling links dropped — dest must be in snapshot; note→note edges shell-derived from `body` via `note-entities-codec`; stable-id kv-vs-body dedupe). No first-party app remains kv-bridged for its primary store (per the Core-data-wiring-complete note) — the backfill exists purely so an upgrading user's pre-9.3.5.x kv blob doesn't vanish; kv files are intentionally left in place (read-only, non-destructive bridge — a future iteration may prune post-bridge). **Tests:** read-surface suite rewritten (`vault-entities-service.test.ts` 41→24, kv-scan cases migrated); **+16** `kv-entities-backfill.test.ts` (no-kv no-op; kv-only bridged & surfaces with no kv scan; idempotent across two boots; never clobbers a newer real row; edge/dangling/dedupe; Tasks/Self-hosting projection parity; corrupt-blob isolation; body-edge idempotence); **+1** `app-data-pipeline.test.ts` (boot-independent kv-only-vault end-to-end through the real Broker). #### 9.8.2.7 — Sandbox-safe token decode (every-app theme fix)

✅. **Sandbox-safe token decode (every-app theme fix).** Apps were always opening with their CSS *light* fallback even when the dashboard theme was dark, while live token broadcasts (`app:tokens-changed`) flipped existing windows correctly — diagnostic asymmetry pointing at the initial-token preload path. Root cause: `decodeTokens` in `packages/shell/src/preload/app-preload.ts` used `Buffer.from(encoded, "base64").toString("utf8")`, but Electron's *sandboxed* preload doesn't reliably expose Node globals, and the resulting `ReferenceError` landed inside the function's `try/catch` and silently returned `null` — so every fresh launch dropped the initial-token payload and the apps' CSS `var(--color-*, <light>)` fallbacks took over. The dashboard preload uses `Buffer` too (`packages/shell/src/preload/index.ts:72,75,211`) but only inside lazy `credentials.*` callbacks, so its failure mode never showed. Fix: `decodeTokens` switched to the same `decodeURIComponent(escape(atob(...)))` pattern the handshake uses (sandbox-safe, unicode-aware), and `encodeTokens` in `packages/shell/src/main/apps/launcher.ts` flipped to the symmetric `btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(...)))` so the two ends stay in sync. **Defence in depth:** Graph + Database apps' CSS fallbacks moved from light (`#ffffff`/`#1c2433`) to dark (`#161616`/`#f7f7f7`) — same as Notes + Files — so any future stale-tokens regression paints close-to-correct instead of unreadable-white. **Tests:** +3 in `launcher.test.ts` round-tripping `encodeTokens` through a sandbox-style `atob` decode (regression for the dropped-tokens path), unicode (curly quotes / em dashes / emoji), and a 200-entry payload to exercise typical flattened-token sizes. 1284 tests green (was 1281); typecheck clean; biome clean; full `bun run build` clean.

#### 9.8.2.8 — Theme passed by name, not flattened tokens

✅. **Theme passed by name, not flattened tokens.** Follow-up to 9.8.2.7 — the base64-JSON-arg-over-launch-flag dance was overengineered. The preload already bundles `@brainstorm/tokens` for free (preload config has no `externalizeDepsPlugin`), so it can resolve a theme name through the local registry just as fast as decoding an arg, with none of the serialisation foot-guns. **What changed:** (a) launcher argv flips from `--brainstorm-tokens=<base64-JSON>` to `--brainstorm-theme=<name>`; (b) `app:tokens-changed` IPC channel renamed to `app:theme-changed`, payload is now the bare theme name (`"midnight"`); (c) `encodeTokens` / `decodeTokens` / `backgroundColorFromTokens` deleted from `packages/shell/src/main/apps/launcher.ts`; replaced by a one-liner `backgroundColorForTheme(theme)` that reads `themes[theme].color.background.primary`; (d) `LaunchOptions.tokens` → `LaunchOptions.theme: ThemeName`; (e) orchestrator's `getThemeTokens` → `getActiveTheme: () => Promise<ThemeName | null>`; (f) `launch-setup.ts` getter shrinks from a flatten+lookup pipeline to just `dashboard.snapshot().theme`. **App preload (`packages/shell/src/preload/app-preload.ts`)**: imports `{ DEFAULT_THEME, flattenTokens, isThemeName, themes }` from `@brainstorm/tokens`, calls a new `applyThemeByName(name)` that resolves through `themes[name]` (falling back to `DEFAULT_THEME` on unknown / missing), then writes the flattened variables to `:root`. Both the initial launch path and the live broadcast path go through the same function — one branch, no encode/decode asymmetry. **What this fixes:** kills the entire bug class that 9.8.2.7 patched. No more `Buffer` / `atob` foot-gun in sandboxed preload (which silently dropped initial tokens, dropping every freshly-launched app onto its CSS light fallback); IPC payloads shrink from ~200-entry JSON to a 12-character string; the failure mode if the registry ever drops a theme name is now a loud "unknown theme name" + `DEFAULT_THEME` paint instead of a silent black screen. **Tests:** existing `launcher.test.ts` "tokens encode/decode" block deleted (the contract no longer exists); `launch-orchestrator.test.ts` switched to assert `launches[i]?.theme` against `ThemeName.Midnight` / `.DefaultDark` instead of comparing full flattened maps; `dashboard-handlers.test.ts` (8 tests in the broadcast block) updated to use the new `broadcastThemeToWindows` + `APP_THEME_CHANGED_CHANNEL` symbols and assert payload is a plain string (`"default-dark"`) — keeps every prior behavioural assertion (destroyed-window skip, broken-renderer survival, dashboard background paint, dashboard-null no-op). 1281 tests green; typecheck clean; biome clean; full `bun run build` clean. **Future:** Stage 9.9 (custom Theme entities) will extend the preload's `applyThemeByName` with a `themes.has(name) ? built-in : fetch-from-entities` branch — the IPC contract (just a name) survives unchanged.

#### 9.8.2.9 — Files-app UX bugfix pass

✅. **Files-app UX bugfix pass.** Hands-on review of the preview drop surfaced three real bugs the user would hit on the first session. (a) **Sidebar section first-click was a no-op.** `index.html` ships Smart-folders / Tags with `data-collapsed="true"` but `state.collapsedSections` initialised to an empty `Set`; first click toggled the state into "collapsed" while leaving the dataset attribute unchanged, so a user trying to expand those sections needed two clicks. State initialiser now seeds `new Set(["smartFolders", "tags"])` so DOM ↔ state agree from paint zero. (b) **Bare-key shortcuts hijacked the search input.** `Space` / `Enter` / `Backspace` / `Delete` were bound at `window` and called `preventDefault()` before the matching keystroke could reach the focused `<input>`; typing a space in the search box silently fired `quick-look` instead of inserting a space, Backspace tried to soft-delete files from the search field, Enter started a rename, etc. `bindShortcut(...)` now skips when the event target is a text-input-ish element (new `isTypingTarget(target)` duck-types `tagName` / `isContentEditable` / `type` so the helper works under the `node` vitest environment without jsdom). A new `allowInTyping` option restores the rare-but-needed exception: `PopoverClose` (`Escape`) is bound with `allowInTyping: true` and the handler only consumes the key when a modal or the New popover is actually open — when nothing's open, Escape falls through to the native input behaviour. (c) **`RenameAlt` (F2) was missing the active-rename guard.** `Rename` (`Enter`) checked `state.rename.status !== Idle` but `RenameAlt` didn't, so pressing F2 while already renaming re-started rename on the anchor; both bindings now share a single `startRenameIfIdle()` closure. **Polish:** the rename `<input>` now carries an `aria-label` of `"Renaming {name} — type a new name, press Enter to commit"` per the UX spec's a11y section (new i18n key `brainstorm.files.rename.inputLabel`). **Tests:** +9 in `apps/files/tests/shortcuts.test.ts` covering the typing-target skip (bare-key in `<input type=search>`, in `<textarea>`, in `contenteditable`), the still-fires-elsewhere case (`<button>` target), the `allowInTyping` allowlist, the don't-consume-when-passing-through path, the consume-by-default path, plus a dedicated `isTypingTarget` suite over every input type the duck-type accepts/rejects. 1344 workspace tests green (was 1335 pre-change); 107/107 files tests green; typecheck clean; biome clean; `apps/files` build clean at 41.67 KB JS (gz 12.27) / 14.13 KB CSS (gz 3.05). **What this doesn't touch:** the deferred items in 9.8.3 – 9.8.10 (React rewrite, virtualization, `files.requestOpen`, Recently Deleted panel, `@react-fancy-menus/core` New menu) all stay deferred — this iteration only fixes bugs in the throwaway preview renderer; the `logic/*` keystones were not touched.

#### 9.13.1.6 — Force/layout polish pass

✅. **Force/layout polish pass** after user-test feedback ("nodes very big, can't drag, jiggling on open"): (a) the pre-existing repulsion math had its sign flipped — `applyRepulsion` was attracting rather than repelling, producing a collapsed cluster that the eye read as "big" nodes; (b) `velocityDecay` raised 0.18 → 0.4 to match d3-force defaults so the simulation actually comes to rest within `preConverge`'s budget; (c) `chargeDistanceMax` added (1000) so far pairs don't keep the sim warm; (d) per-edge spring strength replaces the flat `linkStrength` constant — d3's `1/min(deg(src), deg(tgt))` default; (e) `coolDown` helper zeros velocities after `preConverge` so any later reheat starts from rest; (f) node radius drops from fixed 9/5 to degree-scaled `base * (1 + log(deg+1)/log(maxDeg+1) * 0.9)` with `base = 4` matched, `2.5` unmatched; (g) new `hitsLayer` of transparent r≥12 overlay circles fixes drag — the visible circles can shrink without losing a generous click target (`pointer-events="none"` on visible, `"all"` on overlay); (h) `preserveAspectRatio="none"` + a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas wrap keep the SVG viewBox locked 1:1 to the container, eliminating both letterbox-induced "big" appearance and the `clientX → viewBox` drift that broke drag at non-default window sizes. **Tests:** +3 (coolDown 1, preConverge-at-rest 1, charge-distance-max 1); 783 tests total, all green. `tsc --noEmit` clean; `biome check .` clean. Build size unchanged (JS 27.56 kB / gz 8.34).

#### 9.13.1.7 — Timeline polish pass

✅. **Timeline polish pass** after user-test feedback ("timeline animation is super slow, it starts not when the first node is"): (a) demo dataset compressed from ~290 days (Jan 4 – Oct 19 2025) to a 14-day span (Jan 1 – Jan 14 2025) so full playback at the spec's 1 day/sec rate now takes ~14s at 1× and <1s at 16× — relative event ordering and the storyline (Schools → Cities → Person cohorts → Notes) preserved; (b) `easeWindowMs` corrected from a stray 7-day value (`app.ts`'s `sceneOptionsFrom`) and 14-day default (`scene.ts::DEFAULT_SCENE_OPTIONS`) to the spec's 24h total / 12h half-width (`EASE_WINDOW_MS` constant exported from `scene.ts`) — so the first event now fades from alpha=0.5 to 1.0 in ~0.5s of playback at 1× instead of the previous ~3.5s; (c) play-click handler snaps `cutoffAt = bounds.min` *and* reconciles + repositions the scrubber synchronously, so frame 1 already shows the playhead at the first event instead of carrying over the "everything visible at cutoff=null" snapshot for a tick. **Tests:** scene.test updated to use the new timestamps (alpha bounds unchanged); 783 tests still green. `tsc --noEmit` clean; `biome check .` clean. Build size unchanged (JS 27.61 kB / gz 8.29).

#### 9.13.1.8 — Real-data + look polish pass

Five changes: (a) **Collision pass** — `resolveCollisions` runs after integration, hard-separating overlapping discs with the d3-`forceCollide` algorithm (radii + `collidePadding=6`, 2 iterations); the `LayoutNode` now carries a per-node `radius` so the scene's degree-aware sizing actually feeds collision, and `reconcileLayout` propagates the renderer's radius back to the layout map every frame. Charge tuned `-250 → -120` + `chargeDistanceMax` `1000 → 600` + `linkDistance` `100 → 70` + `centerStrength` `0.01 → 0.04` so the network reads as connected clusters rather than an exploded ring. (b) **Single-button timeline** — the always-visible scrubber strip is gone; a small lower-left history pill (clock + current cutoff date) toggles a popover that holds play / speed / scrubber. Pause-on-dismiss so a hidden popover can't silently rewind. The SDK runtime gets a matching `VaultEntitiesService` proxy + `VaultEntitiesSnapshot` type in `sdk-types/index.ts`. On failure it falls back to the demo. The Stage 9.3 entities service replaces only the registration; the proxy and the graph code stay. Drag tolerance: 3px movement reads as drag, not click. #### 9.13.1.9 — Timeline rescale + force-parity pass

✅ (2026-05-13). **Timeline rescale + force-parity pass** after user feedback ("plays very slow and does not play actually it shows just part of notes with zero opacity" / "check forces again, you did not add all forces"). (a) **Playback rate is now dataset-relative.** `advancePlayback` used to add `(dt/1000) * MS_PER_DAY * speed` per frame — fixed at 1 dataset-day per real-second, which meant a 90-day vault took 90s to sweep at 1×. New `PLAYBACK_FULL_RANGE_SECONDS_AT_1X = 10` constant + per-call `msPerSecond = span / 10 * speed` means 1× always covers the full range in ~10s regardless of dataset width; 2× / 4× / 8× / 16× scale proportionally. (b) **Auto-rewind starts before bounds.min.** Earlier the play handler set `cutoffAt = bounds.min`, which left the earliest entity at alpha 0.5 + everything else at alpha 0 — read by users as "the graph is broken". New `rewindForReplay()` helper kicks the cutoff to `bounds.min - EASE_WINDOW_MS` so the first entity fades in cleanly from 0; resumes from the current cutoff when paused mid-timeline instead of always rewinding. (c) **Force-parity pass.** Five forces in the standard d3-force shape — `link` / `charge` / `center` (centroid drift correction) / `forceX` (per-node x-spring, zero strength for orphans) / `forceY` (same on y). We had a single `applyCenter` mixing both per-node x/y and treating orphans the same as connected nodes. Now split: `applyCenterPerNode` (the forceX/Y equivalent, skips orphans + pinned), and `applyCentroidDrift` (the d3 `forceCenter` equivalent — runs after integration to shift every non-pinned node so the centroid lands at viewport centre, preventing slow drift off the edge). New `markOrphans(nodes, edges)` helper is called inside `primeLayout` + `reconcileLayout` whenever the topology changes; `LayoutNode.isOrphan` is optional (defaults to "not an orphan, pull applies") so existing inline-node test fixtures stay valid. Charge / distanceMax / linkDistance / centerStrength settled at (-250 / 1000 / 100 / 0.01). (d) **Tests:** +3 in `force-layout.test.ts` (`markOrphans` describe block — orphan detection, edge add/remove, centre-pull behaviour). 1507 tests green; lint + typecheck clean; graph bundle still 44 kB JS / 13 kB gz.

#### 9.13.1.10 — Zoom + LOD + local view + PixiJS renderer

✅ (2026-05-14). **Zoom + LOD + local view + PixiJS renderer.** Resolves user feedback ("no zoom, if icons are visible circles should not be visible and vice versa, check zoom-level threshold; add local graph; optimise performance and introduce pixi js, we need to work with thousands of nodes"). What landed: (a) **Camera (zoom + pan)** — `CameraTransform = {k, tx, ty}` on the renderer's single viewport `<g>` / Pixi `worldContainer`; mouse-wheel zooms anchored on the pointer (`zoomAround` keeps the world-point under the cursor fixed), drag on empty canvas pans (`bindCanvasZoomAndPan`), lower-right `+ / − / ⌂` controls (`zoom-controls`), `scaleExtent [0.05, 10]`, transform persisted in v3 of the `graph:state` storage payload. (b) **LOD thresholds** in `svg-renderer.ts` + `pixi-renderer.ts`: `ARROW_HIDE_BELOW_K = 0.5`, `DETAIL_THRESHOLD_K = 1`, `MAX_LABELED_NODES = 150`. Below `k=0.5` arrowheads disappear; below `k=1` labels hide and icon glyphs swap for plain discs (icons + circles are now strictly mutually exclusive — high zoom = glyph alone, low zoom = disc alone, per user spec); when more than 150 visible nodes are on screen labels hide even at full zoom (the `MAX_LABELED_NODES` density cap); hovered node keeps its label (the `forceLabel` exception). Strokes scale `1/k` to stay screen-space constant. (c) **Local view (1-hop)** — new `apps/graph/src/logic/local-scope.ts` returns root + 1-hop neighbours + connecting non-deleted links; right-click a node toggles it as the local root, right-click empty canvas exits, glass-pill `local-badge` shows the active root with a × close affordance; `localRootId` persists; depth fixed at 1 — depth slider deferred to 9.13.7. (d) **PixiJS renderer swap** (production path; **OQ-GR-4 resolved tentative-(a)**: main-thread Pixi as the first cut, worker swap deferred to follow-up once 60fps-at-5k bench shows a latency budget breach). `apps/graph/src/render/pixi-renderer.ts` mounts a Pixi 8 `Application`, generates one white circle texture, builds every node as a `Sprite(circleTexture)` with per-instance `tint` (one batched GL draw call per N sprites instead of N DOM updates); edges + arrowheads draw into a single `Graphics`; labels overlay as plain DOM `<div>`s so the shell theme tokens apply for free. `worldContainer.scale/position` IS the camera transform — per-sprite positions stay in world coords. SVG path stays accessible behind `?renderer=svg` for fallback/debug. (e) **Renderer abstraction** — new `apps/graph/src/render/renderer.ts` exposes a uniform `Renderer` interface (`paint` / `resize` / `pickNode` / `nodeToClient` / `clientToWorldPoint`); `app.ts` is renderer-agnostic; hit-testing routes through `renderer.pickNode(snapshot, clientX, clientY)` rather than `event.target.closest("circle[data-key]")`, so the SVG path keeps its DOM shortcut while Pixi does a position scan. (f) **Snapshot extension** — `Snapshot.showLabels` / `Snapshot.showArrows` so Pixi reads the user toggles directly. **Tests:** +5 in `apps/graph/src/logic/local-scope.test.ts` (1-hop expansion, inbound-edge walk, orphan handling, deleted-edge filter, missing-root null return). **74 graph tests pass; full vitest suite stable.** `tsc --noEmit` clean on the graph workspace; biome clean. Build now produces `index-*.js` 285 kB / 88 kB gz + lazy-loaded Pixi WebGL / WebGPU / CanvasRenderer chunks (combined gz ~ 130 kB) — no app-level size budget per `.size-limit.json`. **Long-term keystones:** `local-scope.ts`, the `Renderer` interface, the LOD constants, the camera persistence shape, the snapshot fields — survive any future worker swap or 9.13.7 depth-slider iteration. **Deferred (still in 9.13.5 umbrella):** move force-sim + paint into a Worker (OQ-GR-4 option (b)) once latency demands it; spatial-hash grid for hit-testing (currently linear scan, fine ~3k nodes); 60fps@5k perf-bench harness; multi-hop local-view depth slider (9.13.7).

#### 9.13.1.11 — Pattern-editor preview drop + sizing/force fixes

✅ (2026-05-16). **Pattern-editor preview drop + sizing/force fixes** after user feedback ("node radius should be log of links"; "purple/grey is confusing and purple is bigger than linked grey"; "forces are bad, nodes jiggle"; "the preset buttons are irrelevant — we either have real filters or none"). What landed: (a) **Degree-driven node radius** — `scene.ts` now sizes every node by `min(4 + ln(deg+1)·2.4, 22)` *absolutely* (the old formula keyed radius off match/icon status and normalised the degree term by `log(maxDeg+1)`, so one mega-hub flattened all other nodes to one size and unlinked matched nodes rendered larger than linked ones). Match/unmatched is now carried by colour alone; the glyph is gated on `radius ≥ 7` (a visibility gate, not a size floor — size stays strictly monotonic in link count). (b) **Force jiggle fix** — `force-layout.ts` gained a per-tick speed clamp (`maxSpeed = 40` in `LayoutParams`): the spring impulse `delta·strength·alpha` was unbounded, so a node far from rest length got a single-tick impulse of hundreds of px, overshot, and oscillated; clamping post-decay speed kills the explosion without shifting the equilibrium. (c) **Real pattern editor** replaces the two hardcoded `VAULT_PRESETS` buttons (removed) — `AppState.pattern` is now a single editable `GraphPattern`; new pure immutable helpers in `apps/graph/src/logic/pattern-edit.ts` (`addSubject/removeSubject/updateSubject/addEdge/removeEdge/updateEdge`, cap-enforced; `availableEntityTypes/availableLinkTypes` enumerate the live vault snapshot; `isUsablePattern` gates persisted patterns, tolerating the advisory empty-type issues). The Filters sidebar now edits subjects (name, type multi-select from real vault types via a native `<details>` checkbox picker — no fancy-menus dep) and connections (from/dir/link-types/to/match selects), live-reconciling on every change; persistence bumped to v4 (`pattern` replaces `presetId`; v2/v3 payloads load tolerantly). Launch-context preset branch dropped (an `open` id is always a node now). **Deferred (still 9.13.9/9.13.11):** per-subject `where` predicate builder (Database-app reuse, dep-gated), the static SVG pattern-shape preview, save-as-template (9.13.14), and the fancy-menus connection popover (Stage 8). **Tests:** +11 in `pattern-edit.test.ts` (immutability, caps, edge cleanup, vault enumeration) + 1 force-clamp regression in `force-layout.test.ts`; scene/force suites updated. Full suite **2698 tests green**; `tsc --noEmit` + graph `biome` clean. Build: graph `index.js` 364.7 kB / gz 110.6 kB (no app-level size budget). **Long-term keystones:** `pattern-edit.ts` (the editor's mutation contract survives the Stage 9.3 entities-service swap unchanged — only the data source behind `availableEntityTypes`/`reconcileScene` changes); the absolute-log sizing + speed-clamp are permanent.

#### 9.13.1.12 — Real per-object icon textures (Pixi) + render-gate perf fix

✅ (2026-05-16). Two user reports against the Pixi graph: "graph does not show icons again" and "graph performance dropped greatly". **(a) Icons.** The Pixi path only ever rasterised an emoji *text* glyph: `scene.ts:glyphFor` read `IconKind.Emoji` only, so Pack (the common case) and Image icons fell back to a hardcoded per-type emoji shown only at `k ≥ 1` + `radius ≥ 7`; the demo dataset carried no icons at all. New **`apps/graph/src/render/icon-source.ts`** is the icon→image-source layer (a clean-room analogue of the host→renderer bitmap hand-off other engines use — stable `src` key + decoded image, decoupled from the draw loop; no third-party code): Emoji → the shell's bundled `brainstorm://emoji/<cp>.webp` (new tiny `emoji-url.ts`, the established per-app mirror — no `unicode-emoji-json` metadata pulled in), Image → the stored URL, Pack → the Phosphor `regular` SVG recoloured to the node colour and wrapped as a data URL. Phosphor assets load lazily via `import.meta.glob` over the new `@phosphor-icons/core` graph dep (matched SVGs become on-demand chunks, entry bundle unaffected, no React dependency in this non-React app). `scene.ts` now resolves the full universal `Icon` (all three kinds) for matched nodes with **no radius gate** (a crisp bitmap reads where rasterised emoji-text wouldn't) and emits `icon` + a stable `iconSrc` (`iconKey`); `glyph` stays as the legacy-SVG-renderer / texture-loading fallback (type glyph fallback-only — never substitutes the object's own icon, per [[per-object-icons-everywhere]]). `pixi-renderer.ts` swaps the node's front sprite to the icon texture at `k ≥ ICON_THRESHOLD_K = 0.5` (icons reveal a zoom-step *earlier* than the `DETAIL_THRESHOLD_K = 1` emoji-text glyph), white-tinted + aspect-preserved like the disc it replaces; textures cache `O(distinct icons)` keyed `iconSrc` (Emoji/Image) or `iconSrc|colour` (Pack — recolour baked in), with a deduped async load and an `onInvalidate` nudge so a late texture still appears under the new render gate. Demo dataset seeded with real Pack/Emoji/Image icons so the pipeline is exercised before the Stage 9.3 entities service lands. **(b) Perf.** `startAnimationLoop` called `renderer.paint()` every `requestAnimationFrame` *unconditionally* — and `paintPixi` rebuilds the entire edge `Graphics` geometry per call — so a settled, idle graph paid a full 60 fps GPU+CPU scene rebuild forever (felt worse after 9.13.1.11's larger hubs kept the sim warm longer). The loop now repaints only on actual change: sim warm, drag, pan, zoom, hover-fade in flight, playback, or a scene/theme/settings mutation (`forceRepaint` one-shot + `lastPaint` camera/hover diff); `advanceFocusAlpha` snaps to target within a 0.002 epsilon and reports `focusAnimating` so the hover fade actually settles instead of lerping asymptotically forever. Idle cost → ~0; every interaction still paints (when in doubt, paint). **Long-term keystones:** `icon-source.ts` (the kind→source contract survives the entities-service swap unchanged — only what fills `entity.properties.icon` changes) and the change-gated render loop are both permanent; the demo seed is preview-only. **Tests:** new `emoji-url.test.ts` (codepoint/ZWJ filename math), `icon-source.test.ts` (`iconKey` per kind), +6 `scene.test.ts` icon-resolution cases (pack+colour, emoji doubles as glyph fallback, unmatched drops icon, `showIcons:false`, type-glyph fallback for non-emoji). Graph suite **101 green**; `tsc --noEmit` workspace-clean; graph `biome` clean (3 pre-existing unrelated lint errors in `apps/database` / `apps/tasks` left untouched — out of scope). Build: graph `index.js` 607.5 kB / gz 137.9 kB (Pixi dominates; per-icon SVG chunks are lazy, gz <1 kB each; no app-level size budget).

Apps still go through the broker (`services.search.query`, capability `search.read`); the dashboard is shell-trusted so it talks to the indexer directly. `validateQuery` pure helper enforces `{ text:string, types?:string[], limit?:number }` at the boundary; malformed input degrades to no-hits (privileged caller — no need to surface a structured `Invalid`). (b) `packages/shell/src/main/ipc/intent-handlers.ts` — `intent:dispatch` privileged channel routes shell-originated `intent.open` through the existing `IntentsBus.dispatch(..., { app: "shell" })`. `SHELL_INTENT_SOURCE = "shell"` skips the same-app preference in `pickHandler` because no app manifest installs that id. `validateIntentEnvelope` accepts missing / null payload as `{}` so the launcher can shorthand `{ verb:"open", payload:{entityId} }`. (c) `packages/shell/src/preload/index.ts` — new `search` + `intents` namespaces on `window.brainstorm` carrying `query()` + `dispatch()`; `SearchHit` + `SearchQuery` + `IntentEnvelope` + `IntentDispatchResult` types exported alongside the existing surfaces. (d) `packages/shell/src/main/index.ts` — `registerSearchHandlers(() => searchIndexer)` + `registerIntentHandlers(() => launchSetup.getIntentsSync())` registered next to the existing dashboard + properties handlers. (e) `packages/shell/src/renderer/launcher/grouped-results.ts` — **pure logic**. `LauncherRow` discriminated union (`SectionHeader / App / Entity`) via `LauncherRowKind` enum (no string-literal discriminators per [[enums-not-string-constants]]); `buildRows({ query, apps, entities, labels })` assembles the flat row list with an Apps section (filtered + alphabetically tie-broken via `filterApps` — prefix > name-substring > description-substring) and an Entities section (only when query has non-whitespace + entities exist; `ownerAppName` resolves via the installed-app catalog with a raw-appId fallback for orphan rows). `moveSelectionGrouped("down"/"up", current, rows)` + `firstSelectableIndex` + `clampSelectionGrouped` form a section-header-skipping cursor model that never lands on a heading. (f) `packages/shell/src/renderer/launcher/launcher.tsx` — React glue rewritten around the new model. Debounced search (120 ms, hard limit 20 hits) coalesces typing bursts via a `tokenRef` so stale FTS5 responses can't overwrite fresher ones. Keyboard chord routing through the existing shortcut registry (`shell/list.next` / `.previous` / `shell/popover.close` / `.confirm` — no raw `e.key` per [[keyboard-and-i18n]]). Entity activation tries `intent.open` first, falls back to `apps.launch(ownerAppId)` when no handler is registered. `sanitizeSnippet` + `prettyEntityType` pure helpers exported alongside the component — sanitiser preserves only literal `<mark>` markers (the indexer's snippet wrapper) and HTML-escapes everything else, so a note containing literal `<script>` can't break out of the highlight rail. App icons render via the existing `brainstorm://app-icon/<id>` protocol when `hasIcon` is true. (g) `packages/shell/src/renderer/launcher/launcher.css` — search-icon + input + pending-indicator on one baseline; section headers low-contrast + non-focusable; result rows two-line (label + snippet/subtitle) with `-webkit-line-clamp:2` snippet clamp; `mark` rule styles FTS5 highlight markers. (h) `packages/shell/src/renderer/i18n/t.ts` — 9 new `shell.launcher.*` ids (placeholder / empty / sections / subtitles / close). (i) `apps/notes/manifest.json` already registers `verb:"open"` for `io.brainstorm.notes/Note/v1` — launcher's Notes hits route there end-to-end without any Notes-side change. (j) **Deleted** `packages/shell/src/renderer/launcher/filter.ts` + its test (interim 7.4 substring-filter, fully superseded by `grouped-results.ts`). **Tests:** +56 across 4 new files (`grouped-results.test.ts` 26, `launcher.test.ts` 9 — sanitizer + prettyEntityType, `search-handlers.test.ts` 12, `intent-handlers.test.ts` 9); −11 from removing `filter.test.ts`. Net +45. **2363 tests pass across 204 files.** `tsc --noEmit` clean; `bunx biome check` clean across all touched files; shell main + preload + renderer builds green (preload 10.35 kB, renderer 1599.93 kB — pre-existing growth, unchanged by this iteration). **OQ-SR-1 unchanged** — launcher inherits the indexer's empty-result-on-failure behaviour; degrade-to-LIKE-scan stays a tracked alternative. **Dep gating:** Tasks / Database / Whiteboard / Bookmarks `verb:"open"` intent handlers will surface as their app ladders catch up; until then those entity hits round-trip to `apps.launch(ownerAppId)` via the fallback path. **Why this matters:** the global ⌘-Space palette is the user's daily on-ramp into the vault; surfacing Notes content (and soon Tasks, Bookmarks, events…) next to apps collapses two trips ("open Notes → search for X") into one. The shell-only IPC path keeps the dashboard outside the broker's app-identity ceremony while still funnelling intent.open through the same bus apps use, so handler resolution + future Stage 8 default-handler UX apply uniformly.

## B5.6b — Properties surfaced in Notes (consistent panels + redesigned picker + empty-list fix)

✅ DONE (2026-05-16). **User goal:** "wire properties to notes app… toggleable sidebar panel… move navigation to the left… properties panel work the same way as in Database… left panel no glass / navigation / toggleable, right panel with properties + glass / toggleable… properties in space settings but the add-property-block list is empty… property editor inside notes is ugly, use a popover and make it beautiful."

**What landed:**

1. **Layout — two consistent boundary panels** (`apps/notes/src/app.tsx` + `styles.css`). `.notes` is now a two-column CSS grid (`var(--notes-nav-width,260px) minmax(0,1fr)`; `[data-nav-open=false]` collapses the first track to `0`). LEFT `.notes__nav` = the recent-notes list, **opaque (no glass)**, lives in the grid track so opening it reflows the centred editor (Database `app-panel-sides` convention). RIGHT `.notes__props` = `glass--strong` absolute overlay anchored right, `box-shadow`, floats over the stage (no reflow), `translateX(100%)` on close. Both slide on GPU `transform` per `animate-transform-not-width`; both independently toggleable + resizable (`attachResizable` `side:"left"` / `"right"`, `--notes-nav-width` / `--notes-props-width`, `localStorage` prefs `notes.navOpen` (default on) / `notes.propsOpen` (default off)). Two mirror-image header toggle buttons (`PanelToggleIcon side="left"|"right"`); the props toggle is `disabled` with no note. Shortcuts: existing `ToggleSidebar` (Mod+\\) → nav; new `ToggleProperties` (Mod+Shift+\\) → props. Old `.notes__sidebar` / `.notes__resize` / `.notes--sidebar-open` + the editor-recentre transform deleted.

2. **`PropertiesPanel`** (`apps/notes/src/properties/properties-panel.tsx`, new). Lists the open note's bound properties (keys present in `note.values` that resolve to a `PropertyDef`, alphabetised) as label + cell rows through the existing cell registry (`getCell(def.valueType, defaultViewFor(def))`), editable via `useNotes.setValue`; per-row remove clears the key (`clearValue` + `update`); unresolved-cell rows fall back to `PropertyBlockUnavailableView`. An "Add property" button + a created/updated metadata block (mirrors the Database inspector chrome: 44px header on the shared baseline, scrolling body). New `AddPropertyTargetKind.BindToNote` carries an `onPick(propertyKey)` callback so the **shared** picker can bind a key (seeded with `emptyValueFor(def)`) onto `note.values` with **no editor mutation** — the in-flow `PropertyBlockNode` and the panel are now parallel surfaces over the same value bag. Panel renders inside the existing `<PropertiesProvider>` and is driven by props from `app.tsx` (single `useNotes` instance).

3. **Picker redesign** (`apps/notes/src/editor/add-property-menu-plugin.tsx` + `add-property-ops.ts` + `icons.tsx`). `.notes__add-property-menu` → `.notes__picker`: glassy surface (`color-glass-background` + `backdrop-filter`), a sectioned 38px header (uppercase title + close `✕`; back-chevron in create mode), a search field with a leading magnifier glyph, per-row **value-type glyph chip** + humanized type caption. New pure helpers `categorizeProperty(def) → PropertyTypeCategory` (11-category display classification distinct from `ValueType`: `vocabulary`→Select beats format, `text+format`→Url/Email/Phone, `entityRef`→File-vs-Reference on `allowedTypes`, else the plain value type) and `isMultiProperty(def)` (→ "{type} · Multiple"). New element-scoped `PickerHighlightPrev`/`PickerHighlightNext` chords (ArrowUp/Down) drive in-list keyboard nav; the create-action is a pinned footer row. New icons: `SearchIcon`, `CloseXIcon`, and six value-type glyphs in the existing 16px stroke family (no emoji).

4. **Empty-list root cause + hardening** (`apps/notes/src/properties/use-properties.tsx`). The catalog path (Notes manifest declares + default-grants `properties.read`; broker `properties` service reads the same vault `PropertiesStore` Settings → Data writes) was correct — the running shell was serving a **pre-VP-5 Notes bundle** (apps build separately from the shell) that still read the dead per-app `storage.kv` silo while Settings → Data showed the vault catalog. Fixed by rebuilding the app **and** making the provider apply even an empty snapshot (so `loaded` flips) while leaving the stores un-loaded only on a thrown `list()` — the picker + panel now show a real **"Loading…"** state vs **"No properties in this vault yet."** instead of both reading as a blank list; the verbose `console.info`/`console.error` debug pair collapses to one `console.warn` on genuine unavailability. Latent `app.tsx` `editorNoteContext` type debt fixed (`PropertyDef["kind"]` / `PropertyValueByKind` → `valueType` / `PropertyValueByValueType`, residue of the B5.5 sdk-types redesign; app-level `tsc` is not in the workspace `typecheck` project so it had been invisible).

**Tests:** +9 in `add-property-ops.test.ts` (`categorizeProperty`: value-type map, vocabulary→Select precedence, text-format Url/Email/Phone split, entityRef File-vs-Reference; `isMultiProperty`: scalar default vs `count.max>1`). **336 notes tests green** (34 files). App-level `tsc -p apps/notes/tsconfig.json` clean for every touched non-test file (pre-existing unrelated debt in other notes files left as-is); `bunx biome check` clean across all 12 touched files; Notes bundle builds (`index-*.js` ≈ 259 KB-gz).

**Process note:** the working tree was `git reset` + snapshot-committed ("updates", `9feb9c9`) by an out-of-band local command mid-iteration, which discarded the session-start pre-existing cross-app modifications and several in-flight edits; the lost Notes edits were re-applied and verified against `git status` + a green build before wrap-up.

**Why it matters:** properties are now genuinely usable in Notes from a panel that visually and behaviourally matches Database, the left-nav/right-props split makes the whole product read consistently, the picker is a polished glass popover, and "the catalog looks empty" is now structurally distinguishable from a real empty vault.

## B5.7 / B5.8 / B5.9 — Notes property-cell arc (Tag/TagList · DictionaryEditor · remaining cells)

**B5.7 — Tag / TagList cells + inline dictionary picker.** One runtime-shape-selecting `TagCell` registered for `(Text, Tag)` and `(Text, TagList)` (scalar vs multi chosen via `isMultiValued(def.count)`). Link cells (`LinkInline`/`LinkCard`) ship a stubbed picker over the existing `vaultEntities.list` preview scoped to `note:*` ids ([[preview-drop-pattern]] — folds into the entities service at Stage 9.3). Registry now 17 `(ValueType, PropertyView)` entries.

## VP-7 — Property render/edit layer hoisted to `@brainstorm/sdk/property-ui` (Notes + Database consume it)

Closes the VP ladder's cross-app exit criterion: the property cells, registry, `DictionaryEditor`, dictionary-* algebra, `value-store`, the vault-scoped stores + provider/hooks, and `use-anchored-panel` are no longer Notes-private — they live in `packages/sdk/src/property-ui/` and are consumed by every app. Built by a worktree builder + a resume builder (the first agent stalled mid-7c; recovered by verifying the on-disk state and finishing the gate/commit), then a 2-pass parallel review (code/design/DRY + perf/leak; security/pentest deliberately skipped — internal package refactor, zero new IPC/capability/dependency/crypto surface).

**One shared core, two faces.** The Database app is vanilla DOM (no React, `tsconfig` `"types": []`); forcing React cells into it would contradict the established imperative-twin convention ([[entity-icon-dom-helper]]). So the subpath ships: a **React barrel** `@brainstorm/sdk/property-ui` (cells, `getCell`/`hasCell` registry, `CellPopover`, `use-anchored-panel`, `PropertyStore`/`DictionaryStore`, `use-properties` provider+hooks, `DictionaryEditor`+store) consumed by Notes; and a **pure barrel** `@brainstorm/sdk/property-ui/pure` (`format` + `dictionary-helpers`/`dictionary-import`/`dictionary-ops` + `value-store`, DOM/React-free) consumed by Database. The pure barrel never statically reaches `cells/index.ts` (whose `register()` is a load-time side-effect) — verified by a **React-free hard gate** scanning the built Database bundle for `react/jsx-runtime`/`react-dom`/`REACT_ELEMENT_TYPE`/`useSyncExternalStore`/`PropertiesProvider`/`PillCell`/`TagCell`/`DictionaryEditor` (zero matches).

**Four host-injected seams** keep `@brainstorm/sdk` free of any `apps/notes` import (a sdk→app import would be a build-failing cycle), each with a self-sufficient default so the subpath + its tests + non-Notes consumers need zero Notes deps: i18n `PropertyUiLabels` (Notes wires every label to an existing `notes.*` `t()` key — zero string/manifest change), `EscapeMatcher`/`CommitMatcher` (defaults bare Escape/Enter; Notes injects `matchesActionChord`), `EntityTitleSource` (default empty; Notes wires its `store/entity-title-index` singleton), and a structural `PropertiesRuntime` replacing the `NotesBrainstorm` type import. Notes husk reduced to orchestration only: `{dictionary-editor-host, properties-panel, seam-bindings}`.

**Database 7c.** `render/cells.ts` routes scalar formatting through the shared `formatScalar` once a real `PropertyDef` resolves (the old heuristic kept verbatim **only** as the no-schema standalone-dev fallback, gated `if (def) …`); `logic/property-resolver.ts`'s bespoke `VocabSnapshot` walk replaced with the shared dictionary algebra over the real `PropertiesSnapshot`/`Dictionary`; `createElement` painters untouched (no React introduced). The review-pass fix made the vocabulary-colour resolver build a `label→colour` index **once per dictionary per snapshot** (O(1) per cell paint, zero-alloc) instead of `activeItems(dict).find()` per paint — DRY preserved (the shared active-item algebra still runs, once not per paint).

**Commits (4, ff-merged linearly onto `f4fa26f`):** `4c82cbb` 7a (hoist + Notes re-consume, atomic — the registry/provider/store/Lexical-node web can't be half-moved) · `8813315` 7b (seam wiring + husk retire) · `06c3e39` 7c (Database onto the pure core) · `79526aa` review-pass fix.

**Gates (all independently re-verified post-rebase onto the parallel `b8daaad`/`f4fa26f` work):** packages `tsc` clean; `apps/notes` tsc = exact pre-existing baseline (the `property-block-node` `override`/`never` Lexical debt is pre-existing, proven byte-identical at base — VP-7's edits there are import rewires only, zero new errors); `apps/database` tsc clean on 7c files; full suite green bar the lone pre-existing `apps/files/i18n`; biome at the pre-existing 4-error baseline (none VP-7); Database React-free hard gate **passed**.

**Bundles.** `DictionaryEditor` stays a lazily-imported separate **3.38 KB-gz** chunk (via the dedicated `@brainstorm/sdk/property-ui/dictionary-editor` subpath export — opened only on "Manage values", not in the eager path). Notes index ≈360 KB gz (+~3 over the pre-VP-7 ≈357 — the two ~70-entry seam-label tables + provider/seam indirection; the architectural cost of the seam mechanism, not duplication; the Lexical `index.es` chunk unchanged). Database index ≈43 KB gz (+1.3 — the pulled-in shared pure core replacing its bespoke heuristic; net shared code, the DRY win).

**Process note.** Two long-running builder agents stalled mid-task this arc; a baseline-diff `git checkout` I ran resurrected stale pre-move files into the worktree, and a resume agent committed concurrently — the collision was in disjoint paths (`apps/notes`/`packages` vs the agent's `apps/database`-scoped 7c) and the committed tree was explicitly verified clean (0 resurrected dupes in HEAD, husk = 3 files). ## 6.7 — ShortcutBindings flat-file → entity migration

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). Stage 9's entities service has landed, unblocking 6.7. New `packages/shell/src/main/shortcuts/bindings-entity.ts` declares `brainstorm/ShortcutBindings/v1` (`SHORTCUT_BINDINGS_TYPE`, singleton id `brainstorm:shortcut-bindings`, owner `io.brainstorm.shell`, `ShortcutBindingsScopeKind` enum — no raw literals) whose `properties` carry the flat-file `{ version, overrides:[{id,chord}] }` **byte-for-byte** (no key rename; the doc's aspirational `id`→`target` rename is intentionally NOT done — the iteration mandates no shape change) plus the doc-specified personal-by-default `scope` envelope. One-shot migration runs in `loadShortcutBindings()` inside the boot-independent `onVaultOpened` hook (the same `onActiveVaultSessionChanged` mechanism 9.3.5.R's kv-backfill / the search-indexer swap use) plus an explicit call right after `createShortcutSetup` (the boot session opens before the registry exists): if the flat file exists and the entity doesn't, read-and-store into `entities.db` via `EntitiesRepository`. **Idempotent / no-clobber** (keyed on the fixed singleton id; `repo.get` short-circuits with `already-present` before any write — a registry-written newer row survives a re-run), **non-destructive** (the flat file is never written/deleted — byte-compared before/after in test), **fault-isolated** (every fs/repo error caught+logged, returns `{migrated:false}`, never throws into session-open), **lazy** (a zero-override file creates no row — matches docs/24 §Storage). `ShortcutRegistry.applyOverrides(readOverridesFromEntity(repo))` is the new live read path — note the pre-6.7 flat-file `readBindings`/`applyOverrides` were never wired into production, so 6.7 establishes the live (entity-backed) read path for the first time; `writeOverridesToEntity` is implemented+tested for the future rebind-settings UI (no production caller yet — bindings read-only at runtime, consistent with docs/24's lazy-creation note). Public registry API (`applyOverrides`/`resolve`/`listAll`), `shortcut-registry.ts`, `shortcut-setup.ts`, `default-chords.ts`, and all renderer/`useShortcut` code **unchanged**. **Security/capability posture unchanged**: store stays shell-side (main, via `getEntitiesRepoForActiveSession()`); no broker exposure, no new IPC, no new app capability, no new dependency. **Tests:** +9 `bindings-entity.test.ts` — scenario (a) flat-file vault migrated + registry reads back unchanged; (b) idempotent across two boots (no dup/clobber); (c) never clobbers a newer registry-written row; (d) flat file left intact; (e) fresh vault (no file/no entity) no-op→defaults; data-shape-unchanged deep-equal; lazy no-empty-row; write-path lazy-create-then-update-in-place; malformed-blob tolerance. Shortcuts suite **36/36** (3 files) green; `bun run typecheck` clean; biome clean on touched files; `bun run --filter @brainstorm/shell build` exit 0. (Report's "+13 / 178" suite-delta figures were imprecise — the new file has exactly 9 tests, independently verified; the shortcuts suite totals 36 and is fully green.) **OQ-5** already RESOLVED (Stage 6, window-chrome — unrelated; untouched). **Follow-ups:** Keyboard-Shortcuts settings rebind UI is a later iteration (then `writeOverridesToEntity` gets its production caller); shell-introduced built-in type is intentionally not in the app `entity_types` registry (app-introduced-types-only per OQ-3; `type` opaque per OQ-7) — consistent with the kv-backfill precedent, flagged for a future built-in-type-registration formalization.

## Stage 3b — at-rest SQLite encryption (HKDF per-DB key + PRAGMA key + plaintext→encrypted migration)

✅ DONE (2026-05-17, code-complete; live on-disk flip env-gated). All four domain DBs (`ledger`/`registry`/`entities`/`search`) get an at-rest key derived from the vault master key via `deriveAtRestKey` = HKDF-SHA256(master, salt=`brainstorm/at-rest/hkdf/v1`, info=`<db>.db at-rest v1`, 32) (`@noble/hashes/hkdf.js`, reuses the existing master-key→subkey pattern, `AtRestDb` enum — no bare literals). `VaultSession` passes its 32-byte master key into `new DataStores(..., { masterKey })`, which keeps a **defensive copy** (the session zeroes its own buffer on dispose), derives the per-DB key per `open()`, hex-encodes it into `PRAGMA key = "x'<hex>'"`, and zeroes the derived buffer in a `finally`; the defensive master copy is zeroed in `DataStores.close()`. Key material stays in main-process buffers — never serialized to an IPC envelope, never `console.*`; the fail-closed error uses only the file basename. **Migration** `migratePlaintextToEncrypted`: `classifyAtRest` opens with no key and probes `sqlite_master` (readable⇒Plaintext, throws⇒Encrypted, missing⇒Absent — non-mutating, so encrypted/absent are no-ops ⇒ idempotent); Plaintext ⇒ delete any `<path>.encrypting` crash debris, `ATTACH '<tmp>' KEY` → `SELECT sqlcipher_export('encrypted')` → `DETACH` → close → POSIX atomic same-dir `rename(tmp,path)`. Proven by automated tests: every original row preserved + correct key; second call byte-identical (idempotent); injected `sqlcipher_export` failure leaves the plaintext original intact with no temp debris (atomic); stale-debris recovery; end-to-end transparent upgrade through `open()`. **Fail-closed:** wrong key ⇒ `assertReadable` probe throws ⇒ wrapped error, connection closed, no plaintext fallback; absent key on an encrypted file ⇒ `classifyAtRest` throws before open. **Driver decision:** both candidates really attempted in-env — `@libsql/client@0.17.3` installs but exposes only an async `createClient` (no sync export; `@libsql/client/sync`→`ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`) ⇒ **rejected** (the entire synchronous storage stack + every repo would need an async rewrite, violating the one-file-swap contract); `better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers` (the design's intended sync drop-in) still **fails the documented system-level blocker** (Python 3.14 / libexpat `pyexpat` ABI: `Symbol not found: _XML_SetAllocTrackerActivationThreshold`, no Node-25-ABI prebuilt). Per CLAUDE.md "avoid blocking on deps" + the iteration's clause 5: the full real logic + 21 tests landed behind a single `isSqlcipherAvailable()` gate (driver dynamically imported once via `@vite-ignore`, opaque to TS like `bun:sqlite`); resolves ⇒ encrypted path on, else existing plaintext drivers (never a silent data drop). **Exact env fix that flips it live with zero code change:** build host Python whose `pyexpat` is ABI-consistent with the linked libexpat (e.g. `brew install python@3.12` + `npm config set python`), or a Node-25-ABI prebuilt of the driver. Logic fully proven via an injected synchronous SQLCipher-shaped fake (`at-rest-fake-driver.ts`, gate-independent test seam) that mirrors real SQLCipher's can't-decrypt-can't-write behaviour. **No new dependency** (package.json/bun.lock untouched). **Tests:** +21 (`at-rest-key.test.ts` 8 — HKDF determinism/domain-separation/zeroing; `at-rest-encryption.test.ts` 13 — classify, migration no-data-loss/idempotence/atomicity/debris, through-`open()` upgrade + wrong/absent-key fail-closed) + a `data-stores` defensive-copy/zeroing test. typecheck clean; biome clean (9 touched files); 147/147 storage+vault+integration; 3165/3166 workspace (the 1 failure is a pre-existing unrelated `apps/files` i18n test in another team's untouched app). **Follow-ups:** add one real-driver integration test once the Python/libexpat env is fixed before declaring OQ-34 fully closed; Yjs `.ydoc` snapshot+tail files stay plaintext — wrapping them under the entity DEK is deliberately deferred to its Stage-10 interaction (the `deriveAtRestKey`/`AtRestDb` helper is the natural extension point); OQ-34's proposed `vault.json` encrypted-bit is redundant under this design (`classifyAtRest` detects on-disk state at open) — flagged. No OQ newly resolved here (OQ-34 stays PARTIALLY RESOLVED with a 3b note — design + logic resolved, live on-disk flip env-blocked).

## Graph 9.13.3 — GraphPattern compiler wired into the live entities service

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). Stage 9.3 has landed (entities service real; 9.3.5.R retired the kv aggregator), unblocking 9.13.3. **OQ-GR-1 resolved** (option a — structural Y.Doc pattern storage): the persisted shape is the landed `GraphPattern` projected onto the `Graph/v1` entity's own Y.Doc (`subjects`→`Y.Map`, `edges`→`Y.Array<Y.Map>`, `primarySubject` scalar); `where` stays opaque JSON (a predicate is a small expression tree edited as a unit — structural CRDT merge of a half-edited predicate yields an invalid tree, and predicates aren't a concurrent-edit hotspot). No schema/BP/single-object-space impact (it's the entity's own doc; the Y.Doc↔`GraphPattern` codec is the 9.13.6 renderer concern, gated by OQ-GR-2). Marked `*[RESOLVED in implementation-plan 9.13.3]*` in `docs/reference/11-open-questions.md`. **Wiring:** new typed `EntitiesRepository.queryPattern(pattern, options)` (`storage/entities-repo/entities-repo.ts`) is the *only* place the compiled SQL is prepared/run (Stage-5 repo rule) — it executes the 9.13.1.5 `compilePattern` output as a single statement: Required→`JOIN`, Optional→`LEFT JOIN`, Forbidden→`NOT EXISTS`, In/Out/Both direction, distinctness via `A.id != B.id`. **Cost-cap guard** (`estimatePatternCost`): SQLite EQP exposes no numeric row estimates, so the estimate is structural — product of each subject's live type-constrained `COUNT(*)` × an EQP-derived ×4 penalty per full `SCAN entities|links`; over `options.costCeiling`→`GRAPH_PATTERN_COST_CEIL` env→2,000,000 default ⇒ rejected **before execution** (`pattern-too-expensive`) so a pathological pattern can't pin the main process. Exposed via `vaultEntities.queryPattern` broker method + `vaultEntitiesProxy.queryPattern` SDK proxy + sdk-types `GraphPatternWire`/`PatternQueryResult`/`PatternQueryError`; returns the matched subgraph in the **same `{entities,links}` shape `list()` returns**, so the Graph renderer surface is unchanged — the only consuming change is additive/opt-in: `apps/graph/src/app.ts` gains a non-fatal `resolvePatternServerSide` that surfaces the documented "Narrow the source" cost-cap banner via the existing `showStatus`; any failure/older shell leaves the client matcher (which mirrors the compiler — documented invariant) as the painted scene; no scene/layout/history code touched. **Latent bug found + fixed (reproduce-first):** the 9.13.1.5 compiler pushed params in code order (subjects then edges) but emits link-type placeholders (FROM) before subject-type placeholders (WHERE); SQLite binds positionally, so **every executed pattern returned zero rows** — invisible because the old tests only asserted substring/`arrayContaining` and never executed the SQL. Fixed via three ordered param buckets (`fromParams`/`whereSubjectParams`/`whereForbiddenParams`) concatenated in SQL textual order; reproduced by 7 failing `pattern-query.test.ts` cases first. **Tests:** compiler suite 30→38; new `pattern-query.test.ts` 23 against a real `entities.db` incl. plan-mandated property tests (edge-order commutativity, identical-edge dedup, estimate monotonicity) + Required/Optional/Forbidden + In/Out/Both + distinctness + cost-cap fires/passes + compile-error passthrough; `vault-entities-service` +9 `queryPattern` cases; 518 pass across entities-repo/entities/sdk/sdk-types/graph. `bun run typecheck` clean; `apps/graph/src/app.ts` clean under app-tsc; biome clean on all 10 touched files; `@brainstorm/shell` + `@brainstorm-app/graph` builds green. **Pre-existing unrelated (flagged, not mine):** 21 app-tsc errors confined to untouched `apps/graph/src/logic/match-pattern.ts|.test.ts` + `render/renderer.ts`; workspace biome errors in other teams' WIP (`apps/database/.../contact-import.ts`, `apps/whiteboard/.../demo/dataset.ts`) — predate this session. Multi-hop stays 9.13.4 (compiler rejects `hops>1` as a tested compile error). Follow-up: fold the server subgraph in as the primary scene source (drop the client matcher) once multi-hop lands.

## Graph 9.13.5a — d3-force moved into a Web Worker (off the renderer main thread)

✅ DONE (2026-05-16). **User-reported:** "graph becomes slow after opening a document," still slow after a debounce + dropping the per-refetch `layoutNodes.clear()`. A performance review found the renderer was fine (Pixi, `unsafe-eval` imported), but the **force simulation ran on the UI thread**: `preConverge` synchronously in `reconcileLayout` and `tickLayout` every `requestAnimationFrame`. Any topology-changing vault write (a new note; or a body edit that changes `@`-mention-derived edges) reheated `alpha`, so the main thread ticked + did a full Pixi edge-geometry rebuild every frame for the whole multi-second cooldown — and an open document autosaving fanned that repeatedly. This is the documented canonical-path violation (memory `svg-is-a-perf-trap`: "pixi + d3-in-worker").

**What landed.** Four new files under `apps/graph/src/render/`:
- `force-engine.ts` — the stateful sim core, extracted from `app.ts`. Owns the node array + `alpha`, steps the unchanged pure `force-layout.ts` functions; zero DOM/Worker/timer deps. `reset()` pre-converges synchronously *inside the engine* (so off-thread in the worker) — the first frame the UI paints is already settled, no public wiggle.
- `force-worker.ts` — module-Worker entry. One `ForceEngine` + a `setInterval(16ms)` pump that posts transferable `Float32Array` position frames and **stops entirely when cool** (CPU → 0 until a reheat).
- `force-protocol.ts` — pure `packGraph` / `applyPositions`. Positions are flat `[x,y]*N` in a per-`epoch` `ids` order; a topology change bumps the epoch and the consumer drops stale frames; a pinned/dragged (`fx+fy`) node is never overwritten by a streamed frame.
- `layout-driver.ts` — `LayoutDriver`: owns the Worker, exposes `reset/pump/setFixed/releaseFixed/reheat/setParams/dispose`. Transparently **falls back to a synchronous in-process `ForceEngine`** when `Worker` is unavailable / throws under sandbox CSP / in tests — behaviour-identical to the pre-9.13.5 path, so the app never hard-fails on the simulation.

`app.ts` rewired: `primeLayout` only seeds (the driver pre-converges off-thread on first `reset`); the RAF loop calls `state.layout.pump(state.layoutNodes)` instead of `tickLayout`; `reconcileLayout` pushes topology via `state.layout.reset(reheat = topologyChanged)`; drag / pin / force-slider / resize / scrubber reheats forward to the driver; the dragged node's paint coordinate is now set explicitly in the pointermove handler (the worker no longer copies `fx→x`, and `applyPositions` deliberately skips fixed nodes so the cursor has zero round-trip lag — a real bug the new tests caught); the `state.alpha` field was removed (the driver owns warmth); the worker is terminated on `pagehide`. Vite emits a separate `force-worker` chunk; `chooseRenderer` still defaults to Pixi.

**Tests:** +8 in `layout-driver.test.ts` — `packGraph` order/fixed-extraction/edge-indexing/dangling-drop; `applyPositions` write + pinned-skip + moved-flag; `ForceEngine` preconverge-then-cool, reheat re-warms, `setFixed` pins to `fx/fy`; `LayoutDriver` sync-fallback settles + a dragged node stays under the cursor while neighbours move. **109 graph tests green** (was 101). App-level `tsc` clean for every new file + the rewired `app.ts` (one pre-existing unrelated `=== "1"` SDK-version error at `app.ts:2113` left as-is — it predates this work, in restored in-progress code, and doesn't affect the build). `biome` clean; graph bundle builds with the worker split into its own chunk.

`bun run size`: the only failing entry is the **app-preload bundle** (48.39 KB vs 20 KB) — pre-existing in the restored tree, **not** introduced here (the graph worker is a per-app chunk, outside `.size-limit.json` scope). Flagged, not a regression from this change.

Stacks on the same-session interim fix (250ms debounce on `vaultEntities.onChange` + removing the per-refetch `state.layoutNodes.clear()` so unrelated edits no longer full-reseed). **OQ-GR-4 fully resolved** (Pixi renderer + d3-in-worker). Remaining 9.13.5 — frustum culling, level-of-detail thresholds, a formal 60fps@5k-nodes bench — still pending.

## Graph 9.13.5 — render-layer frustum culling + LOD honouring + formal 5k-node frame-budget bench

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). Closes the 9.13.5 umbrella. With the force sim off the main thread since 9.13.5a, the per-frame main-thread floor is the renderer's O(nodes + edges) sync pass. The `nodesContainer` carried a comment claiming "we do our own frustum culling via the camera transform" — but it was never implemented: every off-screen node still got a `Sprite`, a `tint`/size write, an icon-cache probe, and a label `<div>`. On a 5k-node vault zoomed in to read one cluster, ~95 % of that work painted pixels outside the viewport.

**What landed.** New pure module `apps/graph/src/render/frustum.ts` (zero DOM/Pixi):
- `computeViewBounds(transform, viewW, viewH, marginPx?)` — inverts the screen viewport (grown by a `DEFAULT_CULL_MARGIN_PX = 220` screen-px skirt so a pan never pops sprites in a frame late) to a world rect, exactly inverting the camera applied on `worldContainer` (`world = (screen - t)/k`). `k` clamped to `1e-4` so a zoom-to-fit on an empty graph yields finite bounds; signed `-0` collapsed to `+0` so the rect isn't a consumer footgun.
- `nodeInView(x, y, radius, bounds)` — circle-vs-rect (disc-bbox; conservative on the keep side, never culls an on-screen node).
- `segmentInView(x1, y1, x2, y2, bounds)` — segment-bbox-vs-rect for edges; a strict superset of true line-rect intersection (a corner-grazing edge is kept then GPU-clipped — cheaper than exact clipping for the rare false positive).

`pixi-renderer.ts` wired: `paintPixi` computes one `ViewBounds` per frame and threads it through the node / edge / label passes. A culled node skips every expensive per-node op; an already-allocated sprite is parked `visible=false; renderable=false` (Pixi skips it in the batch) but **not destroyed** — re-entering the viewport on a pan is a single `visible=true`, no realloc. The hovered node is always kept (popover/ring anchor stays correct mid-pan). Edges whose bbox misses the viewport are not stroked; off-screen label `<div>`s are not created. Per-frame `{visible, culled}` tally exposed on `handles.lastCull` and mirrored to `canvas.dataset.visibleNodes/culledNodes` for debug/CSS/tests. Pre-existing LOD constants (`ARROW_HIDE_BELOW_K`, `DETAIL_THRESHOLD_K`, `ICON_THRESHOLD_K`, `MAX_LABELED_NODES`) are unchanged and now composed with the cull rather than duplicated. `paintPixi`'s public signature is unchanged (`renderer.ts` untouched).

**Tests:** +15 in `frustum.test.ts` — `computeViewBounds` identity / margin / zoom-shrink / pan / k→0 finiteness / negative-margin clamp (6); `nodeInView` inside / outside / radius-graze / boundary (4); `segmentInView` inside / crossing-from-outside / bbox-miss / corner-graze (4); plus a **formal 9.13.5 frame-budget bench** (1): a deterministic 5000-node + 7500-edge frame, camera zoomed in so most fall outside the viewport, run 60×; asserts the per-frame cull pass stays under 8 ms (well inside the 16.6 ms budget — sub-ms in practice) and that it actually culled (visible ∈ (0, N), edges < E) so a no-op can't pass the timing assert. `segmentInView` uses `Math.min/max` (no per-call closures) since it runs per-edge per-frame. **126 graph tests green across 13 files.** App-level `tsc` clean on `frustum.ts` + the rewired `pixi-renderer.ts` (the one pre-existing unrelated `app.ts:2113` SDK-version error left as-is); `biome` clean; graph bundle builds (`index` 1320 kB / 249 kB gz + lazy Pixi chunks; no app-level size budget per `.size-limit.json`).

**Long-term keystone:** `frustum.ts` is renderer-agnostic — it survives any future spatial-hash hit-test or worker-paint swap. **9.13.5 fully done; OQ-GR-4 closed (Pixi + d3-in-worker + cull).**

## Graph 9.13.7 — local-view depth (1..10) + direction toggle + persisted-state version-gate bugfix

✅ DONE (2026-05-17). The local view shipped at 9.13.1.10 fixed at 1 hop; this generalises it and adds the depth/direction UX the design called for.

**Pure core.** `apps/graph/src/logic/local-scope.ts` generalised from a 1-hop walk to a level-synchronous BFS to `depth` hops with a `LocalDirection` enum (`In` / `Out` / `Both`). Semantics, documented in the module: **`depth` gates reachability; `direction` gates which edges BFS may traverse; the returned `links` are *every* live link between two in-scope nodes** (induced sub-graph), so a user at depth ≥ 1 sees real connectivity (triangles, back-references), not just the BFS tree. `clampLocalDepth` floors + clamps to `[1, 10]` and falls back to default on a non-finite value, so a corrupt/hand-edited persisted depth can never crash or unbound the walk. Backward-compatible: `localScope(db, root)` with no options == the old `depth 1, Both` behaviour exactly (the original 5 tests pass unchanged).

**App wiring.** `AppState` gains `localDepth` + `localDirection`; `effectiveDb` passes them through; both persist (payload **v5**) and load back clamp/enum-validated. The local badge (lower-left glass pill) gained a **depth stepper** (`− N hops +`, buttons disable at the 1/10 ends, `aria-live` on the value) and a **direction segmented toggle** (In · Both · Out, `aria-pressed`, `role=group`). New `setLocalParams` mirrors `setLocalRoot`'s re-scope path (clear layout → reconcile → re-converge) but keeps the focal node, and no-ops when the patch changes nothing (no needless reheat). CSS reuses the badge's glass surface with a focus-visible ring (`outline-offset: -1px`).

**Bug found + fixed (was masking persistence entirely).** `tsc` flagged the loader's `raw.version === 1` against the widened union. Root cause: the load gate was a hand-maintained allowlist `version === 1 || 2 || 3` that was never widened when the schema moved to v4 (inline pattern) / v5 — so **every payload a current build wrote was silently discarded on reload** (pattern, pinned positions, camera, local view all lost). `applyPersistedState` is already migration-tolerant, so the allowlist was replaced by a pure, tested `shouldRestorePersisted(raw)` (`apps/graph/src/logic/persisted-version.ts`) — restore any object payload with a finite `version ≥ 1` (incl. newer-build downgrades; reject corrupt/non-object rows). `persistState` now writes `CURRENT_PERSISTED_VERSION` so the literal can't drift again. **This also eliminates the long-carried "pre-existing unrelated `app.ts` SDK-version tsc error"** noted as left-as-is in 9.13.5a/earlier — it *was* this gate.

**UX paths.** Screenshot: the badge now reads `Local · <node>  − 2 hops +  [In|Both|Out]  ✕`. Keyboard: every control is a real `<button>`, tab-reachable, focus-ring visible; steppers disable at bounds. Screen reader: `role=group` + `aria-label` on each cluster, `aria-pressed` on the active direction, `aria-live=polite` on the hop count so a change is announced. Discoverability: controls appear inline the moment a local view is entered (right-click a node), no hidden menu. **i18n note (pre-existing debt, flagged not expanded):** the Graph app has no `t()` harness — every existing string in this file is hardcoded English (`Local · `, `Exit local view`). New strings match that existing convention rather than introduce a half-i18n system mid-iteration; a dedicated graph-app i18n pass remains owed (tracked).

**Tests:** +10 `local-scope.test.ts` (depth 1/2/3 chain expansion, MAX-depth whole-component, induced-cross-link visibility, direction In/Out/Both reachability, `clampLocalDepth` floor/clamp/non-finite, corrupt-depth can't unbound) + new `persisted-version.test.ts` (12: restores v1..current, newer-build downgrade, rejects missing/non-numeric/non-finite/≤0 version, rejects non-object rows). **140 graph tests green across 14 files** (was 126). App-level `tsc` clean on every touched file (the 21 remaining errors are pre-existing app-tsc debt in untouched `match-pattern.*` / `renderer.ts`, unrelated to this diff — `localScope` is imported only by `app.ts`); `biome` clean; graph bundle builds (`index` 1325.79 kB / 250.52 kB gz + lazy Pixi chunks; no app-level size budget per `.size-limit.json`).

**Long-term keystone:** `local-scope.ts` (BFS + direction) and `persisted-version.ts` survive the entities-service swap at Stage 9.3 — only the data source behind `effectiveDb` changes. **OQ-GR-2 (per-view layout coords) still open; 9.13.6 owns it.**

## B7.4 — cover-picker polish + cross-app icon-picker adoption + shared-picker keystone

User feedback drove three changes shipped together.

**1 — Cover radius removed + cover-picker polish.** Covers are always 100%-width full-bleed, so the `radius` 12–14 never applied cleanly: dropped at every product surface (Notes `<CoverBand>`, Database inspector + the `.db-inspector__cover` wrapper that was independently rounding it, Files preview). The SDK `radius` option / `<CoverBand radius>` prop is kept (defaults to 0; only Storybook still demos it). `<CoverPicker>` was reworked from "underdeveloped": a **pending+preview commit model** — all three tabs stage a pending cover that a live full-bleed `createEntityCoverElement` preview band reflects, one Apply commits (disabled until dirty via `sameCover`), Remove stays the immediate escape hatch (Gallery/Color no longer commit-and-close on click); a **drag-and-drop drop zone** replacing the lone upload button + bare empty sentence (file-drop + click-to-browse + dragover/uploading states, doubles as the empty state); **selection rings** on gradient/colour swatches (`--active` + `aria-pressed`, parity with the image library cells); a **curated Colour palette** (dim/subtle/surface tokens dropped — they read as a broken cover). The `CoverPicker` test suite was updated for the staged-then-Apply contract (+Apply-disabled-until-dirty); 7/7 green.

**2 — Shared-picker keystone (DRY; user asked for "the same localisation file for common interfaces used in apps").** New `@brainstorm/sdk/i18n` (`packages/sdk/src/i18n/common-labels.ts`) is the single source for the shared pickers' strings: it owns the canonical `IconPickerLabels`/`CoverPickerLabels` **types** and `DEFAULT_ICON_PICKER_LABELS`/`DEFAULT_COVER_PICKER_LABELS`. Both pickers' `labels` prop is now optional `Partial<…> | undefined`, merged over the defaults inside the component (`const L = { ...DEFAULTS, ...labels }`), so an app gets correct English for free and a localised host overrides only the keys it translates — per-app i18n manifests no longer carry common-UI boilerplate while the no-bare-strings convention holds. New `@brainstorm/sdk/picker-host` generalises Database's `react-dom/client` bridge into the ONE shared imperative mount (`openIconPicker` / `openCoverPicker` / `closePicker`, container `bs-picker-host`); Database's local `ui/picker-host.tsx` collapsed to a 1-line re-export (−~50 lines of hardcoded English) and the now-dead `.db-picker-host` CSS was removed (the `.icon-picker` chrome is itself `position:fixed; z-index:1000`, so the container needs no rule). Subpaths wired in `packages/sdk/package.json` exports + the `vitest.config.ts` alias block (ordering before the bare `@brainstorm/sdk` entry).

**3 — Cross-app icon adoption (every app with a real per-object icon surface).** Whiteboard (header board-icon → button → `openIconPicker`, persists `state.whiteboard.icon` via `persistBoard()` + `paintedHeaderBoardId = null` to defeat the same-id repaint guard), Bookmarks (per-card title-row icon → button, `mutateBookmark(id, b => ({...b, icon, updatedAt}))`, `stopPropagation` so the card link doesn't fire), Tasks (row glyph → button; a presentational `onPickIcon(task)` callback threaded through `TaskRowProps` → `SurfaceViewProps`/`SearchViewProps`/`TaskListOpts` so the app owns the picker mount + persists via the optimistic-then-`saveTask` path, mirroring `onToggleComplete`). Each non-React app gained `react`/`react-dom` deps + the vite `react()` plugin + tsconfig `jsx: "react-jsx"` (the accepted Database/Notes cost, doc 13). **Deferred with rationale (non-starters without inventing a new detail/write surface — the ad-hoc per-app UI the conventions reject):** Journal is a read-only `Note/v1` projection (its icon is owned/edited in Notes; the only sane coverage is the render-only follow-up of projecting the note's icon instead of `null`); Calendar renders a cross-source `ScheduledItem` projection with no event-detail surface; Graph is a canvas visualiser with no per-node DOM and no write path (editing is already delegated via the node-click `openEntity`).

**Verify:** workspace `tsc` clean; per-app `tsc` clean on database/whiteboard/bookmarks/tasks/notes; SDK picker suites 18/18; tasks/bookmarks/whiteboard suites 358/358; 4 app builds green (proves the vite `react()` plugin + the `@brainstorm/sdk/picker-host` subpath resolve and there is no `import type`-used-as-value trap); biome clean on all 23 touched files. No new IPC method, capability, manifest, or dependency beyond the already-sanctioned per-app react/react-dom; not a security-surface change (the pickers write `properties.icon`/`properties.cover` through each app's existing already-authorized persistence path).

### B7.4-fix — two icon regressions caught in use

**Journal showed the book glyph, never the note's real icon (the B7.4 render-only follow-up).** Journal hard-coded `createEntityIconElement(null, …)`, so an entry never reflected the source `Note/v1`'s own icon. Rather than hand-roll a 3rd icon validator (Graph's `resolveIcon` + `createEntityIconElement`'s internal guard already exist — the DRY ceiling is 3), `parseIcon(raw: unknown): Icon | null` was extracted into `@brainstorm/sdk/entity-icon` (re-exporting `Icon` from the same subpath so a consumer doesn't need a separate `@brainstorm/sdk-types` dep). `JournalEntry` now carries `icon: Icon | null`; `journal-projection.ts` (`projectJournalEntries`) + `runtime.ts` (`vaultEntityToNoteLike`/`notesFromSnapshot`) thread `properties.icon` through; `renderEntryHeader` looks the entry up by date key (same as `renderEntryBody`) and passes `entry?.icon ?? null`, keeping the journal-book glyph as the fallback only. Graph's `resolveIcon` was deliberately **not** refactored onto the shared parser — Graph is the documented fragile icon-regression site and is intentionally SDK-light; minimal blast radius wins there. Emoji/Image icons now render; Pack still degrades to the fallback in every imperative DOM app (the `createEntityIconElement` twin doesn't bundle Phosphor — a known, *consistent* limitation, not Journal-specific). Tests: `journal-projection.test.ts` gained an icon-projection case (emoji/pack pass, missing/malformed/non-object → null) + the real-snapshot pipeline test asserts `day.icon`; journal 70 → 78.

**Graph stopped showing object icons (7th occurrence of the chronic regression — see [[feedback_graph_renderer_regression_site]]).** Root cause: `apps/graph/src/render/scene.ts` computed `const showIcon = options.showIcons && subjectName !== null`, tying an object's icon to GraphPattern-subject membership. With `showUnmatched` on (or no active pattern at all — the common default) every node has `subjectName === null`, so **no node rendered its own icon** — bare discs everywhere. This is precisely the "renderer cull/visibility must fail-open" failure mode the memory warns about, re-introduced by commit 541bfb1 ("show only an object's own icon"). Fix: `showIcon = options.showIcons` — subject membership drives node `color` only (unmatched → grey), never icon presence; `resolveIcon` already returns `null` for icon-less objects so they correctly stay plain discs. Two `scene.test.ts` cases asserted the buggy behaviour as intended ("drops the icon for unmatched nodes (colour alone carries identity)") — corrected to assert that an unmatched node still resolves its OWN emoji/Image icon. Graph 193/193; rebuilt. The 21 pre-existing graph `tsc` errors (`match-pattern.*`, `renderer.ts`) are untouched files, on `main` before this session (the apps/*-not-gated baseline) — not this bug, not regressed here; flagged as separate debt. Verify: workspace `tsc` clean; journal app `tsc` clean; graph `scene.ts`/`scene.test.ts` `tsc` clean (zero errors in the files changed); journal + graph builds green; biome clean on all 8 touched files. No new dependency/IPC/capability/manifest; not a security-surface change (pure render/projection over already-authorized reads).
