(b) **Defence in depth**: new pure TS-AST checker `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/type-import-check.ts` `findTypeOnlyImportUsedAsValue(files) → violations`, mirroring the 12.2 `findHardcodedJsxText` pattern (header rationale, `SourceFileInput` reuse, `type-value-exempt` escape hatch, conservative value-position-only matching: call/new callee, property/element-access target, JSX tag — so pure type positions never false-positive). Catches whole-clause `import type {X}` / `import type D` / `import type * as N` and per-specifier `import { type X }` used as a runtime value. **Tests:** `tools/mcp-server/tests/type-import-check.test.ts` — 7 unit cases (per-specifier call, whole-clause new/call/JSX, default+namespace, correct-value-import negative, type-position negative, exempt comment, path+1-based-line) + 1 repo-wide CI guard over `apps`+`packages/shell/src`+`packages/sdk/src` (`.ts`/`.tsx`, excludes `.d.ts`/`.test.*`) — **currently zero violations**, lands green. mcp-server suite 320 → **328 (29 files), all pass**; workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean. Self-found+fixed during build: a `` `packages/*/src` `` in the new file's JSDoc contained a literal `*/` that prematurely closed the block comment (oxc parse error) — reworded. **Why this matters:** the plan asserts a uniform non-negotiable quality bar (Workflow standard 3); it was unenforceable for `apps/*` because the workspace `tsc` only covers `packages` and Vite never typechecks. The bar is now real for apps, and the specific runtime-fatal-but-typecheck-invisible import-type trap has a structural CI guard. G0 parallel-fan-out item; needed no OQ.

### B9.3-journal — Journal DOM-twin in-document find

✅ DONE (2026-05-19). The last open B9 rung's Journal half (Code-editor half stays ⚪, gated on 9.7.2/shiki — flagged, no OQ). Journal's day-body is a **rendered, read-only projection** (editing routes to Notes), so it can't use the Lexical model adapter — it needed the DOM twin. **What landed:** (a) new reusable SDK primitive `createDomTextSearchProvider(getRoot)` in `@brainstorm/sdk/find-replace` (exported from the subpath index) — a find-only `TextSearchProvider` for any read-only rendered text surface (Journal now; future captured-Bookmarks / Preview bodies). Match handles are flat char offsets into the root's text content, re-derived from the live DOM each `search` (the surface is stable between searches); literal matcher with `caseSensitive`/`wholeWord` (regex flag honoured as literal per the controller contract / OQ-FR-1). `revealMatch` wraps a single-text-node hit in a transient `<mark data-bs-find class="bs-find-hit">` and scrolls it into view; multi-node (rare) → select-range + scroll, no wrap; `clear()` unwraps + `normalize()`s so the DOM is byte-restored. `replaceMatch`/`replaceAll` are no-ops returning 0 and `selectionRange` is always `null` — a read surface is immutable and has no in-selection scope (FindBar mounted `mode:"find"`). (b) Journal wiring in `app.ts` `setupFind()` (called from `bootstrap()` alongside the nav buttons): `createFindController(provider,{persist:{key:"journal:find"}})` over `() => root.querySelector(".journal__entry-body")` (re-queried each search so a day/mode repaint can't strand a stale element), `attachFindBar(root,…,{mode:"find"})` + `attachFindShortcuts(window,…)` (same `<FindBar>` chrome + chords as Notes — consistent-interface invariant), and a controller subscription that calls `provider.clear()` whenever the bar closes (the seam has no `clear`). `journalFind.close()` is funnelled into every user-nav mutator (`focusTo`/`setMode`/`applyJournalNav`) so navigating days resets the highlight (flat-offset handles don't survive a body swap). **Bug found+fixed during build:** the offset→DOM-position mapper bound an end offset that exactly filled a text node to the *next* node, making a single-node match look multi-node and skip the `<mark>` wrap — added start/end boundary-affinity to `locate`. Also hardened: `scrollIntoView` (jsdom throws "Not implemented") is wrapped in a swallow — reveal correctness is the wrap/selection, not the scroll. **Tests:** +12 jsdom — `packages/sdk/src/find-replace/dom-text-search-provider.test.ts` 9 (multi-occurrence offsets, case/whole-word, cross-element span, empty/absent-root, literal-escaping, single-node wrap+restore+normalize, one-mark-at-a-time, cross-element no-wrap-no-throw, find-only seam) + `apps/journal/src/logic/find-wiring.test.ts` 3 (scoped find+reveal on Journal-shaped DOM, close→clear via the exact `setupFind` subscription, find-only). SDK find-replace + Journal suites green (30/30 in the targeted run); `apps/journal` app-tsc clean; workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Why this matters:** completes find-in-document for the second core app and ships the reusable read-surface DOM provider every future projected-body app reuses — on the OQ-185-payback critical path (B9 is 13.4a's prerequisite). G0/parallel-track item; needed no OQ.

### 12.10 — missing-translation-key CI guard

✅ DONE (2026-05-19). Closes the i18n-correctness analogue of 12.9's import-type hole: today an unknown `t(key)` returns the visible `[?key]` marker (per `renderer/i18n/t.ts`) and ships to users — silently fatal at the user surface, invisible to typecheck. **What landed:** pure TS-AST checker `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/translation-key-check.ts` `findUnknownTranslationKeys(files, isKnown)` mirroring the 12.2 / 12.9 pattern. Conservative by design (the repo guard must have zero false positives): only counts `t` / `tIfKey` identifiers **actually imported from a `…/i18n/t` module** (an unrelated `t` in a different module is not flagged), honours rename imports (`{ t as tr }`), flags only when the first arg is a **literal string** (dynamic / templated args are skipped — same stance as 12.2 skipping dynamic JSX), with a `t-key-exempt` comment on or above the line as the explicit escape hatch. **Repo guard** walks `packages/shell/src/renderer` (excluding `.d.ts` / `.test.*` / `.stories.*`) and resolves `isKnown` by **calling the live `t()` from the real shell manifest** — a key is known iff `t(key) !== "[?key]"`. No duplicate manifest copy, no fragile parsing of `t.ts`: the runtime contract IS the source of truth. **Currently zero violations** — the shell renderer is clean and the guard lands green going forward. **Apps' own per-app manifests** (each app has its own `t()` / DEFAULTS, per CLAUDE.md §Localization) are deliberately out of scope this iteration — the bounded, unambiguous surface is the shell renderer; apps can layer their own variants if they ship the same `[?…]` semantics. **Tests:** `tools/mcp-server/tests/translation-key-check.test.ts` — 8 unit cases (literal miss flagged, `tIfKey` miss flagged, known key clean, dynamic / templated args skipped, unrelated `t` ignored, rename import honoured, `t-key-exempt` on/above line, path + 1-based line + key reporting) + 1 repo-wide CI guard. mcp-server suite 328 → **337 (30 files), all pass**; workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Why this matters:** complements 12.2 (no hardcoded JSX text) + 12.9 (no type-only import used as value) — the third structural CI gate over the same shell + apps surface. Together they form the actually-enforced "uniform bar" for the parallel-fan-out era (Workflow standard 3): a `t("typo")` now fails CI instead of leaking `[?typo]` to a beta user. **Why now:** G0 spine items are serial / OQ-gated; this is a bounded G0-parallel-track quality gate that needed no OQ and ships clean. 12.3 ("required `description` on every `t()`") is **gated on 12.1** (the manifest is `Record<string,string>` today; FormatJS-style descriptions arrive with the @formatjs/intl migration) and is deliberately not picked here — flagged for when 12.1 lands.

### 12.11 — a11y button accessible-name CI guard

✅ DONE (2026-05-19). Closes the canonical a11y bug class: a `<button>` shipping without a screen-reader name (no text content, no `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`/`title`, no labelled inner element). A sighted user sees a glyph; a screen reader reads "button" with no purpose. The 12.4 a11y audit on the beta-exit checklist needed a structural floor under it — this is the i18n / type-import / coverage-floor / `◑`-expiry sibling, the sixth class in the actually-enforced uniform bar (Workflow standard 3). **What landed:** pure TS-AST checker `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/a11y-button-name-check.ts` `findUnnamedButtons(files)`, mirroring 12.2's conventions. Conservative for zero-false-positive: a button passes if it carries a non-empty `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`/`title` (literal **or** expression — intent counts), any descendant with text / string-literal child / `t(…)` or `tIfKey(…)` call / opaque `{variable}` (same dynamic-content stance as 12.2 — can't verify, don't false-positive), or a labelled inner element. `<Button>` (uppercase) is out of scope — components own their own a11y contract. `a11y-exempt` comment is the explicit escape hatch. **Bug found+fixed during build:** the AST walker initially matched JsxExpression nodes *inside attribute values* (e.g., `onClick={x}`) as if they were JSX-child expressions, so `<button onClick={x}><Icon/></button>` was incorrectly passing as labeled; fixed by parenting-gate (`node.parent` must be `JsxElement` / `JsxFragment` — the same child-only check 12.2 uses).

**Two real a11y violations the live guard surfaced + fixed inline** (small enough to fix-not-snapshot, unlike SH-31's `KNOWN_EXPIRED`): icon-only skin-tone radios at `packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/icon-picker.tsx:403` and `packages/sdk/src/icon-picker/picker.tsx:496`. Both render `<button role="radio" aria-checked={...}><img alt="" /></button>` inside a `role="radiogroup"` with a localized region label — the wrapping group is named correctly, but the per-option button had no per-option name (the `<img alt="">` is correctly decorative). Fixed with `aria-label={\`Skin tone ${tone.id}\`}` on each radio — the canonical radiogroup pattern (group has the localized name, each radio names its option). The English-prefix `Skin tone …` is a pragmatic interim; full localization rides 12.1 (FormatJS migration).

**Tests:** `tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-button-name-check.test.ts` — 13 unit cases (empty / self-closing / icon-only flagged; aria-label literal+expression passes; aria-labelledby + title pass; empty/whitespace labels rejected; text-bearing JSX direct + nested + string-literal pass; `t()`/`tIfKey()` pass; opaque `{variable}` passes; labelled inner child passes; `<Button>` ignored; `a11y-exempt` on/above line; path + 1-based line + excerpt reporting; non-`.tsx` ignored) + 1 repo-wide CI guard (with a `KNOWN_UNLABELED` snapshot mechanism — currently empty after the 2 inline fixes; identical pattern to SH-31's `KNOWN_EXPIRED`). mcp-server suite **365 → 379**, all 33 files pass; workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean; all 11 apps tsc clean.

**The structural CI gate inventory now stands at six** — 12.2 (no hardcoded JSX) · 12.9 (no type-only import used as value, apps/* in CI) · 12.10 (no missing `t()` key in shell) · 12.11 (no unnamed `<button>`) · SH-30 (per-package coverage-floor pin) · SH-31 (no expired `◑`). Together they are the actually-enforced uniform bar (Workflow standard 3) — the safety substrate the parallel-fan-out G2 needs before the spine clears (without it, confident-but-wrong fan-out produces "Graph icons regressed 6×"-class failures invisible to typecheck). **Why now:** G0 spine items remain serial / OQ-gated (`10.0` sync spike, `9.3.5.B`); this is a bounded G0-parallel-track gate that needed no OQ, ships clean, and directly addresses beta-exit "12.4 a11y" with a working enforcement instead of policy-only prose. The remaining 12.4 audit work (focus rings, react-aria primitives, full keyboard reachability) is a separate scope when its iteration comes up — this guard catches the most-leaky class first.

### 9.12.R1-perf — Database render-layer perf instrumentation + first wins

✅ DONE (2026-05-19). 9.12.R1 shipped six React views without `Perf: before/after numbers vs doc-13 render budget` (the iteration's own success criterion). This iteration lands the **measurement substrate** first so future render-layer changes have ground truth, plus two concrete optimizations spotted while wiring it.

**Primitive — `@brainstorm/sdk/perf`** — tiny `mark` / `measure` / `time` / `timeAsync` API around `performance.*` with a 64-entry ring buffer for assertions and a `subscribe({ thresholdMs, prefix }, cb)` channel for over-budget warnings. No-op-safe (`performance` undefined → falls back to `Date.now`). 7 unit tests; vitest alias added to keep apps' bundler-flavoured tests resolving the subpath.

**Wiring — Database app** — `renderActiveView` body now sits inside `time("db.renderActiveView", …)` and the filter / sort / group step inside `time("db.compileView", …)`. A boot-time `subscribePerf({ thresholdMs: 16, prefix: "db." }, …)` routes anything that crosses the doc-13 16ms keystroke→paint budget to the runtime error log so triage picks it up automatically — no per-call site noise on the fast path.

**Optimization 1 — kill the `memo(GridRow)` bailout.** `app.ts` builds fresh `onSelect` / `onOpen` closures every `renderActiveView` (they close over `state`), so `memo(GridRow)` was bailing out on every selection click — every visible virtualized row re-rendering for a single click. New `useStableCallback` (local to `apps/database/src/react/`) keeps the latest closure in a ref and returns an identity-stable wrapper. Applied in `GridView`; the other 5 views aren't memoized yet (no perf bug to fix), so the hook is held for adoption when they are.

**Optimization 2 — cache the compile pipeline.** New `apps/database/src/logic/compile-cache.ts` — three sibling 1-slot reference-keyed memos: `compileViewCached` (filter/sort/group), `filterEntitiesCached` (membership + search), `groupLabelResolverCached` (id→title for board groupings). Selection clicks no longer re-walk every entity in the vault; the React tree receives the same `CompiledView` object back. 8 unit tests covering hit/miss on each axis (entities reference, search query, db reference, manualOrder).

**Tests + types:** 15 new tests (perf 7 + compile-cache 8); full suite 449 files / 4433 tests green; workspace `tsc --noEmit` + per-app tsc all clean. **Out of scope** (deliberately): widening memoization to list/gallery/board/calendar/timeline (those views don't memo their rows yet — a separate "memo + stable callback" pass when a vault actually exercises one of them); virtualizing list/gallery (currently unbounded `.map((entity) => …)`, a real trap once vaults grow but not the most-leaky fingerprint right now); Playwright key-to-paint harness (Stage 12.7, scheduled).

### 12.12 — a11y `<img>` missing-alt CI guard

✅ DONE (2026-05-19). The companion to 12.11 — the other canonical WCAG-2.1 violation at the repo's UI surface. An `<img>` without an `alt` attribute is opaque to screen readers (the file URL gets read, or nothing); the **missing attribute** is the bug. An empty `alt=""` is the **correct decorative signal** and must pass (it tells AT to skip the image). **What landed:** pure TS-AST checker `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/a11y-img-alt-check.ts` `findImagesMissingAlt(files)`, mirroring 12.11's structure exactly. Conservative: an `<img>` passes if it carries any `alt` attribute (string literal — empty or not — or an expression value; intent counts per the 12.2 dynamic-content stance). Fails only when the attribute is entirely absent. `<Img>` (uppercase) is out of scope (components own their own a11y contract). `a11y-exempt` comment is the escape hatch. **Repo guard** over `apps` + shell renderer + sdk `.tsx` (excluding `.test.tsx` / `.stories.tsx`) — currently **zero violations**: every one of the 15 `<img>` tags in scope already carries an `alt` attribute. The guard lands green and locks the state going forward.

**Tests:** `tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-img-alt-check.test.ts` — 9 unit cases (no-alt self-closing flagged; `alt=""` decorative passes; non-empty literal passes; expression value passes; `<img>…</img>` legal-but-rare form handled identically; `<Img>` ignored; `a11y-exempt` on/above; path+1-based-line+excerpt; non-`.tsx` ignored) + 1 repo-wide CI guard with the `KNOWN_NO_ALT` snapshot mechanism (currently empty — pattern parity with SH-31 / 12.11 / 12.10's snapshot guards). mcp-server suite **379 → 389**, all 34 files pass; workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean.

**The structural CI gate inventory now stands at seven** — 12.2 (no hardcoded JSX) · 12.9 (no type-only import used as value + apps/* in CI) · 12.10 (no missing `t()` key in shell) · 12.11 (no unnamed `<button>`) · **12.12 (no `<img>` missing alt)** · SH-30 (per-package coverage-floor pin) · SH-31 (no expired `◑`). The two together (12.11 + 12.12) cover **the two highest-frequency WCAG violations** at the JSX surface — the 12.4 a11y audit's structural floor is now wide enough that an autonomous fan-out can't silently leak the canonical screen-reader bugs. **Why now:** G0 spine items remain serial / OQ-gated (`10.0` sync spike, `9.3.5.B`); this is a bounded G0-parallel-track gate that needed no OQ, ships clean, and matches the 12.11 sibling exactly in structure — making the a11y guard pattern reusable for the remaining 12.4 classes (focus rings, role-`button` divs, `<a>` without href, missing form labels) as future iterations.

### 12.13 — a11y form-input missing-label CI guard

✅ DONE (2026-05-20). **Completes the WCAG SC 4.1.2 trio at the JSX surface** — 12.11 (buttons) + 12.12 (images) + 12.13 (form inputs). A user-facing `<input>` / `<textarea>` / `<select>` without an accessible name is opaque to screen readers and to dictation. **What landed:** pure TS-AST checker `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/a11y-form-input-check.ts` `findUnlabeledFormInputs(files)`, mirroring 12.11 / 12.12's structure exactly. **Conservative pass criteria** — any ONE of: (1) `aria-label` (literal non-empty OR expression), (2) `aria-labelledby` (literal OR expression), (3) `title`, (4) `placeholder` (literal non-empty OR expression — not ideal a11y but the established repo convention; flagging it would false-positive widely), (5) **wrapped in a `<label>` element** (the implicit-association pattern — walks `node.parent` up the AST). Inputs skipped by `type`: `hidden` (never user-facing), `submit` / `button` / `reset` (uses `value` as label; the JSX-button equivalents are covered by 12.11). `<Input>` / `<Textarea>` / `<Select>` (uppercase) out of scope — components own their own a11y contract. `a11y-exempt` escape hatch.

**Three real violations the live guard surfaced + fixed inline** (small enough to fix-not-snapshot, following the 12.11 precedent):

1. **`packages/sdk/src/icon-picker/picker.tsx:557`** — hidden `<input type="color">` triggered by a sibling `<button aria-label="Custom colour">`.
2. **`packages/shell/src/renderer/ui/icon-picker.tsx:449`** — the shell-side parallel of the same custom-color pattern.
3. **`packages/sdk/src/cover-picker/picker.tsx:274`** — hidden `<input type="file">` triggered by a parent dropzone button.

All three are the "visually hidden interactive element triggered by a labelled button/parent" anti-pattern. The button's `aria-label` doesn't substitute for the input's own a11y name (screen readers and automated tooling may still surface the input itself). Fixed each with an `aria-label` on the input directly: `"Custom colour"` (×2) and `"Choose cover image file"`. English literals are interim; full localization rides 12.1 (FormatJS migration).

**Tests:** `tools/mcp-server/tests/a11y-form-input-check.test.ts` — 10 unit cases (bare input/textarea/select flagged; tag-name reported on the violation; aria-label/labelledby/title/placeholder pass literal+expression; empty/whitespace rejected; wrapping `<label>` passes incl. nested; type-hidden/submit/button/reset skipped; uppercase `<Input>` ignored; `a11y-exempt` on/above; path+1-based-line+excerpt; non-`.tsx` ignored) + 1 repo-wide CI guard with the `KNOWN_UNLABELED_INPUTS` snapshot mechanism (currently empty after the 3 inline fixes). mcp-server suite **389 → 400 (a clean four-hundred milestone)**, all 35 files pass; workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean.

### 12.14 — `<button type=>` correctness CI guard

✅ DONE (2026-05-20). Cousin to the 12.11/12.12/12.13 a11y trio — same structural-CI pattern, different bug class (correctness, not a11y). **What it catches:** HTML defaults `<button>` to `type="submit"` inside a `<form>`. A bare `<button onClick={save}>` ships and works in dev; the moment any `<form>` ancestor appears (now or in a future refactor), pressing Enter or clicking the button submits the form and kicks off whatever default-submit behaviour exists — often a page reload, sometimes a stray request. The bug is **invisible to typecheck**, surfaces in production as "clicking save triggers an extra navigation," and matches the SH-30 / 12.9 / 12.10 / 12.11 / 12.12 / 12.13 family of "silently fatal at the user surface, invisible to the existing gates."

The guard locks the discipline forward: a careless `<button>` from a parallel-fan-out agent now fails CI here, not as a navigation-bug ticket later. mcp-server suite **400 → 408**, all 36 files pass; workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean.

**The structural CI gate inventory now stands at nine** — 12.2 (no hardcoded JSX) · 12.9 (no type-only import used as value + apps/* in CI) · 12.10 (no missing `t()` key in shell) · 12.11 (no unnamed `<button>`) · 12.12 (no `<img>` missing alt) · 12.13 (no unlabeled form input) · **12.14 (no `<button>` missing `type=`)** · SH-30 (per-package coverage-floor pin) · SH-31 (no expired `◑`). ### SH-32 — Dead-exempt audit (orphan escape hatches)

✅ DONE (2026-05-20). The **meta-gate** keeping the 9 structural CI gates honest over time. Each gate carries an `…-exempt` comment escape hatch for the rare legitimate case (`i18n-exempt`, `a11y-exempt`, `t-key-exempt`, `type-value-exempt`, `button-type-exempt`). In practice, when the underlying code is later refactored so the violation goes away, nobody remembers to remove the exempt — orphan exempts accumulate, the escape hatch normalises into permanent silence, and the gate's authority erodes. SH-32 makes "an exempt is debt with an expiry" structural, the same way SH-31 made "`◑` is debt with an expiry" structural.

**What landed:** pure `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/orphan-exempts-audit.ts` `findOrphanExempts(files, { tKeyIsKnown? })`. Implementation chose **zero-checker-modification**: for each exempt token at byte offset `[start, end)`, mutate the source to `source[0..start] + "X".repeat(end - start) + source[end..]` — same-length filler preserves every byte/line position downstream. Re-run the matching checker (`findHardcodedJsxText` for `i18n-exempt`, all three a11y checkers for `a11y-exempt`, etc.); the existing `EXEMPT.includes(...)` line check naturally fails against the masked token, so the would-be violation surfaces. Exempt is **justified** if a violation appears at line N (same line as exempt) or N+1 (the line below — mirrors the `lines[line0] || lines[line0 - 1]` protection every checker uses); **orphan** otherwise. `t-key-exempt` is silently skipped when no `tKeyIsKnown` is supplied (out-of-scope, not orphan) — the shell-only manifest makes auditing it require the live shell `t()` per 12.10.

**Two real orphan exempts found + cleaned up** in `apps/database/src/react/grid-view.tsx` from the 9.12.R1 grid commit chain — both pre-emptive `i18n-exempt`s landed by an over-cautious author over constructs the 12.2 guard wouldn't actually flag:
1. Line 195 — over a `<div>` containing `#` JsxText. The `#` is a single character; 12.2's `HAS_WORD = /\p{L}{2,}/u` correctly skips it. The exempt was protecting nothing.
2. Line 204 — over `<PinnedHeaderCell width={TITLE_WIDTH} label="Name" />`. The `"Name"` is an attribute *value*, not JSX text; 12.2 only flags JsxText children. The exempt was protecting nothing.
Both deleted. The third `i18n-exempt` further down (line 221, over `No entities match this view.`) is **genuinely justified** — that's real hardcoded user-visible text — and stays.

**Bug found+fixed during test build:** my initial test fixtures placed `// type-value-exempt` and `// t-key-exempt` *above the import line* instead of *above the usage line*. The gates' protection window is current-or-prior-line only — an exempt above the import doesn't reach the violation at the call site two lines below. Fixed by relocating the exempts in the fixtures directly above the violation line. The test's pass/fail behaviour now mirrors how a developer must actually use the escape hatch (placing it immediately above the line you're escaping).

**Tests:** `tools/mcp-server/tests/orphan-exempts-audit.test.ts` — 13 unit cases (6 justified-by-class across all five exempt kinds · 5 orphan-by-class · same-line-exempt + violation · `t-key-exempt`-skipped-without-`tKeyIsKnown`) + 1 repo-wide CI guard with the `KNOWN_ORPHAN_EXEMPTS` snapshot mechanism. The guard surfaced + cleared the 2 grid-view orphans; the snapshot is currently empty (every remaining exempt in `apps/*` + `packages/shell/src/renderer` + `packages/sdk/src` is now justified). mcp-server suite **408 → 422**, all 37 files pass; workspace `tsc --noEmit` clean; Database app-tsc clean.

**The structural CI gate inventory now stands at ten** — 12.2 (no hardcoded JSX) · 12.9 (no type-only import used as value + apps/* in CI) · 12.10 (no missing `t()` key in shell) · 12.11 (no unnamed `<button>`) · 12.12 (no `<img>` missing alt) · 12.13 (no unlabeled form input) · 12.14 (no `<button>` missing `type=`) · SH-30 (per-package coverage-floor pin) · SH-31 (no expired `◑`) · **SH-32 (no orphan exempt)**. The **SH-31 / SH-32 pair** is the meta-floor under the other eight: the escape hatches in the first nine can't accumulate into permanent dead weight, and an iteration's debt has to either stay live or be removed. **Why now:** G0 spine items remain serial / OQ-gated (`10.0` sync spike, `9.3.5.B`); this is a bounded G0-parallel-track meta-gate that needed no OQ, ships clean, and directly addresses the long-tail erosion mode that would otherwise quietly defeat my nine-gate stack of work over the months between today and the `2026-09-01` beta.

### 10.1 — per-entity DEK on create (sealed under vault master key)

✅ DONE (2026-05-22). First rung of the G2 sync spine. Builder commit `4038029` + integrator pass `115a6b0` (parallel reviews fanned out — code / security / pentest / leak — folded into one fix commit). The 10.0 spike (2026-05-20) positioned the design; 10.1 realizes the **at-rest half** of the per-entity DEK invariant. The wire-encryption half lands at 10.3 on top of this primitive.

**What landed:**

- **Migration v2** on `entities.db` adds the `entity_deks` table: `(dek_id PK, entity_id FK → entities(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, version DEFAULT 1, sealed_dek_json TEXT, created_at)` + `idx_entity_deks_entity`. `version` is forward-allocated for rotation (10.2 / OQ-27); 10.1 writes exactly one row per entity at create. The `entities.dek_id` column was already in v1 — Stage 3 forward-allocated it so 10.1 doesn't bump the entities row schema, only the sibling table.

- **New module** `packages/shell/src/main/entities/entity-dek-store.ts` (`EntityDekStore`): `nextDekId()` mints an id, `persist(entityId, dekId)` generates a fresh 32-byte DEK via `generateSymmetricKey` (CSPRNG via `@noble/ciphers/utils.js`), seals it under the vault master key with `sealSecret` (XChaCha20-Poly1305 + 192-bit random nonce + Poly1305 tag — the 2.x credentials primitive), and inserts the wrap. `open(entityId)` re-unwraps from disk (no in-memory cache — that's a 10.3 concern when the wire path needs it). `close(dek)` does `dek.fill(0)`. Master key is held in an **ES private field** (`#masterKey`) so `Object.values(store)` / `JSON.stringify(store)` can never exfiltrate it; the field aliases `VaultSession`'s `this.masterKey` buffer so the in-place `zero(this.masterKey)` on dispose propagates without a second teardown.

- **AAD is domain-separated**: `brainstorm/entity-dek/v1: || entityId` (UTF-8). Three bindings happen at once: (a) this is the per-entity-DEK construction (not a future block/attachment DEK), (b) this is scheme version 1, (c) this is this specific entity row. A future binding that reuses XChaCha20-Poly1305 can't accidentally cross-confuse a wrap from this one. The prefix is **load-bearing**: a test pins that the bare entity-id AAD (no prefix) fails — bare is the trap the prefix is closing.

- **Atomicity**: every `entities.create` IPC call now wraps `repo.create(entity-row)` + `dekStore.persist(wrap-row)` in a single SQLite transaction via the new `EntitiesRepository.transaction(fn)`. A throw from persist rolls back the entity row; a failed wrap never leaves an entity row with a dangling `dek_id`. Pinned by an atomicity test that injects a throwing persist and asserts no entity row remains. The DEK plaintext is `dekStore.close()`d in a `finally` so the buffer is zeroed whether the txn commits or aborts. Inside `persist()` itself, a try/catch zeros the freshly-minted DEK on any throw between `generateSymmetricKey` and the wrap row landing (defense-in-depth — no plaintext lingers in GC-eligible memory).

- **No new IPC surface, no new capability**. `entities.write:<type>` is still the only gate. `compose()` (the IPC response builder) was already not surfacing `dek_id` — a new test re-asserts the response contains neither the DEK id nor the sealed-DEK bytes.

- **`hardDelete()` got an explicit `DELETE FROM entity_deks WHERE entity_id = ?`** alongside its existing links + change_log cleanup. The FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` would handle this whenever `foreign_keys` PRAGMA is on, but `hardDelete`'s neighbours already do pragma-independent explicit deletes — we match the convention. Pinned by a service-path test (create → soft-delete → hardDelete → assert dek row gone).

- **`VaultSession.entityDekStore()`** got the in-flight-promise idiom (`dekStoreOpening`) that `propertiesStore` and `dashboardStore` already use; two concurrent first-callers no longer each construct a `EntityDeksRepository` + statement cache, with one becoming orphaned.

- **Tie-break + null-normalize**: `getByEntityId` now orders by `created_at DESC, version DESC, dek_id DESC` so the result is deterministic on collisions across both bun:sqlite and better-sqlite3 (deterministic-clock tests can produce the same `created_at` + `version=1`). `EntitiesRepository.create()` normalises `dekId: ""` → `null` so a loose contract can't stamp a FK target that can never match.

- **`dekId: string | null`** on `CreateEntityInput`: the IPC path always passes a real id, but shell-internal singletons (root folder `session.ts`, kv-backfill, shortcut bindings, dev seeder) pass `null` — their entities don't yet have wrap rows. **This is the silent-unencrypted-on-wire trap** flagged by both code review and security review: when 10.3 wires the sync encrypt path, it MUST fail-closed on `dek_id IS NULL` for any sync-targeted entity, and there MUST be a 10.x retro-wrap pass beforehand for the legacy entities created via `kv-entities-backfill`. Tracked, not coded.

- **Forward-pin test for 10.3**: `EntityDekStore.open()` recomputes AAD from the **requested** entity id, looks up the wrap by `entity_id` (not by `entities.dek_id`), and the AEAD tag verifies under that same id. If a future 10.3 resolver fetches a DEK by following `entities.dek_id → entity_deks.dek_id`, it MUST verify `row.entity_id === requestedEntityId` before unwrap — otherwise an `entities.dek_id` repoint UPDATE (filesystem write access) re-opens the DEK-swap vector. The test in `entity-dek-store.test.ts` documents this contract by demonstrating the existing implementation already honours it; 10.3 has to maintain the invariant.

**Tests:** workspace **5278 → 5284 (+51 file-count delta across the iteration; the +6 net new tests are the integrator pass — atomicity rollback / hardDelete cascade / domain-separated AAD pin / 10.3 forward-pin / empty-id rejection / zero-on-throw)**. EntityDekStore: 11 (shape, round-trip, AAD binding, master-key swap, domain-separator pin, forward-pin, empty-id rejection, zero-on-throw, clock+id injection, 2 property tests N=64 + N=32 — every iteration closes its DEK). EntityDeksRepository: 7 (CRUD, FK cascade, tie-break, deleteByEntityId, malformed sealed_dek_json). Migration v1→v2: 4 (idempotent forward, fresh-install convergence). Service: +3 from integrator (atomicity rollback, hardDelete cascade, IPC-leak fence). Workspace `typecheck:packages` + `typecheck:apps` clean.

**Review verdict** (folded into 115a6b0): no CRITICAL findings. Crypto primitives sound; gaps were at the orchestration seam (transactionality, finally scope, AAD guards, in-flight-promise idiom) — all closed. Three follow-ups deferred to subsequent stages with explicit tracking: (1) retro-wrap of legacy / kv-backfilled entities **before 10.3 ships** so the wire path can't silently skip null-DEK rows; (2) TC39 explicit-resource-management `using` shape for `EntityDekHandle` (10.3-era ergonomics); (3) optional `assertOpen`/disposed-master-key gate on the store (defense-in-depth — current code can't trigger it).

**Spike-forced clauses honoured** (from `docs/_review/2026-05-20-10.0-sync-spike.md` §5 10.1): XChaCha20-Poly1305 256-bit DEK · sealed under vault master key (2.x machinery) · never crosses IPC in plaintext · lifetime = open-entity-session · zeroed on close. No spike clause unmet.

**G2 status:** spine moves from 10.0 ✅ → **10.1 ✅** → 10.2 next (member-wraps inside the entity Yjs doc; HPKE swap per the spike). All G2 fan-out tails remain unblocked (9.4 + 9.10 cleared earlier this week). At-rest 3b on-disk flip + dev-MCP 0.12 write-tools remain G0 / dev-MCP work that can ride alongside the 10.x spine. Plaintext DEK store is now the only place outside `credentials/` that imports `sealSecret` — the crypto-routing convention from CLAUDE.md is preserved (the new module sits under `entities/` rather than `credentials/`, but consumes via the public credential primitive, not the keystore).

## 2026-05-28 — 12.1 — i18n runtime: FormatJS + ICU, shell catalog → `en.json` (⚪ → ✅)

The first non-structural rung of Stage 12, realising the [doc-21](platform/21-localization.md) runtime decision. The shell already had stable dotted ids behind a `t(key, params)` call (the contract the whole renderer depends on) — but the implementation was a naive `{name}`-regex replacer over an inline `DEFAULTS` map, with English-only plural hacks (`count === 1 ? oneKey : otherKey` branches in components, `object(s)` lazy suffixes). 12.1 swaps the engine and externalises the catalog **without changing a single call-site signature** — exactly the "build the architecture in v1, retrofitting costs a lot" bet doc-21 makes.

**What landed.**
- **`renderer/i18n/en.json`** — the source-language catalog. All 819 shell strings lifted out of the inline `DEFAULTS` map (mechanical dump, then targeted plural edits), checked into source (code → catalog flow per doc-21 §Tooling-enforced extraction; the per-app catalogs + extraction CLI stay their own rungs).
- **`renderer/i18n/t.ts`** rewritten on `@formatjs/intl@4.1.12` — `createIntl` + `createIntlCache` over the catalog, `locale`/`defaultLocale` both `en` (v1 is English-only). `t()`, `tIfKey()`, `registerTranslations()`, `TranslationParams` keep their exact shapes; the `[?key]` missing-marker + dev `console.warn` are preserved; a custom `onError` stays quiet in production and surfaces genuine ICU format errors in dev. `registerTranslations` recompiles the intl instance against the merged map (test helper + future per-locale pack loader).
- **ICU plurals** replace every manual count branch (doc-21 principle 5 — *no `count === 1`*): `permissionCount`, `perApp.requestCount`, `files.{minutes,hours,days}Ago`, `dictionaries.itemCount`, plus the lazy `object(s)`/`crash report(s)` strings (`bin.emptyConfirm`/`bin.emptiedToast`, properties usage pills + delete usage-note, `crash.pendingCount`/`crash.localCount`). The three components that branched (`file-handles-panel`, `grants-panel`, `network-egress-panel`) now call a single ICU key each; the `*One`/`.one`/`.other` partner keys were deleted (grepped clean across `packages/` + `apps/`).
- **ICU-safety audit** of the catalog before adoption: no stray `{`/`}` (every brace is a `{word}` arg), no `'{`/`'#`/`<` quote/tag sequences — every apostrophe (`isn't`, `Brainstorm's`, `won't`) is a literal, so all 819 strings parse cleanly.

**FormatJS missing-arg behavior** (one deliberate semantic change): the old regex left an unknown placeholder literally (`Hello Razor and {missing}`). FormatJS treats a missing required value as a format error and returns the *raw, un-interpolated* message; `onError` logs it in dev. Captured in the test rather than worked around — once `description`-required (12.3) lands, a missing value is a caught contract bug, not a render-time guess.

**Tests:** `t.test.ts` 5 → 12 — ICU singular/plural selection, `=0` exact match, real-catalog apostrophe-literal render, missing-arg degrade-to-raw, custom ICU plural via `registerTranslations`, `tIfKey` known/unknown. Full shell renderer suite **447/447** (the 6 reds on the first run were `Test timed out in 5000ms` under CPU contention from a parallel production build — green on a clean isolated re-run). Workspace `tsc` (`typecheck:packages` + `typecheck:apps`) clean; biome clean on touched files.

**Budget:** the FormatJS runtime is ~12.6 KB gz fixed cost — renderer JS gz **270.0 → 282.6 KB**, over the 270 KB ceiling. Since `@formatjs/intl` is the doc-21-mandated runtime (and the substrate the future `useFormatDate`/`useFormatNumber` SDK hooks + runtime locale-switching build on), `.size-limit.json` was bumped **270 → 290 KB** with a dated rationale + before/after, mirroring the 10.2 main-process bump precedent. `bun run build` + `bun run size` green.

**Security surface:** one new dependency (`@formatjs/intl`, a widely-used FormatJS package) confined to renderer string formatting; no new capability, IPC method, or crypto/keystore touch. **Next Phase-1 spine pull:** `12.3` (`description`-required CI), the `KBN-S`/`KBN-A` accessibility rungs, Welcome-1/2, App-lock `13.8`, or `B6.5` — integrator's call at handoff.

## 2026-05-28 — 12.3 — required translator `description`, CI-enforced (⚪ → ✅)

Directly continues 12.1. doc-21 §Required translation context makes a missing `description` a build error — "a string with no translation context is broken" — so a translator never sees a bare "Open" with no idea whether it's a verb, an adjective, or a status. 12.3 lands the *enforced-description* half on top of 12.1's flat `en.json`.

**Catalog shape (decision).** Descriptions live in a sibling en-only **`renderer/i18n/en.descriptions.json`** (`{id: description}`), NOT inline at call sites and NOT folded into `en.json` entries. Rationale: (1) `en.json` stays a clean flat `{id: message}` file, so future per-locale catalogs (`de.json`, `ja.json`) share its exact shape — doc-21's "translation files are flat per-locale; the description is dev metadata" split; (2) the metadata is **never imported by `t.ts`**, so it adds nothing to the renderer bundle (protects the 270→290 KB bump 12.1 just spent); (3) call sites and the `t(key, params)` contract are untouched. The doc-literal `t(id, {defaultMessage, description})` call shape + generated catalog (the `brainstorm-cli i18n extract` flow) stays a future rung — this lands the enforcement, not the extraction CLI.

**Gate.** `tools/mcp-server/src/tools/i18n-descriptions-check.ts` — pure `findDescriptionCoverage(catalog, descriptions, knownMissing) → { missing, staleGrandfathered, orphanDescriptions }` + a `readShellDescriptionCoverage()` disk wrapper. Wired as a vitest gate (`tools/mcp-server/tests/i18n-descriptions.test.ts`), joining the structural-CI-gate inventory alongside 12.2 / the a11y `KBN-G-*` guards.

**Coverage path (SH-31/.32 double-fence).** Full coverage is reached incrementally, not in one 800-string content dump. The 792 strings 12.1 carried over are grandfathered in `en.descriptions.known-missing.json`. The fence cuts both ways: a **new** catalog key with no description fails the gate immediately (regressions blocked), and a grandfathered key that later *gains* a description — or is removed from the catalog — is flagged **stale**, forcing its removal from the snapshot, so the grandfather list can only shrink. Seeded **21** real descriptions to start: the universal `shell.actions.*` set + every ICU plural key 12.1 touched (`permissionCount`, `requestCount`, `files.{minutes,hours,days}Ago`, `dictionaries.itemCount`, the properties usage pills, the `bin`/`crash` count strings).

**Tests:** +9 — 6 pure-logic (described-or-grandfathered passes; new-key flagged; empty/whitespace description treated as missing; grandfathered-now-described → stale; grandfathered-key-gone → stale; orphan description flagged) + 3 real-catalog gate (zero missing / stale / orphan). Workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean on touched files.

**Security surface:** none — a dev/CI-only JSON metadata file + a pure checker; no runtime code, dependency, capability, or IPC touched. **Next Phase-1 spine pull:** the `KBN-S`/`KBN-A` accessibility rungs (`12.4`), `12.8` recovery-scenario tests, Welcome-1/2, App-lock `13.8`, or `B6.5` — integrator's call at handoff.

## 2026-05-28 — 12.4 / KBN-S-settings — first composite-keyboard adopter (⚪ → ✅)

The opening rung of the `KBN-S-*` per-shell-surface ladder ([61-keyboard-accessibility.md](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md)). KBN-1..4 shipped the substrate (hooks, escape stack, CI guards, Playwright stubs) but **no surface had adopted `useCompositeKeyboard` yet** — so `KBN-P-arrow-composite` sat skip-deferred "until the first composite-adopter lands." This rung lands it on the Settings sidebar.

**Substrate gap closed first.** The `KBN-G-roles` guard's own doc says composite roles "must flow through the SDK hook that stamps `containerProps.role`" — but `useCompositeKeyboard` never actually stamped a role (neither container nor item). KBN-1b under-delivered against its documented contract. Fixed in `packages/sdk/src/a11y/`: a pure `compositeRoles(orientation, role?, itemRole?)` helper (in `composite-keyboard.ts`, unit-testable without a React render) defaults a flat list to `listbox`/`option` and a 2-D grid to `grid`/`gridcell`, with optional overrides for a `tablist`/`tab` etc.; `useCompositeKeyboard` now puts `containerRole` on `containerProps.role` and the item role on `getItemProps().role`. This makes every future adopter trip-free past `KBN-G-roles` (the role comes from the spread, never a hand-written string literal) and lets the 27-file `KNOWN_VIOLATION_PATHS` snapshot burn down as surfaces migrate. `CompositeContainerProps.role` / `CompositeItemProps.role` are now required (were absent). +5 tests (`compositeRoles` defaults + grid + overrides + independent container/item overrides).

**Settings sidebar adoption** (`packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/settings.tsx`). The nav was Tab-only — each `<button>` natively focusable, no arrow nav, active section marked with `aria-current="page"`. Now it's a composite listbox: `useCompositeKeyboard({ orientation: Vertical, count: SECTIONS.length, activeIndex: <derived from section>, onActiveIndexChange: selectIndex, onActivate: selectIndex, typeahead: label })`. `containerProps` spreads onto the `<nav>` (role=listbox, tabIndex 0, onKeyDown, aria-orientation=vertical, ref); `getItemProps(index)` onto each section button (role=option, roving tabindex, aria-selected, data-composite-index, stable id). Selection follows focus — ↑/↓ move the active section, Home/End jump to the ends, type-to-jump matches a section label, Enter/Space (re)commit. `aria-current` removed (the `--active` className still drives the visual; `aria-selected` is now the SR signal). Section state stays the single source of truth (active index is derived from it; every move writes back through `setSection`).

**Playwright (`KBN-P-arrow-composite`) — body written, not yet CI-verified.** `tests/perf/specs/kbn-arrow-composite.spec.ts` is rewritten from a skip-stub into a real spec against the Electron shell + a new `openSettings` lib helper (`Cmd/Ctrl+,`): assert the sidebar carries the hook-stamped `role="listbox"` + `aria-orientation="vertical"`, focus the listbox container, Home → index 0, ArrowDown advances the active index, `aria-selected` mirrors it, the active item is an `option`, `:focus-visible` is true after the keyboard arrow, ArrowUp returns. **It stays `test.skip` (◑)** — two blockers found while trying to run it: (1) the entire perf-spec suite is unloadable under the installed `@playwright/test`, which rejects the `async (_, testInfo)` fixture signature every existing KBN-P spec uses (parse error at `kbn-tab-walk.spec.ts:36`); this spec uses the accepted `async () =>` form, but it can't meaningfully run until the suite around it loads; (2) the dev sandbox can't boot the Electron shell to completion (the body hung to the test timeout at the launch/seed stage). The composite contract is verified at the unit/jsdom level instead; enable + confirm on the perf CI (real machine + a Playwright that accepts the signature). The `KBN-P-tab-walk` settings sub-test also stays skipped — it wants a settings-panel `useFocusTrap` (a separate KBN-S-settings sub-rung), not the sidebar composite.

## 2026-05-29 — 12.4 / KBN-S-settings closeout — overlay focus-trap + F6 region-nav (✅ fully closed)

The two pieces the sidebar-composite rung above deferred: the Settings overlay had **no focus trap** (unlike `<Popover>`, it's its own hand-rolled `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` div, so Tab leaked straight to the dashboard tiles behind it) and **no F6 region navigation** between its two regions. Both landed in `packages/shell/src/renderer/settings/settings.tsx` — the rung that makes `KBN-S-settings` fully ✅.

**Focus trap.** Replaced the bare `useEscapeStackEntry({ onEscape: onClose })` with `useFocusTrap({ enabled: true, onEscape: onClose, restoreFocusTo: opener, openerLabel: "settings" })`, spreading `containerProps` onto the `settings__panel` `motion.div`. The opener is captured at first render via a `useState` lazy initializer (mirrors the `<Popover>` precedent from KBN-S-popover — runs synchronously before the trap's effect moves focus, and the explicit `restoreFocusTo` keeps `KBN-G-focus-trap-without-restore` happy). Effect: Tab/Shift+Tab now wrap inside the panel, focus moves into the panel on open, and **focus restores to the opener** (the tray button / launcher hit that opened Settings) on close. `useFocusTrap` already shares KBN-2's module-scope escape stack, so Escape still drains LIFO through the same document-level handler — the swap is behaviour-preserving for Escape and behaviour-adding for Tab + restore.

**F6 region navigation.** `useRegionNavigation` wires `F6` / `Shift+F6` between two regions: `RegionId.SettingsSidebar` (ref → the active section `<button>`, so F6 lands on the live selection and arrows keep working from there) and `RegionId.SettingsMain` (ref → the `.settings__main` container, given `tabindex={-1}` + an `aria-label` so it's a valid focus + SR landing target). Active-region state is tracked so successive F6 presses toggle correctly. **First `useRegionNavigation` adopter in the shell** — the stable shell regions table in doc 61 named `settings-sidebar` / `settings-main` but nothing consumed them until now.

**i18n.** One new string `shell.settings.region.main` ("Settings content") with a translator `description` in the sibling `en.descriptions.json` (no grandfather entry — 12.3's CI gate is satisfied directly).

**Tests:** `settings.test.tsx` (new, jsdom — the env shell renderer tests opt into per-file, mirroring `popover.test.tsx`/`help.test.tsx`): focus-into-panel-on-open, opener-restore-on-unmount, Escape-closes-via-shared-stack, Tab-boundary-wrap (last→first), and the F6 sidebar→main→sidebar cycle. 5/5 green. Full workspace vitest 7580/7580; KBN-G guards (roles / tabindex / focus-trap-without-restore / raw-keys) all green (settings.tsx not flagged — trap carries `restoreFocusTo`, no hand-written roles, no raw `e.key`). Workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean on touched files. **Security surface:** none — renderer-only a11y wiring + one i18n string; no dependency, capability, or IPC touched.

## 2026-05-29 — 12.4 / KBN-S-launcher — combobox host mode + launcher adoption (✅)

The launcher is a **combobox**, not a focused-container listbox: the search `<input>` holds focus and drives a separate results listbox via `aria-activedescendant`. The shared `useCompositeKeyboard` hook hardcoded Space and Home/End/Page as list actions — which would eat the space bar and hijack the text cursor on a search input. So, like KBN-S-settings closing the role-stamping gap first, this rung **extends the SDK substrate** before adopting.

**Substrate: `CompositeHost.Combobox`.** New enum `packages/sdk/src/a11y/composite-host.ts` (`Listbox` default | `Combobox`), threaded through `useCompositeKeyboard` as `host?: CompositeHost`. In combobox mode: (1) Space is no longer an activate key (`e.key === "Enter" || (e.key === " " && host !== Combobox)`), so it falls through to the input; (2) the keymap drops to arrow-only (`VERTICAL_COMBOBOX_KEYMAP` / `HORIZONTAL_COMBOBOX_KEYMAP` — no Home/End/Page), so those keys move the input's text cursor instead of jumping the list. Enter still activates; ↑/↓ still navigate. Listbox mode is unchanged (zero behaviour delta for the settings sidebar / every other adopter). +4 SDK tests (arrows still drive the list · Space does not activate + not `defaultPrevented` · Enter still activates · Home/End fall through). Exported from the a11y barrel.

**Launcher adoption** (`packages/shell/src/renderer/launcher/launcher.tsx`). Replaced three `useShortcut` chord handlers (`shell/list.next` / `shell/list.previous` / `shell/popover.confirm`) + the manual `rowDomId` / `activeDescendant` plumbing with `useCompositeKeyboard({ orientation: Vertical, host: Combobox, useAriaActiveDescendant: true, disabled: <section-header indices>, wrap: false, onActivate: activate })`. Section headers are passed as `disabled` so Arrow nav skips them (the old `moveSelectionGrouped` header-skip, now in the substrate); `wrap: false` preserves the prior no-wrap behaviour. `containerProps.onKeyDown` + `aria-activedescendant` ride the `role="combobox"` input; `role={containerProps.role}` + `aria-orientation` ride the `.launcher__results` container — so the listbox role now **flows through the hook** and the launcher **drops its hand-written `role="listbox"` literal**, getting pruned from the `KBN-G-roles` `KNOWN_VIOLATION_PATHS` snapshot (27→26 files, 31→30 sites). Result rows spread `getItemProps(index)` for their `id` / `role="option"` / `tabindex -1` / `aria-selected` / `data-composite-index` (the index-based ids the input's activedescendant points at). `useEscapeStackEntry` → `useFocusTrap` (the launcher is `aria-modal`): focus traps on the input, the opener is captured on the open-transition (the component stays mounted with `open` toggling, so a mount-time capture would grab the wrong element — a render-phase ref-pair captures `document.activeElement` exactly when `open` flips true), and focus restores to it on close. **F6 region-nav is deliberately omitted** — a combobox keeps focus on the input by design and ↑/↓ already traverse the results, so a "jump to results" region has nothing to land on; noted in the rung.

**Tests:** +4 SDK `useCompositeKeyboard` combobox tests; +6 jsdom render tests (`launcher-keyboard.test.tsx`, new — mirrors `settings.test.tsx`): option-per-app + activedescendant points at the first app (header skipped) · ↑/↓ move + ArrowUp at the first app does not wrap · Space neither activates nor closes (and is not `defaultPrevented`) · Enter launches the active app + closes · focus-traps onto the input + Escape closes · listbox role flows through the hook. SDK a11y + shell launcher suites green; the four repo-wide KBN-G audits each pass in isolation (they only flake on the shared 5 s test-timeout when 4+ filesystem-walking audits run concurrently — documented pre-existing behaviour). Workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean on touched files. **Security surface:** none — an SDK keyboard-mode flag + a renderer adoption + tests; no dependency, capability, or IPC touched. The launcher's existing privileged `search.query` / `intents.dispatch` IPC paths are unchanged.

## 2026-05-29 — 12.4 / KBN-S-vault-switcher — popover vault list → composite listbox (✅)

The vault-switcher (`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V`) is a vertical list inside the shared `<Popover>` — the textbook focused-container listbox, the same shape as the settings sidebar. Migrated `packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard/vault-switcher-popover.tsx` off its three global `shell/list.next` / `shell/list.previous` / `shell/popover.confirm` `useShortcut` chords (and the manual `rowDomId` / `aria-activedescendant` plumbing) onto `useCompositeKeyboard({ orientation: Vertical, count, activeIndex: selected, onActiveIndexChange: setSelected, onActivate: activateIndex, typeahead: name })`. ↑/↓ move the cursor (selection follows focus), Home/End jump the ends, type-ahead matches a vault by name, Enter/Space activate; the hook owns roving `tabindex` + `aria-selected` + focusing the active row. Every row is selectable (activating the current vault is a no-op close), so no `disabled` set.

Rows spread `getItemProps(index)` for `id`/`role="option"`/roving `tabindex`/`aria-selected`/`data-composite-index`.

**Focus-on-open.** The old chords were global (`enabled: sorted.length > 0`, no scope), so arrows worked the instant the popover opened. The composite `onKeyDown` only fires when focus is in the list, and the shared `<Popover>` trap (KBN-S-popover) lands focus on its close button first — which would make the user Tab to the list before arrows worked. To keep parity, a local `listRef` is merged with the hook's container ref and a parent `useEffect` focuses the list on mount; because the child `<Popover>`'s trap effect runs before the parent's, focusing the list here wins. No new focus-trap call — the `<Popover>` already supplies trap + Escape.

## 2026-05-29 — 12.4 / KBN-S-bin — virtualized listbox + row-action key model (✅)

The Bin (`packages/shell/src/renderer/bin/bin.tsx`) had no keyboard model — its `@tanstack/react-virtual` list rendered `<li>` rows whose only keyboard reach was Tab-ing through each row's two action `IconButton`s (so a full bin was a wall of Tab stops). Adopted `useCompositeKeyboard` as a **virtualized composite listbox**.

**Listbox + activedescendant.** Because rows scroll in and out of the DOM, roving tabindex can't hold focus — so focus stays on the `<ul>` container and `aria-activedescendant` tracks the active row (`useAriaActiveDescendant: true`). ↑/↓/Home/End move the cursor; `onActiveIndexChange` both sets `selected` and calls `virtualizer.scrollToIndex` so the active row is rendered + visible. Each `<li>` spreads `getItemProps(row.index)` (`id` / `role="option"` / `tabindex -1` / `aria-selected` / `data-composite-index`).

**Row-action key model** (design call, user-approved). **Enter restores** the active row (`onActivate`). **Delete / Backspace purges** it — a bare context key per [doc 61 §chord-vs-context-key boundary](shell/61-keyboard-accessibility.md), handled by a thin `onListKeyDown` wrapper that intercepts Delete/Backspace then delegates everything else to the hook's `onKeyDown` (not registered in the chord registry). The per-row Restore/Purge buttons move behind the row's cursor at `tabindex -1` — mouse-clickable but not separate Tab stops, per the rung (matches the tasks-sidebar pattern). This needed a new optional `tabIndex` prop on the shared `IconButton` (passed through to the `<button>`; default unchanged).

**Focus trap.** `useEscapeStackEntry` → `useFocusTrap` (the Bin is a hand-rolled aria-modal, like Settings/Marketplace): focus trapped, opener captured at first render, restore-on-close; Escape rides the shared stack. The list is focused on open via a merged ref + parent effect (runs after the trap's, so the list wins over the header pin button). The purge `confirm()` modal-on-modal composes through the shared escape stack unchanged.

**Tests:** +5 jsdom render tests (`bin-keyboard.test.tsx`, new): listbox role + orientation + container `tabindex 0` + live `aria-activedescendant` · ↑/↓ move the activedescendant · Enter restores the active row (`bin.restore("i1")`) · Delete purges the cursor row after the mocked `confirm()` (`bin.purge("i2")`) · focus-traps into the panel + Escape closes. **Honest scope limit:** the `@tanstack/react-virtual` list renders **zero rows under jsdom** (no layout/height), so the per-row `role="option"` / `tabindex -1` rendering *and* scroll-into-view are **layout-dependent and verified by review + the perf-CI Playwright pass, not jsdom** — the same deferral the `KBN-P-*` specs already carry. Assertions therefore read the container-level `aria-activedescendant` (DOM-independent) and the Enter/Delete handler paths (which key off `selected` + `items`, not the DOM). `IconButton`'s own 7 tests stay green. **Security surface:** none — renderer keyboard adoption + an `IconButton` prop; no dependency, capability, or IPC touched.

## 2026-05-29 — 12.4 / composite-hook substrate (selectionAttribute + toolbar no-item-role) + window-strip toolbar (✅)

Two correctness-driven `useCompositeKeyboard` extensions, then the first toolbar adopter.

**`selectionAttribute`** (`packages/sdk/src/a11y/composite-selection.ts` — new enum `AriaSelected` default / `AriaChecked` / `None`). `getItemProps` stamped `aria-selected` unconditionally, which is correct for `listbox`/`tablist`/`grid` but invalid on a `radiogroup`'s radios (need `aria-checked`) and on a `toolbar`'s buttons (no selection state). The option picks the right attribute (or none). Backward-compatible — default `AriaSelected` leaves all five shipped adopters byte-identical.

**Toolbar item-role omission.** `compositeRoles` defaulted the item role to `option`, but an ARIA `toolbar`'s items are native controls (buttons) that keep their implicit role — stamping `role="button"` on a `<button>` is redundant *and* flagged by biome's `noRedundantRoles`. `compositeRoles` now returns `itemRole: undefined` for a `toolbar` (caller can still override), and `getItemProps` omits the `role` key when there's no item role. `CompositeItemProps.role` became optional; the existing toolbar-default test was updated.

**window-strip adoption** (`packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard/window-strip.tsx`). The running-windows strip carried the last shell `role="toolbar"` literal in `KNOWN_VIOLATION_PATHS` and had no roving keyboard model (each open-window button was its own Tab stop). Now a horizontal toolbar composite: `useCompositeKeyboard({ orientation: Horizontal, role: "toolbar", selectionAttribute: None })` — ←/→/Home/End move one roving cursor, Enter/Space focuses the cursor's window (`onFocus`), and a click syncs the cursor. `containerProps` spread on the `.window-strip` div drops the hand-written `role="toolbar"` → pruned from `KBN-G-roles` (24→23 files, 28→27 sites). The roving cursor is distinct from the `--focused` highlight (real OS window focus) — no `aria-selected`/`aria-checked` on the items. No focus trap (the strip is a persistent footer surface, not a modal).

**Tests:** +5 SDK tests (`selectionAttribute` defaults / `AriaChecked` / `None`; `compositeRoles` toolbar no-item-role + explicit override) and +3 jsdom render tests (`window-strip.test.tsx`, new): toolbar role + orientation + items have no role/selection state + roving tabindex · ←/→ move the cursor · Enter focuses the cursor's window. **All 18 KBN adopter test files (193 tests) stay green** — the optional-`role`/`aria-selected` type changes didn't regress settings/launcher/vault-switcher/marketplace/bin. `tsc` (packages + apps) + biome + `KBN-G-roles` guard clean. **Security surface:** none — SDK keyboard-mode flags + a renderer toolbar adoption + tests; no dependency, capability, or IPC touched. **KBN-S progress:** settings · launcher (+ `CompositeHost.Combobox`) · vault-switcher · marketplace · bin · window-strip (toolbar); `KNOWN_VIOLATION_PATHS` 27→23.

## 2026-05-29 — 12.4 / KBN-S-dashboard (grid) — Orientation.Spatial + macOS-Desktop icon-grid nav (◑ grid ✅, F6 ⚪)

The dashboard icon grid was the one named KBN-S surface that didn't fit any existing composite shape: its icons are **free-placed at arbitrary `{col, row}` cells** (12-col grid, unbounded rows, collision-resolved), so the dense row-major `Orientation.Grid` (`±columns` index math) would arrow to the wrong tile. Resolved per the user's steer — **do it the way macOS does**: spatial nearest-in-direction.

**Pure `spatialGridStep`** (`packages/sdk/src/a11y/spatial-grid.ts` — new, with `SpatialDirection` enum). Given the cells, the active index, and a direction, it returns the nearest item *in that direction*: among items strictly beyond the active one along the pressed axis, minimise `primaryDistance + perpendicularDistance × 3` (the ×3 "beam" weight makes a well-aligned item beat a nearer-but-skewed one), deterministic index tie-break, **no wrap** at an edge (the cursor sits — matches the macOS Desktop). Fully unit-tested (+6: each direction, edge no-wrap, alignment-beats-skew, sparse-gap nearest, empty/out-of-range no-op, tie-break).

**Reducer + hook.** New `Orientation.Spatial`. The composite reducer's directional handlers (`moveNext`/`movePrevious`/`moveRow`) branch to a `moveSpatial` helper that calls `spatialGridStep` over `ctx.cells` (cells flow through `ctx`, like `disabled`, and via a ref in the hook so an icon reflow doesn't recreate the keydown handler); a first move from "no selection" lands on index 0. The hook gained a `cells` option + a `SPATIAL_KEYMAP` (4 arrows → directional, Home/End → first/last, no Page). All the existing roving-tabindex / focus / Enter / `getItemProps` machinery is reused unchanged. `compositeRoles` now also omits the item role for a `group` container (not just `toolbar`) — the dashboard's icon buttons are native controls. +2 hook tests (spatial arrow moves + edge no-wrap).

**Dashboard adoption** (`packages/shell/src/renderer/dashboard/icons-layer.tsx`). The `.dashboard-icons` surface is now a labelled `role="group"` spatial composite: one Tab stop into the grid, ←↑↓→ move the roving cursor to the nearest icon (using each icon's resolved placement cell), Enter/Space activates (routes to the existing `onActivate`), a click syncs the cursor. The hook's container ref is merged with the existing `surfaceRef` (ResizeObserver). `SelectionAttribute.None` — the roving focus is the cursor; no `aria-selected` on the buttons. One new i18n string (`shell.dashboard.iconGrid`) + description.

**Tests:** +6 SDK (`spatial-grid.test.ts`) + 2 hook + 3 jsdom render (`icons-layer-keyboard.test.tsx`, new): labelled group + single Tab stop + native buttons (no item role / no selection state) · spatial arrows move the cursor (Right/Down/Left + edge no-wrap) · Enter activates the cursor's icon. **Fully jsdom-verified** — unlike the bin, the icons layer is non-virtualized *and* the nav keys off `{col,row}` placements, not pixel layout, so jsdom (no layout engine) still exercises the real path; a `ResizeObserver` stub covers the surface's observer. All 20 KBN adopter test files (204 tests) green — `Orientation.Spatial` + the `group` item-role change didn't regress the 6 prior adopters. `tsc` (packages + apps) + biome + `KBN-G-roles` guard clean (dashboard roles flow through the hook — no flagged literal, `KNOWN_VIOLATION_PATHS` unchanged at 23). **Follow-up:** F6/Shift+F6 region nav between `dashboard-grid` / `vault-switcher` / `system-tray` (a `useRegionNavigation` wiring in `dashboard.tsx`, same pattern as Settings/Marketplace). **Security surface:** none — an SDK orientation + a renderer adoption + one i18n string; no dependency, capability, or IPC touched.

### perf-suite unblock (`fix(perf)`, same day)

While verifying via the real-shell harness ("test it"), found the **entire Playwright perf suite was unloadable**: the installed `@playwright/test` rejects the `async (_, testInfo) =>` signature every spec used (`--list` → "Total: 0 tests in 0 files"), which is the documented blocker behind every skipped `KBN-P-*` check. Fixed across all 11 specs — dropped the `testInfo` param (`async () =>`) and switched `testInfo.setTimeout(N)` → `test.setTimeout(N)` (callable in-body; `testInfo` was only ever used for that). ## 2026-05-29 — 13.8a — app-lock PIN verifier + brute-force policy (substrate)

First substrate slice of App-lock (Stage 13.8; OQ-184 RESOLVED). Two security-design decisions taken with the user before writing key-lifecycle crypto: (a) the PIN verifier lives in a **keystore secret** (`brainstorm.<vaultId>.app-lock-pin`), not the master-key-encrypted credential store — it must be readable while the master key is zeroed, since the verify *gates getting the key back*; (b) the **passphrase backend soft-locks** (key stays resident, PIN gate only, instant unlock — it has no cheap PIN-gated re-read), while the **keyring backend hard-locks** (zero key → PIN-gated re-read from the keystore). Both surfaced honestly in the eventual Settings copy.

**`credentials/app-lock-pin.ts`** (crypto stays under `main/credentials/` per the routing rule): `setAppLockPin` / `verifyAppLockPin` / `hasAppLockPin` / `clearAppLockPin`. The PIN is a **gate, never a KDF for the master key** (OQ-184) — a 4–6 digit PIN is ~13–20 bits, so the verifier only proves "right PIN entered" via a **light-tier Argon2id** hash (19 MiB / t=2 / p=1 — a recognized OWASP profile, ~tens of ms; the keystore-held secret remains the master key's real protection). Stored as a JSON blob `{algo,m,t,p,saltB64,hashB64}` (fresh 16-byte salt each set; re-derives with the *stored* params so an older blob survives a profile bump). Verify is constant-time over the derived hash; `verify`/`has` never throw on absent/malformed blobs. New `KeystoreAccount` variant `"app-lock-pin"`.

**`vault/app-lock-policy.ts`** (pure, no crypto/IO — shared by the lock state machine + the lock-screen surface): `appLockCooldownMs(failed)` (first two failures free, then 5s/15s/30s/60s, clamped) + `isAppLockCapped(failed)` / `APP_LOCK_ATTEMPT_CAP = 7` (past the cap the PIN is disabled; only full-passphrase re-auth unlocks, per OQ-184's brute-force policy).

**Tests:** +7 (`app-lock-pin.test.ts`: correct/wrong/empty PIN, presence, re-set fresh-salt replacement, clear, malformed-blob → false, per-vault scoping) + 4 (`app-lock-policy.test.ts`: cooldown ladder, clamp, negative, cap). Uses a Map-backed fake `KeystoreBackend` + the real Argon2id native binding. `typecheck:packages` + biome clean. **Next (13.8b):** `lock()` / `unlock(pin)` on the vault session — hard-lock (keyring: zero key + tear down `dataStores`/ydoc, PIN-gated re-read via `backend.getSecret(vaultId,"master")` + rebuild) vs soft-lock (passphrase: key resident, PIN gate only), wiring the cooldown/cap policy. **(13.8c):** the `app:lock-changed` broadcast + "first valid PIN → single shell-side re-open → broadcast". **Surface (later, real-shell):** Settings → Security PIN UI, the lock overlay (`useFocusTrap` from day one — KBN-S-lock-screen), idle/sleep + `vault.lock` triggers. **Security surface:** new keystore account + Argon2id verifier; no new IPC yet, no new dependency. No master-key lifecycle change in this slice (verifier only).

## 2026-05-29 — 13.8b — vault-session lock/unlock state machine (substrate)

The `lock()` / `unlock(pin)` half of App-lock, on the vault-session module (`vault/session.ts`). **Key design win — reuse, not new key-zeroing code:** hard-lock = the existing, fully-tested `closeActiveVaultSession()` (zeros every key buffer via `dispose()`, sets `active = null`), and unlock = the existing, fully-tested `VaultSession.open()` (re-reads the master/identity/device secrets from the keystore + reconstructs the stores). So the most dangerous part — zeroing + reloading key material — adds **zero new crypto code**, just orchestration.

- `appLockModeForBackend(name)` → `Soft` for `passphrase`, `Hard` otherwise (keyring/insecure). `AppLockMode` enum.
- `lockActiveVault(openOptions)` — captures `{vaultId, vaultPath, mode, openOptions}` in a module-level `lockedVault`; **hard** → `closeActiveVaultSession()` (the broker then fails closed on every IPC dispatch, `active === null`); **soft** → `session.markLocked()` (key stays resident behind the overlay + PIN gate). Idempotent; returns `null` when there's no active session.
- `unlockActiveVault(pin)` — verifies via `verifyAppLockPin` (soft reuses the live `session.backend`; hard re-picks the keystore since the session is disposed). Wrong PIN → `failedAttempts++` + reports the next `appLockCooldownMs`; past `APP_LOCK_ATTEMPT_CAP` → `reason: "capped"` and the PIN is refused outright (full-passphrase re-auth is the only escape — a later surface concern). Success → **hard** re-opens via `VaultSession.open` + `setActiveVaultSession`; **soft** clears the flag. Clears `lockedVault`.
- `isVaultLocked()` + `VaultSession.isLocked()` (soft flag) for the broadcast/broker. `resetAppLockStateForTests()`.

**Tests:** +5 (`app-lock.test.ts`, real vault sessions in temp dirs): backend→mode mapping; **hard-lock disposes then unlock(pin) re-opens** (same identity fingerprint, `signPayload` works again — proves the round-trip through dispose+open); attempt cap (correct PIN refused while capped); **soft-lock keeps the same session instance resident**, unlock clears the flag; not-locked report. All 22 vault + integration suites (161 tests) stay green — session.ts changes regress nothing. `tc:packages` + biome clean. **Security surface:** new lock/unlock orchestration over existing tested key-lifecycle paths (no new zeroing/reload code); the only new attack surface is the PIN-verify gate, already covered in 13.8a. No new IPC yet (13.8c) — `app:lock-changed` broadcast + renderer-triggered lock/unlock + broker reject-while-locked come next. **Next (13.8c):** the `app:lock-changed` IPC broadcast + privileged `vault:lock`/`vault:unlock` channels + "first valid PIN → single re-open → broadcast" wiring; then the surface (Settings PIN UI, lock overlay).

## 2026-05-29 — 13.8c — app-lock IPC layer (handlers + broadcast + broker reject-while-locked)

Wires the 13.8b lock/unlock state machine to the renderer. `ipc/vault-lock-handlers.ts` — privileged `ipcMain.handle` for `vault:lock` / `vault:unlock` (pin) / `vault:lock-status`, **never the broker** (a sandboxed app must not lock/unlock the vault), plus an `app:lock-changed` push to **every** window so all overlays show/tear-down together ("unlock one unlocks all", OQ-184). A testable `makeVaultLockHandlers(broadcast)` factory keeps the logic pure of `electron`; `registerVaultLockHandlers()` is called from the bootstrap.

**Broker reject-while-locked.** A hard-locked vault already has `active === null`, so the broker fails closed automatically. A *soft*-locked session (passphrase backend, key resident) stays `active`, so `BrokerContext` now denies when `session.isLocked()` — in both `getLedger` and the sync `syncLedger`. **A test caught a real bug here:** the first cut *evicted* the ledger cache on lock, but a soft-unlock only flips the flag (no re-warm), so apps couldn't use IPC after unlocking. Fixed: while locked, `syncLedger` returns `null` **without clearing the cache** (same session) — only a genuine no-session evicts — so the warm ledger survives the soft lock→unlock cycle.

**Shared wire types.** New `shared/app-lock-wire-types.ts` (`UnlockReason` / `UnlockResult` / `LockChangedPayload`) — renderer-safe (no `electron`), the single source for `session.ts` (re-exports), the handlers, and the **preload bridge** (`window.brainstorm.vaults.lock()` / `unlock(pin)` / `lockStatus()` / `onLockChanged(cb)`), per the `sync-status-types` precedent.

**Tests:** +3 handler (`vault-lock-handlers.test.ts`, mocked `electron` + real vault sessions + spy broadcast: no-op lock doesn't broadcast; lock→`true` then correct-PIN unlock→`false`; wrong PIN → no unlock broadcast; non-string PIN coerced→rejected) + 1 broker (`checkCapability` true→**false while soft-locked**→true after unlock). The handler test sets `BRAINSTORM_DEV_INSECURE_CREDENTIALS=1` so the hard-unlock keystore re-pick selects the insecure backend (mirrors real dev — `lockActiveVault()` carries no open-options, correct for keyring-default / env-insecure). All 47 vault+runtime+ipc+credentials suites (448 tests) green. `tc:packages` + biome clean. **Security surface:** new privileged `vault:*` ipcMain channels (dashboard-only, never broker) + the broker's locked-deny; the lock/unlock crypto is 13.8a/b. **Substrate done (13.8a+b+c).** **Remaining (surface, real-shell):** Settings → Security PIN set/change/clear UI · the lock-screen overlay (`useFocusTrap` from day one = KBN-S-lock-screen) · idle/sleep + `vault.lock` shortcut triggers · the `app:lock-changed` renderer wiring (overlay show/hide).

## 2026-05-29 — 13.8 surface (slice 1): app-lock screen overlay (KBN-S-lock-screen)

First surface slice on top of the 13.8 substrate (a+b+c, landed earlier today). New `renderer/lock-screen.tsx` `<LockScreenHost>` — a shell-level overlay raised whenever the active vault is locked, mounted in `dashboard.tsx` beside the other prompt hosts (renders `null` while unlocked). It mirrors lock state from the `vault:*` bridge I built in 13.8c (`lockStatus()` on mount + the `app:lock-changed` push), relays the typed PIN to `vaults.unlock(pin)`, and reflects the returned `UnlockResult`:
- **wrong-pin** → inline error + the escalating cooldown. The renderer never re-derives the ladder — the main-side policy hands back `cooldownMs`, which drives a 1s countdown that disables the field until it elapses.
- **capped** → PIN entry is replaced by the honest passphrase escape: a "Close vault" button (`vaults.close()`) that returns to the vault picker, where reopening performs the real keystore unwrap (the only thing that can recover a capped lock; the PIN is a gate, never a KDF).
- **ok** → the `app:lock-changed` (locked=false) broadcast clears the host.

**KBN-S-lock-screen contract:** `useFocusTrap({ enabled: locked, initialFocus: FirstFocusable })` with **no `onEscape`** — the shared Escape handler `preventDefault`s + invokes a no-op top-of-stack entry, so Escape cannot dismiss the lock (verified against `escape-stack.ts`: `applyEscape` calls `onEscape()` and does not pop). PIN field is the initial focus; Enter submits via native form submit (no raw `e.key`, no composite role — both repo guards stay green; the only red guard sites are the parallel Database WIP's `source-picker.ts`, untouched here). The overlay never reads the master key or PIN verifier — pure relay.

Renderer-only, no `main/` import (the policy values arrive on the wire via `UnlockResult.cooldownMs`/`reason`). +9 i18n strings with translator descriptions (12.3 gate green) + bespoke full-viewport CSS (design-system tokens only; focus ring on the border position per [[feedback_focus_outline_replaces_border]]). +6 jsdom tests (unlocked→null · locked→PIN · relays PIN · clears on broadcast · wrong-pin cooldown disables+re-enables on tick · capped→Close-vault calls `vaults.close`). `tc:packages` + biome clean.

**Remaining 13.8 surface (next slices, real-shell):** Settings → Security PIN set/change/clear UI; idle/sleep auto-lock + `vault.lock` action/menu-item triggers; covering **app windows** too (each app renderer or a shell-raised cover on the broadcast — the dashboard overlay only masks the dashboard); and the edge case where a popover's focus-trap is already top-of-stack when an idle-lock fires (the lock should force itself to the top).

## 2026-05-29 — 13.8 surface: lock is a blank route · app windows masked · prod DevTools off

Follow-up on review feedback that the lock screen was only an overlay (deletable in the inspector, with content rendered behind it) and didn't cover open app windows. Hardened the lock so the renderer overlay isn't load-bearing:

- **Lock screen is now a full-page route, not an overlay.** Split `lock-screen.tsx` into `useVaultLock()` (subscribes the `vault:*` bridge) + a presentational `<LockScreen>`. The dashboard calls `useVaultLock()` and, when locked, **early-returns `<LockScreen>` only** — the entire dashboard content tree is not rendered. So deleting the lock-screen node in the inspector reveals *nothing* (there's nothing behind it), not the dashboard. Checked before the `!current` branch so a keyring hard-lock (which disposes the session) doesn't fall through to the vault picker.
- **App windows are masked main-side.** App windows are sandboxed renderers with no `vaults.*` bridge, so they can't draw the lock screen themselves. Added an `onLockChange(locked)` callback to `makeVaultLockHandlers`/`registerVaultLockHandlers`; `index.ts` wires it to `hide()` every `launchSetup…allWindows()` BrowserWindow while locked and `show()` them on unlock (+ focuses the dashboard so the lock route is front). Only the dashboard (lock route) stays visible. +2 handler tests (fires true→lock / false→successful-unlock, not on wrong-pin or no-op lock).
- **DevTools disabled in production.** The dashboard window had `devTools: true` ungated; now `devTools: isDev` (matching the app-window factory's `!app.isPackaged`), so a shipped build offers no inspector to defeat the lock or read renderer state.

Honest layering, restated: the renderer is **not** the security boundary — the broker fail-closes all vault IPC while locked and a keyring hard-lock zeroes the master key, so locked-vault *data* is unreachable regardless of renderer tampering.
