## 2026-05-29 — Net-2a (part 1): readable-extraction substrate — sanitize + isolate

First two of the three pure extraction-substrate modules under `packages/shell/src/main/network/readable/` (no IPC, no worker, no renderer surface — mergeable alone):

- **`sanitize-html.ts`** — the **security boundary**. `sanitizeReadableHtml(html) → string` over the `sanitize-html` lib, configured as a strict **allowlist** (exactly the 1:1 importable tag set: `h1–h6 p ul ol li blockquote pre code em strong br hr a img table/thead/tbody/tr/th/td`; attrs `a[href,title]`, `img[src,alt,title,width,height]`, `code/pre[class]`, `table[summary]`; schemes `http(s)/mailto/brainstorm` + relative/anchor). Drops `<script>/<style>/<iframe>/<object>` (tag **and** content), void `<embed>/<base>`, every `style`/`on*`/off-allowlist attribute, and `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:`/`file:`/protocol-relative URLs. +16 tests incl. adversarial (script-content drop, on* strip, style/CSS vector, scheme smuggling incl. entity-encoded `&#106;avascript:`, protocol-relative, unknown-container flatten). The full adversarial sweep is the later Net-2e `/pentester` pass.
- **`extract-html.ts`** — `extractReadable(html, baseUrl) → ReadableResult | null` via **Mozilla Readability** over a **`linkedom`** DOM (no script engine). Strips nav/aside/footer chrome → article column; returns `null` for no-article pages (JS shells, login walls). Captures `{ title, byline, siteName, excerpt, lang, publishedAt }` + the unsanitized article HTML + `textContent` + `length`. A `<base href>` is injected so Readability absolutises relative URLs against the page. +5 tests (isolation, metadata, empty→null, JS-shell→null, relative→absolute).

New runtime deps in `packages/shell` (worker-only — **zero** dashboard/app bundle impact): `@mozilla/readability@0.6.0`, `linkedom@0.18.12`, `sanitize-html@2.17.4` (+ `@types/sanitize-html` dev). 21 tests green; `tc:packages` clean (readable module); biome clean. **Next:** `html-to-blocks.ts` (the editor-coupled HTML→Lexical-`SerializedBlock` conversion — done carefully against the editor's exact node shapes + a round-trip test) closes Net-2a; then Net-2b (worker) → Net-2c (IPC+caps) → Net-2d (golden corpus) → Net-2e (pentest).

## 2026-05-29 — Net-2a COMPLETE: html-to-blocks closes the extraction substrate

Third + final substrate module: **`html-to-blocks.ts`** — `htmlToSerializedBlocks(html) → SerializedBlock[]`. Walks the sanitised article DOM (`linkedom`, no JS) and **hand-emits the editor's clipboard serialized-node shape** (block-clipboard.ts) so a captured page drops into a Bookmark's universal body with zero transform. Does NOT import `@brainstorm/editor` (would pull `@lexical/html`); emits JSON literally. Mapping: `h1–h6`→heading(tag) · `p`→paragraph · inline `strong/b`→bold, `em/i`→italic, `code`→code (text-format bitmask) · `a`→link(url,title) · `ul/ol/li`→list(listType)+listitem(value) · `pre>code`→code(language from `language-*`) · `blockquote`→quote · `img`→paragraph-wrapped image node (`SerializedImageNode`) · `br`→linebreak · unmapped container → flatten (nested blocks survive, bare inline → paragraph). +10 tests.

**Validity is pinned by a round-trip through the real editor:** the test parses the hand-built `SerializedBlock[]` into a `createBrainstormHeadlessEditor` (the exact Brainstorm node set, via the vitest alias), re-exports, and asserts the block-type sequence survives — so every emitted shape is provably importable by Lexical (no latent shape bug). (Fixed a linkedom gotcha en route: `parseHTML` only populates `document.body` with the full `<html>` scaffold, not a bare `<body>`.)

**Net-2a done — 31 tests** (sanitize 16 · extract 5 · blocks 10); `tc:packages` + biome clean. The substrate is the reusable core all three feeders share. **Next:** Net-2b (extraction utility worker) → Net-2c (`network.readable` IPC + caps + SDK proxy) → Net-2d (golden corpus) → Net-2e (`/pentester`).

## 2026-05-29 — Net-2b: extraction utility worker

Moves the CPU-heavy Net-2a parse off the broker main loop (OQ-RX-3), mirroring the storage/ydoc worker layout:

- **`workers/extraction/index.ts`** — envelope protocol over `process.parentPort` (`handleExtractionEnvelope` + the parentPort-gated listener so Vitest tests the handler in-process). `extract({html, baseUrl})` composes the three Net-2a modules → `{ meta, blocks, textContent }` (or `blocks: null` on no-article). The deps (readability/linkedom/sanitize-html) bundle **into the worker only** — never the dashboard/app bundle. +9 tests (extract real article · no-article→null · `<script>` never reaches blocks · invalid args coerce · ping · wrong-service / unknown-method / malformed-envelope errors · parentPort unwrap).
- **`main/extraction/extraction-worker-handle.ts`** — `createExtractionWorkerHandle(bridge)` wraps `WorkerBridge` with a **single-in-flight, bounded FIFO queue** (cap 8; over-cap evicts the oldest *queued* job with `ExtractionQueueFullError`, never the in-flight). Per-call timeout passes through. +4 tests (serialization · ok/error mapping · backlog eviction · timeout passthrough).
- **Wiring** — `main/workers.ts` widens the worker-name union to include `extraction`, spawns it, and exposes the queue handle as `WorkersHandle.extraction` (NOT a broker service — it's internal, called by the `network.readable` service at Net-2c); `electron.vite.config.ts` adds `workers/extraction` to the build matrix (mirrors storage/ydoc). Real-shell-verified at build; orchestration unit-tested.

+13 tests; `tc:packages` + biome clean. **Next:** Net-2c — `services.network.readable` IPC + `network.readable`(.private) caps + SDK proxy (reuses `executeNetworkFetch` for the fetch leg → forwards to `workers.extraction.extract`).

## 2026-05-29 — Net-2c: `network.readable` IPC + caps + SDK proxy

Wires the Net-2b worker to the network broker + the app-facing SDK:
- **SDK contract** (`sdk-types`): new `SerializedBlock` (structural, editor-decoupled) + `NetworkReadableResult { preview: LinkPreview; blocks: SerializedBlock[] | null }`; `NetworkService.readable(input)`.
- **SDK proxy** (`sdk/runtime.ts`): `network.readable` declares `network.readable` (+ `network.readable.private` when `allowPrivate`), parallel to `fetch`'s cap pattern. +2 tests.
- **Handler** (`network-service-handler.ts`): `NETWORK_READABLE_CAP` + `NETWORK_READABLE_PRIVATE_CAP`; `handleReadable` reuses `executeNetworkFetch` for the fetch leg (every Net-1 invariant — SSRF / size / time / audit / proxy — carries through unchanged), with the larger doc-58 budgets (3 MB / 8 s), same per-vault privacy gate as previews, then `extractLinkPreview` for the OG record + forwards the fetched HTML to the injected extraction worker for `blocks`. No worker wired → `blocks: null` (graceful, metadata-only). +5 tests (preview+blocks · blocks-null fallback · privacy-gate blocks before fetch · arg validation · extractor-error propagation).
- **Wiring** (`index.ts`): the production handler injects `extractReadable: (input) => workers.extraction.extract(input)` (the Net-2b queue handle).

Caps are free-form strings checked against grants — no registry to update. The readable egress is its own cap, so an app wanting only a card asks for `network.preview` and never gets bodies. +7 tests; `tc` clean (mine) + biome clean. **Next:** Net-2d (fixture-corpus golden tests) → Net-2e (`/pentester`).

## 2026-05-29 — Net-2d: fixture-corpus golden tests

A regression net for the extraction substrate: `extract-corpus.test.ts` runs the full composed pipeline (extract → sanitize → html-to-blocks) over a corpus of representative pages and compares `{ meta, blocks }` against committed `.golden.json` baselines. Fixtures are in-repo snapshots (never re-fetched); each `.url` sidecar records provenance. An orphan-guard pins that every `.html` has a `.url` + `.golden.json` and vice-versa. Goldens regenerate via `BRAINSTORM_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`.

**Documented limitation (golden-captured, OQ-RX-6 "degrade predictably"):** code-block **language inference is `null` through the static feeder** — Mozilla Readability strips `class` attributes from its output, so the `language-*` hint is gone before `html-to-blocks` sees it. The inference logic itself works when the class survives (proven by the Net-2a `html-to-blocks` test); the live-DOM feeder (Net-3), which hands the rendered DOM with classes intact, can preserve it. Not a blocker — code blocks are still captured, just without a language tag on this path.

`tc` clean (mine — the 2 unrelated `LinkPreview`-literal errors are the parallel favicon WIP adding a `favicon` field) + biome clean. **Next:** Net-2e — adversarial `/pentester` pass over the sanitizer (closes the Net-2 row).

## 2026-05-29 — Net-2e: adversarial /pentester pass — CLOSES Net-2

Ran the `/pentester` red-team over the Net-2 extraction surface (the only path that processes untrusted fetched web HTML). Findings in `docs/_review/2026-05-29-net-2-pentest.md`.

**No must-fix.** The load-bearing mitigation is that the output is **block JSON, not DOM** — `html-to-blocks` only emits known node types, so even a sanitizer miss can't become executable. Allowlist-bypass (SVG-nesting, namespaced attrs, entity-encoding, data:, meta-refresh, quoting confusion), worker-crash, ReDoS, and prototype-pollution paths all traced closed.

Closed one **defense-in-depth** finding: `htmlToSerializedBlocks` now re-checks `href`/`src` schemes against the same allowlist (`http(s)`/`mailto`/`brainstorm` + relative/anchor) before emitting a link/image — unreachable in-pipeline (the sanitizer strips dangerous schemes first), but keeps the module safe if ever called out-of-order. +3 regression tests. Documented one DoS-hardening follow-up (no hard in-worker time cap → a pathological page can keep the single-in-flight worker busy; bridge timeout rejects the caller; needs kill-and-respawn — isolated process, 3 MB-capped, not beta-blocking).

Expanded the sanitizer's adversarial corpus to a dedicated Net-2e block (26 sanitizer tests total), each vector asserting both neutralisation AND no-over-stripping.

**Net-2 COMPLETE** (2a substrate · 2b worker · 2c IPC+caps+SDK · 2d golden corpus · 2e pentest) — ~90 tests across the readable surface. Unblocks **Bookmarks 9.18.5** (capture → `Bookmark/v1` body via the Notes importer) and **9.18.6** (OG → properties). The live-DOM feeder (Net-3) and clipper (Clip-1) are additive later channels onto this same core.

## 2026-05-29 — Encrypted asset subsystem — Part A (offline favicon/cover for Bookmarks)

User directive while diagnosing "the Wikipedia bookmark didn't parse": **offline-first** (no remote files painted in the renderer), **encrypted at rest**, and design for the coming **sync + collaboration/sharing** (self-hosted or our endpoints). Diagnosis confirmed two causes — a stale shell (the scrape wasn't deployed) AND that favicon/cover were remote URLs blocked by the app `img-src` CSP (and an IP-leak vector). The fix is a real binary-asset subsystem; the bookmark favicon/cover is its first consumer. Designed via the architect agent (per-asset random DEK, blind-relay equality-leak analysis), then built Part A:

- **A1 — encrypted asset store** (`packages/shell/src/main/assets/asset-store.ts` + `asset-dek-store.ts`): `entities.db` **v3** migration adds `assets` / `asset_deks` / `asset_refs`. `writeAsset` mints a fresh per-asset DEK, seals the blob via new `sealBytes`/`openBytes` raw-binary helpers in `credentials/crypto.ts` (AAD `brainstorm/asset-blob/v1:<id>`), wraps the DEK under the master key (`AssetDekStore`, AAD `brainstorm/asset-dek/v1:<id>` — distinct domain from entity DEKs), and writes `<vault>/data/assets/<prefix>/<id>.enc`. **Per-asset random keys, not convergent** (OQ-236) — identical favicons → distinct ciphertext, no plaintext-equality leak to the blind relay. `content_hash` is a local-only dedupe hint; on-disk name is the random id. `readAsset` decrypts (DEK zeroed in `finally`); `deleteAsset` cascades + unlinks; `markBound`/`reapOrphans` are the (Part-B) bind/GC primitives. Wired into `VaultSession.assetStore()` (master key by reference, cleared on dispose). 15 store + 6 DEK + 5 schema tests; FK cascades verified.
- **A2 — `brainstorm://asset/<id>` protocol** (`assets/serve-asset.ts` + a branch in `index.ts`): UUID-validate → decrypt-and-serve → fail-closed (404 on tampered/wrong-key/unknown). `no-store` cache (decrypted vault bytes). Access posture = active-session gate, matching the existing `cover`/`app-file` handlers; tighter owner-graph enforcement is OQ-237. 4 tests.
- **A3 — preview stores favicon/cover** (`network-service-handler.ts`): `handlePreview` sub-fetches the favicon + OG cover through the same `executeNetworkFetch` (SSRF/privacy/size guards; per-host privacy re-check; non-image responses skipped; favicon 512 KiB / cover 5 MB caps), stores them via an injected `storeImageAsset`, and returns `faviconAssetUrl`/`coverAssetUrl` on the `LinkPreview` (added to both the `preview.ts` and `sdk-types` shapes). Graceful: any image failure leaves the preview's remote URLs intact. 5 handler tests + a full preview→encrypt→serve **integration test**.
- **A4 — Bookmarks consumes asset URLs** (`apps/bookmarks/src/app.ts`): `enrichBookmarkMetadata` stores ONLY `preview.faviconAssetUrl`/`coverAssetUrl` (never the remote URLs), painted under the existing `brainstorm:` CSP. `Bookmark.faviconUrl`/`coverImageUrl` now hold `brainstorm://asset/<id>`. No new bookmarks capability (the existing `network.preview` covers the round-trip; the protocol serves to any session).
- **Verify:** typecheck (packages + apps) clean, biome clean, 560 asset+network+bookmarks tests green, bookmarks app builds. OQ-236..240 filed. **Part B** (sync envelope + member-wrap share fan-out + bind/orphan-GC + range-streaming) and the **legacy-blob-encryption** iteration (OQ-240) are follow-ons.

## 2026-05-29 — Net-1 fix: two latent bugs blocked ALL `network.preview` parsing

A **real-shell probe** (Playwright: open Bookmarks → invoke `network.preview` for a live Wikipedia URL → inspect the result) surfaced why the user's bookmark "didn't parse" — and it was NOT the asset work. `network.preview` had been broken in production since Net-1; the unit tests use a stub `fetchImpl`, so the real Electron `net.fetch` path was never exercised until a real app first called preview. Two stacked bugs:

1. **`Host` header → `net::ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT`.** `executeNetworkFetch` sets `forwardHeaders.Host = hostname` (intended for an IP-pinned fetchImpl), and `productionFetchImpl` passed it straight to `net.fetch`. `Host` is a *forbidden* header in Chromium's Fetch — `net.fetch` rejects the whole request. Fix: new exported pure `sanitizeFetchHeaders()` strips the forbidden set (`host`/`connection`/`content-length`/`transfer-encoding`/`keep-alive`/`upgrade`/`proxy-connection`) at the `net.fetch` boundary (`net.fetch` derives them from the URL itself).
2. **Large pages never preview.** `PREVIEW_SIZE_CAP_BYTES` is 64 KiB but `executeNetworkFetch` *rejects* (`SizeCap`) when the body exceeds the cap — and a Wikipedia page is ~1 MB, so every large page (Wikipedia, news) failed. Fix: new `truncateOnSizeCap` request flag — when set (preview only), the drain loop keeps exactly `sizeCapBytes` and returns normally instead of throwing. The `<head>` (OG/JSON-LD) is in the leading bytes, so the preview still extracts. `fetch`/`readable` keep the byte-exact reject behaviour.

**Verified end-to-end in the real shell:** after both fixes, `network.preview` for the Wikipedia URL returns `title`/`favicon`/`image` + `faviconAssetUrl`/`coverAssetUrl` (`brainstorm://asset/…`), and an `<img>` painting the favicon asset URL loads (`naturalWidth > 0`) — the full broker → encrypt → `brainstorm://asset` serve → render chain works. (`siteName` falls back to the hostname on very large pages where the JSON-LD publisher sits past 64 KiB — acceptable; og:title/og:image are in `<head>`.) Regression tests: `sanitizeFetchHeaders` (forbidden-header strip) + truncate-on-cap (`network-service.test.ts`); the existing "rejects >64 KiB" preview test flipped to assert truncation + extraction. 441 network tests green. The real-network probe was one-off (deleted — flaky/offline-hostile for CI; the unit + integration tests are the durable coverage).

## 2026-05-30 — KBN-S-cap-prompt: deny-by-default keyboard contract for the capability-grant modal

The one clean, unblocked, release-blocking item left on the user's Phase-1 list (the rest are gated on the 9.3.5 remodel / Stage-9.3 swap / Phase 2 / real-shell). The capability-grant modal already inherited the shared `<Popover>` focus trap + opener-restore (KBN-S-popover), so the trap itself wasn't the gap — the gaps were **security**:

1. **Removed the global `shell/popover.confirm` (Enter-grants) shortcut.** While the prompt was open, a stray `Enter` *anywhere* called `respond(true)` — silently granting a capability regardless of focus. Removed; `Enter` now only activates the focused control (native button). After the fix a stray Enter on the default focus *denies*.
2. **Initial focus now lands on the safe Deny action**, not the header ✕ or the destructive Allow, so the keyboard/screen-reader default fails safe. Implemented via a new reusable **`<Popover initialFocusRef>`** prop, backed by extending `useFocusTrap`'s `explicitInitialFocus` to also accept a `RefObject<HTMLElement | null>` resolved *inside the mount effect* (after React attaches refs — avoids the first-render-`null` timing trap). `InitialFocusMode.Explicit` is selected automatically when `initialFocusRef` is set; default behaviour (first-focusable) is unchanged for every other popover.

Escape / backdrop / close all deny (shared `onClose`); granting requires deliberately focusing + activating Allow. The `initialFocusRef` lever is the "copy two" home for every destructive-confirm dialog (Bin purge, vault delete) that wants to land on its safe default — extracted into the shared primitive, not hand-rolled.

**Files:** `packages/sdk/src/a11y/use-focus-trap.ts` (ref-or-element `explicitInitialFocus`, resolved at effect time) · `renderer/ui/popover-types.ts` + `popover.tsx` (`initialFocusRef` passthrough) · `renderer/settings/capability-prompt.tsx` (drop the global confirm shortcut + dead `acceptRef`; `denyRef` on Deny; `initialFocusRef={denyRef}`). **Tests:** +1 SDK (`use-focus-trap.test.tsx`: Explicit accepts a `RefObject`, resolved at effect time) + 5 jsdom (`capability-prompt.test.tsx`: deny initial-focus · stray-Enter-never-grants · Escape-denies · Allow-grants-on-activation · Deny-denies). Touched-area suites green: a11y + renderer ui + settings **352**, plus the new files. Typecheck clean (packages + all 11 apps); biome clean on touched files. doc 61 KBN-S-cap-prompt + KBN-S-popover rows updated.

## 2026-05-30 — 12.8 — vault corruption & registry recovery (all doc-28 scenarios)

Advanced 12.8 (recovery-scenario tests, doc 28 §Recovery) — the safe, low-collision, release-blocking forward step while a parallel agent held the apps/network area. First **audited all 7 scenarios against the code** to separate "test what exists" from "build the gap":

- **Already implemented + tested** (no new work): 1 empty-vault seeding (`vault.ts:createVault`), 3 Yjs corruption — per-update CRC32 loads to last-good (`ydoc-store.ts`, `ydoc-store.test.ts`), 4 outdated-vault forward migrations (`vault-migrations.ts` scaffold; list empty at the 10.8 freeze), 5 newer-vault refuse-to-open (`assertVaultFormatSupported`, `vault-format-rejection.test.ts`).
- **Genuine gaps:** 2 (SQLite corruption → rebuild-from-Yjs) and 7 (registry rebuild-by-scan) are unimplemented; 3's truncation flag is computed but never surfaced to the user; 6 (lost identity) is v1-no-recovery by design (v2 Recovery Kit, doc 51).

**Built scenario 7 — vault-registry rebuild-by-scan.** Previously `readRegistry()` silently degrades to an empty registry on a corrupt/missing `registry.json` — the vaults on disk are intact but the shell has forgotten where they are, and there was no rebuild path. New pure `packages/shell/src/main/vault/registry-recovery.ts`:
- `scanForVaults({ scanRoots, knownPaths, listSubdirs, readVaultJson })` — collects every directory carrying a valid `vault.json` from the standard root's subdirectories (`defaultVaultRoot()`) **plus** any `knownPaths` salvaged from the corrupt registry (checked directly), deduped by vault id (known-path wins over a re-scan), best-effort (an unreadable dir / bad JSON is skipped, never thrown).
- `vaultEntryFromVaultJson(path, parsed)` maps a found `vault.json` → registry `VaultEntry` (`lastOpenedAt` falls back to `createdAt` since the real value died with the registry).
- `productionScanForVaults(knownPaths?)` binds the core to `node:fs` over `defaultVaultRoot()`.
- **Read-only by design** — honors doc 28's load-bearing decision *"recovery operations always prompt before mutating"*: it returns candidates and writes nothing; the vault-picker surfaces them as an "Add back" offer (the renderer half, filed).

Dependency-injected so it runs entirely in-process (no FS, no Electron). +9 tests (`registry-recovery.test.ts`: mapper valid/missing-icon/null; subdir scan; known-path-direct; id-dedupe known-wins; skip-non-vault; best-effort-never-throws; empty-result-no-mutation). `typecheck:packages` clean; biome clean.

**Remaining 12.8** (filed in the plan): scenario 2 SQLite-corruption rebuild-from-Yjs is its own iteration (corruption-detect on `DataStores.open` + a Yjs→entities/search rebuild pass + restore/re-init prompt UX); scenario 3's `LoadResult.truncatedTail` → wire the "recent edits may be lost" warning into the vault-open notify path; scenario 7's vault-picker "Add back" renderer surface.

## 2026-05-30 — 12.8 (cont.): SQLite-corruption recovery substrate (scenario 2)

Built the substrate for the "Corrupted SQLite file" recovery scenario (doc 28 §Recovery), the second of 12.8's two real gaps. Previously a corrupt domain DB just threw out of `DataStores.open` and bricked the vault open with an opaque driver error.

- **New pure `packages/shell/src/main/storage/recovery-plan.ts`:** `CorruptionRecovery` enum + `recoveryForCorruptDb(kind)` policy total over `DataStoreKind` — `search → RebuildDerived`, `entities → PromptRebuildFromSources`, `ledger`/`registry → PromptRestoreOrReinit` (the doc's "rebuild from Yjs where possible; ledger/registry irrecoverable → prompt"). `isCorruptionError(err)` classifies the malformed-file case across drivers (SQLITE_CORRUPT / SQLITE_NOTADB codes + "not a database" / "disk image is malformed" / "file is encrypted" messages) while NOT matching transient/logic errors (BUSY, missing-table, unable-to-open). Typed `VaultCorruptionError` carries `{kind, recovery, cause}`.
- **`DataStores.open` integration:** open + migrate now route through `openMigratedOrRecover`. On a corruption-class failure: **search.db** (a derived FTS index) is dropped — file + `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal` sidecars — and recreated empty (re-indexes lazily, no prompt, the only auto-mutation); **entities/ledger/registry** are **never auto-destroyed** — they throw `VaultCorruptionError` carrying the recovery action so the caller can prompt (restore from backup, re-init, or a confirmed rebuild-from-Yjs). Honors doc 28's load-bearing "recovery operations always prompt before mutating". Non-corruption errors (migration bug, permissions) propagate unchanged — happy path untouched.

+17 tests (4 corruption + 13 recovery-plan): `recovery-plan.test.ts` (per-kind policy, exhaustive `DataStoreKind` coverage, corruption-code + message classification incl. negative cases, `VaultCorruptionError` shape) + `data-stores.test.ts` corruption block driving **real on-disk corruption** (write garbage over a created DB file → search auto-rebuilds + is queryable; ledger → `VaultCorruptionError` w/ `PromptRestoreOrReinit`; entities → `PromptRebuildFromSources`; healthy DB untouched). Full storage suite 150/150; `typecheck:packages` clean; biome clean.

## 2026-06-02 — B6.4b transclusion live body preview (nested mount) + table-resize fix

**B6.4b render-half landed — Notes (9.6).** The `!@`-transclusion now paints the target's *live* body inline, read-only, gated by the `decideTransclusionRender` keystone (5/31). Chose a **nested read-only `<BrainstormEditor>` mount** over the Lexical-free `EditorPreview` the plan first sketched: a transcluded body keeps full fidelity (mentions / embeds / images / tables / *nested* transclusions all render through the same `NOTES_ADDITIONAL_NODES` set), whereas feeding `EditorPreview` would have required a fragile Yjs-XmlText→`SerializedEditorState` reconstruction (the reverse of the `@lexical/yjs` binding) that doesn't exist.

- **Wiring.** New `transclusion-render-context.tsx` — a context carrying `{ ancestorChain, renderBody }`. `TransclusionNode.decorate()` (exported `TransclusionView`) reads it, runs `decideTransclusionRender(ancestorChain, entityId)`, and on `Render` invokes the injected `renderBody`; on `CycleElided`/`DepthElided` shows a muted "open source" hint under the header card. New `transclusion-body.tsx` — `renderTransclusionBody` mounts a read-only `<BrainstormEditor editable={false}>` bound to `useYDoc(entityId)` with the full Notes node set + `<EditablePlugin editable={false}>`, and re-provides the context with `entityId` appended so a deeper transclusion of an ancestor collapses instead of recursing.
- **Two non-obvious constraints solved.** (1) The chain provider is mounted *above* `<BrainstormEditor>`, not as a composer child: Lexical paints decorators through `RichTextPlugin` → `useDecorators` → `createPortal`, so a decorator's React-context ancestors are the ancestors of `RichTextPlugin` (i.e. providers above `<LexicalComposer>`, where `EditorI18nProvider` already sits) — a composer-*child* provider is a sibling of `RichTextPlugin` and invisible to decorators. (2) `renderBody` is *injected through context* rather than imported, because the body renderer imports `NOTES_ADDITIONAL_NODES` (→ `TransclusionNode`); a direct import back would cycle. Verified from the `@lexical/react` source before building, not assumed.
- **Tests.** `transclusion-render.test.tsx` (+5 jsdom, stub `renderBody`): render mounts the body · host-first chain passed minus the target · target-in-chain elides *without* invoking the renderer · 10-deep chain depth-elides · header-only degraded mount when no renderer wired. Real-shell `tests/perf/specs/notes-transclusion-body.spec.ts`: note H seeded with a marker, note T transcludes H → H's marker paints inside the read-only `.notes__transclusion-body-content`, `data-decision="render"`, `contenteditable="false"`. New keystroke-free dev hooks `insertTransclusion` + `currentNoteId` (Playwright keystrokes corrupt the Yjs editor). Workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) clean; biome clean; apps/notes suite green apart from one **pre-existing** `property-block-decorator` failure (reproduces with these changes stashed).

**Table column-resize fix (B11.3 follow-up).** The drag handle is `position: fixed` off a viewport rect but was only recomputed on `mousemove`, so a pure scroll stranded it at a stale screen position detached from the column edge ("moves with the scroll"). Added capture-phase `scroll` + `window` `resize` listeners that drop the hover handle (re-tracks on the next move); a live drag now recomputes the table rect each move so it stays aligned. Restyled `.bs-editor__table-col-resizer` from a hard 2px bar to a rounded 3px line that brightens on `[data-dragging]`. Extended `tests/perf/specs/notes-table-resize.spec.ts` with a scroll-clear regression assertion (real-shell green); `table-ops` 13/13; typecheck + biome clean.

**B11.4 Shiki syntax highlighting — COMPLETE (Notes code blocks).** Copy / language-picker / word-wrap / line-numbers had already shipped; this lands the highlighter — the "one large piece left".

- **Extraction (DRY, copy-two).** The code-editor's Shiki engine (singleton highlighter, github-light/dark themes, JS-regex engine, grammar code-split table, test DI seam) moved to a string-keyed shared `@brainstorm/sdk/code-highlight`: `tokenizeShiki(code, shikiId, theme)` / `ensureShikiLanguage(shikiId)` / `isHighlightableLanguage` / `HighlightTheme` / `setHighlighterFactory` / `resetHighlighter`. The code-editor's `logic/highlight.ts` is now a thin `LanguageKey`→shiki-id adapter delegating to it — its 11 tests pass unchanged. `shiki` becomes an SDK dep; `cpp` added to the grammar table for Notes' picker set.
- **Notes overlay.** Shiki tokenization is async (grammars load on demand), so it can't drive a synchronous Lexical node transform. New read-only `CodeHighlightPlugin` paints a per-block `<pre>` overlay (never touches the node tree / serialization, like the line-numbers gutter): portalled into `.notes__main` (the `position: relative` scroll container) at each block's content-space offset so **vertical** scroll moves it natively (no rAF lag); the block's own **horizontal** scroll on long lines is mirrored onto the overlay's inner `<code>` via `translateX(-scrollLeft)` off the block's `scroll` event. The block text goes transparent (`caret-color` kept) so the coloured overlay shows through; every block keeps a plain fallback paint so the transparent text is never unbacked. Theme follows the app's resolved root `color-scheme` (luminance-derived by the preload from the active theme bg, not the OS) via a style-attr `MutationObserver` — light tokens never land on a dark code bg. A module-level `(theme, grammar, text)` token cache avoids re-tokenizing unchanged blocks.
- **Why overlay, not in-model.** Lexical's native `@lexical/code` highlighting is Prism + synchronous; we standardised on Shiki (async, TextMate grammars). An async-then-mutate pipeline would bake per-token colour into serialized `CodeHighlightNode`s (theme-coupled, body bloat). The overlay keeps the model clean and theme-switchable.
- **Tests.** SDK `code-highlight.test.ts` (+10, DI'd fake highlighter: lazy-load / singleton / concurrent-share / unknown-id / chunk-null / load-throw / tokenize-throw / theme passthrough); code-editor `highlight.test.ts` 11/11 green through delegation; real-shell `tests/perf/specs/notes-code-highlight.spec.ts` (a TypeScript block grows a `.notes__code-highlight` overlay with coloured `span[style*=color]` tokens mirroring the source). New `setSelectedCodeLanguage` dev hook. Workspace `tsc` (packages + apps) + biome clean; the one pre-existing `property-block-decorator` failure is unrelated (reproduces stashed). Size budgets are shell-only and the shell doesn't import the subpath, so unaffected.

## 2026-06-04 — 9.17.14 — Whiteboard snap-to-guides (alignment magnet)

✅ DONE (2026-06-04). Completes 9.17.14 (align + distribute landed 2026-06-03). Pure `logic/snap.ts` `computeSnap(moving, others, threshold)`: pairs the dragged rect's three vertical reference lines (left / centre-x / right) and three horizontal (top / centre-y / bottom) against every neighbour's lines, picks the smallest in-threshold nudge per axis (X and Y independent, so a node can snap to one neighbour's left edge and another's centre at once), returns `{dx, dy, guides}` with each guide spanning the union of the moving rect + the matched neighbour. Wired into the node drag `pointermove`: the raw pointer position is magnetised before the delta is computed, so the node sticks to a neighbour's edge/centre within `6px / zoom`; `snapNeighbours` excludes the moving set (the node, its group, a frame's captured contents) + hidden nodes. Guides render as thin accent lines in a new world-transformed `.whiteboard__guides` layer (thickness `1/zoom` → ~1px on screen) and clear on drag-end. A `__brainstormWhiteboardDev` hook (parallel to `__brainstormNotesDev`) drives the same snap+move primitives so a real-shell spec can verify the path — Playwright's synthetic pointer can't drive `setPointerCapture`. +7 tests (`snap.test.ts`) + a real-shell visual spec (`whiteboard-snap.spec.ts`, 44s). apps/whiteboard 239/239; tsc + biome clean. ## 2026-06-06 — 11b.1 — Automations scaffold + four contracts + capability keystone

✅ DONE (2026-06-06). **Automations started as a priority insert** ahead of serial order (by request — the engine spine drives the dogfood business ladder: recurring reminders/cadence + entity-event workflows). The table's `gate Stage 11 + 7b + Net` one-liner is softer per-iteration: `7b` notifications ✅ (11b.5), `Net-1` ✅ (11b.8), `9.10` Files host ✅ (11b.10), `9.3` ✅ (11b.6) are all cleared — only `11b.7` (Stage 11 AI broker), `.9` (OQ-167 Code step), `.11` (OQ-166 builder) stay parked.

New `@brainstorm/sdk-types/automations.ts` (contract leaf, only `enum-guard` imported): freezes the four canonical types — `Workflow/Trigger/WorkflowRun/Reminder/v1` payloads + the full `WorkflowStep` union (12 kinds; `BranchStep` uses `consequent`/`alternate`, not `then`/`else`, to dodge the thenable/reserved-word trap the `noThenProperty` lint guards) — plus the `StepKind` / `TriggerKind` / `WorkflowRunStatus` / `MemoryMode` / `EntityOp` / `ConcurrencyPolicy` / `EntityEventVerb` enums (each with a frozen table + `enumGuard`), `ENGINE_STEP_KINDS` / `ENGINE_TRIGGER_KINDS` subsets marking what the spine builds vs. what's gated, and structural validators (`validateWorkflow/Trigger/WorkflowRun/Reminder` → stable `AutomationIssueCode`s).

**Security keystone** (doc 39 §Capabilities): `capabilityImplies` mirrors the shell ledger's scope rule (same `service.verb`; exact scope, `*` wildcard covering any scope, or both unscoped — an unscoped request is *not* satisfied by a `*` grant); `stepCapabilities` + `aggregateWorkflowCapabilities` walk the step tree (incl. branch/for-each children) into the sorted union the user grants at save-time; `validateCapabilityTiers` enforces the three-tier intersection `agent-tools ⊆ workflow-caps ⊆ app-caps`, **fail-closed at every tier** (a broad app cap does NOT let an agent escape the workflow's narrower frozen set — covered by an explicit test).

App graduated from the coming-soon stub: `manifest.json` registers the 4 types with inline JSON schemas + narrow per-type read/write caps + `entities.read:*` + `notifications.post` + `intents.dispatch:open` (no AI/network/files surface yet — those arrive with their step kinds), `Workflow/v1` as primary opener/intent. The scaffold (`app.ts` + `automation-repository.ts` defensive mappers + `runtime.ts` bridge) lists Workflows / Reminders / Runs through `services.entities` with an empty-workspace preview-drop fallback. +51 tests (35 contract incl. the three-tier fail-closed cases + 16 app: manifest validator + round-trip/persistence); typecheck (packages + 19 apps)/biome/build all green. **Next: 11b.2 SchedulerService** (reuse the 9.15.5 recurrence engine; pin OQ-165 RRULE-only). Full detail in [implementation-plan.md](implementation-plan.md) (Automations §11b).

## 2026-06-06 — 11b.2 — Automations SchedulerService (timer-free core + restart-survival)

🟡 PARTIAL (2026-06-06). The shell-main owner of automation triggers' fire schedule (apps aren't background processes, so the schedule can't live in the renderer — a workflow fires whether or not its window is open). **OQ-165 resolved**: rather than a cron dialect or a parallel RRULE store, time triggers carry the structured `@brainstorm/sdk-types` `Recurrence` (its `Custom { rrule }` arm holds raw RFC-5545 for the long tail) and the scheduler reuses the 9.15.5 `nextOccurrence` engine wholesale — one recurrence representation across Tasks/Calendar/Automations, zero parallel engines.

Pure `trigger-schedule.ts`: `computeNextFire(config, after)` (one-shot + recurrence, earliest-wins, null once spent/empty/Custom-RRULE), `dueFires(fires, now)` (armed + `<= now`, deterministic by `nextFireAt` then `triggerId`), `rescheduleAfterFire` (recurring re-arms from the fire instant so a late wake jumps to the next *future* slot instead of replaying every missed one; spent one-shot → dormant), `earliestFireAt`. `SchedulerService` over it: in-memory `Map`, `register`/`unregister`/`tick(now)→WorkflowRunRequest[]` (one request per due trigger × workflow)/`nextWakeAt`, restart-survival through an injected `SchedulerStore` port (sync-or-async, so a better-sqlite3 adapter stays sync). The clock stays out of the class — the timer is the wiring's job — so the whole fire/reschedule/persist path is unit-tested incl. an explicit process-restart (`hydrate` over a shared store) and a 5-day-late-wake case. +20 tests (12 schedule core + 8 service); shell typecheck + biome clean.

**Remaining 11b.2**: the concrete registry.db `SchedulerStore` adapter (registry-schema migration + repo), the real-timer drain loop, `workers.ts` + broker registration, and an in-process pipeline integration test (per CLAUDE.md §4). `EntityEvent`/`Manual` trigger wiring is 11b.6. Full detail in [implementation-plan.md](implementation-plan.md) (Automations §11b.2).

## 2026-07-21 — Clip-1 (web clipper) DROPPED — superseded by in-app Browser clipping

**Web clipper removed from the plan entirely (user directive 2026-07-21).** The external-browser extension clipper (`Clip-1`) is **not needed** — clipping is delivered in the in-app Web Browser via **Net-3** live-DOM capture (`web.capture` → the same Net-2 extraction core → the same `Bookmark/v1`). This is doc-54's original "the in-app browser subsumes the web-clipper" stance, confirmed. Prior states: reinstated post-v1 (2026-05-19) → removed-to-separate-effort (2026-05-30) → now fully dropped. Edits: `implementation-plan.md` Clip-1 rung → ❌ dropped-superseded note (OQ-RX-7 retired); `docs/apps/58-readable-content-extraction.md` retitled §Web clipper "DROPPED 2026-07-21", feeders count 3→2 across intro/decision/phasing-table/summary; `reference/11-open-questions.md` OQ-RX-7 `[RETIRED — clipper dropped 2026-07-21]`; `00-index.md` 25f + 25j feeder lists trimmed to two. Nothing in v1 depended on it, so removal costs nothing. Net-3 (in-app clipping) remains a tracked, queued rung.

## 2026-07-24 — four-feature parallel drop (Agent-11c · Browser-6 · Form 8.10.5 · i18n 12.15/15d)

Four independent iterations authored in parallel isolated shell worktrees, integrated as separate PRs (shell #271–#274, all merged onto `main` @ `16c664cf`). Each test-first; `typecheck:packages` + full `lint` green per branch; the two sdk-types consumers (agent, browser) app-typechecked against branch sdk-types via a paths override (the worktree symlink resolves `@brainstorm-os/*` to the main tree — documented cross-package caveat).

- **Agent-11c — provenance + back-links (#271).** Agent-created entities carry a server-authoritative `agentProvenance = { agent, conversationId, createdAt }` (new `@brainstorm-os/sdk-types/agent-provenance`, mirroring `aiProvenance`-on-Message; no migration). Non-forgeable: entities service strips any caller-supplied reserved key on create/update then re-stamps `agent` from the broker-verified `envelope.app`; the model never reaches the write path (only the human approve gesture persists, supplying just the conversation id). Chat renders created-object chips derived reactively from the vault snapshot, opening via the cap-checked `open` intent. +17 tests. Threads into 11d/11e.
- **Browser-6 — downloads → Files host (#272).** Session `will-download` captured in the web-view host → buffered under a size cap → sealed into the encrypted asset store → `File/v1` via the shared `entities.create` path (per-type cap, DEK, asset-ref bind, live change event). Untrusted-input hardening isolated in pure `web-download.ts` (basename filename sanitize, served-mime allow-list, 256 MiB ceiling, http(s) source validation). New `DownloadStarted/Completed/Failed` events + chrome notice. +24 tests. Open: private-tab downloads currently persist.
- **Form-designer 8.10.5 — apply-to-type + install-contract round-trip (#273).** Forms persist their type `scope`; `toAppLayoutEntry`/`formLayoutIssues`/`isFormApplicableToType` project a form through the frozen `validateAppLayouts` (the install SSoT); the Builder "Apply to type" action gates on it before persisting. Real `resolveLayout` + `validateAppLayouts` round-trip tests. Gate was 8.5 (✅), not the post-v1 8.3 pipeline — visible render of an applied default stays 8.3-gated. +9 net (78 form-designer green).
- **i18n 12.15/15d — declare shipped overlay packs (#274).** The fr/de/it/pt catalogs (#266) were on `main` but the 12 apps' `manifest.json` `i18n.locales` still said `["en","es"]`, so the shipped packs were undeclared and `check-app-i18n` failed (48 orphan errors, lint red). Declared `["en","es","de","fr","it","pt"]` across all 12 manifests; added e2e tests (chat + contacts) resolving the real `LOCALE_PACK_IMPORTERS` to prove de/fr/it/pt overlay English per app. Runtime seam (handshake `locale` + `app:locale-changed` → `app-preload.setLocale` → `useLocale`/`useLocalePackT`) confirmed connected end-to-end. +8 tests. Lesson: a locale pack + importer without the manifest declaration is a silent lint-gate failure — declare in the same change.
